## Title Section
-> **This is the Book of the Rectifications of the Splendor** <-
<note>original: "Sefer Tikunei ha-Zohar." The word "Tikunim" refers to "rectifications" or "arrangements," specifically seventy commentaries on the first word of the Torah, "In the beginning."</note>

---

## Archival Description
-> *Rectifications, that is, Preludes to the book* <-
-> *of Zohar. By Rabbi Simeon, son of Jochai.* <-
<note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, a 2nd-century sage, is traditionally credited with the core teachings of the Zohar, the foundational work of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah).</note>

*It was written by Rabbi Chaim in the year of the world*
*4971, that is, the year of Christ 1211. On*
*parchment pages where it is written in various places.*
<note>The "year of the world" refers to the Hebrew calendar (Anno Mundi). While the inscription dates the manuscript to 1211 CE, modern scholars often debate these early dates for Zoharic manuscripts, as the Zohar first appeared publicly in late 13th-century Spain.</note>

*Number 391.*
*Vatican Manuscript.*

---

**Translation of Latin description:**
*Rectifications, that is, Preludes to the book of Zohar. By Rabbi Simeon son of Jochai. Written by Rabbi Chaim in the year of the world 4971, that is, the year of Christ 1211. On parchment pages where it has text sporadically. No. 391. Vatican Manuscript.*

<summary>This frontispiece identifies the manuscript as the Tikunei ha-Zohar, attributing it to Shimon bar Yochai and noting it was copied by a scribe named Rabbi Chaim in 1211 CE. It serves as an official archival record for the Vatican Library's Hebrew collection.</summary>
<keywords>Tikunei ha-Zohar, Kabbalah, Shimon bar Yochai, Vatican Library, Hebrew manuscript, 13th century, Rabbi Chaim</keywords>

--- Page 10 ---
<meta>This page serves as the formal identification leaf for Vatican Hebrew Manuscript 391. It establishes the traditional attribution of the text to the 2nd-century sage Shimon bar Yochai and records a specific, albeit controversial, medieval date for this particular copy.</meta>

## Main Text

-> **Reparations <note>original: "Tikunim"</note> from the Radiance <note>original: "Zohar"</note> and the Book of Leviticus** <-
-> **by Rabbi Shimon son of Yochai, peace be upon him** <-

---

-> **Reparations, that is, Preludes to the Book** <-
-> **of Radiance <note>original: "Zoar"</note> by Rabbi Simeon son of Jochai.** <-

-> *Written by Rabbi Chayim in the year of the world* <-
-> *4871, that is, the year of Christ 1110, as* <-
-> *is well noted on page 438, verso, where it says: "finished and completed."* <-

-> **Vatican 391.** <-
-> **Number 226 Vatican.** <-

---

<note>
The Hebrew text identifies the volume as "Tikunim from the Zohar and the Book of Vayikra" (the latter referring to the Zohar's commentary on the biblical book of Leviticus) by "Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him." 

The Latin note translates this as "Tikunim, i.e., Preludes to the Book of Zohar by R. Simeon son of Jochai." It claims the manuscript was written by a scribe named Rabbi Chayim in the Hebrew year 4871 (corresponding to 1110/1111 CE). This dating is highly significant and debated by scholars, as the Zohar is generally thought to have been disseminated in the late 13th century. 

The references "Vat. 391" and "Nro. 226" are the cataloging numbers for the Vatican Library's collection.
</note>

<note>
**Technical Vocabulary:**
- **Tikunim:** Literally "Reparations" or "Rectifications"; specifically referring here to the *Tikkunei HaZohar*, a collection of seventy commentaries on the first word of the Torah.
- **Zohar:** "Radiance" or "Splendor"; the foundational work of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah).
- **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai:** A 2nd-century Tannaitic sage to whom the Zohar is traditionally attributed.
- **Peace be upon him:** A common honorific used for the deceased.
</note>

<summary>This title page identifies Vatican Manuscript 391 as a collection of Zoharic texts and Tikkunim attributed to Shimon bar Yochai. It includes a Latin inscription dating the transcription to 1110 CE by a scribe named Rabbi Chayim.</summary>
<keywords>Tikkunei HaZohar, Shimon bar Yochai, Vatican Library, Kabbalah, Hebrew manuscripts, 12th century, Rabbi Chayim</keywords>

## Pekudei - The Palaces

Holy and the radiance from above—from where do we derive it? From the place called **Shoshan** <note>The Lily; a symbolic name for the Shekhinah or the Divine Presence</note> and... <note>The text continues according to the Zohar: "and the Lily is the secret of the Bride"</note>
She is crowned with the grace of her husband, and the radiance is hers because she gazed for a moment like the radiance of holi... <note>Likely: "holiness"</note>
And the secret of the Covenant <note>The sefirah of Yesod, representing the procreative/connective force</note>—behold, beneath his charge are all the kinds of beings in the firmament.
Precious is the secret of the Covenant that stands above and below, and they dwell [therein].
And behold, we have said that all of them are within the secret of this Name. Holy is their radiance on the right, within which
are many colors. Holy is the radiance corresponding to this in the upper firmament; they were created in peace and in dominion
by the secret of the Holy King. The secret of the Covenant is over them, over the radiance that stands, and every decree and law is for us
and does not depart. How holy is the King over the radiance! And this is the first time, and the time, and the one who is summoned <note>original: "Zimna" and "Zamin"; these are names of angelic powers or functional forces within this specific Palace</note>
Holy is the radiance that stands over them, and it is understood that he is holy and the radiance is his, which is
holy and his radiance. And it is found that at that time they are summoned, since there was a soul
and he is certainly summoned. And so it is hidden above. A "holy" time he called, and this radiance is holy.
It went forth and its radiance is holy, and because of this, He is the Unique of the Unique.
And the radiance of the Holy One leads them and sustains them all his days; and the time and radiance—what is the meas... <note>measure</note>
The Holy One went forth to them, the King over the holy, and the holy radiance, and they go forth from it.
[The scales] of the serpent—behold, they are under the authority of the Holy One, and they are like the colors and the light of the horse for eternity.
The elders and the precious ones of the world is He, and over the judge and the hidden, and between the hands of those that were cre... <note>created</note>
So again, and at the time that the Holy Covenant is over them, and all is within the secret.
Myriads and tens of thousands <unclear>ministering</unclear>—it is certainly He and the radiance.

<summary>This manuscript page describes the mystical Second Palace (Heichal ha-Zekhut), emphasizing the "radiance" (Ziv) that emanates from the union of the Divine Bride and the Covenant. It details the angelic hierarchies and the "Unique" nature of the Divine light that sustains the celestial firmaments.</summary>
<keywords>Zohar, Heichalot, Palace of Merit, Shoshan (Lily), Covenant (Yesod), Radiance (Ziv), Angelic Orders, Pekudei</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Divine Countenance, specifically focusing on the "Beard" (Dikna) of the Macroprosopus (the Long Face), a central theme in the Zohar's Idra Rabba. It transitions from the hidden aspects of the crown to the revealed attributes of mercy.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar / Kabbalistic Manuscript)

...And those are the seven that are not seen when it speaks of the crowns of the beard <note>original: "Tikunei Dikna" — the thirteen configurations or "repairs" of the Divine Beard representing attributes of mercy</note> before they emerge and encircle that which covers the small crown <note>The "small crown" likely refers to the head of the Lesser Countenance (Zeir Anpin)</note> that covers it. From the crown, thirteen configurations are awakened, which are the holy garments of the Holy One, Blessed be He. These are visible and flow down, and His beard is gathered between the holy [realms], and all those things that are hidden within it in the paths of the way. And thirteen engraved worlds emerge from beneath its branches, and concerning this it is written and this is said:
> **"The wings of a dove are covered with silver, and her pinions with shimmering gold"** <note>Psalm 68:14</note>
This is the secret of the Shekhinah <note>The Divine Presence, often personified as feminine or as a dove</note> which covers Him with the color of holiness from the whiteness of Mercy <note>original: "Chesed" — the sephirah of loving-kindness</note>. And they flow at that hour when the beard is engraved within it as one, and the Accuser <note>original: "Satan"</note> is removed from behind. And so it is written regarding it, and all who gaze upon the power of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and it is enough to look upon this, and it is enough to look upon the image of the supernal holy living beings <note>original: "Chayot" — high-ranking angels</note>. For they are worthy of the longing that belongs to those who see, for the righteous are those who see and reveal the revelation of mercy upon Israel. And within it are thirteen engraved worlds, and all of them awaken the holiness of holies from the color of the Holy One. And by this judgment, they awaken the Lamp <note>original: "Butzina" — a term for a source of divine illumination or a great sage</note>. And anyone who does not know how to arrange [these secrets] and pass over them, certainly of him it is said that it is as if he trespassed against the holy things of Heaven. But happy is the portion of the righteous who know the way of their Master and look upon Him through the Torah. And concerning this it is written: **"Gaze, O pillars of light"** and the branches of the Tree, so as not to treat with disrespect the unity of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhintieh"</note>.

---

<summary>This manuscript page provides a mystical interpretation of the "Thirteen Attributes of Mercy" symbolized as the configurations of the Divine Beard, using the imagery of a silver-winged dove to represent the Shekhinah. It warns that these secrets must be handled with proper knowledge and reverence to maintain the unity of the Divine.</summary>

**Terminology and Contextual Notes:**
The presence of terms like **image** (the divine archetype), **above and below** (the mirroring of spiritual and physical realms), and **secret** suggests a passage discussing the correspondence between the divine realms and the physical world. This is a central theme in Zoharic cosmogony <note>theories regarding the origin of the universe</note>, often found in the Prologue or the beginning of the commentary on Genesis.

<summary>This fragmentary page from the Zohar discusses the mystical creation of the world and the "Holy Name," emphasizing the "secret" correspondence between the divine image and the lower realms. --- Page 20 ---
<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the construction of the Tabernacle (Mishkan), focusing on the metaphysical correspondence between the physical structure built by Bezalel and its celestial counterpart.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Observe this Tabernacle: whenever the Tabernacle stands in its proper arrangement, the celestial Tabernacle likewise stands in perfection as is fitting. <margin>It is written</margin> For it is written, **"And the Tabernacle became one"** <note>Exodus 36:13</note>. The use of the definite article <note>the Hebrew letter 'He'</note> serves to include the other Tabernacle, the one above, which was made as one with it. As Rabbi <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note> Shimon said: At the moment Bezalel constructed the Tabernacle below, the Tabernacle above was constructed <strike>the Tabernacle which is one</strike>. And come and see: at the time it stands [below], it is likewise the mystery of the one above, all of them as one, and regarding this it says, "And the Tabernacle became one."

The mystery of this is because at this time, when it is holy and shines above and below, all things cling to a single mystery, and regarding this <note>original: "ve-al da"</note> "And the Tabernacle became one." <margin>And the Tabernacle became one</margin>
---
<strike>To find within it the holiness from above; in this manner, all are found in the single mystery of the Holy Name.</strike>
---
To be found in perfection as one, and all of them are the conclusion of this verse, "And the Tabernacle became one."
And come and see: at the time it is holy and shines as one, to find within it the holiness from above, in this manner all are found in the single mystery of the Holy Name <term>Shema Kadisha: the Divine Name of God representing His essence</term>. And regarding this it is written **"The Tabernacle, The Tabernacle"** two <note>original: "trei"</note> times, to show that they are all one mystery above and below. And because it is holy above, it is holy below; holy above, for this is the mystery of the holiness of the Holy Name that we have mentioned. <strike>within it</strike>
**"And the Tabernacle became one."** This is to show that they are all a single mystery, and this is the mystery of the Holy Name <strike>of the Name</strike>, for the Great Name, which is the Holy Name above and below, is so because it is exactly in the likeness of the one above, and regarding this: "And the Tabernacle became one."

<summary>This page explores the Zoharic concept of "as above, so below," asserting that the physical Tabernacle built by Bezalel mirrored a spiritual Tabernacle, creating a unified channel for the Holy Name. The repetition of the word "Tabernacle" in scripture is interpreted as a sign of this dual reality becoming a single mystical unity.</summary>

## Portion of Bereshit (In the Beginning)

The secret of the matter <note>Genesis 1:3</note> **"And God said, let there be light"** is that he saw, and a light was visible, and it was possible to see by it from one end of the world to the other. But it was hidden away and remained as the light of the worlds, which is "Let there be light"—the light of the <term>Ancient One (Atika)</term> <note>The most hidden, primordial aspect of the Divine</note> which is hidden and remains for the time to come, when the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>The standard rabbinic name for God</note> is destined to give it to the righteous. When He said to him, **"Let there be light,"** all that light was hidden and remained.

One should look well to the merit of those who are worthy to delight in that light of the <term>Holy Ancient One</term>, for it is because of merit that it is set apart; this is the <term>Merciful One (Rachmana)</term>. And no one is able to see all the lights that come except to know that the light is based on the truth of this hidden Ancient One, as it is written: **"Let there be light, and there was light."** It was revealed and then hidden within it forever, for it is the World to Come. And because of this, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, passed it by and hid it so that the wicked should not see it or gaze upon it.

And if you should say: "Righteous are those who merit to see that light eye to eye!" Happy are they, for this is the sun of the world that shines on every side, and whoever merits it, merits the light of the Life of the World which is above all. **"And there was light"**—this is a hint to the Holy Ancient One, which is the light that shines for the King above and below. Therefore, when this light shines, it never diminishes; and all of this is in the lamp that goes out from those holy paths for those who have merited to know this.

<summary>This page discusses the "Hidden Light" (Or HaGanuz) created on the first day of Genesis, explaining that it allowed for infinite vision before being reserved by God for the righteous in the World to Come.</summary>
<keywords>Creation, Primordial Light, Ancient One, World to Come, Righteousness, Zohar, Genesis 1:3, Mysticism</keywords>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

What did you see? Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai said that he saw Rabbi Isaac as he was departing from the world <note>original: "דנפיק מעלמא"; a common Zoharic euphemism for dying</note>, and Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Eleazar stood up and took hold of his hands. When he entered, Rabbi Shimon said:

->**By the Life**<-

of the High King! <note>original: "בחיים די מלכא עלאה"; the manuscript emphasizes "Life" where printed editions often say "By the merit of the High King."</note> Whatever the son of Yochai has done, he has done. 

There is no life from this world; there is no life except **in this Life**, which is the life of "line by line" <note>original: "קו לקו"; a reference to Isaiah 28:10, interpreted here as the measured flow of divine energy</note> in the House of Study. And at that time, for behold, Life was present...

What is "Life"? It is that which takes up lives and sustenance <term>Chayyin ve-Mezoni: the spiritual and physical nourishment required for existence</term>, and holds them, and establishes them to be taken up by the day and its reception <note>The text is fragmented here; it likely refers to the cyclical reception of divine light between day and night</note> and prepares for them. There, the milk was gathered...

->**Line by Line**<-

He said to him: What is **line by line**? He said to him: He who said it, said it. He said to him: **Line by line**—these are lives and Life...

What did he do for him? He said to him: He who made the line. Because this Life, which is... <note>The original Zohar text clarifies: "Because the Life above is a Line"</note> ... **in the Life** of Life they act... ...Yochai said...

---

### Contextual Notes
*   **Narrative:** This text captures a dramatic moment where Rabbi Isaac is on the verge of death. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the master of the circle, uses his spiritual authority to "seize" Rabbi Isaac and prevent his soul from departing, swearing by the "Life of the High King" (God).
*   **The "Line" (Kav):** The discussion of **line by line** refers to the *Kav*, the thin thread of divine light that penetrates the void to create and sustain the universe. In this mystical context, "Life" is not an accident but a measured flow of light that can be extended through the study of Torah and the intervention of a Tzaddik (righteous leader) like Rabbi Shimon.
*   **Manuscript Variation:** This fragment is significant because it repeatedly uses the term **In Life** (**בחיים**), suggesting a specific liturgical or meditative emphasis on the divine name associated with eternal life, differing slightly from standard printed versions.

<summary>A mystical manuscript fragment from the Zohar depicting Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's intervention to save Rabbi Isaac from death by invoking the divine "Line" of Life. It explores the metaphysical nature of life as a flow of sustenance from the High King.</summary>
<keywords>Zohar, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, Rabbi Isaac, Life (Chayyim), The Line (Kav), afterlife, divine sustenance, Sephardic manuscript</keywords>

## Main Text (The Hidden Midrash)

And behold, I have heard from those pious ones <note>original: "chasidaya" — refers to a circle of early mystics or "saints"</note> regarding this matter, concerning the business of the **supernal image** <note>original: "dyokna" — the divine form or spiritual blueprint of a human being</note>. **And He distributed to them** a portion and a holy expansion, holy above and below. And what does the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He acquired and taught a certain inheritance, and He called out over that body of the Holy One, blessed be He, and all inherit it until King David comes, who said: *Preserve my soul, for I am pious* <note>Psalms 86:2</note>. And I heard that this expansion goes on through the worlds, and every matter that is required in the petition for life, as it is written: *The fear of the Lord leads to life* <note>Proverbs 19:23</note>.

And this one shall be blessed; blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever. *I have loved you with an eternal love* <note>Jeremiah 31:2</note>—He called out over it and went within it, and it goes forth for salvation, for resurrection, and for the destiny <note>original: "mazala" — constellation or spiritual flow</note> seen in the portion of the spirit that goes out through it, in the sustenance of life. And it comes to the door of life and the sustenance that is required; concerning this, we say:

---

## Genesis (Bereishit)

Rabbi Eleazar said: Is it not concerning the Supernal Image <note>Aramaic: *Demuta*; the spiritual archetype of humanity</note> that the scripture speaks, regarding the beauty of that form? ## Main Text (Zohar)

->From the House of Study: What is the meaning of that which is written: *Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is One*?<-

The unification is one within the six sides <note>original: "shit sitrin" — referring to the six spatial directions or the six emotional attributes of the divine realm</note>, and this unification is what we are required to perform: to unify the Holy Name in a single union throughout the six sides of the worlds. Even though we have established that they are all one single unity, nevertheless, here the unification is at the highest level.

**Hear, O Israel** <note>Deuteronomy 6:4</note> — We have already established that these represent the "Grandfather and Grandmother" <note>metaphors for the divine faculties of Wisdom (Chokhmah) and Understanding (Binah)</note> who are male and female, even though they exist as a single unity.

**The Lord** <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHWH</note> — This is the head of all, the primacy of all.

**Our God** — This is the mystery found within **Understanding** <term>Binah: the divine mother/womb</term> which waters everything.

**The Lord** — This is the strength of all, the root of all levels.

**One** — The unification of everything as one. And come and see <term>Aramaic: "Ta Chazi" — a call to contemplate a deeper truth</term>, we have established that *The Lord, our God, the Lord* are all one in a single unity, and because of this, He is called **One**. Behold, these three names are one, and they are called one in the mystery of the audible voice, which is one, yet contains three colors <note>or qualities</note> as one.

So too are *The Lord, our God, the Lord* one. They are the mystery of the voice which is one, yet they are three. Here is the mystery of that which is three-in-one, for they are one. *The Lord, our God, the Lord*—this is the mystery of the three supreme levels which are one. The mystery of the voice that is heard is one, yet it contains three colors as one. And because of this, He is called One, for the unification of everything is found within Him. And come and see: in the mystery of the levels above, they are three-in-one, and this is the mystery of **Hear, O Israel**...

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic analysis of the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy, specifically focusing on the phrase "Passes over transgression" from the Prophet Micah. The scribe uses a mix of Aramaic and Hebrew typical of Zoharic literature to explain how Divine Kindness (Chesed) neutralizes the effects of sin.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar Commentary)

"Passes over transgression" <note>original: "Over al Pesha"</note> refers to a skilled practitioner of kindness who passes over the transgressions committed against him and finds comfort in explaining the right path to the sinner. This is a special treasure, not merely an offering, but a way of life, because such a person acts as one who is poor and seeking <note>i.e., acting with humility rather than entitlement</note>.

"Passes over transgression"—this means he removes the "moth" <note>a metaphor for the corrosive nature of sin</note> and everything that came before. When a person unifies these attributes within themselves, it provides support and strength through the wisdom of their Master. Through this, he is able to grant forgiveness. A <term>Commandment</term> <note>Aramaic: Pekuda; a divine decree or mitzvah</note> touches and awakens us, passing over the sins. Such a person's soul will not suffer punishment in Gehenna <note>Purgatory/the afterlife realm of purification</note>.

This is the power of God, lest it befall him, etc. He passes by and does not remain stuck, because of <term>Kindness</term> <note>Hebrew: Chesed; the Sefirah of expansive love and benevolence</note> which goes along with him. The <term>Divine Presence</term> <note>Hebrew: Shekhinah; the immanent feminine aspect of God</note> accompanies him even in the face of debt/sin. It is said <unclear>like a line</unclear> of a tree; whoever walks in this path of Kindness, which is characterized by great compassion—and He is Great—this is the Kindness that erases the "screen" <note>the barrier between man and God created by sin</note>. He is blessed and protected by it; he passes through and has no standing accusation against him.

And this "Passes over transgression" is because he is pure of name, and it never ceases. This is the goodness of Kindness, and it is the rectification for the sin of "These are your gods" <note>referencing the Golden Calf</note>. Be strong, for at all times the Old One <note>Ancient of Days/Keter</note> leaves His servants' sins behind. This is what we have heard: "Behold, your Queen is in your hand; go and do not fear."

Kindness shall be the appointed time, for this is the Supernal Kindness. Faces are changed and they shine. This is the wiping away of the heart's stains. Whoever merits <term>Humility</term> <note>Hebrew: Anavah</note> and compassion on the path toward God—the secret is that he shall return to merit despite the transgression. These are the voices out of the noise and the strengths.

He shall <term>Subdue</term> <note>Hebrew: Yichbosh; Micah 7:19: "He will again have compassion on us; He will subdue our iniquities"</note>—meaning, he buries them in the ground. The "curve of the thigh" <note>referencing Jacob's struggle</note> is a sign before you, as it is written that He shall forgive. <meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra), specifically focusing on the opening word of the book and the nature of Divine communication.</meta>

## And He Called

"And He called to Moses" <note>Leviticus 1:1</note> is as it is said: "And one called to another and said: Holy..." <note>Isaiah 6:3</note>. And what is the difference? There [in Isaiah], it was with awe and fear, but here [with Moses], it was with joy and the desire of the heart.

"And He called to Moses"—what is this "calling"? This calling is a secret of the matter: this is a calling and that is a calling, but how does this one differ from that one? Rather, this is the calling of the **Sabbath** <term>Shabbat; the day of rest representing the realm of holiness and joy</term> and that is the calling of the weekday. The Sabbath is with joy and desire; the weekday is with awe and fear. This one comes from the inner palace, and that one from the outer palace.

Come and see: at first it is written, "And He called to Moses," and then, "and the Lord spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying." Rabbi Eleazar said: "Tent of Meeting" <term>Ohel Moed</term> is as it is said, "A tent that shall not be taken down" <note>Isaiah 33:20</note>, and as it is said, "The house of meeting for all living" <note>Job 30:23</note>. From here we learn that there is no "calling" except in the "meeting" <note>The Hebrew word 'Moed' means both an appointed time/festival and a meeting place</note>.

And come and see: "And He called to Moses"—by what name was he called? By the name of the angel **Metatron** <term>The supreme archangel and heavenly scribe in Jewish mysticism</term>, as it is said, "For My name is within him" <note>Exodus 23:21</note>. And we have established that he [the angel] called to him from within the Tent of Meeting. But that which says, "and the Lord spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting," this refers to the **Holy King** <term>The higher Divine aspect, often associated with the Sephirah of Tiferet</term> who spoke with him.

From here we learn that "calling" comes from below and "speaking" comes from above. For this reason, the word *Vayikra* ("And He called") is written with a **small Aleph** <note>original: "Aleph Ze'ira"; in Torah scrolls, the final letter of the first word of Leviticus is written smaller than the others</note>. This is the "small point" <term>The Sephirah of Malkhut/Kingship, the lowest of the divine emanations</term> where every "calling" is found. And because it is a small point, it requires a "calling" to draw it down from the side above; because it is a small point, it has no substance of its own until it is drawn from above.

And for this reason, *Vayikra* is written with a small Aleph. This is the secret of the Sabbath which comes from the **Left Side** <term>Gevurah; the attribute of Judgment/Strength</term>. Therefore, a "calling" is necessary, because the Left calls to the **Right Side** <term>Chesed; the attribute of Mercy/Kindness</term>, and it comes to the Right to be united with it in joy and the desire of the heart. Regarding this, it is called a "calling," and therefore a calling is in joy and desire. This is the secret of what they said regarding the "Tent of Meeting": a "Tent" of the "Appointed Times of the Lord," which are the Sabbaths and the Festivals, for "calling" is found in them, as it is said: "Proclamations of Holiness" <note>Leviticus 23:4; the word for 'proclamations' shares the same root as 'calling'</note>.

<summary>This page explores the mystical significance of the opening word of Leviticus, "Vayikra," explaining that the "Small Aleph" represents the Divine Presence (Malkhut) needing to be awakened from above. It distinguishes between the fearful calling of the angels and the joyful, Sabbath-like calling experienced by Moses.</summary>

<keywords>Vayikra, Small Aleph, Metatron, Tent of Meeting, Sabbath, Malkhut, Right and Left Sides, Divine Union, Moses</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And if you should say: is it because of this that one is changed from the other? Come and see, this one depends on that one, and that one on this one, as it is written: ->"And a **spirit of jealousy** passed over him, and he was jealous of his wife"<- <note>Numbers 5:14</note>.
And if you should say, what is the meaning of **spirit of jealousy**? It is because there is a **spirit of impurity** <note>original: "ruach mesavuta"</note> that dwells upon her, and she is defiled by it. What is the reason? Because this is from the **Other Side** <note>The "Sitra Achra," the realm of evil or demonic forces in Kabbalistic thought</note>. And this is the **spirit of jealousy**. 

And if you should say that the **spirit of jealousy** is actually the **Holy Spirit** <note>original: "ruach kudsha"</note>—come and see that it is both this way and that way. And because of this, it is written: "And a **spirit of jealousy** passed over him." What is the meaning of "passed over"? It is as you say: a "passing" or an "overflow" <note>The Hebrew word "v'avar" (passed) is linked here to "evrah" (wrath/overflow)</note> of that spirit of impurity upon them. And regarding this, it is written: "and he was jealous of his wife," for this is a jealousy of significance. 

Come and see: **spirit of jealousy** is a spirit of impurity that goes and dwells upon her. And regarding this, it is written: "And a **spirit of jealousy** passed over him." What is "passed over"? It is as it is said: ->"And a wind passed and cleansed them"<- <note>Job 37:21</note>. And this is what we have said: because it is a spirit of impurity that passed over her, and she was defiled. 

And if you should say that the **spirit of jealousy** is the **Holy Spirit**—it is certainly so, for it is the jealousy of **the Holy One, Blessed be He**. Come and see: at the moment she is defiled, the **spirit of impurity** dwells upon her, and the **spirit of jealousy**, which is holy, passes over him <insert>the husband</insert>. And regarding this, it is written: "And a **spirit of jealousy** passed over him." That **Holy Spirit** we mentioned and that **spirit of impurity** passed over her and she was defiled. Come and see, this **spirit of jealousy**...

## Ezekiel

And this is the secret of the verse: **"And it came to pass in the thirtieth year..."** etc. <note>Ezekiel 1:1</note> from the outside to the inside, upon the river. And this is the River Chebar, of which it is said that it is one of the four rivers that went out from Eden. And this is a river whose waters never cease, and because of this, it is the river that has existed "already" <note>The Hebrew word for "already" is *Kevar* (כבר), identical to the name of the river Chebar. The text plays on this linguistic connection to suggest the river's primordial nature.</note> from the very beginning. And it says: **"And I was among the exiles by the River Chebar, the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God."** What are "visions of God"? These are the visions that showed the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed in Kabbalah as the feminine aspect of God that dwells with the people in exile.</note>, and for this reason, it says "visions of God." And the secret of this is in all the light that never ceases.

And it says that the living beings went out, and five <unclear>living beings</unclear> from the wilderness. And what are they? Man, Lion, Ox, and Eagle. And upon their backs was revealed the secret of the Torah, and the secret of this light shines in all of them. And this is the secret of what is called the <term>Holy Living Beings</term> <note>original: *Chayot HaKodesh*. These are the highest order of angels in Ezekiel's vision who carry the Divine Throne.</note>. And these four letters are the secret of the Holy Name, which is <term>Y-H-W-H</term> <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter essential name of God.</note>. And this secret was revealed by the River Chebar, which is this very secret. And it was revealed through the secret of the "visions of God." And you shall see darkness from within the light. And this is the secret of the <term>Throne</term> <note>original: *Kurseya*. Referring to the Throne of Glory.</note>.

And it says: **"And I looked, and behold, a stormy wind came out of the north..."** etc. <note>Ezekiel 1:4</note> What is this "stormy wind"? This is the storm that enters into those things that were revealed. And regarding this, it says: **"A stormy wind came out of the north."** And the secret of this is from the "Left Side," which is called "North" <note>In Kabbalistic geography, the North represents the attribute of *Gevurah* (Strength/Judgment) and the "Left Side," which is the source of challenges and harsh forces.</note>. **"A great cloud, and a fire flaring up, and a brightness was around it."** These are the secrets of the Divine Presence while she is in exile. **"And a brightness was around it."** This is the secret of the light that shines out from within the darkness. <unclear>And all these</unclear> secrets are called the Holy <term>Chariot</term> <note>original: *Merkavah*. The divine assembly or vehicle seen by the prophet.</note> which was shown to the prophet. <unclear>And because of this</unclear>, the <term>Divine Presence</term> was revealed upon this river.

## Main Text (Zohar)

He enters and prepares according to the hour the hiddenness of the most hidden, which prepares the voice that comes from within the shells <note>original: "kelippot" — the spiritual husks or layers of concealment</note> and brings down sixty-two "eyes." Through it, they go out and enter, returning and responding. From within, he draws sixty-eight watchers <note>original: "irin" — a class of high-ranking angels</note> over him; he is concealed, yet draws and prepares them. Then they shall see. He enters and draws one hundred and one hundred branches <note>original: "se'ifin" — extensions of divine light or angelic groups</note>, supporting and preparing and drawing them all.

And he draws, **as we have learned**: Come and see, for it is taught that at the time when He stands to perform vengeance, and when the service is completed at that time, it is written:
-> *And sorrow and sighing shall flee away* <note>Isaiah 35:10</note> <-
And surrounding him are sixty-four watchers who take one hundred and fifty-eight branches, surrounding him on every side. They are hidden within him so that they are not seen outside of him. And inside of him are forty-five other hidden things that are not seen. **And then, this is the Hidden of all Hidden** <note>original: "Setima de-kol Setimin" — a reference to the highest, most unknowable aspect of the Divine</note> which is not known to any eye. He enters, prepares, and ascends higher and higher until he reaches a place that is not known except to himself. When the preparation comes, it stands facing this and this and this, for he is the deepest of all depths. Because this is known higher and higher within the coverings, and because he is thus within, he prepares what he prepares to be seen, for he stands facing another place. For from that hidden place above, seventy-one ministers go out below toward this place, and they are appointed over all the rest of the world. And when they hear that he is a voice from that place, they all tremble and fall upon their faces and say:
-> *Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place* <note>Ezekiel 3:12</note> <-
**It was taught** that when that hidden place is perfected in its arrangements, it is gathered within, and then the testimony stands. At that hour, it is found, and <unclear>seventy</unclear>-five others cover over it...

<summary>This passage describes the intricate celestial hierarchy and the "Hidden of all Hidden," detailing how divine light descends through watchers and branches while remaining concealed from external view. It emphasizes the awe of the heavenly ministers who fall prostrate upon hearing the divine voice from the hidden realms.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the emanations from the highest realm of the Divine, specifically focusing on the "Ancient One" (Atika) and the emergence of the Primordial Light. ## In the Primordial Light of the Secrets of the Ancient One

In the primordial light, based on the secrets of the Ancient One <note>Aramaic: Atika; refers to the most hidden, ancient aspect of the Divine Will</note>, a path went forth from there. And the primordial light made thirty thousand gates and gardens between them. As it is hinted at by the name *Aleph* <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing unity and the beginning of emanation</note>, eighty thousand worlds stand surrounding it. And because of this, it was hinted—and He made a path and another way.

Like this path of the deep eyes that the serpent made and hid within it <note>Likely a reference to the "primordial serpent" or the hidden forces of judgment that are concealed within the paths of wisdom</note>. And this is the path of the stones of fire <note>original: abnei esha; a reference to Ezekiel 28:14, often used in Kabbalah to describe the radiant, burning nature of the higher sefirot</note> that do not come to be known by the seven <note>Possibly the seven lower emotional attributes or "days" of creation</note> and the likeness of the heart.

A cloud was made, for behold, it was not revealed to the Torah nor to all the wise men. For from here, prophecy goes forth, and the letters of the "House of Remembrance" <note>original: d'bei zachor; referring to the masculine principle or the source of memory/consciousness</note> for every male. This path shall be called by the name of *Aleph* itself, because through it, the primordial light was not revealed. And the letters came, and through it, the worlds were made, as it is written.

And in it was made a hint of the Name, which are like those of which it was said: "The Living One of the Ancient One." In it, He struck <note>original: batash; a technical term in Kabbalah for the "collision" of lights that produces new emanations</note>, and the primordial light began to shine, and Understanding <note>original: Binah; the third Sefirah, associated with the divine womb and analytical processing</note> was hinted at in its day.

Exactly like those letters, He made in the end an eye itself from it in one. And the letter that He struck within it in the primordial light is for all who do not know the light on the right. And regarding this, a path was spoken of in the primordial light. And why a path? Because it shines for all who do not know its way. And the letter within it made a *Nun* <note>The Hebrew letter representing "fish" or "emergence"</note> of water in the hinted light. These letters are upon letters, surrounding the world.

In it, the primordial river <note>Often refers to the flow of emanation from Binah</note> shines in the light of His name, which He told to shine for all who bow to the letter that He struck within it. And it is the primordial light to shine, and around it, He revealed five in the hinted light, and revealed fifty <note>Likely referring to the Fifty Gates of Understanding</note> in the light.

<summary>This manuscript page describes the mystical emanation of the "Primordial Light" from the Ancient One (Atika), detailing how hidden paths and divine letters like Aleph and Nun form the structure of the spiritual worlds. It emphasizes that these processes remain hidden from ordinary wisdom and are the source of prophecy.</summary>

<keywords>Atika Kadisha, Primordial Light, Aleph, Binah, Fifty Gates of Understanding, Kabbalistic cosmogony, Divine Letters, Path of Fire</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And at that time, King Solomon made a great festival and rejoiced
in the Holy Temple, because through him the Holy Temple was built, and for this reason <note>original: "u-ve-gin kakh"</note>
and after this, a "Covenant of Peace," because the Divine Presence <note>term: Shekhinah; the feminine aspect of God that dwells among humanity</note> is the Sabbath.
And because of this it is written that in the evening it shall be done, "And it shall be on that day, the Lord shall be one <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>
and His Name one." And that "Name" is the Divine Presence of whom it is said
that it shall be, and it does not change, and upon it peace depends, and this is the work.

-> **And you shall sanctify** <- <note>A reference to the consecration of the Tabernacle or Temple</note>
These are the ones of whom it is said
that all of them sanctify: "Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord of Hosts" <note>Isaiah 6:3; the Trisagion prayer</note>
-> **And you shall sanctify** <-
The second is the third holiness,
for all of them are the three upper emanations <note>term: Sefirot; the ten attributes or channels of Divine energy</note>: Wisdom, Understanding, and Knowledge <note>term: Chokhmah, Binah, and Da'at; the intellectual triad of the Sefirotic tree</note>
through which the Holy Temple was built, and regarding this, it is "Sanctuary" and "Holy."
And that Sanctuary is the Holy of Holies, and when He is within it,
the Sanctuary is completed, and the Patriarchs <note>note: Referring to the Sefirot of Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet, symbolized by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob</note> are crowned within it as one.
And when He is joined with it, then it is complete from all sides,
and this third holiness goes to rest upon them.

which is "Holy," and "Sanctified," and "Holiness," and for this reason <note>original: "u-ve-gin kakh"</note> it is called
this place "The Holy of Holies," because it is a holiness
within a holiness, and this is all within a single sanctity.
And regarding this it is written: "And you shall be holy unto Me, for I the Lord am holy" <note>Leviticus 20:26</note>
This is the supreme holiness that rests upon Israel;
and when they are sanctified below, then the holiness above is increased.

## Genesis

**In the beginning God created...** <note>Genesis 1:1</note> Rabbi Isaac opened his discourse with the verse: 
> **The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord; a good understanding have all those who do them; His praise endures forever.** 
<note>Psalms 111:10</note>. "The beginning of wisdom." It should have said "Wisdom is the beginning." Why does it say "The beginning of wisdom"? Rather, it refers to the "Beginning" which is itself <term>Wisdom</term> <note>Chokhmah: the second Sephirah or divine emanation, representing the first point of conscious revelation</note> to be contemplated. It is the beginning of all levels. This is the highest level. And when it is joined with Wisdom, it is called "The Beginning of Wisdom." And this is the <term>Fear of the Lord</term>. This "Fear" is the place where awe dwells, which is the gateway to enter within. For we have learned: they made it a gateway to the interior. And regarding this it is written: 
> **Open to me the gates of righteousness; I will enter into them, I will praise the Lord.** 
<note>Psalms 118:19</note>.

**And this is the first gateway** of all the higher levels. And in this gateway dwells the <term>Higher Wisdom</term>. For this reason, it is called "The Beginning of Wisdom." "A good understanding have all those who do them." Who are "those who do them"? These are the commandments of the Torah. For they are literally the "makers" of them. As it were, they *make* it <note>The Zohar suggests that by performing commandments, humans "build" or "sustain" the divine presence on earth</note>. For we have learned: anyone who labors in the Torah and performs the commandments of the Torah, it is as if he made it. "His praise endures forever." This "Praise" refers to the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>Knesset Yisrael: a mystical term for the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note>. "Endures forever," because her existence is established only through that Wisdom, which is the Higher Wisdom.

**Rabbi Yose opened** with the verse: 
> **Lift up your eyes on high and see: Who created these?** 
<note>Isaiah 40:26</note>. "Lift up your eyes on high"—to the place where all eyes depend. And what is that? The "Opening of the Eyes." And there you shall know that the "Hidden of all Hidden" which is unknown, "Created these." And who is He? <term>Who</term> <note>Hebrew: Mi. In Zoharic thought, the interrogative "Who" represents the hidden, higher aspect of the Divine (Binah) that can be asked about but not fully grasped</note>. The Holy One, blessed be He, created "These." Because He is called "Who." One asks: "Who created these?" This is a place that does not stand for questioning <note>Meaning it is beyond human comprehension</note>. And because it is hidden above and does not stand for questioning, it is called <term>Who</term>.

<summary>This page provides a mystical interpretation of the first word of Genesis, linking "Beginning" to the Sephirah of Wisdom and the "Fear of God" as a gateway to the divine. It also introduces the linguistic play between the Hebrew words 'Mi' (Who) and 'Ele' (These) to explain the process of creation from the hidden realms.</summary>

<keywords>Bereshit, Wisdom, Chokhmah, Fear of God, Gateway, Commandments, Assembly of Israel, Shekhinah, Creation, Hiddenness, Binah</keywords>

## Vayetze (And he went out)

...of the house of <term>Rav Hamnuna the Elder</term> <note>A prominent, often legendary figure in the Zohar, representing ancient wisdom</note>, they brought him in...
...to him, and gave him half a cup to drink...
And a voice went out and said: "Awaken, you who sleep in the dust! How fortunate is your portion, O righteous ones..."
The <term>Holy Name</term> <note>original: "Shema Kadisha"</note> with which the children of faith are sealed...

> **"And behold, a ladder was set upon the earth, and its top reached to heaven..."** <note>Genesis 28:12</note>

<term>Rabbi Judah</term> opened his discourse and said: The companions have already established the meaning of this verse. But come and see:
This ladder represents Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob <note>The three Patriarchs, who in Kabbalah represent the three primary divine attributes of Kindness, Strength, and Beauty</note>. This ladder is the <term>mystery</term> <note>original: "Raza"</note> of the levels of the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>. "Set upon the earth"—this is the mystery of the level that is the ladder set upon the earth, which is the <term>Land of Life</term> <note>A mystical term for the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence as it relates to our world</note>. "And its top reached to heaven"—this is the mystery of that which is "Heaven" above, the level of the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>.

> **"And behold, the angels of God were ascending and descending on it."** <note>Genesis 28:12</note>

These are the hosts appointed over all those <term>levels</term> below, who are appointed over all the other nations. And because of this, they are "ascending and descending on it." They ascend through this level and they descend through it. Therefore, Jacob saw all those levels clinging to one another within this specific level. And the mystery of this [verse?] is written...

## Main Text (Zohar)

Their wrath was such that there was no one to wage war against them or to strike their hands <note>original: "לממחי בידוהי" - a common Aramaic idiom for preventing or protesting an action</note> for their sins, for they are all before Him. Yet the honor of perfection did not depart from Him and His throne. **"Humble and riding on a donkey"** <note>Zechariah 9:9</note>—this refers to the humility that is associated with Him in this matter. And all of this was because he became haughty in his heart and thought that he himself was doing everything he did. For this reason, it is written "in every place," etc., until it was found at that moment that humility is honored and perfect. These are two Names <note>referring to divine names or attributes</note> among all the Names that are always joined as one and are never separated forever. All of this was revealed at that moment. Because of this, it is written that the kingdom is "complete" <note>original: "שלם" (Shalem), a play on the name Jerusalem</note>, and in the word "Jerusalem," the letter *Yod* is missing <note>The defective spelling of Jerusalem (ירושלם) is a common Zoharic theme regarding the Shekhinah in exile.</note> to show that this was found to be "extra" without humility, without the **Shekhinah** <term>Shekhinah: The feminine aspect of the Divine that dwells within the world</term>. His throne was lacking, and it shall be as it was when there was a holy desire above.

And come and see: Rabbi Eleazar said, it is written: **"The Lord of Hosts"** <note>original: "י' ה' צבאות"</note>—this is extra. Rabbi Eleazar said: Happy is the portion of the **Righteous** <term>Zaddikim: Spiritually perfected individuals</term> in the World to Come! Because of this, they are all wrapped in His service and [the light] shines in their hearts, etc. Happy is the portion of that person who merits the counsel of the wisdom of the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "קודשא בריך הוא" (Kudsha Brikh Hu) - the standard Aramaic title for God</note>. For he fears and says: "To whom is it fitting for us to sanctify ourselves before the King?" Regarding this, he said: "O worthy companions who are occupied with the **Torah** <term>Torah: Divine Law/Instruction</term>, the **Shekhinah** does not depart from among them." The Holy One, Blessed be He, is found with them always. Because of this, it is written: **"He who walks with the wise shall become wise."** <note>Proverbs 13:20</note> Happy is his portion, for he is found to be more than this before the Holy One, Blessed be He; He considers him as if he were His own son. Regarding this, it is written: **"You are children to the Lord your God."** <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note>

Come and see: at every hour that human beings are worthy before the Holy One, Blessed be He, they are all kings, wise men, and righteous ones before Him. Because of this, they are the portion of the Holy One, Blessed be He, for they all inherit the inheritance of their Holy Father. In every place where they dwell, the **Shekhinah** dwells with them. For here it is found that they are all worthy to be crowned with the crown of eternal life. Therefore, they are meritorious; they are meritorious in this world.

## Terumah (The Offering)

And if you should say, you have spoken well: what is the reason that when human beings go up to their beds, their souls <note>original: "nishmathon"</note> depart from them and go wandering throughout the world, yet people do not perceive anything within their own beings? They see dreams in a vision that resembles the form of the body, appearing at the head of the body. And if you say the soul departs from them and does not rest at that hour in the hands of the One to whom it was entrusted—behold, it is written <note>Psalm 31:6</note>:
> **Into Your hand I entrust my spirit**
and so on; and he lies down, satisfied and cleaved unto the Holy One, Blessed be He. We have learned that when the soul departs from a person and goes wandering, those <term>shells of impurity</term> <note>original: "klipin de-masaba" — the spiritual husks or forces of evil that conceal the divine light</note> who are called "human sins" seize it. They show the soul false dreams, showing it one thing that resembles another, and another thing that resembles yet another. We have established this regarding the "fine hair" <note>referring to a subtle spiritual gateway or thread</note> from within those spirits of impurity that wander the world. For if the soul did not depart and go wandering, the person would not see the dream. Regarding this, we have established that it is the soul that enters the Holy Mountain and sees what it sees, each person according to their deeds.

And here Rabbi Shimon said: Certainly, you have spoken well. But come and see, for it is written <note>Proverbs 3:24</note>:
> **And you shall lie down, and your sleep shall be sweet.**
For we have learned that when a person lies on their bed, the soul departs, but there remains in the body a vitality from the side of the <term>Nefesh</term> <note>the lowest level of the soul, associated with physical life and biological functions</note> which never departs and is never taken from him. This vitality is the connection of the body, which is drawn from two sides: the vitality that burns in the gaze of the eye and in the understanding of the heart. From this vitality that remains in the body, a person sees the dream. For the higher soul has departed and ascended, but the likeness of the body remains. They see dreams in a vision that resembles the form of the body, and it is the substance of the vitality remaining in the body. From this side, those who do not merit for their souls to ascend see their dreams.

---
<margin>
*Catchword:* And afterward
</margin>

<summary>This passage from the Zohar explains that while the higher soul (Neshamah) ascends to the divine realm during sleep, a lower vital force (Nefesh) remains in the body, which allows for the experience of dreams and maintains physical life.</summary>
<keywords>soul, dreams, sleep, Nefesh, shells of impurity, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, Zohar, Terumah</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Come and see <note>original: "Ta Chazi" — a standard Zoharic opening inviting the reader to contemplate a mystical truth</note>: whenever a person performs a commandment of the Torah and a deed of mitzvah <note>term: mitzvah — a religious duty or good deed</note>, then he is cleaved to the Holy One, Blessed be He. This is because the Shekhinah <note>term: Shekhinah — the Divine Presence, often conceptualized as the feminine or indwelling aspect of God</note> dwells upon him in all his deeds. But when he separates himself from the mystery of the Torah, another spirit—an impure one—dwells upon him. Regarding this, King David, peace be upon him, said: **"Cast me not away from Your presence, and take not Your Holy Spirit from me"** <note>Psalms 51:13</note>. This is the Holy Spirit that dwells upon the righteous.

Come and see: this Holy Spirit only dwells in a place where a holy soul dwells. For the Torah and the Holy One, Blessed be He, are all one <note>A central Zoharic principle: God, the Torah, and Israel are an ontological unity</note>. And it is the Holy Spirit that enters into those words of the Torah; when a person exerts himself in them, the Holy Spirit dwells upon him. But if he does not exert himself in them, that spirit flies away from him.

Regarding this, David said: **"and take not Your Holy Spirit from me."** When he sinned, he said: **"Cast me not away from Your presence."** What is meant by **"Your presence"** <note>original: "mi-lifanekha" — literally "from before Your face"</note>? This refers to the Shekhinah, who is called "Face." **"And take not Your Holy Spirit from me"**—this refers to the Holy Spirit that he exerted through the Torah. [David prayed:] May it be Your will that it shall never be nullified from me.

Come and see: happy are the righteous who exert themselves in the Torah day and night, for they take hold of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and they are cleaved to Him through the Torah.

<summary>This page explains that the Holy Spirit and the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) are maintained through active engagement with the Torah and its commandments, using King David's plea in Psalm 51 as a prooftext for the fear of losing this divine connection.</summary>
<keywords>Shekhinah, Holy Spirit, Torah study, King David, Psalms 51, Divine Presence, commandments, spiritual purity</keywords>

I cleave to the Master of All, in whom I look and learn that which I did not know <unclear>and forty</unclear> <note>The unclear word likely refers to the "forty years" or "forty levels" of wisdom often cited in Zoharic literature</note> who are as one in one bond and in one will without any separation at all. ## Main Text (Zohar / Rectifications of the Zohar)

And when he sanctifies the tongue, "a watcher and a holy one" <note>original: *ir ve-kaddish*; a reference to Daniel 4:13</note> and so on; and when these two thousand years shall be for her <note>referring to the period of exile or preparation</note>, and this is the time prepared when there shall be no soul <term>Nefesh: the lowest level of the soul, associated with vitality</term> that does not possess its own tree. Because of this, the poor man who rejects this time is liable, and is destined to be cast into death in the **River of Fire** <note>original: *Nehar Dinur*; the stream of fire that purifies souls or consumes the wicked, mentioned in Daniel 7:10</note>. For this reason, a man must guard his soul from evil. From that time when the **Messiah** comes, there will be no one who does not desire the **Torah** <note>original: *Oraita*</note> and become involved in it, as it is said: "every man to his neighbor and every man to his brother, saying, Know the Lord" <note>Jeremiah 31:33</note>. And this shall be revealed and shine within them, that which was established concerning his companion, the **Shekhinah** <term>The Divine Presence; the feminine aspect of God dwelling in the world</term>, and every man shall benefit from her according to what is fitting for him. He shall be able to know that which was from the beginning of time. In the days of this Messiah, those commandments of the Torah, like those who perform them, will be seen as a "designation," which is to say a **Sacrifice** <term>Korban: literally "drawing near"</term>; they are of a standing degree. And that which is said, "a sacrifice to the Lord," hints at the degree called "Sacrifice" at the place where it stands, as it is written:
> "When any man of you brings an offering <note>Sacrifice/Korban</note> to the Lord, of the cattle..." <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>

And we have established that they are all included in the **Nefesh** <gloss>Vital Soul</gloss>, the **Ruach** <gloss>Spirit</gloss>, and the **Neshamah** <gloss>Higher Soul</gloss>. Because of this, in prayer, one must draw near before the Holy King. And that which he desired to bring near to the Lord, the Torah teaches us: it must be with a "whole heart," as it was stated. Come and see:

---

->**The Sixth Rectification**<-
It is a commandment to perform the sacrifice of the daily offerings and the additional offerings every day. Regarding this, that the sacrifice shall be, this world is compared to it. And this we established in the portion of *Vayikra* <note>The Book of Leviticus</note>, that these sacrifices awaken [the realms] above. And he who is liable shall invite upon himself the Holy Spirit. And that which we established concerning "Blessed be He," which is the sacrifice that is complete; and that which we established concerning the commandment in prayer, that one must draw near with a whole heart, as is explained in the Rectifications, in the **Eleventh Rectification**, which is: "In the seventh month, it is a commandment to sound the Shofar..."

## Genesis

And the voice of the pleasantness of the Levite is the song that praises the Left Side <note>Zohar I, 24a; the Levites represent the attribute of Gevurah or "Strength," which is the Left Side of the divine tree</note> which emerges from that Left Side, along with all other kinds that resemble it which shine, and the other lights that shine and are called by the name of Fire. For then they are all called by one name because they all come from the side of the Left. And the Left is called by this name: **Isaac** is called the Left, and this is <term>Samael</term> <note>The primary archangel of the "Other Side" or shadow realm</note>, and this is the **Crooked Serpent**, and this is the **Woman of Harlotry** <note>A personification of the seductive, destructive forces of the "Other Side"</note> who is on the side of the Left. And if you say that Isaac and Samael are both the Left, behold, we have learned that Isaac is a holy <term>Sefirah</term> <note>One of the ten divine attributes or "spheres" through which God interacts with the world</note> and Samael, who is the Serpent, is called the Left? Rather, certainly this and that emerge from the "Hard Left" side. And the masters established that this verse:
> "And darkness was upon the face of the deep" <note>Genesis 1:2</note>
refers to the Serpent and the Woman of Harlotry, and they are called the Left. However, the Holy Left is Isaac, and they are called the Unholy Left. And because of this, Isaac possesses the pleasantness to praise the Holy One, Blessed be He, and to take up his Left Side within the side of holiness. But they are called the Left because they seek to do evil to the world. For thus there is a Left for Holiness and there is a Left for Impurity. And the side of Holiness is the pleasantness for praise and song, because his Left Side which shines is praised and prepared at all times. And all those who emerge from this Left are all called by this name because they are on its side, and the Woman of Harlotry is on its side, and because of this they are all called by this name. And there is a Left Above and there is a Left Below. The Left Above is Isaac, and the Left Below is Samael and the Woman of Harlotry, and this is the secret of the matter.

<summary>This passage explores the dual nature of the "Left Side" (Gevurah), distinguishing between the holy severity embodied by the patriarch Isaac and the unholy forces of Samael and the Serpent. It explains that while both originate from the same cosmic direction, one leads to divine song and the other to worldly harm.</summary>

## Pekudei

...And to make known the Holy Name through you, and you shall merit to enjoy the beauty from above. All of this is so that they shall know and understand that the Holy One, Blessed be He, is called thus. And when He is [revealed] so that they may know Him, He is called by this name. But because everything is hidden and He is not known at all, He is called:
-> **"What is His name?"** <note>Exodus 3:13</note> <-
What do you ask of My name? Just as it is said:
-> **"Why is it that you ask after my name?"** <note>Judges 13:18</note> <-
And because of this, He is certainly called thus, all within the secret of the Holy Name <term>Shema Kadisha: the essential name of God, often referring to the Tetragrammaton</term> as we have established.

Come and see: the **Shekhinah** <term>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God that dwells within the world</term> does not abide in any other place except in the location where all the holy names—upper and lower—are gathered. And when they are all gathered within Her and joined as one, then She is called "Shekhinah," and the **Holy Name** is complete as is fitting. Therefore, when the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, is seen within the Shekhinah, then the Holy Name is known to be complete.

And come and see: when the Holy Name—which is the Holy One, Blessed be He—is completed within the Shekhinah, then everything that did not exist previously is created. This is because the Holy Name was completed within Him, as it were. Just as everything emerged from the **Supernal Thought** <term>Machshava Ila'ah: the primordial, infinite divine mind</term> which has no end. All of this is so that they may know that there is a dominion above and below.

Because of this, that which did not exist previously is created now, and therefore He is called **Creator** <term>Borei</term>. Every single word that the Holy One, Blessed be He, spoke, a single complete and enduring creature emerged from it. Because of this, it is known that He is the Creator. And from where do we know that when the Holy Name is completed, a creation is then formed? As it is written:
-> **"You send forth Your spirit, they are created"** <note>Psalms 104:30</note> <-
"Your spirit"—this is the Supernal Spirit that emerges from the [Divine] Thought and shines within the Shekhinah. And then all the holy names exist in perfection and everything is created. Regarding this it is written, "they are created." And then:
-> **"And You renew the face of the earth"** <note>Psalms 104:30</note> <-
"The face of the earth"—this refers to the Shekhinah.

<summary>This passage from the Zohar explains that God is only called "Creator" and His Name is only "complete" when the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) unites with the upper spiritual realms. It describes creation as a process of divine speech and light flowing from the Infinite Thought into the world.</summary>

## Main Text (The New Zohar - The Hidden Midrash)

And the Holy One, Blessed be He, departed from him, and he stood weeping before the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah," the feminine immanence of God</note>. This is a new matter that the companions established; even though he did not fully receive it, there is certainly some truth in what we have said. For all those three hundred and ninety-five years that the companions were engraved <note>or "established"</note> in Arabia, they said that in the days of this King, they are restored through Him. And the companions are those who say that there were six hundred and five years that Rabbi Shimon was in the clay <note>or "mire," possibly referring to his time hiding in the cave</note> in the earth. And he [Rabbi Elazar] saw this but did not know what he was saying. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, departed from him, and he stood and wept until Elijah encountered him. 

Elijah said to him: "What is this, Rabbi Elazar?" 

He replied: "It is because of what I saw, and yet the Holy One, Blessed be He, has departed from me." 

Elijah said to him: "If the 'engraved companions' are with you, do you still not know?" 

He asked him: "What does this mean?" 

He replied: "The 'companions' you spoke of—they are the Names. And all of them are Holy Names with which the Holy One, Blessed be He, is crowned. And all of them were inscribed with the strength that he saw: the name of Abraham and the name of Sarah. And he saw that their names were completed in the spirit and as a sign:"

->**"And Abraham came to eulogize Sarah and to weep for her"** <note>Genesis 23:2</note><-

And what is the meaning of "And Abraham came"? Abraham came through the Holy Spirit to eulogize that spirit of Sarah which had reached perfection. And even though we have not established this matter in this exact way before, these words of the companions are truth. And because of this, Abraham and Sarah were found [perfected] in both spirit and body. In this same manner, Rabbi Shimon said: "Any man who is complete in spirit and in body is called 'complete in all.' And therefore, any woman who does not have a male <note>referring to the mystical union of masculine and feminine energies</note> is not called complete..."

<summary>Rabbi Elazar receives a revelation from Elijah the Prophet explaining that the "companions" mentioned in his vision are actually Divine Names. The text interprets Abraham's mourning for Sarah as a mystical union of perfected spirits and emphasizes the necessity of both physical and spiritual wholeness.</summary>

# Vayechi (And He Lived)

## Main Text (Zohar)

"And his right hand embraces me." Concerning this, the scripture says: *His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me* <note>Song of Songs 2:6</note>. When he saw this, it was certain; for in the time when the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> dwells in exile, the "Left" is under the head, as it is written: ->*His left hand is under my head*<-. Because of this, she lies in the dust. But the Righteous One, who is the **Foundation** <note>The Sefirah of Yesod, the procreative and stabilizing force in the divine realm</note>, who is the "Right," he "embraces me"—meaning he embraces her and lifts her up from the dust, as it is written: ->*and his right hand embraces me*<-. Because she is in exile, it is found that the Left is under the head, but when she goes out of exile, the Right embraces her, and she says: "and his right hand embraces me." **Rabbi Isaac** said: What is the meaning of the verse *His left hand is under my head*? This refers to **Isaac** <note>Associated with the attribute of Gevurah/Judgment or the "Left"</note>. *And his right hand embraces me*—this refers to **Abraham** <note>Associated with the attribute of Chesed/Kindness or the "Right"</note>. This is because the Left awakens love and the Right embraces. **Rabbi Eleazar** said: Fortunate is the portion of the righteous, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires their honor in this world and in the world to come. Come and see: at the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, comes to take the soul of a person, He does not take it except with a kiss, just as it says: *Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth* <note>Song of Songs 1:2</note>. This is the love of the Holy One, Blessed be He, toward the righteous, and all this is because they are constantly clinging to Him, as it is written: *and to Him you shall cling* <note>Deuteronomy 10:20</note>. **Come and see:** Fortunate is the portion of Jacob our father, of whom it is written: *and of all that You give me I will surely give a tenth to You* <note>Genesis 28:22</note>. **Rabbi Hezekiah** said: What is the meaning of *and of all that You give me*? Did Jacob need to give a tenth to the Holy One, Blessed be He? For He said that everything is His, and the whole world is His! Rather, Jacob said: "I have awakened the mystery of the Tithe <note>Ma'aser</note> above." And regarding this: "I will surely give a tenth to You" <note>The Hebrew "Asser A'assreno" uses a double verb for emphasis</note> above, so that all those worlds shall be blessed because of You. For it is written *I will surely give a tenth* <note>literally: "Tithing I will tithe"</note> twice: once to awaken the "Tenth" which is the **Divine Presence**, and once to awaken the "Tenth" above. Regarding this, he said: *I will surely give a tenth to You*. **Rabbi Shimon** said: What is the meaning of the verse: *And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years; so the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were a hundred and forty-seven years* <note>Genesis 47:28</note>? Seventeen years—because these were the days of goodness that Jacob saw in Egypt, and he had not seen such days of goodness since the day he came into the world...

<summary>This passage explores the mystical union between the Divine Presence and the Sefirot, interpreting Jacob's tithe as a cosmic awakening and explaining his seventeen years in Egypt as his only period of true "goodness."</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar Commentary)

At that hour, they are appointed over it by the trustee of that firmament and from that portion, and upon it merit depends. They were not appointed [randomly], for so we have learned regarding the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</note> and a person who stands with greater strength than her; for at times and seasons, that merit protects him when the time arrives and changes.

Section <note>original: "ס'" - likely an abbreviation for 'Secret of the Torah'</note> and in it they stand. And even though it is not his portion, illness finds healing by way of his portion. And they say: when did he receive from him the kingdom? Strength [is lost] because of him, for he sinned against his fellow. And this is the meaning of **"And he slept and dreamed"** <note>Genesis 28:12</note>. His sleep is not considered [merely physical]; the verse calls it "half a kab" <note>A small measure; a reference to sleep being a fraction of prophecy</note> and in it we have learned, "I have heard."

What is the meaning of **"And behold, a ladder"** <note>Genesis 28:12</note>? It is that which explains his strength. And the entire kingdom—these are the "place of the ladder." <term>Samael</term> <note>The primary angelic figure of severity/judgment</note> and <term>Gabriel</term> <note>The archangel of strength and judgment</note>, all of them are attached to his strength. And what is this? What did he do that he was seeing in that ladder? It is the ascent of human beings—the ascent of the soul. And it is an ascent and all its matters are in this manner. And this is your vision of the "definite article" <note>original: "תקון הידיע" - referring to the specific 'He' (The) used in the Hebrew word for 'The Ladder'</note>. And in this we have heard, and from it: **"And he saw"**.

In the "Lamed" <note>The Hebrew letter L</note> is the stretching of the earth, a footstep, for thus we have seen. And the noise comes before the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, and he saw noise and a voice, and behold a voice, and he said that He is Blessed. And in it we have heard and we have learned: **"And behold, the Lord stood over him and saw"** <note>Genesis 28:13</note> and He said—this is the glory of the Master of the Kingdom. Illness—and this is what is written...

In the whiteness of the head above, it spreads into the rest of the other locks <note>original: "kotzin," referring to the curls or "thorns" of the hair</note> and remains hidden within them, a knot and a height of great life. <meta>This page marks the beginning of the commentary on the Book of Genesis (Bereshit). It describes the primordial, mystical origins of the universe according to the Zohar, focusing on the transition from the Infinite to the first point of creation.</meta>

## Genesis

When the will of the Supreme King began to take effect, desiring to create the world, He engraved engravings into the Supernal Purity. A "Lamp of Darkness" <term>emerged (nefiq)</term> <note>original: "botzina de-qardinuta"; a paradoxical term referring to a powerful, blinding light that acts as a catalyst for differentiation</note> from within the most hidden of the hidden, from the mystery of the <term>Infinite (Ein Sof)</term> <note>original: "Ein Sof"; literally "Without End," referring to God's essence before any self-manifestation</note>. It was like a mist attached to a ring, neither white nor black, nor red nor green, nor any color at all. When He extended the measuring line, He produced colors to shine within. Deep within the lamp, a spring emerged from which the colors were painted below. It remained hidden within the secret of the Infinite. It cleaved and yet did not cleave its "ether" <note>the primordial space or atmosphere of the divine</note>. It was not known at all until, from the pressure of its cleaving, a single <term>Hidden Point</term> <note>original: "nequda setima"; representing the first Sephirah, Wisdom (Chokhmah)</note> shone forth. Beyond that point, nothing is known. For this reason, it is called <term>Beginning (Reshit)</term> <note>original: "Reshit"; the first word of the Bible, interpreted here as the first utterance of all</note>, the first of all utterances.

> And those who are wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and those who turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever. (Daniel 12:3)

The <term>Radiance (Zohar)</term> <note>original: "Zohar"; the title of the work, meaning a brilliant, mystical light</note>, most hidden of all hidden things, cleaved its ether and shone into this Point. Within this "Beginning," that hidden one which is unknown constructed a Palace for its glory. That Palace is called <term>God (Elohim)</term> <note>original: "Elohim"; here interpreted as a "vessel" or "palace" for the divine light</note>. And this is the secret of the verse: "In the beginning, [the Infinite] created God [the Palace]." <note>The Zohar reinterprets the first verse of Genesis, suggesting the Infinite (the unspoken subject) created the name 'Elohim' as a garment or palace for the light.</note>

<summary>This page describes the mystical emergence of the universe from the Infinite (Ein Sof), detailing how a "Lamp of Darkness" carved out the first hidden point of light, which then expanded into a spiritual "Palace" known as Elohim.</summary>
<keywords>Creation, Ein Sof, Radiance, Hidden Point, Palace, Elohim, Bereshit, Mystical Light</keywords>
