<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Genesis, specifically focusing on the creation of Eve and the spiritual implications of the Fall of Man. It follows the discussion of the primordial Adam.</meta>

# Genesis

## Main Text (Zohar)

The Holy One, blessed be He, acted in order to establish the world upon its proper restoration, for until a "help" was made facing him, the restoration was not complete. And concerning this it is written:
> **"It is not good that man should be alone;** <note>Genesis 2:18</note>
**I will make him a helpmate facing him."** What is a "helpmate facing him"? This is the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed in the Zohar as the feminine aspect of God</note> who was made as a help facing him so that they would be as one. And this is the <term>mystery</term> <note>original: "raza"</note> of the Holy Name, which is complete from all sides. And come and see: when Adam was completed in his restoration, all the worlds—above and below—were sweetened, because everything was bound together as one and made fragrant. And now we have learned: when Adam sinned and caused a blemish in this "help" that was facing him, all those blessings were nullified and the world was damaged. This is because everything exists within the mystery of faith, and faith is the <term>Shekhinah</term>. If a person sins against this "help," it is as if he sinned against the totality of everything. And come and see: when Adam caused a blemish and ate from the "Tree of Diminishment," which is the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, he caused death for the entire world. He caused a blemish in himself and in all those who came from him. Because he is the foundation of the world, and when the foundation is blemished, everything is blemished. And concerning this it is written:
> **"And the Lord God sent him forth from the Garden of Eden..."** etc. <note>Genesis 3:23</note>
Afterward, what is written?
> **"And He drove out the man; and He placed at the east of the Garden of Eden the Cherubim, and the flaming sword which turned every way, to guard the way to the Tree of Life."** <note>Genesis 3:24</note>
What is "to guard the way to the Tree of Life"? This is the mystery of another level called the "Way to the Tree of Life," which is the <term>Shekhinah</term>. This was done so that another branch—which is the Tree of Death—would not come and cause a blemish within Her. And this has already been established.

<summary>This page explains that the creation of a 'helpmate' for Adam represents the union of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) with humanity, and that Adam's sin caused a cosmic blemish that led to his expulsion and the guarding of the Tree of Life.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the creation of the soul, specifically focusing on the hierarchy of spiritual levels (Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah) and their cosmic counterparts in the Sefirot and the nations of the world.</meta>

## Genesis

The "living soul" <note>Hebrew: *Nishmat Chayah*</note> extends upward to the end of all levels, for there, everything is a unity, mirroring that which is above. A person is obligated to unify this [soul], for it is singular within the ten *Sefirot* <note>The ten creative attributes or emanations through which the Infinite interacts with the universe</note> which ascend to the seven names, and within them are all other names. Because of this, it is said that "holy shall be for the living," and this refers to the "living holy creatures" <note>The *Chayot HaKodesh*, a high order of angels</note>. It is all-inclusive, and the seventy elders are within it. Seventy branches are revealed, and surrounding them are the seventy nations who subjugate Israel and receive their sustenance from these branches. These branches are included within twelve; from them come the twelve tribes of Israel, and surrounding them are the twelve constellations. Surrounding those are the seventy nations, the seventy branches, and the seventy names of the Holy One, Blessed be He. All of this was held in separation due to the sin of the first man <note>Adam</note>. But when the Messiah comes, it is said:
> "And the Lord shall be king over all the earth; in that day shall the Lord be one, and His name one." <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>

Because they exist in a state of separation [currently], we call those at the first level <term>Masters of Souls</term> <note>Aramaic: *Marei Nafshin*; refers to those who have attained the basic level of spiritual vitality</note>, which is the *Nefesh* <note>The lowest level of the soul, associated with physical life and action</note> as hinted at in the "seventh." Regarding this, they said "the seventh within the seventh," which is revealed. Concerning this it is written:
> "I am the Lord, that is My name; and My glory I will not give to another." <note>Isaiah 42:8</note>

To the second level, we call them <term>Masters of Torah</term> <note>Aramaic: *Marei Torah*</note>, which is the <term>Ruach</term> <note>The middle level of the soul, associated with emotion and speech</note> that blows within it. This is the "Voice" that emerges from the seventh, which is the "Daughter of a Voice" <note>Hebrew: *Bat Kol*; a heavenly echo or divine inspiration</note>.
And this is:
> "Behold the bed of Solomon; sixty mighty men are round about it." <note>Song of Songs 3:7</note>
These are the sixty tractates of the Torah <note>The Mishnah, the foundational text of Jewish law</note> which hang from that Voice, which is the six *Sefirot* <note>The emotive attributes from Chesed to Yesod</note> that include them; and those *Sefirot* are from those sixty mighty ones.

To the third level, we call them <term>Masters of Mishnah</term> <note>Aramaic: *Marei Mishnah*</note>, which is the <term>Neshamah</term> <note>The highest level of the soul, associated with pure intellect and divine spark</note>, which is *Malchut* <note>The Sefirah of Sovereignty or Kingship</note>. For all of this is grasped one within the other, and whoever separates them causes a blemish.
And this is "the living soul according to its kind," etc. <note>Genesis 1:24</note> "Let the earth bring forth the living soul according to its kind," etc. All of this is said concerning the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>The spiritual archetype of the Jewish people, often identified with the Sefirah of Malchut</note> in exile.

<summary>This passage describes the mystical hierarchy of the soul (Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah) and its connection to the Sefirot, explaining how the current state of cosmic separation caused by Adam's sin will be mended in the Messianic era. It links the structure of the Torah and the nations of the world to these divine emanations.</summary>

<keywords>Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Sefirot, Seventy Nations, Twelve Tribes, Messiah, Assembly of Israel, Malchut, Zohar</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the final portion of the Book of Genesis, known as Vayechi ("And he lived"). The text focuses on the final days of the patriarch Jacob in Egypt and his preparations for burial in the Land of Israel.</meta>

# Vayechi

...And the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were etc.

**And Jacob lived**
Why is this section "closed"? <note>original: "parashah setumah." In a Torah scroll, this section begins without the usual paragraph break, appearing "closed" or blocked.</note> Because as soon as Jacob descended to Egypt, the eyes and hearts of Israel were closed <note>or "dimmed"</note> from the suffering of the subjugation. Another explanation: Jacob sought to reveal "the End" <note>the secret timing of the final Redemption</note> but it was closed off from him.

**And the days of Jacob were**
Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse with the verse: <note>Isaiah 38:10</note> *I said, in the noontide of my days I shall go to the gates of the netherworld; I am deprived of the residue of my years.*
Come and see: all the days a person spends in this world are all written before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and there is not a single day that passes from them that is not recorded above...

**And the days of Israel drew near to die**
Rabbi Chiya opened with the verse: <note>Psalms 102:12</note> *My days are like a lengthening shadow, and I wither like grass.*
Come and see: at the hour of that day when the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires to return the spirit to Himself, all of a person's days come and draw near... <note>The Zohar suggests that at the moment of death, a person's lifetime of days physically manifest to accompany the soul.</note>

**And he called for his son, for Joseph**
Rabbi Yossi said: Why did he call for Joseph and not for his other sons? Rather, it was because Joseph had the power to bring him into the Land of Israel, and because he knew that Joseph was the ruler over the land of Egypt...

**And he said to him: "If I have now found favor in your eyes"**
Rabbi Judah opened with the verse: <note>Psalms 37:3</note> *Trust in the Lord and do good; dwell in the land and nourish yourself with faithfulness.*
Come and see, just as he trusted in the Lord, etc...

**"And deal with me in kindness and truth"**
Rabbi Abba opened with the verse: <note>Psalms 115:1</note> *Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but to Your name give glory, for the sake of Your kindness and Your truth.*
Why does it say "kindness and truth"? <term>Kindness (Chesed)</term> refers to the attribute of Abraham, and <term>Truth (Emet)</term> refers to the attribute of Jacob... <note>In Kabbalistic thought, the Patriarchs represent different divine emanations or "Sefirot."</note>

**"Please, do not bury me in Egypt"**
Rabbi Isaac said: Why did he not want to be buried in Egypt? So that his body would not become an object of foreign worship <note>idolatry</note>. For the Egyptians knew that the blessing had been with them from the moment he arrived...

**"And I shall lie with my fathers"**
Rabbi Eleazar opened with the verse: <note>Psalms 31:20</note> *How great is Your goodness, which You have hidden away for those who fear You, etc.*
Come and see: at the hour when the soul descends to this world...

<summary>This page contains Zoharic commentary on the beginning of the Torah portion Vayechi, exploring why Jacob's final days were "closed" to him and the mystical significance of his impending death. Various rabbis interpret biblical verses to explain the spiritual weight of a person's lifetime and Jacob's insistence on being buried in the Land of Israel rather than Egypt.</summary>

<keywords>Jacob, Joseph, Zohar, Vayechi, afterlife, burial in Israel, kindness and truth, the End of Days, Egyptian exile</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the construction of the Tabernacle, specifically focusing on the symbolic architecture of the altars as described in the Zohar on the Torah portion Terumah.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

What is the meaning of that which is written: **"And you shall make the altar of acacia wood... five cubits long and five cubits wide; the altar shall be square, and its height shall be three cubits"** <note>Exodus 27:1</note>?
Come and see: This altar is below and stands on the "Left Side" <note>In Kabbalah, the Left Side often represents the attribute of Judgment (Gevurah) and the physical realm</note>, and this is called the <term>Outer Altar</term> <note>original: "mizbe'ach ha-chitzon"</note>.
It is on the outside and originates from the Left Side. And if you should say: "But the Tabernacle stands in the image of that which is above, and is modeled after the supernal realm?" Come and see: All those vessels that were in the Tabernacle all stand in the supernal image; because of this, they all stand within the mystery of Faith <note>A Zoharic term for the system of Divine emanations or the Shekhinah</note>. Come and see: The Outer Altar is certainly on the Left Side, and the Inner Altar is on the side of the Right Arm.
And concerning this it is written: **"An altar of earth you shall make for Me"** <note>Exodus 20:21</note>. This refers to the Outer Altar. And it is written: "An altar of fragrant incense" <note>Cf. Exodus 30:1, 7</note>, and this is the <term>Inner Altar</term> <note>original: "mizbe'ach ha-p'nimi"</note>. And this altar is called "earth" because it stands in union with the "Earth" above. For there is "Earth" and there is "Earth": there is the Earth that is holy and above, and there is the earth below. And because of this, it is written: "An altar of earth you shall make for Me," which is the Outer Altar. The "altar of fragrant incense" is the Inner Altar.
What is the reason it is called the "altar of fragrant incense"? Because these spices correspond to those levels of theirs that stand against the strength of the spirit. And this is their mystery: they stand against the strength of the spirit, and this is the Inner Altar. Come and see: The Inner Altar certainly corresponds to the strength of the spirit, while the Outer Altar corresponds to the strength of the body. And because of this, and for this reason, they are called the Outer Altar and the Inner Altar. This [inner] one is called the <term>Golden Altar</term> because it stands on the side of the Gold above, and the Outer Altar is called the <term>Copper Altar</term> because it stands on the side of Copper. And come and see, it is written: **"And you shall make the altar of acacia wood."** What is "acacia wood" <note>Hebrew: Atzei Shittim</note>? These are the angels who stand corresponding to this altar.
And if you should say: "Do angels originate from the side of Copper?" Come and see: The angels <unclear>below are those who stand corresponding to this, and they are called "acacia wood."</unclear>

<summary>This passage from the Zohar explains the mystical duality of the two Tabernacle altars, linking the Outer Copper Altar to the body and the "Left Side," while the Inner Golden Altar relates to the spirit and the "Right Side." It further interprets the "acacia wood" of the altar's construction as a reference to specific classes of angels.</summary>

<keywords>Zohar, Tabernacle, Outer Altar, Inner Altar, Copper Altar, Golden Altar, Acacia Wood, Body and Spirit, Left Side, Right Arm, Angels</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of divine light, focusing on the mechanics of spiritual perception and the emanation of Wisdom (Chokhmah).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar/Kabbalistic Manuscript)

[...]<note>The top of the first line is partially obscured or faded</note> the power when he saw his voices, immediately they were driven away... this vision is very great.

He opened his discourse and said:
> **"And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament"** etc. <note>Daniel 12:3</note> 

These "wise ones" <note>original: "maskilim"</note> are the firmament that includes within it those celestial chariots and their divisions. Fortunate are those wise ones who contemplate the secret of **Holy Wisdom** <note>Chokhmah Kadisha</note> so as to be worthy of knowing the world. And even among those who come to dwell upon them, they are called by the name of the Holy Knowledge, which is **Wisdom**. And this is why they are called "wise ones" <note>maskilim</note> of Wisdom—referring to those who receive it, etc.

And because Wisdom is found at the end of Thought <note>the highest point of conscious intellect</note>, it is in the manner where there is the **Subject who knows** <note>maskil</note>, the **Object known** <note>mushkal</note>, and the **Act of knowing** <note>haskalah</note>, and they are all one in a bond that takes hold of everything.

And when these wise ones merit to be bound to that "Object known" etc., they **"shall shine as the brightness of the firmament."** What is this "brightness of the firmament"? This is the firmament spread over those high holy ones who are called the **Scribes of the Torah**.

This is a firmament that is above all the firmaments we have mentioned—the ten—and this is the firmament that is a sapphire <note>original: "sapir"</note>, a sapphire-stone that shines above and below. It shines above upon those ten lights that shine and are found within that sapphire-stone, which shines and illuminates all lights, sustaining everything, surrounding and shining.

And even like every firmament, all lights surround that radiance <note>Zohar</note> and stand there; then it is called the "Radiance of the Higher Light." This is like a parable of a king when he goes out to battle and shines; when he is revealed, he illuminates that sun which is the "brightness of the firmament." And in that light which is found directly in its place, it stands and shines—from this light and from that light it shines to all sides, and is called "Radiance" <note>Zohar</note>.

And all those who are wise in that radiance are hinted at in these letters: **"They shall shine"** <note>original: "Yazhiru"</note> with a single light that is prepared for every single righteous person, which opens and illuminates everything.

---

<summary>This page provides a Kabbalistic commentary on Daniel 12:3, explaining that the "wise" are those who achieve union with Divine Wisdom (Chokhmah) through the triad of the knower, the known, and the knowledge. It describes a supreme "Sapphire Firmament" that illuminates all other spiritual realms and provides the light reserved for the righteous.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Not because it surrounds him, but all those legions and all those "masters of eyes" <note>angelic observers or spiritual entities with heightened perception</note> who are washed beneath the kidneys <note>a metaphorical reference to the seat of internal counsel or hidden wisdom</note> that shine below, while he is in the center. And this is the <term>Middle Column</term> <note>The central axis of the Sefirotic tree, representing balance and the attribute of Beauty/Tiferet</note> which draws forth and sends to them the "living being" that is called the "shining living being," through the lights that stand firm, calm, and settled. And he is **The Lord** <note>original: "יהוה" - the Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God</note> because it is He who sustains them and holds them so that they do not separate toward the <term>Other Side</term> <note>original: "Sitra Achra" - the realm of evil or impurity</note> at all.

"And it was so" <note>original: "Vayehi Ken"</note>—this is a <term>mystery</term> <note>original: "Raza" - a hidden spiritual truth</note> regarding everything, because they stand within this great mystery on the side of the world to assist and to be under the authority of the Master of Lovingkindness. And they are the masters of harsh judgment, and all of them are constantly involved in the matters of the world; in their hands is the judgment to do good or to do evil. And this is compared to the work performed by Moses and Aaron and the magicians of Egypt <note>cf. Exodus 7:11-12</note>.

And we have learned in this portion that it is written, "And it was so," and this is the mystery that we have established in the mystery that is seen above, in this manner, in all works. Even though they come from the <term>side of impurity</term> <note>original: "Sitra de-Masaba"</note>, they are able to be under the authority of <term>the Holy One, blessed be He</term> and to exercise power and strength to establish matters according to their proper arrangement. Even though they are outside of the faith, they know and observe this mystery. Regarding this it is written:

-> "And the magicians did so with their secret arts" <note>Exodus 7:22</note> <-

"And it was so"—meaning, the power of the Other Side is meant to be rectified and to send all that is needed through this, to establish the things that they do, even though they were theirs. And in all this, the Holy One, blessed be He, gives strength. All this is because there is no thing in all the world that does not have [divine] power, and all this is so that there shall be knowledge of all this, to establish matters as is fitting.

<summary>This page explains that even the "Other Side" and the magic of the Egyptians operate under the ultimate authority of the Divine "Middle Column." It interprets the phrase "And it was so" as a mystical mechanism that allows even impure forces to manifest reality under God's sovereignty.</summary>

<keywords>Middle Column, Other Side, Egyptian Magicians, Divine Sovereignty, Mystery, Judgment, Moses and Aaron, Sitra Achra, Tetragrammaton</keywords>

## Genesis

Upper and lower worlds are found within it as one mystery, as one Spirit of the Messiah <note>original: "Ruach de-Mashiach"</note>. And this Spirit goes forth from the Ancient Holy One <note>original: "Atika Kadisha," referring to the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note>, who is the Spirit of Life. Within Him hang the upper and lower worlds, for He has no fixed place. He does not descend into the world except when the Soul <note>original: "Nishmata"</note> is made known through Him.

And this Spirit is the Holy Soul of the Messiah, which is hidden and concealed in a certain holy treasury. It is not known above or below until that Spirit is awakened. For thus they have established the mystery of the words written in the scripture:

-> **And the Spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters** <-

And this Spirit is the Spirit of the Messiah, which goes forth from the Ancient Holy One, the High One over all high ones, who is hidden and concealed within Him. "And it hovered over the face of the waters"—this refers to the river that goes out from Eden to water the Garden <note>a reference to the flow of divine influence from the source of Wisdom into the lower realms</note>, which is the source of life for all inhabitants of the world. At that time, that Spirit is awakened, and through it, all worlds shall be known, and the Holy One shall be seen in the eyes of the whole world. For then the Holy Living Creatures <note>term: "Chayot HaKodesh," a high order of angels</note> shall be awakened and shall stand before Him. And this Spirit goes forth and is found hidden and concealed in one place.

**He opened and said:** When this shall be, and the Spirit is found within it as one mystery, it is the Soul that is found hidden within it. Through it, all the life of the world shall be awakened, and through it, the Holy Mystery shall be revealed to all inhabitants of the world. Then the mystery of life shall be found in Him, and He shall be the one known to all inhabitants of the world, and they shall prophesy from Him, just as it is said:

-> **Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy** <-

And through Him, all the mysteries of the Torah shall be awakened, and the whole world shall be sustained through Him. Blessed be the Lord forever, Amen and Amen.

<summary>This page provides a mystical interpretation of the "Spirit of God" in Genesis, identifying it as the Spirit of the Messiah emanating from the highest divine level (Atika Kadisha) to bring life and prophecy to the world.</summary>
<keywords>Spirit of Messiah, Ancient Holy One, Genesis 1:2, prophecy, Eden, Holy Soul, Zohar, Jewish Mysticism</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the creation narrative in Genesis, specifically focusing on the transition from the primordial "Thought" to the physical and spiritual structures of the world as represented by the four elements and the Divine Name.</meta>

# Genesis

## Main Text (Zohar)

...at first, and it was above what was, and the action of the action was in this manner and this secret: **"And the earth was unformed and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep, and the spirit of God..."** etc. <note>Genesis 1:2</note> These are four signs.

**It was taught:** At the time when the **Supreme Thought** <term>Machshavah Ila'ah: The first glimmer of divine intellect in the Sefirot</term> was crowned with the crown of **Father and Mother** <term>Abba and Imma: The Sefirot of Wisdom (Chokhmah) and Understanding (Binah)</term>. Father and Mother hang between them and were not crowned until the names were established. And when they were crowned, they brought forth that Thought and gave birth to what that Thought birthed; and it brought forth that light which scatters to all sides and gave birth to those **seven lights** <note>The seven lower Sefirot or days of creation</note> that are included within it. From where do we know this? As it is written: >In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth< <note>Genesis 1:1</note>. "And the" <note>original: "Ve-et"</note> certainly brought forth seven lights, and they were all crowned in that light. And when this one brought forth and gave birth, it gave birth in the secret of this name: **Mah** <note>The numerical value of the name Adam (45), associated with the Sefirah of Tiferet</note>. And this is what brought forth that light and shines to every side, and they are separated into their paths and draw from that light as it was said, for they were filled from it.

**It was taught:** It is written: >And the earth was unformed and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep, and the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters< <note>Genesis 1:2</note>. Four signs are mentioned here: **Unformed (Tohu), Void (Bohu), Darkness, and Spirit.** And these are the four foundations <note>elements</note> of the world that are separated from it, and all of them were established from it.
<term>Tohu (Unformed)</term>: This is the **green line** <term>Kav Yarok: A mystical line that encircles the world, from which darkness emanates</term> that surrounds the whole world, as it was said in that place where it is written: >He shall stretch over it the line of confusion [Tohu]< <note>Isaiah 34:11</note>.
<term>Bohu (Void)</term>: These are the **slimy stones** <term>Avnin Mafulmat: Sunken or "moist" stones located in the abyss from which water flows</term> from which the waters emerge.
<term>Darkness</term>: This is the supernal fire.
<term>Spirit</term>: This is the Holy Spirit <note>Ruach HaKodesh</note> which emerges and draws forth and stands over the water, as it was said.

**It was taught:** These are the four foundations that are separated, and they are the foundation of the entire world, and all of them are the secret of the Holy Name which is **Y-H-V-H** <term>The Tetragrammaton</term>.
The secret of **Tohu** is the letter **Yod (י)**.
The secret of **Bohu** is the letter **Heh (ה)**.
The secret of **Darkness** is the letter **Vav (ו)**.
The secret of **Spirit** is the **latter Heh (ה)**.

**It was taught:** These four letters are everything; they are the engraved Name that is included in all of them, and from them are separated four winds <note>or directions</note> to every side. And that radiance that went out and gave birth to them is in this manner <unclear>to all those sides</unclear>. <unclear>And they are all joined in this secret of unity</unclear>. <unclear>And all the workings of the world are in this manner</unclear>.

<summary>This page provides a mystical interpretation of the four primordial states mentioned in Genesis 1:2 (Tohu, Bohu, Darkness, and Spirit), mapping them onto the four letters of the Divine Name (Y-H-V-H) and the four elemental foundations of reality.</summary>
<keywords>Tetragrammaton, Tohu and Bohu, Four Elements, Sefirot, Creation, Green Line, Slimy Stones, Holy Spirit</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Vayishlach, focusing on the mechanics of divine forgiveness and the spiritual hierarchy of repentance.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

This secret must be known: that Repentance <note>original: "Teshuvah"</note> stands above, and there is an Upper Repentance and a Lower Repentance. This is because there are two levels that are destined to be called by this name: one is the Upper World <note>The Sefirah of Binah, the divine "Mother" and source of cosmic return</note> and the other is the Lower World <note>The Sefirah of Malkhut, the earthly manifestation of the divine</note>. Each one is called Repentance. Regarding this, Rabbi Isaac said: What is the meaning of that which is written, *You return man to contrition, and say, "Return, O children of men"*? <note>Psalms 90:3</note> This verse is difficult; for when is a person called "contrite" <note>The Hebrew word "Daka" (contrite/crushed) is interpreted here as the state of a person broken by sin who then turns toward God</note>? It is at the time when those human beings enter into repentance. And so they have established it.

Rabbi Eleazar said that Rabbi Simeon said: Fortunate are the righteous who know the way of the Holy One, blessed be He, to walk in it. And what of that which is written: *If there be for him an angel, an intercessor, one among a thousand, to vouch for a man’s uprightness...*? <note>Job 33:23</note> Come and see: because three hundred and fifty-four accusers <note>original: "Kategorin." This number corresponds to the days of the lunar year, suggesting that every day carries its own potential for spiritual accusation</note> stand over a person when he sins before the Holy One, blessed be He. When a person comes to sin, how many are the witnesses who stand over him and testify before the Holy One, blessed be He! And what of that which is written: *For a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which has wings shall tell the matter*? <note>Ecclesiastes 10:20</note> Indeed, they have established this in many places.

And because of this, at the hour when a person gives birth to the Evil Inclination <note>The "Yetzer Hara," the internal drive toward selfishness or sin</note>, it becomes an accuser against him for the World to Come. Even so, the Holy One, blessed be He, stretches out His right hand to receive them in repentance. And this is what is written: *As a father has compassion on his children...* <note>Psalms 103:13</note> and they have established this. How much more so does the Holy One, blessed be He, have compassion on them, because this world is a world of imagination <note>original: "Demyo." This suggests the physical world is a fleeting shadow or illusion compared to the spiritual reality</note>. And every time that he is in a state of repentance, they atone for him for his sins, and many are those who come forward to forgive him. When a person comes to sin, certainly the Holy One, blessed be He, has compassion on him, and all this is because he has *one intercessor among a thousand.*

<summary>This page explores the mystical concept of Teshuvah (Repentance), distinguishing between its "Upper" and "Lower" cosmic forms and explaining how a single advocating angel can defend a sinner against 354 celestial accusers.</summary>
<keywords>Repentance, Teshuvah, Upper World, Lower World, Accusers, Intercessor, Compassion, Evil Inclination, Zohar</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the creation narrative from the Zohar, specifically focusing on the flow of divine emanation and the transition from the Sabbath to the generative power of the Patriarchs.</meta>

## Portion of Bereshit

More so, and because of this, all blessings are blessed from that river <note>The "river" refers to the flow of divine light from the higher Sefirot (emanations) down to the lower ones.</note> that flows and goes forth, for all blessings of the upper and lower worlds dwell within it. And this river is called **All** <note>Hebrew: *Kol*. In Kabbalah, this term often refers to the Sefirah of Yesod, which gathers all the divine energies to transmit them further.</note>, as it is written:
> For **all** that is in heaven and on earth (1 Chronicles 29:11)
And its Aramaic translation is: "that which takes hold of heaven and earth."
And because it is **All**, all blessings are blessed from it, and on each and every day they are blessed from it. For this reason, it is called the "Seventh Day," and this is the Sabbath of the Sabbath Eve <note>The feminine aspect of the Sabbath, the Shekhinah.</note>, in which all blessings dwell. Regarding this, it is written:
> And God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on it He rested from all His work... (Genesis 2:3)
And this is the day from which all other days are blessed, and within it dwell the six days that were blessed from it each and every day. Because of this, all six days dwell within it, and it is called the "Seventh Sabbath." This is the seventh level <note>The Sefirah of Malkhut/Kingdom, the seventh of the lower emanations.</note> in which all blessings dwell. And when it rests in blessings, as it were, it rests and is at ease. Because of this:
> ...because on it He rested from all His work which God created **to do** (Genesis 2:3)
And this is the "Lower Sabbath." What is the meaning of **to do**? It means that all the work of the world is done through it. And regarding this, it is written:
> These are the generations of the heavens and the earth **when they were created** (Genesis 2:4)
Do not read it as **when they were created** <note>Hebrew: *Be-hibara’am*</note> but rather as **through Abraham** <note>Hebrew: *Be-Abraham*. This is a classic Zoharic wordplay (anagram) linking the act of creation to the merit or attribute of the Patriarch Abraham.</note>. As it is written:
> And Abraham was old, advanced in days (Genesis 24:1)
These are the "Upper Days" <note>The divine Sefirot</note> which Abraham took hold of.
And because of this, it is written "when they were created," meaning "through Abraham." And regarding this, it is written:
> ...on the day that the Lord God made earth and heaven (Genesis 2:4)
For all of them were made through this level.
And everything is within him, within Abraham, who is the upper level <note>The Sefirah of Chesed/Lovingkindness</note> in which all days are united, and he is called the "First Day" in which all other days are united. And come and see: all the works of the world were made through it, for it is the level of the upper and lower worlds united within it. Regarding this, it is written:
> On the day that the Lord God made earth and heaven. (Genesis 2:4)
"On the day of making," certainly.
And regarding this, it is written:
> No shrub of the field was yet in the earth, and no herb of the field had yet sprung up; for the Lord God had not caused it to rain... (Genesis 2:5)

<summary>This page explains the mystical "River" of divine blessing (Yesod) and the sanctity of the Sabbath as the source of all temporal blessings. It also uses an anagram to link the creation of the world to the Patriarch Abraham, representing the divine attribute of Lovingkindness.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar, specifically focusing on the spiritual status of the human soul and the necessity of Torah study and the fear of sin, as taught by the elders of the tradition.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

...and the holy, pious Rav Hamnuna the Elder <note>A prominent scholar and mystic frequently cited in the Zohar for his deep piety</note>, who at every time that he would pray and
...sustenance was prepared before him, he would say: "Here the Divine Presence <note>original: *Shekhinah*; the feminine, indwelling aspect of God</note> dwells, and here the Holy One rests."
...a word of Torah to labor in, the Divine Presence rests upon him, and in every
...every person who does not labor in the Torah—which is called "The Holy One, Blessed be He" <note>A central Zoharic concept that God and the Torah are one</note> and is the Law
...of the world—and that light of the Torah which illuminates for him all his paths.
...Because all the time that they are above, this matter is not revealed.
**Fortunate** is the portion of the righteous who are cleaved unto Him,
**unto the Holy One, Blessed be He**, and unto His Torah, and they are those who fear sin; for anyone who does not
**fear** sin is not considered a "human being" <note>term: *Bar Nash*; literally "son of man," implying a person who has achieved their full spiritual potential</note> at all. And this
**matter** I heard from the Holy Lamp <note>original: *Butzina Kadisha*; a title for Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note> who said thus: "Every person
**who does not** fear sin is not considered a human being at all." And regarding this it is written:
> **"And man became a living soul"** <note>Genesis 2:7</note>
What is a "living soul"? If you say
**that they** are "living" like the rest of the animals—for they are all called "living souls"—
**rather**, "living soul" refers to Israel, who are holy and the children of holy ones.
**For them** there is a "living soul." But what is a "living soul"? It is a holy soul
**from** heaven, living in the Holy of Holies, and because of this it is called a "living soul."
**And anyone** who is not marked <note>likely referring to the sign of the covenant or spiritual purity</note> is not a human being at all, because there is
**within him** that which is within him—for he has damaged his body with another, impure soul.
**Fortunate** is the portion of the righteous who know the ways of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
**and cleave** to Him and to His Torah. And everyone who merits to know the Torah
**of life** merits to do the will of his Creator, and merits to see the light that shines...

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Tabernacle's vessels, specifically focusing on the Copper Laver (Kiyor) used for priestly purification. It transitions from the general construction of the Sanctuary to the specific symbolic meanings of copper and the prophetic visions associated with the "Entrance of the Tent of Meeting."</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

> **And he made the copper laver and its copper stand from the mirrors of the legions who assembled at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.** <note>Exodus 38:8</note>

**Rabbi Eleazar** opened his discourse and said:
> **Splendor and majesty are before Him; strength and beauty are in His sanctuary.** <note>Psalms 96:6</note>

This verse has been established by the colleagues. However, "Splendor and majesty are before Him" refers to everything being in a single union, for these two <note>the sefirot of Hod and Hadar</note> are joined as one, and this constitutes the "before Him." "Strength and beauty are in His sanctuary" refers to when they are all joined together as one; then there is strength and beauty in His sanctuary. This is the literal secret of "in His sanctuary." The Laver and its stand represent "Splendor and Majesty" <note>Hebrew: Hod and Hadar</note>. All of this is to show that on the side of the Feminine <note>the Shekhinah</note>, there is copper. And what is copper? This is the <term>Serpent</term> <note>original: "Nachash," a wordplay on "Nechoshet" (copper)</note>. Because it is the Serpent, one must bring holiness into it. Through this, the sanctuary is sanctified, which is embodied in the Laver and its stand. This is why we say the Laver and its stand are Splendor and Majesty. All of this is made of copper because this is the place of the Serpent. From here, power is given to awaken the lower realms. Therefore, **"he made the copper laver..."**

Come and see: **"The entrance of the Tent of Meeting"** is the place where the legions <note>armies of angels or souls</note> assemble. And who are they? The **"mirrors of the legions."** They are called this because they all appear in that place in this manner. How do we know they all appear in that place? As it is written:
> **And by the hand of the prophets, I used parables.** <note>Hosea 12:11; original: "adameh," meaning to liken or visualize</note>

For this reason, they are called "mirrors." This place is called the "entrance of the Tent of Meeting." Therefore, it says, **"who assembled at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting."**

**Rabbi Shimon** said: **"Splendor and majesty are before Him"**—Splendor and Majesty are the two true prophets <note>referring to the sefirot Hod and Netzach, the sources of prophecy</note>. Both of them come from the side of copper. For this reason, they are called copper, because copper comes from the side of the North. The sign for this is:
> **Out of the north comes gold.** <note>Job 37:22</note>

It says gold, but they actually come from the side that is copper. Because they are called copper, he made from them the Laver and its stand. What is the Laver? It is the secret of the <term>Throne of Elijah</term> <note>the chair used during a circumcision, representing the presence of the prophet</note>, may he be remembered for good. This is the Laver, as it is written:
> **For Solomon had made a copper laver and placed it in the midst of the court.** <note>2 Chronicles 6:13</note>

This Laver is the "measure of five" <note>referring to its dimensions or its symbolic link to the five fingers or five levels of the soul</note>. Its stand is the secret of the **Righteous One** <note>the sefira of Yesod</note>, who is the <term>Foundation of the World</term>. Therefore, it is a **"copper laver and its copper stand."** Here an upper secret is hinted at: that these two stand in copper. Therefore, all of them are in copper. Thus, the Laver and the throne that was in it were entirely of copper, because this is the place of the North. From here, the secret is revealed <unclear>greatness and in it</unclear>...

<summary>This page provides a Kabbalistic interpretation of the Copper Laver, linking its material (copper) to the "Serpent" and the "North," while identifying the Laver and its stand with the divine attributes of Splendor, Majesty, and the Foundation.</summary>
<keywords>Copper Laver, Nechoshet, Serpent, Hod, Hadar, Yesod, Prophecy, Mirrors of the Legions, Tabernacle, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Vayishlach, focusing on the preservation of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) during the Jewish exile and the sublime nature of human creation.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

When those ancient ones who are in the world of the Holy One, blessed be He, dwell there, He remembers them and appears before them; they all stand in desire and joy, as we have established. And at the time when they see and delight in that sweetness of theirs, they are awakened by those songs that they all say in joy, and they speak joy within joy because the Holy One, blessed be He, is revealed upon them.

Rabbi Isaac opened his discourse and said:
> (Psalms 106:3) **"Happy are those who keep justice, who perform righteousness at all times."**

"Happy are those who keep justice"—these are the ones who guard the faith <note>original: *meimanuta*</note> of the Holy One, blessed be He, because "Justice" is the essence of faith. And regarding this, "Happy are those who keep justice." "Who perform righteousness at all times"—is it truly possible for a human being to perform righteousness <note>The Hebrew *tzedakah* means both righteousness and acts of charity.</note> at all times? Rather, this refers to the <term>Holy One, blessed be He</term> <note>The primary name for God in the Zohar, representing the masculine aspect of the Divine.</note> who performs righteousness and kindness with the world and with man at every hour and every moment, and at all times.
<term>Another interpretation</term> <note>original: *davar acher*</note>: "Who perform righteousness"—this is the Holy One, blessed be He, who performs righteousness with the <term>Congregation of Israel</term> <note>The *Knesset Yisrael*, representing the Shekhinah or the feminine Divine Presence in exile.</note> to strengthen her at all times within the exile in which she dwells. For were it not for the righteousness that the Holy One, blessed be He, performs with the Congregation of Israel, she would not be able to survive in exile, as the companions have established.

Rabbi Judah and Rabbi Isaac were walking on the road; when they reached an inn, they sat down. Rabbi Judah opened the discourse and said:
> (Isaiah 43:1) **"But now, thus says the Lord who created you, O Jacob, and He who formed you, O Israel: Fear not, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by your name; you are Mine."**

How much must human beings look into the service of their Master! For there is no man in the world who knows how to observe and to know upon what he stands in the world and how he was created. Come and see: the Holy One, blessed be He, created man and arranged for him supernal arrangements <note>original: *tikkunin*; the mystical structures or "rectifications" of the Divine realms.</note> and arranged for him lower arrangements, and gave him strength and power to rule over all.

<summary>This passage discusses how God's "righteousness" sustains the Jewish people and the Divine Presence during exile, followed by a reflection on the profound spiritual structure of the human being.</summary>
<keywords>Justice, Righteousness, Exile, Shekhinah, Creation of Man, Tikkun, Divine Service</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original Aramaic: Kudsha Brich Hu</note>, when it arose in His will to create the world, He looked into the Torah and created the world. And with every single word that the Holy One, blessed be He, performed, He looked into the Torah and performed it. Thus it has been stated, and the scripture is written:
-> I was beside Him as a confidant <note>Proverbs 8:30</note> <-
Do not read *amon* [confidant] but rather *uman* [artisan/architect]. The Holy One, blessed be He, looked into the Torah and created the world. And the Torah said, etc., He looked into the Torah and created the world. In this same manner, a human being must look into the Torah to know the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, according to the supernal example. It is found that anyone who exerts themselves in the Torah is as if they sustain the world. For behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, looked into the Torah and created the world; when human beings exert themselves in the Torah, she is the sustenance of the world. For because of her the world is sustained, as it is said:
-> If My covenant be not with day and night <note>Jeremiah 33:25</note> <-
And so on. And because of this, these are the paths of uprightness. And at all times when one is to pray, there was a belovedness, etc., and He receives the prayer from the depths of the heart. As it is written:
-> Out of the depths I have called to You, O Lord <note>Psalms 130:1</note> <-
And at all times when prayer is from the depths, the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, is found toward them, and He receives this prayer, and His will goes forth to bless them and crown them. And because of this, the Holy One, blessed be He, is found for a person and receives them with love, and the supernal will is awakened, as it is written: "And I will bless you," etc. From the blessing. And because of this, the Holy One, blessed be He, is found for those who walk in the path of truth. And in every word that one prays, the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, is ready for them, for prayer is a beloved thing that is considered before Him more than all sacrifices and burnt offerings. And at all times when a person prays, they must pray from the depth of the heart because of what is said: **"Out of the depths I have called to You, O Lord."** And they have already established that at all times when one needs to pray, they should pray, etc., for the Holy One, blessed be He, is present for them and receives this prayer. And through the Torah, a person is beloved to the Holy One, blessed be He; their belovedness is like clusters of grapes <unclear>in the desert</unclear>... For the Torah is like a body, and those Torah scholars who exert themselves in it are like the soul of the Torah. And because of this, a person must know and look into the matters of the Torah, because whoever exerts themselves in it, it is as if they sustain the world perfectly and as if they created the world, because the Torah was the tool of the craft of the Holy One, blessed be He, with which He created the world, as it is said: **"In the beginning God created."** And the Torah said: "I was the tool of the craft of the Holy One, blessed be He, to create the world."

<summary>This manuscript page explains the Kabbalistic doctrine that God used the Torah as a blueprint or "architect's tool" for Creation and posits that human study and sincere prayer from the heart sustain the universe.</summary>
<keywords>Creation, Torah study, Prayer from the heart, Architect of the world, Sustenance of the world, Divine Will</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar on Exodus (Parashat Bo), focusing on the distinction between divine appointed times and the false astrological or idolatrous timings used by the Egyptians.</meta>

## Portion of Bo

For this reason, they established times and seasons <note>original: "zmanin u-moadin"</note> when they stood ready to depart from Egypt. And those who performed worship <note>original: "pulchana"</note> for them—and every person who follows those times and seasons established by the Egyptians—stand before them. When their worship emerged, that appointed minister <note>The celestial power or angel governing a specific nation</note> of theirs [emerged] to depart from exile, and he sought to establish times and seasons for them. Through these, those who thought to perform worship through them remain in error, as it is said:

> **"And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall punish the host of the high heaven on high, and the kings of the earth upon the earth."** <note>Isaiah 24:21</note>

Because of this, those times and seasons are the commandments of the Holy One, blessed be He, for they are His times and seasons. He gazes into them and reveals them to His prophets, as it is said:

> **"Surely the Lord God will do nothing, unless He reveals His secret unto His servants the prophets."** <note>Amos 3:7</note>

And every word, season, and time of the Holy One, blessed be He, which He has ordained, the Holy One, blessed be He, reveals to the prophets. But those times and seasons of theirs [the Egyptians/idolatrous nations], they make them to lead mankind astray. And those who perform worship to them are judged by them, as it is said: **"And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall punish the host of the high heaven on high, etc."** Therefore, those times and seasons are called "times of destruction," and those who observe them are foolish and mislead mankind. Rabbi Shimon said: Worthy is the portion of those who labor in the Torah <note>original: "Oraita"</note>, for the Torah reveals to them all the secrets <note>original: "razin"</note> and all the times and all the seasons of the Holy One, blessed be He. And everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, has done and is destined to do, He reveals to them. Regarding this it is written:

> **"O Lord, why hast Thou made us to err from Thy ways, and hardened our heart from Thy fear? Return for Thy servants' sake, the tribes of Thine inheritance."** <note>Isaiah 63:17</note>

---

Rabbi Shimon opened [his discourse] and said:

> **"A Song of Ascents. I will lift up mine eyes unto the mountains: from whence shall my help come? My help cometh from the Lord, who made heaven and earth."** <note>Psalms 121:1-2</note>

The companions <note>original: "chavrayya" — the circle of scholars surrounding Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> have already established the meaning of this verse, but this verse should be looked at in this way: **"I will lift up mine eyes unto the mountains"** — these are the pure mountains... <note>A mystical reference to the Patriarchs or high spiritual emanations</note>

<summary>This page contrasts the divinely ordained "appointed times" revealed to prophets and Torah scholars with the deceptive astrological timings used by the Egyptians. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai emphasizes that true knowledge of time and destiny is found only through the secrets of the Torah.</summary>
<keywords>appointed times, prophecy, Egypt, celestial host, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, Torah secrets, mountains, idolatry</keywords>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

->**Portion of Vayikra**<-

**And He called** to Moses, and the Lord spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying... <note>Leviticus 1:1</note>. Rabbi Eleazar opened his discourse and said: "Bless the Lord, you His angels, mighty in strength, who perform His word, obeying the voice of His word" <note>Psalms 103:20</note>. Come and see <note>original: "Ta chazi" — a common Zoharic invitation to contemplate a mystical truth</note> how much a person must guard themselves from their sins and mend their ways before the Holy One, Blessed be He. For behold, every single day a herald goes forth and proclaims: "How long, you simple ones, will you love simplicity?" <note>Proverbs 1:22</note>. And it is written: "To you, O men, I call, and my voice is to the sons of man" <note>Proverbs 8:4</note>. And it is further written: "She calls out at the head of the noisy streets, at the entrances of the gates..." <note>Proverbs 1:21</note>.

**Come and see** how much a person must strive in the Torah <term>Torah: the sacred law and mystical teachings of Judaism</term>, for anyone who strives in the Torah is saved from the Higher Judgment, and is saved from all those accusers who are aroused in the world. Because when a person sits idle and ceases from the Torah, it is as if the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the feminine, indwelling aspect of God</term> stands before him and says: "The tongue of the wise makes knowledge good, but the mouth of fools pours out foolishness" <note>Proverbs 15:2</note>. And we have established that anyone who ceases from the Torah, it is as if he has removed the Divine Presence from the world.

**Come and see**: at the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, comes to execute judgment in the world, those who strive in the Torah have no fear of all those judgments in the world. What is the reason? Because the Torah is grasped within the Tree of Life, and anyone who holds fast to the Tree of Life does not fear all those judgments that affect the rest of humanity.

<summary>Rabbi Eleazar explains that diligent Torah study acts as a spiritual defense against divine judgment and connects the soul to the Tree of Life. He emphasizes that neglecting study causes the Divine Presence to withdraw from the world.</summary>

<keywords>Vayikra, Torah study, Divine Presence, Shekhinah, Tree of Life, Judgment, Rabbi Eleazar, repentance</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Song of Songs from the Zohar, specifically focusing on the linguistic and Sefirotic structure of the title "Shir HaShirim." It follows the previous discussion regarding the various songs of the Bible and why this specific song is considered the pinnacle of divine praise.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> 35 <-

The secret of the matter is that Solomon composed all these songs and praises <note>referring to the various songs in the Bible</note> to unify the sacrifice of the Name <note>original: "shma"; referring to the unification of the Divine Name</note> this with that in perfection. For this reason, he called the song the **Song of Songs**. "Song" <note>original: "Shir"</note> consists of six rings <unclear>of the beginning</unclear> in the Holy Name, in which all names are held. Therefore, this "Song" is five; "Song of Songs" <note>original: "Shir HaShirim"</note> is five, because it is five and is found within it five, because this is the supreme level called the **Holy of Holies**.

When this is joined with that, then it is called the **Song of Songs**, for the peace <note>original: "shlama"; a play on the name Solomon/Shelomo</note> of above is found within it. The desire of the Song of Songs is because the Holy Wisdom <term>Chokhmah: the second Sefirah, representing the first flash of divine intellect</term>, which is called the **Holy of Holies**, shines and illuminates this place called "Song." When it illuminates it with its light, then it is found to be the "Song of Songs" as we have said. For this reason, it is called the **Holy of Holies**.

And because this "Song" is found in greater perfection than all other songs in the world—even though all the songs in the world are all holy—the Song of Songs is the **Holy of Holies**. For Rabbi Shimon said: This Song of Songs is everything, because the **Shekhinah** <term>The Divine Presence; the feminine aspect of God</term> is in her perfection in all colors as is fitting, and all the songs of the world are included within it.

Come and see: In the Song of Songs, the Lower *He* <note>The final letter of the Tetragrammaton, representing the Shekhinah</note> is included in the Upper *He* <note>The second letter of the Tetragrammaton, representing Binah or Understanding</note>, and the entire secret of faith is found within it. All the secrets of the Torah and all the secrets of the Holy Name are included within it. Therefore, this Song of Songs is the perfection of everything, and all matters of the Torah are included in it. Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Eleazar and all the companions would open with this "Song of Songs" when they sat to engage in the study of the Torah. And this Song of Songs is a "Song" because it includes "Song" within "the Songs" as we have said. And even though it is everything...

## Main Text (The Hidden Midrash)

... "And You shall hear from the heavens and forgive the sin of Your people Israel, and return them to the land which You gave to their fathers." <note>I Kings 8:34</note>
For a short time they returned and were hungry for the "snow and ice" <note>original: *sheleg ve-galid*</note> of the Repetition of the Torah <note>The Book of Deuteronomy</note>. Who is he and what is he that made it so?
He ascended to that place and established a restoration <note>term: *tikkun* — a mystical mending or rectification</note> for them. For behold, below it was frozen and icy, and it was dark.
It was dark and did not shine until the Sun <note>original: *shimsha*</note> arrived and shone upon it; then that snow melted.
And when that Sun shines upon it and gives light within it, it glows, and that snow gives birth to water.
From them, rivers and streams emerge and flow, and from them the world is watered and illuminated. And who is this Sun?
This is Moses, who shines from the Supernal Light and gives light below to restore the world, as we have established.
For he is the Sun, and that snow and ice is the Divine Presence <note>term: *Shekhinah* — the feminine aspect of God that dwells within the world</note> who is in Exile <note>original: *galuta*</note>, for she is frozen and icy.
She gives of her lights, and because she is in that "stronghold," Moses comes and gives her light.
He warms her until she shines, and from that light, waters emerge and she gives birth, providing a path to sustain the souls of the righteous above and below, as the Sages established. Furthermore, it is written: "And a river went out from Eden to water the garden, and from there it parted and became four heads" <note>Genesis 2:10</note>. These are the Sages of the Talmud,
who shine through the Torah. The early Sages established that when Moses found what he found—
which was snow and ice—he raised it up and restored it with a supernal restoration through the Light from Above.
And the Sages said that this Sun and Moses are on the same level. There are **Thirty Seals** <note>original: *L' Chatimot* — mystical symbols of authority or protection</note> of that level,
the level in which the light dwells and shines from it, as we have said. Moses, the Faithful Prophet <note>original: *Moshe Neviya Meheimna*</note>, raised her up
and restored her with a supernal restoration through the higher lights, to shine with the light that is the Sun.

The **Thirty** Seals are hidden and concealed for those Sages of the Talmud and for Moses the Faithful Prophet.
And their seals are hidden and concealed within those Sages of the Talmud and within Moses the Faithful Prophet.
Concerning this, the early Sages said: the seals of Moses are "Moses" without the seal of "You shall have no other gods before Me" <note>Exodus 20:3</note> ...

## Main Text (Zohar)

As it was taught, Rabbi Phinehas said: At the time when that river flows and goes forth from Eden <note>In Kabbalah, the river represents the flow of divine life or "Yesod" emanating from the source</note> to water the Garden, that **Man** <note>original: "Adam"</note> is crowned by virtue of the Image <note>original: "dyokna," referring to the divine prototype or form</note> which is supreme over all. And this mystery is that all is one.

And we have learned that when this **Man** is crowned with all those holy crowns, and those supreme holy Names are all crowned within him, then all is one. And concerning this it is written:
> The Lord shall be one and His name one <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>
What is "The Lord shall be one"? This refers to what is supreme over all. And "His name one"? This refers to what is below. Yet all is one. And because of this, **Man** includes everything. And the Torah is entirely included within him, because **Man** is the Torah, and the Torah is **Man**. As it is written:
> This is the Torah: Man... <note>Numbers 19:14; the Zohar reads this verse midrashically to equate the essence of the Law with the structure of the human form</note>
And the mystery of this is:
> The Torah is light <note>Proverbs 6:23</note>
Because light is **Man**. And it is a light that shines in all worlds. And this is the mystery of the **Supernal Man**. When this **Man** is illuminated, all the worlds are illuminated and blessed through him. But when this **Man** is not illuminated, all the worlds exist in darkness. All the springs of the river that goes and flows forth from Eden—when it goes forth from Eden and spreads out—all is one. As it is written:
> A river went out from Eden <note>Genesis 2:10</note>
And this river is the **Supernal Man**, who goes forth from Eden. What is **Eden**? This is **Supernal Wisdom** <note>original: "Chokhmah Ila'ah," the second Sephirah or divine attribute representing the first point of conscious revelation</note>, which is hidden above all. And the mystery of this is:
> No eye has seen it, O God, beside You <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>

<summary>This page explores the Kabbalistic concept of the "Supernal Man" (Adam Kadmon) as a cosmic bridge, identifying him with both the Torah and the divine river flowing from the hidden source of Wisdom (Eden).</summary>

## Genesis

...the Holy One, blessed be He. And concerning this it is written: ->"And the Lord God built the rib which He had taken from the man..."<- <note>Genesis 2:22</note>
The Holy One, blessed be He, separated her in a specific chamber <note>original: "cheder"</note> and purified her, and prepared her for the man, as we have said:
->"And He brought her to the man."<- <note>Genesis 2:22</note> "And Adam called his wife’s name Eve, because she was the mother of all living" <note>Genesis 3:20</note>. This refers to the <term>Matronita</term> <note>The Divine Matron or Queen, a title for the Shekhinah</note> of everything over the world. Come and see: because of this it is written, ->"And he shall cleave unto his wife, and they shall be one flesh"<- <note>Genesis 2:24</note> as we have said, for she was separated from his own bone and then clung back to him; this matter has been explained. Come and see: Adam came and was built from the heavens as one, as it is written: ->"Male and female He created them, and blessed them, and called their name Adam in the day they were created"<- <note>Genesis 5:2</note>.
And at the time that they are as one, they are called "Adam." Because of this, the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, viewed in the Zohar as the feminine aspect of God</note> does not dwell in a place where male and female are not together, and blessings do not flow from it and are not found within it. For this reason it is written, "and He blessed them and called their name Adam in the day they were created," so that he would be complete in this name. Come and see: everything that is not complete is not called by its name except when joined as one, because when this one and that one are found as one, total peace is found within them. And because of this, male and female as one are "complete," and this peace is the letters *Yod* and *He* <note>The first two letters of the Tetragrammaton, often representing the union of the male and female divine principles</note>; within them dwells peace. Therefore it is written, "and He blessed them and called their name Adam in the day they were created"—all as one. And regarding this, when they were separated from their sides, one from the other, everything was found to be flawed in this manner. Afterward, the Holy One, blessed be He, rested upon her and endowed her with everything, and it was a complete structure as has been stated. The supernal <term>Covenant</term> <note>Brit; often referring to the sefirah of Yesod, the principle of connection and procreation</note> is complete without flaw; through this union, everything was rectified. Because of this, the supernal Covenant is complete, and the Name is called complete, and completeness is found. And regarding this it is written, "And the Lord God built the rib etc."—this is the complete Covenant.

**And come and see:** the Name is complete. From this point forward, everything was rectified in a perfect rectification; the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world and it was in a perfect state.

**And come and see:** ->"In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made He him"<- <note>Genesis 5:1</note>. What is the meaning of "in the likeness of God made He him"? It is as we have said: that he was found complete without flaw. And because of this, Adam is complete in the likeness of his Master, for he is complete without flaw. And the name *Elohim* <note>God</note> is complete. Therefore, Adam is complete in the likeness of that which is complete. And come and see: as long as he is complete without flaw, the <term>Shekhinah</term> dwells upon him.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Vayechi, focusing on the divine structures (Sefirot) that govern the world and the spiritual roles of the Patriarchs.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

It is written: *Behold, the <term>fear of the Lord</term> <note>original: Yirat Adonai</note> is <term>wisdom</term> <note>original: Hokhmah</note>, and to depart from evil is <term>understanding</term> <note>original: Binah</note>.* <note>Job 28:28</note> This verse is difficult; for if so, is <term>wisdom</term> itself <term>fear</term>? Rather, we have learned that there is no <term>wisdom</term> except that which comes out of <term>fear</term>, for without <term>fear</term> there is no <term>wisdom</term> in the world at all. Because of this, <term>fear</term> is called <term>wisdom</term>. And this refers to the <term>Lower Wisdom</term> <note>The Sefirah of Malkhut/Kingship, the lowest of the ten divine emanations, which acts as the gateway to the higher realms</note>, and with this wisdom the world was made. For this reason, David said: *The <term>Lord</term> by wisdom founded the earth* <note>Proverbs 3:19</note>; it was with this specific wisdom that <term>the Holy One, blessed be He</term> established the earth. And so we have learned: *In the beginning God created...* <note>Genesis 1:1</note>. "In the beginning" <note>original: Bereshit</note> refers to <term>wisdom</term>, and this is <term>fear</term>.

And it is written: *and to depart from evil is <term>understanding</term>.* What is the reason for this? Because <term>understanding</term> <note>original: Binah</note> comes from the side of <term>Might</term> <note>original: Gevurah; the attribute of judgment and restraint</note>. From the side of <term>Might</term>, punishment and judgment are decreed upon the guilty. <term>Understanding</term> is <term>Repentance</term> <note>original: Teshuvah; literally 'returning' to the divine source</note>, and it encompasses both <term>Upper Repentance</term> and <term>Lower Repentance</term>, and from it emerge all the forces and ministers of the world. It is called <term>Understanding</term> <note>Binah</note> because it "understands" <note>original: mevinah</note> or distinguishes every single side. Therefore, *to depart from evil is <term>understanding</term>*, for whoever walks in this path—which is <term>understanding</term>—separates himself from evil.

Rabbi Eleazar opened his discourse and said: *The voice of the <term>Lord</term> is upon the waters; the God of glory thunders; the <term>Lord</term> is upon many waters.* <note>Psalm 29:3</note> The companions have already established the meaning of this verse. But come and see: *The voice of the <term>Lord</term> is upon the waters*—this refers to <term>Abraham</term>, who is <term>Loving-kindness</term> <note>original: Hesed</note>, which is called "water." *The God of glory thunders*—this refers to <term>Isaac</term>, who is called "God of glory" because he comes from the side of <term>Might</term> <note>Gevurah</note>; and this is the meaning of *the God of glory thunders*, for He is the "God who is great, mighty, and awesome." *The <term>Lord</term> is upon many waters*—this refers to <term>Jacob</term>, who is comprised of both <term>Loving-kindness</term> and <term>Might</term>, grasping both sides.

Come and see: three "voices" are mentioned here: *The voice of the Lord*, *the God of glory thunders*, and *the Lord is upon many waters*. These are a hint to the three <term>Patriarchs</term> <note>original: Avot</note> who constitute the <term>Holy Chariot</term> <note>original: Merkavah; the divine structure that carries the presence of God</note> on high. Because of this, the verse says *The voice of the Lord is upon the waters...* until it reaches seven "voices," corresponding to the seven levels <note>The seven lower Sefirot</note> that ascend upward <unclear>and eight</unclear>...

<summary>This passage explains the mystical link between Wisdom and Fear, and Understanding and Repentance. It identifies the Patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob with the divine attributes of Kindness, Might, and Beauty, forming the 'Holy Chariot.'</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

This is the mystery of the soul and its support. The first two letters are as one, the mystery of **Y-H**, and it is within, while the [other] **H-H** <note>Likely a scribal variation or reference to the external manifestations</note> is on the outside. ## Main Text (Zohar)

Rabbi Hezekiah opened his discourse and said: <note>Numbers 28:2</note> At the hour when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world—when it arose in His Will <note>Aramaic: *Re'uta*; the primordial desire or intent</note> to create the world—He was crowned with that Crown <term>Keter: the highest of the ten spiritual emanations (Sefirot), representing the Divine Will</term> which is called **Will** (*Ratzon*). And this Will is what is found within all those hidden treasures and ancient matters; it illuminates them all and is crowned by them.

-> **My Offering** <-

What is being said here? Rather, this is the "Time of Will" <note>Aramaic: *Et Ratzon*; a moment of divine favor</note> from which all treasures and subtle essences exist. What is it? It is the Supernal Crown called Will. And from this Will, all those springs emerge, flowing and streaming until they flow into <unclear>the Lesser Countenance</unclear> <note>original: *Ze'ir Anpin*; the emotive attributes of the Divine, often personified as the "Son" or the "Holy One, blessed be He" in relation to the feminine Presence</note>. When this Will rests upon Him, all things exist in joy and goodness. And at that time when this "Time of Will" rests and crowns the Lesser Countenance, the sacrifice is found to be as it should be, and because of this, it is said: **My offering, My bread for My fire-offerings.**

And what is **My offering** (*Korbani*)? It is that sacrifice <note>The word *Korban* (sacrifice) shares a root with *Karov* (to draw near)</note> which is brought close, and the Supernal Will rests upon it. Because of this, it is written: *Command the children of Israel and say to them: My offering, My bread...* and so on. And if you should ask: what is the difference between this offering of the Holy One, blessed be He, and other offerings? Rather, this one is hidden and concealed, unknown, and regarding this it is written: **My offering**. We give the sacrifice to the Holy One, blessed be He, and their yearning <note>Aramaic: *Te'avta*; the spiritual desire of the person bringing the offering</note> ascends on high, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is crowned by that sacrifice which rules over all. This is the "Bond of Faith" <note>Aramaic: *Kishura de-Meimanuta*</note>—all things bound in one connection.

Come and see: this sacrifice is what brings everything close and is the bond of all in one Will, without any separation at all. And Israel below, by drawing down this Will and through their prayer, must raise their yearning toward the Holy One, blessed be He. And the secret of the matter is that through the "Self-Sacrifice" <term>Mesirut Nefesh: literally 'giving over the soul,' referring to total devotion or martyrdom</term> by which they surrender their souls for the Sanctification of the Name, it is, as it were, the sacrifice of the Holy One, blessed be He, which ascends on high. The Supernal Will then rests upon it, and because of this, blessings rest upon all worlds. And the secret of this is: *Israel is holy to the Lord...* <note>Jeremiah 2:3</note> and so on. Come and see: whenever they surrender their souls, it is called a "Sacrifice to the Lord," as it were.

# Genesis - The Second Palace

Then the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"; the feminine aspect of the Divine</note> stands over them, because this is the secret of the Name in which all the letters are joined to one another. These three hosts surround that firmament from all its sides, and they are called the "Openers of the Firmament." These are the inscribed letters, and they learned the secret of the sign **Void** <note>original: "Chalal"; referring to the space or vacuum of the palace</note>. When these three letters join as one, then it is called the Holy Name. Each and every letter stands on one side and fills the 

void <margin>of the Palace</margin>. These are the holy hosts standing before that firmament, and all the pillars of that firmament stand upon them. This is because those pillars are on the outside, while these are on the inside, for the pillars rest upon the letters, and they support one another. Because all the letters are in a single union, when they join as one, then the Name is complete. Those hosts are found to be <term>Endurance</term> <note>original: "Netzach"; the seventh of the ten Sefirot or divine emanations, associated with victory and the right leg</note> and <term>Splendor</term> <note>original: "Hod"; the eighth Sefirah, associated with majesty and the left leg</note>, which are from the right side and the left side. They are all in a single union, and they are the secret of the Holy Name in which the letters are included. When they join as one, then it is found to be the secret of the Holy Name. Each one stands on one side and fills the void of the Palace. These are the holy hosts standing before that firmament, and all the pillars of that firmament stand upon them; for these are the pillars outside and these are inside, because these pillars support one another, and this is established because of that. He learned the secret of that firmament, which stands over them and surrounds it from all its sides.

## The Section of Pekudei

Three thousand <note>original: "tlat alpin"</note> of the Chariot <term>Chariot: The Merkabah, or the divine structure of the celestial realm</term> stand beneath three supreme lights that stand over them. <term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> <note>The son of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional author of the Zohar</note> said: Father, behold, we have learned that the key is in the hand of this one. The House of the Holy of Holies, of which it is said: "By wisdom a house is built" <note>Proverbs 24:3</note>, because this house is hidden and concealed.
