## Section on Genesis

Those which are without the name of "God" <note>original: Elohim</note>, as it is written: *Behold, the heaven and the heaven of heavens* <note>1 Kings 8:27</note> *cannot contain You.* And these were included within the generalization of a single verse, as it is written: *In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.* <note>Genesis 1:1</note> In this same manner, "God created the heaven" certainly serves to bring forth the "heaven of heavens." And these are called the **Mind** <note>term: Mocha; the inner spiritual essence or "brain" of a level of reality</note>, while "earth" is the **Shell** <note>term: Klipa; the outer covering or "husk" that protects or conceals the inner light</note>.

In this same manner, from within **Thought** <note>term: Machshava; the highest level of divine planning</note>, "and the heaven" <note>original: ve-et ha-shamayim</note> is meant to include the **Feminine** <note>term: Nukva; the receptive aspect of the divine emanations</note>, and this is what is called "The Heaven," in which the "heaven of heavens" is included. "And the earth" <note>original: ve-et ha-aretz</note> refers to the "Desirable Land" which stands upon the waters, which is the "Land of the Living."

And this [word] is called ***Et*** <note>note: The Hebrew word 'Et' is an untranslatable accusative particle spelled Aleph-Tav, the first and last letters of the alphabet</note>, for it includes all the letters within it. And this is "Earth." "And the heaven" is meant to include the letter **Vav** <note>note: The letter Vav (ו) often symbolizes the masculine connecting force or the six directions of space</note>, which is "Heaven," and this is certainly called so. "And the heaven" includes the Feminine, who is certainly "The Heaven," and this is the "heaven of heavens" that is included within it. "And the earth" includes the lower earth, which is called "earth" just like the Earth above.

And all of this is the **Secret of Thought**: *In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.* In this manner:
*   **In the beginning** <note>original: Bereishit</note> is Thought.
*   **Created God** <note>original: Bara Elohim</note> is Heaven.
*   **The heaven** <note>original: Et ha-Shamayim</note> is the Mind.
*   **And the earth** <note>original: Ve-et ha-Aretz</note> is the Shell.
*   **And the heaven** includes the Feminine.
*   **And the earth** includes the lower earth.

And this is the secret of **Perfect Faith** <note>term: Mehemanuta; the unified system of divine emanations</note> above and below, because Thought includes everything. And this is the secret called the **Living God**: the God above and the God below. And this is the secret of Thought: *In the beginning God created...*

**Rav Hamnuna the Elder** <note>note: A prominent sage often quoted in the Zohar for deep mystical traditions</note> said the following: *In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.* In this manner:
*   **In the beginning** is **Wisdom** <note>term: Chokhmah; the first flash of intuition</note>.
*   **Created God** is **Understanding** <note>term: Binah; the expansion of that flash into a conceptual structure</note>.
*   **The heaven** is the Mind.
*   **And the earth** is the Shell.
*   **And the heaven** includes the Feminine.
*   **And the earth** includes the lower earth.

And this is the secret of Perfect Faith above and below, because Thought includes everything, and this is the secret called the Living God.

<summary>This page provides a Kabbalistic decoding of the first verse of Genesis, mapping the words to the divine structure of Thought, Mind, and Shell. It emphasizes the unity of the "Living God" across the higher and lower realms of existence.</summary>
<keywords>Genesis, Thought, Mind, Shell, Rav Hamnuna the Elder, Wisdom, Understanding, Feminine, Heaven and Earth, Kabbalah</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the soul's transition from the physical world to the spiritual realm, specifically focusing on the final accounting of one's life and the preparation of the celestial garment.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **40** <-

At that time, when the soul is taken from the body, all the deeds that a person performed in this world are enumerated before them. They are proclaimed aloud, and the person confesses to them, as it is written <note>Job 37:7</note>: **"He seals the hand of every man, so that all men may know His work."** And regarding this, it is written <note>1 Samuel 25:6</note>: **"And thus shall you say to him that lives: 'Peace be to you, and peace be to your house, and peace be to all that you have.'"** What does this teach us? Rather, it is a hint to what we have established: that at the time the soul departs from this world, all the deeds a person performed are inscribed before them and enumerated before them, and they confess to them. What is the reason? Because the book is open, and in it is written: **"He seals the hand of every man, so that all men may know His work."** And from where do we know that they are enumerated before them and all those deeds are seen before them? As it is written: **"And all that you have is peace."** "All that you have"—these are the deeds a person performed in this world, for they all come before them and they confess to them; and all this occurs at the time the soul departs from the body.

After the soul departs, it goes to appear before the Master of the World to be beneath the <term>Throne of Glory</term> <note>original: "Koursaya de-Yakra"; the highest level of the created universe where souls originate and return</note> of the King. ## The Zohar on Exodus

Those worlds are the one hundred and twenty that the Holy One, Blessed be He, loves; they are hidden <note>original: "ganizin"</note> so that no one sees them except for Him alone <note>Cf. Zohar Shemot 12a</note>. He hides them away for the righteous in the World to Come. As it has been established, they are precious before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and these are called the "one hundred and twenty." These are what he [Moses] merited, and they are under the hand of Moses, for he was worthy of them. Whoever merits them merits to know <term>Wisdom</term> <note>Hebrew: Chokhmah; refers here to both divine inspiration and the specific Sephirah or "attribute" of Wisdom</note> at every moment and at every time.

We have learned: there are one hundred and twenty, and this is what is meant by the "one thousand and three hundred" that are under the hand of the Holy One, Blessed be He. And these one hundred and twenty belong to the Wisdom of the Torah, which is the <term>Upper Wisdom</term> <note>Chokhmah Ila'ah; the primordial divine intellect in Kabbalistic thought</note>.
<unclear>And all those worlds are all precious before the Holy One, Blessed be He.</unclear>
<unclear>And all those who labor in the Torah merit those worlds.</unclear>
And behold, we have been taught: who are the "wise of heart"? They are those who gaze into Wisdom. How fortunate is the portion of one who merits to know this Wisdom, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, reveals to them what He does not reveal to others. And concerning this it is written:
-> He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who have understanding <- <note>Daniel 2:21</note>
For they know the paths of the Torah, and whoever merits this Wisdom merits everything. Because of this, we have learned: whoever merits the Torah, merits all. Fortunate is the portion of the righteous in this world and in the World to Come, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to grant them this portion. And regarding this we have learned: there are one hundred and twenty that are hidden, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, never removes His eye from them.

## Portion of Vayera

And come and see: in all those times when the King Messiah shall come, many signs and wonders will be awakened in the world. And as the companions <note>The circle of scholars surrounding Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> have established, a single column of fire will be awakened in the world, standing from above to below for sixty days, and it will be visible to all the peoples of the earth. At that very time, the King Messiah will be awakened to go forth from within the Garden of Eden, from the place called the **Bird's Nest** <note>original: "Ken Tzippor" — a celestial chamber where the soul of the Messiah is said to dwell until the time of redemption</note>. And he shall be awakened in the land of Galilee <note>Zoharic tradition places the initial revelation of the Messiah in the Galilee region of northern Israel</note>. On the day that he goes forth there, the whole world will be shaken, and all the people of the world will hide within caves and the clefts of the rocks, for they will not think they can be saved. And concerning that time it is written:
> And they shall go into the holes of the rocks, and into the caves of the earth, for fear of the Lord, and for the glory of His majesty, etc. <note>Isaiah 2:19</note>
"For fear of the Lord" refers to the shaking of the entire world; "and for the glory of His majesty" refers to the Messiah. And when he is awakened and revealed in all the Land of Israel, many nations, mighty and great, will gather against him, and they will stir up wars against him throughout the entire world. At that time, the seventy celestial ministers <note>The spiritual patrons appointed over the seventy primordial nations of the world</note> who are appointed over the seventy nations will be awakened to stir up war in every corner of the world, and they will be awakened to wage war against Jerusalem. And concerning this it is written:
> Woe to the multitude of many people... and to the rushing of nations... <note>Isaiah 17:12</note>
And all of them will gather against Israel and against the Messiah. Then the Holy One, blessed be He, will be awakened to redeem Israel. At that time, the seventy ministers who are over the seventy nations will be awakened, and the Holy One, blessed be He, will be awakened against them, and concerning this it is written:
> And I will turn you about... <note>Likely referencing the war of Gog and Magog in Ezekiel 38-39</note> and for the glory of His majesty, etc. And come and see...

## Main Text (The Zohar)

Blessed is the portion of the righteous, for they know the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Berikh Hu," the standard rabbinic name for God</note>, to walk in them in the path of truth. For when the students of the school of Rav Hamnuna the Elder <note>A prominent Babylonian sage often appearing in the Zohar as a source of hidden wisdom</note> were traveling on the road, they encountered a certain elder who was carrying <unclear>behind him</unclear> Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Abba. Rabbi Abba raised his voice and burst into weeping, saying: "Blessed is our portion, for we have merited to see the face of the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah," the feminine, indwelling aspect of God</note> on this journey. The path we have walked until now was a path of death; now it is a path of life! And because of this word of Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, sent it to us to grant us merit in the life of the World to Come. And we have merited this elder of ours, whom we have merited now."

---

->**And concerning**<-
this, we have learned: in every place where the righteous travel with words of Torah between them, the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Divine Presence are found with them. And all the members of the Holy Chariot <note>The celestial assembly of angels and divine forces described in Ezekiel's vision</note> travel before them and travel with them. Then the Divine Presence envelops them with her wings from this side and from that side. And concerning this it is written:
> And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead them on the way (Exodus 13:21).
This is as it is written:
> And it came to pass, when the ark set forward, that Moses said: "Rise up, O Lord" (Numbers 10:35).
Who is the "Ark"? This is the Divine Presence, who is the Ark of the Covenant. And because of this, she goes before the righteous who travel on the road with words of Torah between them.

And if you should say, "Behold, that was specifically in the time of the wilderness and among the people of Israel," come and see: in every time and in every place where the righteous travel and exert themselves in the Torah, the Divine Presence goes before them. And concerning this it is written:
> Righteousness <note>original: "Tzedek"</note> shall go before him, and shall make his footsteps a way (Psalms 85:14).
"Righteousness"—this is the Divine Presence. "Shall go before him"—it shall go toward him to <unclear>pave</unclear> the way for him. And if you should say, "From where do we know that the Divine Presence is called 'Righteousness'?" It is because it is written:
> Righteousness, righteousness shall you pursue (Deuteronomy 16:20).
And it is written:
> As for me, I shall behold Your face in righteousness (Psalms 17:15).

<summary>This passage describes the mystical protection afforded to scholars who study Torah while traveling, identifying the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) with the biblical Ark and the concept of "Righteousness" (Tzedek).</summary>

...so that the Holy Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, would be complete on all sides. This is the secret found in every place. When the Tabernacle was prepared and Moses erected it, then:

->**And He Called**<-

<note>Leviticus 1:1</note>
> **And He called to Moses, and the Lord spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying.**

<term>Rabbi Eleazar</term> <note>The son of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> opened his discourse and said: <note>Job 28:12</note> **"But where shall Wisdom be found? And where is the place of Understanding?"** The companions have already established the meaning of this verse. However, "Wisdom shall be found from *Ayin* <note>literally 'Nothingness'</note>," it is certainly found from *Ayin*. This is the place that is not found, not known, and not revealed; therefore, it is called <term>Ayin</term> <note>The highest, most unknowable spark of divinity from which all thought begins</note>. Come and see: Higher Wisdom is a secret that is both found and not found; it is the secret of all secrets that is not known at all, and it is the place from which light goes out to every side. And when the light goes out and shines, it is then called <term>Binah</term> <note>Understanding; the womb-like divine quality that gives shape to the flash of Wisdom</note>. And Understanding is a secret that is found and revealed more than Wisdom.

---

->**And He Called**<-

**And He called to Moses.** <term>Rabbi Shimon</term> <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the central figure of the Zohar</note> opened and said: <note>Isaiah 46:3</note> **"Listen to Me, O house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, who have been borne by Me from the belly, who have been carried from the womb."** Come and see how great the love of Israel is before the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, for even though they are in exile and in poverty, the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, personified as a feminine indwelling light</note> has not departed from them. Regarding this, it is written: "borne from the belly." What is this "belly"? This is the Higher Mother <note>The Sefirah of Binah</note>, who is the "belly" of all worlds.

And so, when the Shekhinah is in exile, the Holy One, Blessed be He, watches over her and says, "And He called to Moses." And He called to him from the midst of the cloud, so that the sacrificial service might begin. Regarding this, it is written: "And He called to Moses, and the Lord spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting," which is the <term>Shekhinah</term>. And because Moses was outside, He called to him to enter within her.

<summary>This page introduces the Book of Leviticus by exploring the mystical origins of Wisdom and Understanding, and emphasizes God's enduring connection to Israel through the Shekhinah even during times of exile.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the spiritual anatomy of man, specifically focusing on the relationship between the earthly body, the celestial image (Diyukna), and the soul's origin. It transitions from general principles of faith to the specific consequences of sin as a "blemish" that manifests both above and below.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The unity of all is the essence of faith. The **image** of the body is made in the likeness of this world, while the soul is a <term>portion from above</term> <note>Aramaic: *chulka de-le'eila*; referring to the divine spark originating from the higher realms</note>. For this reason, when a <term>righteous man</term> <note>Aramaic: *zaka'ah*; one who is meritorious or pure</note> is seen in this world, and during the time he exerts himself in the Torah and performs the commandments of the Torah, the soul remains within the body. Because of this, when the soul departs from this world, that <term>image</term> <note>Aramaic: *diyukna*; the spiritual archetype or celestial form of a person</note> is hidden away. As it has been said, it is concealed and hidden in the earth; this is the punishment of the body, which is a portion of this world. Therefore, it is hidden in the earth—a portion returning to its portion—while the soul, which is a portion from above, ascends to the place from which it was hewn. This is as it is written:
> And the spirit shall return unto God who gave it. <note>Ecclesiastes 12:7</note>
And because of this, when a righteous man appears before the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>Aramaic: *Kudsha Brich Hu*; the standard rabbinic title for God</note>, the Holy One, Blessed be He, rejoices in him. At the time he is righteous, his image is before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and as long as he is righteous, the Holy One, Blessed be He, rejoices in him and his image is before the Holy One, Blessed be He. <unclear>When he was righteous</unclear>, He rejoiced in him and his image was above. 

But when he blemishes the Torah and blemishes himself, he creates a blemish above. His celestial image is changed, and he makes his portion above blemished. Accusations <note>literally "upright ones" or "prosecutors"</note> emerge from him above, and the <term>side of impurity</term> <note>Aramaic: *sitra de-mas'ava*; the "Other Side" or the realm of spiritual uncleanness</note> gains dominion over him. His celestial image, which belongs to the All, is made blemished. Furthermore, when that blemish which he committed above is enacted upon himself, a punishment is decreed upon his body, and a blemish appears on his body externally. As it has been said:
> When the plague of leprosy is in a man. <note>Leviticus 13:9</note>
And the blemish of the Torah is seen, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not rejoice in him, for his celestial image is blemished. Because of this, we have learned regarding prophecy above, that when a prophet appears, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is revealed to him in His image and in the image of that prophet when he is righteous. And regarding this it says:
> And when the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle... but if the cloud were not taken up. <note>Exodus 40:36-37; the text implies the cloud's movement reflects the state of righteousness</note>
For he is righteous. But when a blemish appears above, his image and the celestial image are changed. When we see that he is blemished, it is said that he is blemished and his celestial image is blemished; for he is blemished and his portion above is blemished. And all those who receive from him are all made blemished <unclear>because it was changed</unclear>... Therefore we have learned that all those who receive from that prophet when he is blemished <unclear>are changed</unclear>...

<summary>This passage explains that a person's spiritual image (Diyukna) reflects their moral state; righteousness brings divine joy and preserves the image, while sin creates a "blemish" that manifests physically as leprosy and disrupts prophetic reception.</summary>
<keywords>Diyukna, Soul, Righteousness, Blemish, Leprosy, Prophecy, Holy One Blessed be He, Torah</keywords>

## Genesis

And behold, from all the diligence of the children of faith, when they come toward the Sun <note>The "Sun" here refers to the central divine light or the sefirah of Tiferet</note> and are joined with it, to take upon themselves the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven and to know that this matter is the service of the heart, which is the essence above all. The will of the heart depends upon this, for it is the essence above all. And if you say these words are the service—behold, the service of the heart is the essence of all, to cleave therein to the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> in every single word that a person must cleave to Him with his will.

**When he went out**

Rabbi Isaac and Rabbi Judah were sitting one day and they rose to rejoice in the joy of the Torah. Rabbi Judah said: Behold, we have learned that when the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world, He made it entirely according to the pattern of that which is above. Everything that is above has its likeness below on the earth, and everything that is below on the earth has its likeness above. Because of this, they are all bound together as one. All the <term>chariots</term> <note>Hebrew: "Merkavot"; celestial formations or angelic assemblies that carry the Divine Presence</note> of above have their likeness below on the earth. And because of this, it is written:
> Truth shall spring out of the earth; and righteousness shall look down from heaven. <note>Psalms 85:11</note>
And they have already established this matter: those chariots of above spread out upon the earth, and that which is above is the pattern for below. There are myriads [of angels], and there are <term>husks</term> <note>Aramaic: "Kliphoth"; the outer shells of existence that conceal the divine spark, often associated with the forces of impurity</note> below. Everything that is above is a pattern for below, and so it is with those from the side of above; so they are below on <term>the Left Side</term> <note>Aramaic: "Sitra de-Smala"; the side of Judgment (Gevurah) or the realm of spiritual impurity</note>, and everything is a pattern of what is above. This is the <term>mystery</term> <note>Aramaic: "Raza"</note>: everything that is on the earth stands as a pattern for what is above, and they all join together as one. In this manner, there are nine firmaments, one on top of the other like the layers of an onion, and so too there are seven lands, one on top of the other, and every single land has in it the pattern of what is above...

<summary>This page explores the Zoharic concept of "As Above, So Below," explaining how human intention in prayer connects the physical world to the divine hierarchy. It describes the universe as a series of interconnected layers, where even the "Left Side" or impure forces mirror celestial structures.</summary>
<keywords>intention of the heart, divine service, chariots, husks, Left Side, macrocosm and microcosm, nine firmaments, seven lands</keywords>

<meta>This page contains the opening discourses for the Torah portions of Vayikra (Leviticus) and Tzav from the Sefer ha-Zohar, the foundational work of Jewish mysticism. The text transitions from the call of Moses to the internal struggle between the human inclinations.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

**And the Lord called to Moses, and spoke to him out of the tent of meeting, saying.** <note>Leviticus 1:1</note>
Rabbi Eleazar opened his discourse and said: <note>Psalm 103:20</note> **Bless the Lord, you His angels, you mighty in strength, who do His bidding, obeying the voice of His word.**
Come and see how much a person must guard themselves from their sins and strive in the path of truth! For all the deeds of a person are written in a book before the Holy King. And all those who keep the commandments of the Torah <term>Torah: the Five Books of Moses and the broader body of Jewish law and wisdom</term> and labor in the Torah are all inscribed above in the light of the Holy One, blessed be He. Many hosts and camps of angels gaze upon such a person, and they are called the "Ministering Angels" of the Holy One, blessed be He. Regarding them it is written: "Bless the Lord, you His angels, you mighty in strength." And who are these "mighty in strength"? They are those who overpower their [evil] inclination and stand firm in the Torah, which is referred to as "doing His bidding." And who are they? They are those who perform the commandments of the Torah. And the end of the verse says: "obeying the voice of His word."

---
->**Tzav / And He Went**<-
---

Rabbi Eleazar opened his discourse and said: <note>Psalm 103:14</note> **For He knows our inclination; He remembers that we are dust.** How much must a person guard themselves from their sins! For the Evil Inclination <term>Yetzer Hara: the innate human drive toward physical gratification or selfishness</term> stands over a person every day to accuse them and to turn them away from the path of truth. Come and see: on the day a person enters the world, the Evil Inclination comes with them, and it is their constant accuser. But the Good Inclination <term>Yetzer Tov: the moral or divine conscience</term> does not come to a person until they begin to be purified. And from when? From thirteen years of age and onward. Because at this point, a person is partnered with both this one and that one—this one on the right and that one on the left. This is the Good Inclination and that is the Evil Inclination; this is a holy angel and that is a defiled angel. If a person is worthy and labors in the Torah, the Good Inclination prevails over the Evil Inclination, and the Evil is subdued before it, and the person is purified. But if they are not worthy, the Evil Inclination prevails over the Good Inclination and turns them from the path of truth, and they become defiled. Come and see: the Evil Inclination stays with a person constantly. Therefore, a person must guard themselves from it every day so that it does not turn them from the path of truth and they do not sin before the Holy One, blessed be He.

<summary>This page explores the mystical significance of the "mighty" who keep the commandments and describes the psychological and spiritual battle between the Good and Evil Inclinations that begins in adolescence.</summary>

For at the time when Israel was exiled among the nations, they were far—"the distance between you and Him." And because of this, even though the Shekhinah is with them always, and behold it is before me: "And it came to pass when he sent," thus shall you say to the women and children... and he included his ways for him, and his hand was merit, he struck it and said: "Fortunate is my portion that the **Holy One, Blessed Be He** <term>K.B.H.: Kudsha Brich Hu, the standard Hebrew/Aramaic title for God</term> is over me," and he merited to know.

## Main Text (The Zohar)

[---] was sitting before the house of Rabbi Simeon the Pious. 
He said to him: "What truly is the difference between Joseph and his other brothers?"
**Rabbi Eleazar opened** his discourse and said:
> **"A woman of valor, who can find? Her worth is far beyond pearls."** <note>Proverbs 31:10</note>

**"A woman of valor"**—this refers to the Community of Israel <note>The *Shekhinah*, the feminine aspect of the Divine</note>. **"Who can find?"**—this is as it is said: "But where can wisdom be found?" <note>Job 28:12</note>. **"Her worth is far beyond pearls"**—this is certainly she, as it is written: "She is more precious than pearls" <note>Proverbs 3:15</note>. **"And spoil shall not be lacking"**—this refers to Joseph the Righteous, for he is the "spoil" <note>original: *shalal*; here interpreted as the bounty or flow of blessing</note> from whom all blessings go forth; he fills her constantly, and she shall never lack for all eternity. **"The heart of her husband trusts in her"**—this is the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>The masculine aspect of the Divine, *Tiferet*</note>.

**Rabbi Simeon said:** "She does him good and not evil all the days of her life." "She does him good"—this is the light that shines upon her constantly and never ceases. How do we know that Joseph is called **"Good"**? Because it is written: "And she saw him, that he was good" <note>Exodus 2:2. While originally referring to the infant Moses, the Zohar applies this quality of 'Goodness' to Joseph as the archetype of the Righteous</note>. And why is he called "Good"? Because he guarded the covenant <note>term: *Brit* — referring here to Joseph’s sexual purity and his connection to the Sefirah of *Yesod*</note> as is fitting. Anyone who guards the covenant is called "Good." And we have learned: "Say of the righteous that he is good" <note>Isaiah 3:10</note>. And it is written: "And she saw him, that he was good." Because of this, the "woman of valor" does him good and not evil, for she allows no stranger to enter her. Joseph guarded the covenant so that no stranger entered it, and therefore "spoil shall not be lacking," for he takes everything and waters the blessing.

> **"She seeks wool and flax, and works with willing hands."** <note>Proverbs 31:13</note>

"She seeks wool and flax"—these are the levels <unclear>that are distinguished</unclear> [---]

## Main Text (The Zohar)

And we saw that before he spoke these words, that entire generation wept; they thought that these matters would not be revealed through the words of those righteous ones above. And even though these things are now seen in writing, they are revealed more now than they were before, when permission was first given to write them. Rabbi Shimon said: "Fortunate is the portion of one who is awakened by his words. For whoever is worthy to hear his words now in this world will not go to judgment in the world to come. Fortunate is the generation that I am within." Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse and said:

> Moses would speak, and God <note>original: Elohim</note> would answer him with a voice. <note>Exodus 19:19</note>

What is the meaning of "Moses would speak"? It means that at the hour when the Holy One, blessed be He <note>term: *Kudsha Brich Hu* — the standard Aramaic name for God in the Zohar</note>, desired to give the Torah to Israel, Moses went and invited them and prepared himself with them. And then he opened and said:

> Hear, O My people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against you; I am God, your God. <note>Psalms 50:7</note>

Because for a faithful prophet such as Moses, it was necessary to warn them further. Come and see what is written: "Hear, O My people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against you." This was at the hour when the Holy One, blessed be He, gave the command.

---

-> **Rabbi Elazar opened and said:** <-

> Who is this that comes up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all the powders of the merchant? <note>Song of Songs 3:6</note>

Come and see: when Israel traveled in the wilderness, the Cloud of Glory <note>term: *Anana de-Yikra* — the divine protective presence that guided the Israelites</note> went before them and they were crowned by it. And because all the heavenly hosts traveled with it, they [the nations or the angels] said, "Who is this that comes up from the wilderness?" And it is written, "like pillars of smoke," because that cloud rose up before the Tabernacle like smoke that is refined and purified from all filth. And for this reason, it rose like smoke. And why like smoke? Because the fire of the Altar rose within it. "Perfumed with myrrh and frankincense"—this refers to Abraham and Isaac <note>note: The patriarchs represent the divine attributes of Mercy and Severity/Judgment which "scent" the divine presence</note>. "With all the powders of the merchant"—this refers to Jacob, who is included from all sides, for he is the "Supernal Merchant" in whom all the spices are contained. Come and see: when the people entered the Holy Temple and the sacrifice was offered, then that smoke would rise like a pillar of cloud, and the scent within it would rise until it reached its place, then...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the spiritual preparation for the Sabbath, focusing on the internal state of the believer and the transition from the weekday to the holy day.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

Rabbi Isaac said: What is the meaning of that which is written:
> He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds? <note>Psalm 147:3</note>

Rather, these are those who occupy themselves with the Torah and perform the will of their Master, and who purify their souls and their bodies for the Holy One, Blessed be He. Certainly, these are the **brokenhearted**, and they are the supreme pious ones, the saints of the Most High, who possess an abundance of humility. They are the "brokenhearted" because they are not arrogant in the upper worlds or the lower worlds. And regarding this it is written:
> The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise. <note>Psalm 51:19</note>

And regarding this, Rabbi Isaac said: Do not read it as "brokenhearted" <note>Hebrew: *Shevirei Lev*</note> but rather as **strong-hearted** <note>Hebrew: *Sharirei Lev*; a wordplay suggesting that spiritual "brokenness" or humility is actually the ultimate inner strength</note>. What is the meaning of "strong-hearted"? It refers to those who are powerful in the service of their Master and strong in the holy soul; that is the "strong-hearted." But those who are "brokenhearted" <note>in the negative sense</note> are those who are stubborn and do not gaze upon the holy soul, but only upon the matters of this world, because their Master is found with them forever <note>meaning God dwells even with the lowly</note>. And who is he who does not have a heart strengthened for his Master? What is the meaning of "their wounds" <note>literally "their sorrows"</note>? It is as we have said.

---

**Rav Hamnuna the Elder**, when he would arrive at the threshold of the Eve of the Sabbath, would sit and rejoice, saying: "Rise and join with me, for we are invited to behold the desire of the Holy One, Blessed be He, who has sent to us the **Additional Soul** <term>Neshamah Yeterah: a mystical 'extra soul' believed to inhabit the believer during the Sabbath to allow for deeper spiritual perception</term>." And for one who carries heavy sorrow, the Additional Soul is a different matter entirely, because this Additional Soul is the gateway to the Garden of <unclear>Eden</unclear>...

Blessed are You, O Lord <unclear>our God, King of the Universe</unclear>...
And this one, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to dwell with him... as it is fulfilled through him as it is written:
> Commit your way to the Lord; trust in Him, and He will act. <note>Psalm 37:5</note>

And He is destined to provide for <unclear>him</unclear> <term>at that time</term> so that he will not need any other person, but only the Holy One, Blessed be He. And when a man enters the <unclear>gateway</unclear> of the Sabbath, he should invite it with joy, with diligence, and with perfection.

<summary>This page explores the mystical definition of the 'brokenhearted' as those who possess spiritual humility and strength, and describes Rav Hamnuna the Elder's joyful preparation to receive the 'Additional Soul' on Sabbath Eve.</summary>

<meta>This page transitions from the conclusion of the laws regarding the leper (Parashat Metzora) into the mystical secrets of the burnt offering at the beginning of Parashat Tzav. The text follows the Zohar’s homiletic style, moving from the physical affliction of leprosy to the spiritual elevation of the soul and the Divine Presence.</meta>

# Metzora / Tzav

## Main Text (Zohar)

> **"This is the law for every swelling of leprosy, and for a scall, and for the leprosy of a garment, and for a house. And for a rising, and for a scab, and for a bright spot. To teach when it is unclean, and when it is clean; this is the law of leprosy."** <note>Leviticus 14:54-57</note>

**Rabbi Pinchas opened** his discourse and said: **"But the Lord is in His holy palace; let all the earth keep silence before Him"** <note>Habakkuk 2:20</note>. Does it truly mean "all the earth"? Rather, it refers to one who gazes upon the Palace <term>Heikhala; the Divine chamber or dwelling</term> which contains the supernal forms. Regarding this it is written, "But the Lord is in His holy palace." We have established that the supernal Palace contains seventy-two shades of light that shine. One who merits to see it enters those palaces and says, "But the Lord is in His holy palace." Blessed is the portion of the righteous who are not governed by the Other Side <term>Sitra Achra; the realm of evil or impurity</term>. And why is it called "the law of the leper"? Because we have established that this is certainly the law of the leper: for whoever has these afflictions within him is pushed outside of the Palace. For this reason, "the Lord is in His holy palace" <note>implying the King remains inside while the impure are excluded</note>. And when that affliction is removed, then it is written: **"And the Lord shall be King over all the earth; in that day shall the Lord be one, and His name one"** <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>. All of these [afflictions] stand on the Left Side. But there is a supernal side which is the Side of Purity <term>Sitra de-Dachio</term>, which is the mystery of the Left <note>The "Holy Left" associated with the attribute of Gevurah/Judgment</note>. Concerning this it is written: **"This is the law of the burnt offering: it is the burnt offering because of the burning upon the altar all night..."** <note>Leviticus 6:2</note>. This is because its time is during the night, when that supernal side holds sway. Blessed is the portion of the righteous forever and for all eternity.

---
-> **Tzav (Command)** <-
---

**Rabbi Chiya opened** his discourse: **"Command Aaron and his sons, saying..."** <note>Leviticus 6:2</note>. **Command** <note>Hebrew: *Tzav*</note>. This is the secret of idolatry <note>The Zohar links the word "Command" to the prohibition of foreign worship, following the Talmudic tradition in Sanhedrin 56b</note>. **"Eth" Aaron** <note>The word "Eth" is an untranslatable accusative marker often interpreted as an inclusion</note>—this is the secret of the Woman of Valor <term>Eshet Chayil; a reference to the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</term>, as you say: **"You have affirmed [He-emarta] the Lord this day"** <note>Deuteronomy 26:17</note>. **"And his sons"**—this is the secret of the righteous. **"Saying"**—this is the secret of the sum of all things. And because of this, it is called **"This is the law of the burnt offering"** <note>Hebrew: *Olah*, meaning "that which ascends"</note>. We have established this secret: that the offering ascends of its own accord, as you say: **"And a chariot came up [Ta'al] and went out of Egypt"** <note>I Kings 10:29</note>.

**Rabbi Yose opened** his discourse: **"Command Aaron..."** This is a warning to all those who are occupied <unclear>in the service</unclear>...

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Tabernacle furnishings, specifically focusing on the Menorah as a symbolic map of the divine realms and the unity of the Creator.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

There are those who are crowned with light, and light surrounds them; it is both without and within, that which has been hidden from the beginning. <note>Zohar II, 148b</note>
And the pillars support the heart within the Menorah <note>The seven-branched candelabrum of the Tabernacle</note>, and the sources of radiance from this "constellation" <note>original: *mazal*; here referring to a divine flow or influence</note> are this hidden light. This light is the limb that extends to the eight leaves, which are the letters H, V, R <note>original: ה' ו' ר'</note>, which are the secret of the flames.
They shine within the lamp of the **central shaft** <term>central shaft: the middle branch of the Menorah, representing the balance and source of the other six branches</term>, which is the secret of all the lamps.
And all those lamps were lit from within that central shaft; and this is how it was: all those lamps were lit from within that central shaft, and all seven would ascend and sparkle from within that central shaft. And this is the secret of our **Tabernacle** <term>Tabernacle: the portable sanctuary in the desert; in Hebrew, *Mishkan*</term> of the center. For there were seven branches in the Menorah, and the secret of the central shaft is the secret of the Tabernacle. It is the secret of the radiance that stands over all those branches. And those seven branches are the secret of the **seven clouds of glory** <note>The miraculous clouds that protected the Israelites in the wilderness</note> that went before Israel. And at the time when they shine into one another, then the Holy One, blessed be He, clings to His people Israel, as it is written:

> "And I will set my Tabernacle among you: and my soul shall not abhor you." <note>Leviticus 26:11</note>

And then they all would shine with a single radiance, and they were all within the secret of "One."
And concerning this, it was said:

> "And the Tabernacle shall be one." <note>Exodus 26:6</note>

And this is the secret: He shines in all those lamps, and they shine in Him with the supernal radiance of all lamps. And this is the **secret of faith** <term>secret of faith: the mystical realization that all diverse forces in the universe are actually a single, unified divine reality</term>, for everything together is within a single secret. All those lamps shine from within that supernal lamp that illuminates them all. And when they all shine as one, then it is the secret of "One," for all is one.
And this is the secret of the Perfect Name, which is the supernal Name that illuminates all, and they shine in Him. And all of this is the secret of the **Menorah** and the Tabernacle, for all is one within the secret of faith.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Exodus, specifically focusing on the Revelation at Mount Sinai. The text transitions from the physical description of the mountain to the metaphysical nature of the sounds heard by the Israelites.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

... "And the voice of the shofar grew louder and louder" <note>Exodus 19:19</note>.
"And all the people saw the voices, and the torches, and the voice of the shofar, and the mountain smoking; and when the people saw it, they trembled and stood far off" <note>Exodus 20:15</note>. The companions have already established the meaning of this verse. But come and see: at the hour that the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: Kudsha Berikh Hu; the standard Rabbinic name for God</note> revealed Himself upon Mount Sinai, all of Israel were seeing and hearing that "voice of the shofar."

And what is this "voice of the shofar"? This is the voice that emerges from within the shofar. And this shofar is the "Higher Shofar," the "Great Shofar." That voice is called "voice of shofar" <note>original: kol shofar</note> and not "the voice of the shofar" <note>original: kol ha-shofar; noting the absence of the definite article 'the' in certain mystical contexts</note>. What is the reason? Because this shofar is not like other shofars <note>the ram's horn used in ritual</note>. This shofar is the <term>mystery</term> <note>original: raza</note> of the <term>World to Come</term> <note>original: Alma de-Ate; in Kabbalah, this refers to the divine realm of Binah or 'Understanding,' the source of cosmic liberation</note>. And regarding this it is written:
> (Isaiah 27:13) "And it shall come to pass on that day, that a great shofar shall be blown."

Because this shofar is the Great Shofar, and it is the shofar that pours out all blessings, all joys, and all lights to the worlds. And when this Higher Shofar desires to shine and to bring forth lights from within itself, it then crowns itself with a single voice, which is the voice that emerges from it. And this is called the "voice of the shofar." Come and see: when the Torah was given to Israel, that voice was heard from within the shofar. And regarding this it is written, "and the voice of the shofar." This is the voice that includes fire, water, and wind <note>or spirit</note>, all as one. And this is the voice that was heard upon Mount Sinai. And this voice is the "voice of the shofar." Because this voice was heard throughout the whole world, and it was "going and strengthening greatly" <note>growing louder and louder</note>. What is the meaning of "going and strengthening"? Rather, "going" refers to the <term>mystery</term> of the higher level, and "strengthening" refers to the power of Judgment...

<summary>This passage provides a mystical interpretation of the Shofar heard at Sinai, identifying it not as a physical instrument but as a divine emanation from the "World to Come" (the Sefirah of Binah) that unites the elements of fire, water, and spirit.</summary>
<keywords>Shofar, Mount Sinai, Revelation, World to Come, Binah, Divine Voice, Mysticism, Elements</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar)

It is well written: **Pinchas, the son of Eleazar** etc. <note>Numbers 25:11</note> for the entirety of the Torah returns to the merit of Pinchas, which he performed before the Holy One, blessed be He. Because he released the Foundation <note>original: "Yesod" — the ninth Sefirah, representing the divine channel of procreation and connection</note> and rose up in awakening, for this reason, he is the measure of all other days of the world. And it is not that there were others who should have been given this; it is difficult to grasp that he awakened a supreme merit from the Holy of Holies, and they merited to give him a supreme gift. And all the merit of the world was said to be given to him, which he received from that which was prepared for here. Furthermore, all the righteous ones <note>original: "Tzaddikaya"</note> who were in every single generation, and all those five <note>likely referring to the five levels of the soul or five dimensions of the Sefirot</note> of the Holy One, blessed be He—ultimately He gives him an extra portion. He was chosen, and the joy of the Holy One, blessed be He, was great in him because he performed a holy act among the priests, which is considered the spreading of peace. And He gave him peace, just as you say: **Pinchas [is] Peace** etc. <note>Numbers 25:12; the text refers to the "Covenant of Peace"</note>, the place where the merits of all the souls that were made and stood in the preparation of peace are increased. And this "Peace" is the **Foundation** <term>Yesod: the divine attribute of connection and truth</term> of above, and this is the **Righteous One** <term>Tzaddik: the human or divine figure who maintains the world through holiness</term> of Heaven. And in every place it is so; he prepared for this an extra merit. The merit and all the service that they performed as individuals, and the merit of all Israel as well, was for the completion of the measure of every day of every generation. And all merits are toward Pinchas, and each and every one of their merits is above, and that merit of theirs is holy. And all of Israel shall have peace and children, and all of them are in peace. He is in these paths according to the secret that every generation has within it peace and the perfection of every day. And this place of Pinchas was prepared, as we have said, by the power of the Holy One, blessed be He, as we have said ---

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Ki Tissa (Exodus 30:11–34:35), specifically focusing on the moment Moses receives the Tablets of the Covenant. ## Ki Tissa

...And because of this, the word **when He finished** <note>original: "Kekhalloto" (Exodus 31:18). The Zohar plays on the similarity between "finished" and "Kallah," meaning Bride.</note> is written, for she is the Bride who is comprised of everything. And then: **"And He gave to Moses... the two tablets of the Testimony, tablets of stone, written with the finger of God."** What is the meaning of **two tablets**? Rather, this refers to the Written Torah and the Oral Torah <note>The Written Torah refers to the Five Books of Moses; the Oral Torah refers to the traditions and interpretations later recorded in the Talmud and Midrash.</note>, and they are all one. And because of this, they are **tablets of stone**, because this is the place of "harsh judgment" that emerges from that precious stone of which it is written:
-> **"From there is the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel"** (Genesis 49:24) <-

**Written with the finger of God.** What is the **finger of God**? This is the finger that points to everything, as it is written:
-> **"It is the finger of God"** (Exodus 8:15) <-
And because it is a "finger," the name **God** <note>original: "Elohim," the Divine name associated with Justice/Judgment.</note> is written and not the Tetragrammaton <note>The four-letter name of God (YHWH) associated with Mercy.</note>, for this is the place of judgment, and judgment issues forth from it.

---

And when these tablets were in the hand of Moses, as it is written:
-> **"And the tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved upon the tablets"** (Exodus 32:16) <-
Do not read the word as **engraved** <note>original: "Charut"</note> but rather as **freedom** <note>original: "Cherut." This is a famous wordplay in Jewish mysticism suggesting that true freedom is only found through the law.</note>: freedom from the Angel of Death, and freedom from the subjugation of earthly kingdoms, because within the Torah, freedom from everything is found. And then, there was joy in all things, and Moses had more joy than all of them. But once Israel sinned <note>Referring to the sin of the Golden Calf.</note> and that glory of the crown with which they were crowned at Sinai was removed from them, then it is written:
-> **"And Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, and behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come near to him"** (Exodus 34:30) <-
And because of this, they were broken...

<margin>to come near</margin> <note>Catchword at bottom center, repeating the first word of the next page.</note>

<summary>This passage from the Zohar explains that the two Tablets of the Covenant represent the unity of the Written and Oral Torah and explores the mystical "freedom" from death and oppression granted at Sinai, which was lost after the sin of the Golden Calf.</summary>

## Behaalotcha

This and that are included within a single river, one within the other and the other within the one, all at once. And the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: "Kadosh Baruch Hu," the standard rabbinic title for God</note>, is destined to redeem the people of Israel from the midst of exile. At that time, it is written: *And the Lord shall be King over all the earth...* <note>Zechariah 14:9</note> At this hour, the Holy King and the Assembly of Israel <note>The "Shekhinah" or Divine Presence, viewed as the feminine communal soul of Israel</note> shall be united as one. The Evil Inclination <note>term: Yetzer Hara — the innate human impulse toward selfishness or sin</note> shall be nullified and removed from the world, for it is written: *And I will cause the spirit of impurity to pass out of the land.* <note>Zechariah 13:2</note>

Corresponding to this, the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to slaughter that Serpent <note>The primordial snake from Eden, representing the source of death and evil</note> who opened the way and caused death for all the inhabitants of the world. He will break it and remove it from the world. Regarding this it is written: *He will swallow up death forever; and the Lord God will wipe away tears from off all faces...* <note>Isaiah 25:8</note> and it is written: *And the Lord shall be King over all the earth; in that day shall the Lord be one, and His name one.*

***

->**"And it came to pass, when the ark set forward, that Moses said..."**<- <note>Numbers 10:35</note>

Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse and said: Happy are the righteous who know how to walk in the paths of the Torah <note>The "Law" or divine teachings</note> and to labor in it before the Holy King. Come and see: at the hour when the Ark was moving, it moved and traveled, and Moses would say: *Rise up, O Lord, and let Your enemies be scattered...* Now, who are these "enemies" of the Holy One, blessed be He? They are those who go to prosecute and accuse Israel; they are truly the enemies of the Holy One, blessed be He.

Because of this, he would say, "Rise up, O Lord." What is this "rising"? It is a rising that is characterized by joy, and this is the secret of the matter. At the time the Ark moved, the Divine Presence <note>term: Shekhinah — the immanent, indwelling presence of God</note> moved with it, and She is the Bride. Therefore he said, "Rise up, O Lord."

And when it rested, he said: *And when it rested, he said: Return, O Lord, unto the ten thousand thousands of Israel.* <note>Numbers 10:36</note> What is the meaning of "Return, O Lord"? It refers to the "Return" which is the rest on this side. Therefore, at the hour the Ark moved, the Divine Presence moved with it, along with all those myriads and tens of thousands of holy angels. Moses would say: *Rise up, O Lord, and let Your enemies be scattered.* In every place where the Divine Presence dwells among them, Israel does not fear any side of the world. It is written: *The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?* <note>Psalms 27:1</note>

Rabbi Isaac said: At the hour that the Ark moved, Israel knew that the Divine Presence was with them, going before them. Because of this, Moses would say: *Rise up, O Lord, and let Your enemies be scattered; and let them that hate You flee before You.*

***

<summary>This passage from the Zohar describes the ultimate redemption when God will destroy the "Serpent" (death/evil) and achieve perfect unity. It also explains that Moses's prayer when the Ark moved was a mystical invocation to protect Israel by activating the Divine Presence (Shekhinah).</summary>

<keywords>Redemption, Evil Inclination, Serpent, Ark of the Covenant, Shekhinah, Moses, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, Divine Unity, Protection</keywords>

<meta>This page marks the transition from the conclusion of the portion of Noah to the beginning of the portion of Lech Lecha. ## Main Text (The Zohar)

And because the Holy One, blessed be He, is eternally <term>holy</term> <note>original: "kadosh"</note>, anyone who cleaves to Him is holy. 
And at the time when one is bound to Him—who is holy—it is found that this act is likewise holy. 
Thus, holiness is found above and below; and when the <term>Holy One, blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu," a standard Aramaic title for God</note> is sanctified, He connects with him, and the <term>Divine Presence</term> <note>original: "Shekhinah," the feminine immanence of God</note> rests upon his head. Then the supernal angels come and inquire about this person who is holy. 
It is found that he is an image of the <term>Holy One, blessed be He</term>; just as He is holy, so too is this man holy.

It is found that supernal holiness did not descend upon Abraham until he was circumcised. Because he was circumcised, Abraham was found to be a supernal holy one. Regarding this it is written <note>Psalms 16:2</note>: **"I have said to the Lord, 'You are my Master; my good is not beyond You,'"** referring to when he was circumcised. And regarding this <note>Psalms 106:2</note>: **"Who can express the mighty acts of the Lord, or declare all His praise?"** Who is able to express them? Because of this, Abraham was called "Beloved," as it is written <note>Isaiah 41:8</note>: **"The seed of Abraham, My friend."** 

Regarding this, they are the righteous ones who shall dwell and exist within the holiness of their Master, as it is written <note>Song of Songs 3:7</note>: **"Behold the bed of Solomon... sixty mighty men are around it, of the mighty men of Israel."** All of them come from the power of the <term>Covenant</term> <note>original: "Brit," referring here to circumcision</note>, which is supernal strength. Anyone who guards this <term>Covenant</term>—which is the ancient root of all hidden secrets—merits it in this world and in the world to come, and takes hold of <term>Understanding</term> <note>original: "Binah," the third of the ten Sefirot or divine emanations</note>.

---
-> ### **Portion of Lech Lecha (Go Forth)** <-
---

**"And the Lord said to Abram: 'Go forth from your land...'"** <note>Genesis 12:1</note>. Rabbi Eleazar opened his discourse and said <note>Psalms 45:11</note>: **"Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline your ear..."** This refers to the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>original: "Knesset Yisrael," a mystical term for the Sefirah of Malkhut</note>, whom the <term>Holy One, blessed be He</term> called "Daughter," and called "Sister," and called "Mother." For the <term>Holy One, blessed be He</term> called her by all these supernal names. 

He said to her: "Hearken, O daughter, and consider," because this matter was present in Abraham. Since the <term>Holy One, blessed be He</term> desired to purify him, when the time drew near for Abraham to be perfected before Him, He brought him out from his father’s house, from his land, and from his birthplace where he had been dwelling, and gave him a supernal spirit. For this reason, He called to him: "Go forth."

<summary>This page explains that Abraham only achieved true holiness and a direct connection with the Divine Presence after his circumcision. It then introduces the command for Abraham to leave his homeland as a process of spiritual purification and elevation.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar/Kabbalistic Manuscript)

Certainly, these are the paths of the Torah and these are the commandments of the Torah, and they stand before the King, who is Wisdom <note>Hebrew: *Chokhmah*, the second of the ten emanations or Sefirot</note>. And concerning this it is written: **And all her paths are peace** <note>Proverbs 3:17</note>. For indeed, all the paths of the Torah are peace, and concerning this it was said: **Great peace have those who love Your Torah** <note>Psalms 119:165</note>. And whoever exerts themselves in the Torah and walks in the paths of the Torah, they sanctify the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and say "Amen," and they shall abide in that holiness which sanctifies the Holy Name. And concerning this it was said: **And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light** <note>Genesis 1:3</note>. And this is the mystery <note>Aramaic: *Raza*</note> of those who exert themselves before the King. And concerning this, it is beautiful that they are **ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace** <note>Proverbs 3:17</note>.

And this is the Right and the Left <note>Refers to the polarities of Mercy (Chesed) and Judgment (Gevurah) in the divine realm</note>. And when the Holy One, Blessed be He, came to create the world, and no merit was found in them at all—but whoever exerts themselves in the Torah and rectifies <note>Aramaic: *Metaken*, referring to the process of *Tikkun* or spiritual restoration</note> in the manner that is found in them, and whoever walks in the straight path and rectifies themselves—happy is the portion of that person who is worthy to know the paths of the Torah and to know the commandments of their Master. For in every single commandment of the Torah, there are supreme mysteries, and whoever is worthy to know them is worthy of the World to Come.

And by this, it is recognized who is righteous before the Holy King. And then, happy are the righteous who are worthy to cleave to the Life Above <note>Aramaic: *Chayim d'le'eila*, referring to the source of divine vitality</note> and to know before the Supreme King, who gives them life every day. For indeed, it was stated, and concerning this: **Happy is the man who finds wisdom, and the man who gains understanding** <note>Proverbs 3:13</note>. The Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is revealed before the King, and concerning this it is written: **Happy is the man who fears the Lord, who greatly delights in His commandments** <note>Psalms 112:1</note>. Happy are the holy pious ones, the servants of their Master, who occupy themselves with the Torah every day and are sanctified with the holiness from Above. They are meritorious in this world and in the World to Come, because they are recognized...

It emphasizes that every commandment contains hidden "mysteries" that allow the righteous to connect with the divine attributes of Wisdom and Understanding.</summary>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

-> **51** <-
-> **At the End** <-

"And it came to pass at the end of two full years..." <note>Genesis 41:1</note> **Rabbi Eleazar** opened his discourse with the verse: <note>Job 28:3</note> "He sets an end to darkness, and searches out every limit, the stones of thick darkness and the shadow of death."

**He sets an end to darkness**: This refers to the "End of the Left," <note>The "Left Side" in Kabbalah represents the attribute of Judgment and the source of potential evil or "Other Side."</note> which emerges from darkness. By this "end," the entire world is judged. **And searches out every limit**: This refers to the <term>End of the Right</term> <note>The "Right Side" represents Mercy and Holiness; its "end" refers to the ultimate goal of redemption and light.</note>, from which all joy and all light emerge. And when the <term>End of the Left</term> <note>The boundary where darkness and judgment hold sway.</note> is awakened in the world, what is written? "The stones of thick darkness and the shadow of death." And why is it called an "end"? Because it is the conclusion of all the lower levels. Everything that comes from the side of darkness is completed at that "end." This is the "end" that rules over darkness and the shadow of death.

Come and see: when that End of the Left ruled over the world, then **Joseph**—who represents the conclusion of the holy levels <note>Joseph corresponds to the Sefirah of Yesod, the "foundation" that gathers all spiritual energies to channel them downward.</note>—was found in the prison house. What is the reason? Because darkness ruled the world and covered the light. And this is the meaning of **two full years**. What are "two full years"? These were the days of Joseph's exile in the prison house, because he forgot [his faith] and said: <note>Genesis 40:14</note> "But think on me... and make mention of me unto Pharaoh." But when the End of the Right arrived, then light was awakened in the world and darkness passed away. Then Joseph was released from the prison house.

**And Pharaoh dreamed**. It specifies that Pharaoh dreamed, because the End of the Left is a "bad dream," belonging to the side of darkness. **Rabbi Isaac** said: Regarding the "two full years," when one year passed and Joseph was not remembered, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "You relied on a human being; therefore, you shall remain here until this point." After the two years were completed, what is written? "And it came to pass at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed." And then Joseph went out from the prison house. All of this occurred because that [holy] "end" was awakened and the End of the Left passed away.

Come and see: when that time of the dominion of darkness was completed, then the light was awakened and Pharaoh dreamed. And who is Pharaoh? He is the level upon which all bad dreams of darkness depend...

<summary>This page explores the spiritual mechanics behind Joseph's release from prison, contrasting the "End of the Left" (darkness/judgment) with the "End of the Right" (light/mercy). It explains that Joseph remained imprisoned for two extra years as a punishment for relying on the Egyptian cupbearer rather than God.</summary>

<keywords>Joseph, Pharaoh, Miketz, End of the Left, End of the Right, Darkness and Light, Dreams, Prison, Divine Providence</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar - Hidden Midrash)

And these are the four sides of the world through which the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God that dwells within the world</note> guides the universe. These are the four camps of holy angels, which correspond to the mystery of the <term>Chariot</term> <note>The Merkabah, or celestial throne-chariot described in the visions of the prophet Ezekiel</note>. They originate from the side of the realms above and are situated beneath the <term>Shekhinah</term>. And as for what was stated, for behold, in the <term>Hidden Midrash</term> <note>Midrash HaNe'elam; a specific layer of the Zohar that blends philosophical inquiry with mystical tradition</note> they established that these four camps are Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, and Nuriel.

They guide this world and are appointed over the four sides of the world. The mystery of the matter is this: when the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>The standard Hebrew/Aramaic title for God</note> desired to create the world, the mystery of the four sides was completed in the likeness of the realm above. These four camps above are beneath the <term>Shekhinah</term> in the manner of the <term>Chariot</term>, and they are called the four <term>Holy Living Creatures</term> <note>Chayot HaKodesh; the highest order of angels who support the Divine Throne</note>.

And as for what was said in the <term>Hidden Midrash</term>—that they guide this world—it is indeed so. For in every place, they are the ones who guide this world. When the <term>Shekhinah</term> is revealed below, they descend with Her, and from that time forward, the world is guided by their hands. And if you should say: "But are there not other angels who are appointed over the other nations?" It is certainly so; however, these four are the essence of them all, and all other appointees are under their hand, and they guide them. This is the mystery of the four sides of the world.

It clarifies that while many angels exist to oversee various nations, these four serve as the primary governors of the world's four directions.</summary>

# Vayechi

## Main Text (The Zohar)

He is cleaved to it because the male and female principles <note>original: "dekhura ve-nukba"</note> are always present within him. Because of this, the source that waters the entire world issues forth from him. Thus, the source is found above and below, and it is prepared to water the world. Concerning this, it is said: **The fountain of life** <note>Psalms 36:10</note>—this refers to the realm above; **and the fountain of living waters** <note>Jeremiah 17:13</note>—this refers to the realm below. The "fountain of life" is above, and upon it depend the four rivers that issue from Eden <note>see Genesis 2:10</note>; all of them depend on this source.

And this is the meaning of **as the herb of the field** <note>Genesis 2:5</note>, which draws nourishment from the river. Therefore, there is an "herb" found above and an "herb" found below. Regarding this source, it is written that it "found a place to lodge"—these are the rivers found within it. For this reason, this river issues from Eden; when it emerges, it is greater than its point of departure. That which departs from the male and is delivered into the hands of the female implies that the source emerges more abundantly than it was within him. Regarding this, it says: **and watered the whole face of the ground** <note>Genesis 2:6</note>. We do not find a "mate" for this river except in the verse: **and every herb of the field before it grew** <note>Genesis 2:5</note>.

Because of this, when those rivers unite in this source, those called "souls" <note>original: "nefashot"</note> appear. These are none other than all those souls below that come from the male and female as one. For from those souls that come from above as one, the soul that issues from it is later divided when it emerges from those higher waters <note>original: "mayin ilain"</note>. This is implied by what is written: **And every shrub of the field and every herb of the field** <note>Genesis 2:5</note>—these are the male living beings <note>original: "chayyot"</note>, and the soul of the male is the mate of the female, which is called "living beings" and the "strength of fire" together. So it is for all spirits, souls, and bodies; they all come from the "herb of the field," meaning that which was below the river. All this is because the river is found to be five hundred years [in extent], and so it appears to the whole world. And this is what is meant when it is written: <margin>as it is written</margin>

***

<summary>This passage explores the mystical origins of souls and divine sustenance, explaining how the union of male and female divine principles creates a "fountain of life" that waters both the upper and lower worlds.</summary>

<keywords>Zohar, Vayechi, male and female principles, Garden of Eden, four rivers, souls, divine emanations, creation</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> 54 <-

...which is beautiful and fitting <note>The text discusses the alignment of the spiritual worlds</note> for it is the **Male World** <note>original: "Alma de-Dkhura," referring to the higher, active spiritual realm</note>. Because of this, it is the beginning of every secret and all holiness belongs to it, for in that place holiness dwells and is found. It brings forth all holy secrets to the outside. Therefore, this is a holy mystery, the **Secret of Faith** <note>original: "Suda de-Meimanuta"</note>, and all sanctities of the upper and lower realms. This is the **Female World** <note>original: "Alma de-Nukba," the receptive realm or Shekhinah</note>, and regarding this is the secret: every person who comes to sanctify themselves and exerts effort in this deed should direct their **Thought** <note>original: "Machshavah," often associated with the high sefirah of Binah</note> toward this place. Then, he receives blessings <margin>in Thought</margin> from the place above, and from that holy Thought, he is sanctified. Concerning this, it is written:
> **"Consecrate yourselves and be holy"** <note>Leviticus 11:44</note>
As we have said, this is "Thought," which is the beginning of all things; from that place, holiness and blessings emerge and are found for all.

---

Come and see: Rabbi Isaac said, when the **soul** <margin>soul</margin> <note>original: "Nafsha"</note> of a person departs from this world, it does not leave until it looks upon those who were beloved to it and what occurred during the time it was in this world. Rabbi Judah said: Happy is the portion of the righteous, for **the Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>The standard Rabbinic name for God</note> delights in them both in this world and in the World to Come. 
Come and see: when **Joseph** passed away from the world, along with all those tribes, the faces of the children of Israel grew dark and their radiance was changed. It was then that the Egyptian exile began to take hold of them. For as long as Joseph was alive, they were not in servitude; rather, they were in freedom and great affection. 
Rabbi Abba said: when Joseph saw **Benjamin** his brother <note>Reference to the meeting of Joseph and Benjamin</note>, the love of his heart was awakened toward him, and there was found in him the secret of the **Holy Covenant** <note>original: "Berit Kadisha," referring to the sefirah of Yesod</note> which rested upon him.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Leviticus, specifically focusing on the laws of the Jubilee year as described in the portion of Behar. The text transitions from legal requirements to the hidden spiritual structures of the universe.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The commandment: **"And you shall proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants"** <note>Leviticus 25:10</note> is given because within it <note>the Jubilee</note> is found freedom for all.
**"It is a Jubilee; the fiftieth year shall be for you"** <note>Leviticus 25:11</note> because it is the fiftieth year.
Why must there be fifty years? Because that <term>Jubilee|Yovel: In Jewish mysticism, the Jubilee represents the fiftieth gate of understanding (Binah), a divine source of return and liberation.</term> stands over fifty years.
**"And you shall proclaim liberty throughout the land"**—this refers to the lower world, for from it <note>the Jubilee</note> freedom is found, just as the word "liberty" <note>original: *deror*</note> signifies freedom. And this freedom goes out from it to everyone, because it is freedom for all. **"And you shall proclaim liberty"**—this is the freedom for this world, which is freedom for all. When the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He|Kudsha Brich Hu: The standard Aramaic name for God used in the Zohar.</term> desired to bring Israel into the Holy Land, He commanded them this commandment, because within it is found freedom for all. And anyone who is under the authority of another shall go out to freedom, because that Jubilee stands ready to release all those souls and all those who entered under the authority of another.
Because that Jubilee stands over them, and this freedom goes out from it to everyone. And regarding this: **"And you shall proclaim liberty throughout the land,"** which is the lower land, for from it freedom goes out to all.
**"And you shall proclaim liberty"**—this is freedom. And regarding this: **"It is a Jubilee, it shall be for you,"** and **"you shall proclaim liberty"**—this is freedom. And regarding this, because it is the Jubilee and it is freedom, it is called "Jubilee" because of this freedom that is within it; and for this reason, it is the Jubilee. And anyone who is liberated, who was under the authority of another, shall go out to freedom, because that Jubilee stands over fifty years.
And regarding this, it is a Jubilee, and **"you shall proclaim liberty"**—this is freedom for this world. And as it was said, that liberty is freedom for all. And when the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to bring Israel into the Holy Land, He commanded them this commandment, because within it is found freedom for all.
And anyone who is under the authority of another shall go out to freedom, because that Jubilee stands over them. And anyone who was enslaved under the authority of another shall go out to freedom. And this is the Jubilee, as we have said. And regarding this: **"And you shall proclaim liberty throughout the land,"** which is the lower land, and this freedom goes out from it to all...

<summary>This passage explores the mystical nature of the Jubilee year (Yovel), explaining that it serves as a cosmic source of "liberty" (deror) that releases souls and servants from external authority. It links the fifty-year cycle to a higher spiritual realm that grants freedom to the "lower world" or the Land of Israel.</summary>
<keywords>Jubilee, Yovel, Liberty, Freedom, Fiftieth Year, Holy One Blessed be He, Holy Land, Souls, Authority, Binah, Leviticus</keywords>

--- Page 232 ---
<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar, specifically focusing on the spiritual significance of the lives of the patriarchs and matriarchs. It transitions from a discussion on the "Seventh Spring" to an analysis of the biblical descriptions of Abraham and Sarah's lifespans.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

The seventh spring is superior and hidden above all other "sevenths" in all the worlds.
Rabbi Yose stretched out his hands and blessed him, saying: "May it be the will [of Heaven] that the *Shekhinah* <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</note> shall guard you on this path and at all times that you are found upon it." When he stood before Rabbi Phinehas ben Yair, he said to him: "I have seen that this word was crowned with seventy crowns before the King, and it prevailed before the Holy One, Blessed be He. The masters of supreme mysteries have caused the *Shekhinah* to rest upon you, as well as all the twenty-seven kings who are appointed and lead upon the wings of the Holy Spirit—and all this is because of the secret found within you at this hour." Rabbi Eleazar rose and kissed the hands of Rabbi Yose. Rabbi Shimon wept and said: "Certainly, this secret is among us," and he was about to depart. Rabbi Isaac said: "Fortunate is our portion that we have heard the words of the Ancient of Days <note>original: "Atik Yomin" — a title for the most hidden, ancient aspect of the Divine</note> which are more precious than all the pearls in the world. It is forbidden to turn back, and since we find ourselves here, let us praise the Holy One, Blessed be He, and exert ourselves in the Torah." He opened his discourse and spoke of a matter found regarding Abraham, as it is written: <note>Genesis 24:1</note> **"And Abraham was old, advanced in days."** It should have simply written "Abraham was old"; why does it say "*And* Abraham"? Rabbi Yochanan said: "This contains a secret, for the letter *Vav* <note>The Hebrew letter meaning 'and'</note> is at the beginning of the word..."

---

He opened his discourse and said: <note>Genesis 23:1</note> **"And the life of Sarah was a hundred years, and twenty years, and seven years; the years of the life of Sarah."**
In all of these, the word "year" <note>singular</note> is written, except for "seven years" <note>plural</note>. And why is the phrase "the life of Sarah" repeated twice?
Come and see: The righteous are fortunate, for their lives are all hidden within the life of the World to Come. When the Holy One, Blessed be He, takes account of the service they performed before Him in this world, the days in which they performed the service of their Master all stand before the Holy One, Blessed be He. They are the "life of the world," and in the days that they have life, the life of that [higher] world endures.

<summary>This passage explores the mystical rewards of the righteous, using the biblical descriptions of Abraham and Sarah's ages to demonstrate how earthly deeds are transformed into eternal spiritual "life" in the World to Come.</summary>
<keywords>Shekhinah, Ancient of Days, Abraham, Sarah, World to Come, secrets of Torah, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, Rabbi Yose</keywords>
