<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of King Solomon’s wisdom, specifically linking his earthly reign and throne to the celestial mechanics of the Divine attributes.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

[...] precious, because the wisdom of King Solomon—which is the <term>Moon</term> <note>original: "Sihra"; a reference to the Sefirah of Malchut, the feminine Divine principle which reflects the light of the higher realms</note>—when it was filled from all sides and complete in all its "limbs" <note>parts or aspects</note>, then that wisdom stood in his hand in perfection. And then he was worthy to rule over all the inhabitants of the world. Fortunate is the portion of the righteous ones of the Torah who fear the Holy One, Blessed be He, and all their wisdom does not ascend to another <note>i.e., to the "Other Side" or unholy forces</note> but only to the Holy One, Blessed be He. Come and see: because King Solomon feared the Holy One, Blessed be He, he merited that wisdom. And regarding this it is said:
> **"And the Lord gave wisdom to Solomon"** <note>1 Kings 5:26</note>
What is the meaning of "And the Lord" <note>original: "V'Adonai"; the addition of the letter Vav (And) signifies the King and His Court</note>? It is He and His House of Judgment. Because this wisdom comes from <term>Kingship</term> <note>original: "Malchuta"; the lowest of the ten Sefirot, associated with Divine authority</note> which stands in the House of Judgment above. 

Come and see: there are six levels to the Moon, and six levels to the <term>Throne</term> <note>original: "Korseya"</note>. What is the reason? Because the Moon is itself the Throne. And when the moon is full, it is in the perfection of all its limbs. And when this wisdom—which is the Moon—was completed in perfection, then the Throne was completed with six steps. And because of this, the Throne of Solomon had six steps. Come and see: this wisdom of Solomon, for whoever is wise in it, is found to be in the likeness of that which is Above. Because all the works of King Solomon were according to the pattern of Above. His Throne was the Moon, and the six steps to the Throne were the six levels of the Moon. For behold, here is the "Moon of Solomon"—the Moon Above which is the Throne in which the Wisdom of Above is found. When this Moon comes to rule in the world, all the inhabitants of the world tremble before it, because [this] dominion is found in it according to the pattern of Above.

<summary>This passage explains that King Solomon's wisdom and his famous six-stepped throne were earthly reflections of the Sefirah of Malchut (the Moon), which receives its power from the six Sefirot above it. It emphasizes that Solomon's authority was a mirror of Divine sovereignty, established through his awe of God.</summary>

<keywords>Wisdom of Solomon, Moon, Malchut, Throne of Solomon, Six Steps, Sefirot, Divine Judgment, Kingship</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the Zohar's mystical commentary on the Torah portion Vayeshev. The previous section likely discussed the spiritual mechanics of human action and divine providence. Here, the text transitions into a profound discourse on the pre-existence of the soul and its reluctant descent into the physical body.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

... to give a portion and sustenance. And all of this occurs at a time when those human beings below do not awaken <note>In some editions, the line begins with: 'appointed over them to strengthen'</note> as is fitting; for if they were not meritorious, they would not know how to commit sins.
And it is written: > **And she conceived again, and bore a son; and called his name Shelah: and he was at Chezib, when she bore him.** <note>Genesis 38:5</note>
Come and see: we have established that when the soul goes out into the world, the Holy One, Blessed be He, speaks to each and every soul before they enter the world. And each and every one says before Him: "Master of the Universe, it is pleasing to me to remain in this place and not to enter that world, where sins are many and the filth of transgressions is great." The Holy One, Blessed be He, says to it: "From the day you were created, you were not created except to enter this world." And because of this, the Holy One, Blessed be He, sends it into this world against its will.
And regarding this, Solomon said: > **Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead** <note>Ecclesiastes 4:2</note>—since they have died and departed from this world. "I praised the dead"—meritorious are they who did not sin.
As it is said: > **Yea, better is he than both they, which hath not yet been** <note>Ecclesiastes 4:3</note>. What is the reason? Because he has not seen the evil works that are done under the sun. And because of this, those souls, before they enter the world, all stand before the Holy One, Blessed be He, in the supernal light, in the actual <term>form</term> <note>original: "dyokna" - a spiritual prototype or "image" that mirrors the physical body</note> of the body as it will be when the time comes to enter the world. And this is the secret we have learned.
Come and see, it is written: > **If thou buy a Hebrew servant** <note>Exodus 21:2</note>. This refers to the soul, which is in exile in this world. And this body is a servant of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as is fitting. If a person is meritorious in their soul, they are a <term>free daughter</term> <note>original: "bat chorin" - a status of spiritual liberation and nobility</note>. And yet, the soul is a servant to the Holy One, Blessed be He. Regarding this, David said: > **O Lord, truly I am Your servant; I am Your servant, the son of Your handmaid; You have loosed my bonds.** <note>Psalms 116:16</note>
And we have established that the soul is in <term>exile</term> <note>original: "galuta" - the state of being separated from its divine source</note> both above and below. Because of this, all souls that enter the world are "servants." And for this reason, the Holy One, Blessed be He, sends them down; for there is no one who is made a servant and sold unless they have sinned. And this is the <term>mystery</term> <note>original: "raza"</note> of the soul that descends from the <term>World to Come</term> <note>original: "Alma de-Atei" - the higher realm of emanation</note> to this world. And this is what we have established...

->in the secret<- <note>Catchword for the next page</note>

<summary>This page explores the soul's resistance to entering the physical world due to the prevalence of sin, explaining that the soul exists in a spiritual form before birth. It uses the biblical "Hebrew servant" as a metaphor for the soul's "exile" within the human body.</summary>
<keywords>soul, pre-existence, exile, Hebrew servant, King Solomon, King David, spiritual form, World to Come</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Which rises and stands above all those connections
that emerged from there. And this is what Rabbi Shimeon said:
Come and see, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Noah:
> **"Come into the Ark"** <note>Genesis 7:1</note>
which is the <term>Secret of the Covenant</term> <note>Hebrew: Sod Ha-Brit; refers to the mystical bond between God and creation, often associated with the procreative and foundational forces of the universe</note>. And this is

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Vayechi (Genesis 47:28–50:26). The narrative follows two sages traveling together, a common literary device in the Zohar to introduce deep spiritual teachings.</meta>

## Vayechi

Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Hezekiah were walking along the road and reached a field just as the sun was beginning to set. Rabbi Hezekiah said: "The time for the afternoon prayer <note>original: "Mincha"</note> has arrived. Anyone who prays this specific prayer must focus with great intent, for this is the hour when 'harsh judgment' <note>original: "dina kashya"</note> hangs over the world, and there is no one to mitigate it."

Rabbi Yose opened his discourse and said: <note>Psalms 89:7</note> **"For who in the skies can be compared to the Lord? Who among the sons of the mighty can be likened to the Lord?"** What is the meaning of "Who in the skies"? What is this verse speaking about? Come and see: there are times when all the heavenly hosts and all those who hold positions of authority are summoned to be established, each one in its proper place, according to the Will that arose to create the world.

He began by saying: At the moment that the <term>Point of the Curtain</term> <note>original: "nekuda de-parsa"; refers to a mystical boundary or a specific stage in the emanation of Divine light</note> was established in its proper form and all the celestial lamps were kindled, it was then called <term>Sky</term> <note>original: "shachak"</note>. And why is it called *Shachak*? Because it is the place of "ground fire" <note>a wordplay on the Hebrew root Sh-Ch-K, meaning both 'sky' and 'to grind'</note> that grinds manna for the righteous. In that sky, all the supernal crowns and all the hosts are summoned to be arranged and to shine as is fitting.

Therefore, the verse says: **"Who in the skies can be compared to the Lord?"** For there is no one who can arrange the order before the Holy One, blessed be He, in the skies, except for those celestial levels called "Skies" <note>original: "Shechakim"</note>. And what is this "order"? We have learned that at the hour when the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to create the world, He summoned before Him every future generation and every single soul <note>original: "nishmata"</note> that was destined to come into the world. He also summoned all the righteous who were destined to be leaders over the inhabitants of the world. He saw them all and envisioned them before Him in the exact <term>Image</term> <note>original: "dyokna"; from the Greek 'eikon', referring to the spiritual form or prototype of a person</note> that they would possess in this world. This is what is written: <note>Psalms 139:16</note> **"Your eyes saw my unformed substance; in Your book they were all written."**

And what is this "Book"? This is the book of the <note>Genesis 5:1</note> **"Generations of Adam."** For we have learned that all the people of the world, before they ever arrive in this world, all stand in the rank of the supernal angels, possessing a single spiritual form. But when they descend to this world, they clothe themselves in the garments of this world.

<summary>Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Hezekiah discuss the spiritual gravity of the afternoon prayer before transitioning into a mystical explanation of the pre-existence of souls, which exist in a divine "image" before birth.</summary>
<keywords>Mincha prayer, Judgment, Skies, Shechakim, Pre-existence of souls, Divine Image, Dyokna, Book of Adam</keywords>

## Leviticus

And this King said: all the hidden treasures of kindness <note>original: "chasidu"</note> and the "pity of His hand" <note>original: "chas yado"</note>—they called His hand "The King," which bears witness before the decree goes out against the transgressors. **The Golden Scepter**—this is the letter *Vav* <note>The letter Vav has the numerical value of 6 and represents the central pillar of the divine attributes</note>, engraved with the letters of the Holy Name. <meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Vayechi. The previous section likely concluded a discussion on the spiritual significance of the patriarchs, transitioning here into the nature of the Torah itself as a divine structure.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **[Folio 58]** <-

Rabbi Abba opened his discourse and said: **"Let your eyes look directly forward"** <note>Proverbs 4:25</note>. The words of the Torah are "straightforward" or "direct" in accordance with the path of the Torah, just as one’s eyes see a true image without deviating to the right or to the left. So too, the words of the Torah are all straightforward, as it is said: **"They are all straight to him who understands, and right to those who find knowledge"** <note>Proverbs 8:8</note>. Come and see: the words of the Torah all stand within a supreme mystery and are explained according to the verse: **"God understands its way, and He knows its place"** <note>Job 28:23</note>.

Rabbi Shimon said: The mystery of the matter is that the Supernal Torah <note>The primordial Torah before it manifested in the physical world</note> stands in the place called the <term>Holy of Holies</term> <note>original: Kodesh ha-Kodashim; refers to the highest inner sanctum of the Temple, representing the hidden Sephirah of Binah/Understanding</note>. And the lower Torah is called the <term>Written Torah</term> <note>original: Torah she-bi-Khtav</note>; this is the mystery of Judgment, and they are all contained one within the other, and they are the names of the Holy One, Blessed be He. For this reason, "God understands its way"—which is the holy supreme mystery—"and He knows its place"—which is the <term>Oral Torah</term> <note>original: Torah she-be-Al Peh; the tradition of interpretation that accompanies the written text</note>—and all is one Name.

Come and see, it is written: **"And God said, 'Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters'"** <note>Genesis 1:6</note>. This is the mystery of Abraham and Isaac <note>Representing the attributes of Mercy/Water and Judgment/Fire</note>, because this firmament stands between water and water: the upper waters and the lower waters. Rabbi Shimon said: Does this firmament merely divide between waters and waters? No. Rather, "let it divide between water and water" is like that which is said: **"And the veil shall divide for you between the Holy and the Holy of Holies"** <note>Exodus 26:33</note>. So too here, it divides between the upper waters and the lower waters.

Rabbi Eleazar said: The Written Torah and the Oral Torah—this is the meaning of "Let there be a firmament." And if you say this matter implies a separation of importance? No. For we have learned: whenever this firmament is visible, it distinguishes between the above and the below. What are these? These are the upper waters and the lower waters. But when this firmament is not found <note>i.e., when the division is transcended in mystical union</note>, the upper waters and the lower waters appear as one, for all is one.

<summary>This page explores the mystical unity of the Written and Oral Torah, using the biblical "firmament" as a metaphor for the boundary that both separates and connects the divine and earthly realms. It emphasizes that while the Torah appears divided into different levels of sanctity, it ultimately constitutes a single divine Name.</summary>

<keywords>Zohar, Written Torah, Oral Torah, Firmament, Upper Waters, Lower Waters, Holy of Holies, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, Divine Names, Unity</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the creation of the world, specifically focusing on the second day of the Genesis narrative. It follows the discussion of the primordial light and moves into the formation of the firmament and the nature of cosmic division.</meta>

## Genesis

... "Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters." This is the firmament of the heavens, as it is said <note>Genesis 1:8</note> **"And God called the firmament Heaven."** And it is written <note>Exodus 20:22</note> **"For from the heavens I have spoken with you."** And we have learned: because fire and water were together, the fire was calmed by the water, and from between them, the firmament emerged. And that firmament is called *Shamayim* <note>Heavens</note>, which is *Esh* <note>Fire</note> and *Mayim* <note>Water</note>. And we have learned: this firmament stands in the middle, between the waters above and the waters below. And regarding this it is written, **"And let it divide the waters from the waters."** For we have learned: "And it was so"—"Let there be light, and it was so"—because it stands in the supernal path <note>the divine realm</note>. And regarding this it is written, **"And it was so."** And the firmament went forth and was established and grew great within the firmament from the side of *Gevurah* <note>the divine attribute of Strength/Judgment</note> and stood in the supernal path.

And we have learned: this firmament is the **Middle Pillar** <note>the central balance of the divine emanations</note>, which is both male and female. Male from the side of the above, and female from the side of the below. For all things were within the mystery of the Heavens. And this is the mystery of the two names: *YHVH Elohim* <note>The Lord God</note>, which are one name. And regarding this: **"Let there be a firmament... and it was so. And let it divide the waters from the waters."**

We have learned: "And let it divide"—for those upper waters are not like the lower waters. The upper waters are male, and the lower waters are female. For everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, created in the world, He created them male and female. And because these waters are male and those are female, when the male waters descend toward the female waters, the female waters are aroused toward them and they are found as one. How do we know they are female? As it is written <note>Psalms 42:8</note> **"Deep calls unto deep at the noise of Your waterfalls."** "Deep" <note>Tehom</note> is female, as you might say <note>Job 38:16</note> **"And in the search of the deep have you walked?"** And we have learned <note>Job 38:30</note> **"The waters hide themselves as a stone, and the face of the deep is frozen."** Therefore, this "deep" is female, and it calls to the male, which is the other "deep." For "Deep calls unto deep"—female toward male.

And how do we know they are male and female? As it is written <note>Proverbs 10:8</note> **"The wise in heart will receive commandments."** And we have established that "wise in heart" refers to the male. The female is as you might say <note>Song of Songs 4:9</note> **"You have ravished my heart, my sister, my bride."** Therefore, the upper waters are male and the lower waters are female, and that firmament—which is the Middle Pillar—divides between them.

And we have learned: this firmament emerged from within fire and water and stands between them and divides them. And therefore, on the second day it is written, **"And let it divide the waters from the waters,"** but it is not written of it **"that it was good."** This is because division <note>dispute</note> was found in the world. And in any place where there is division, "it was good" is not written. And because of this, **Gehenna** <note>Hell/Purgatory</note> exists on the second day. And if you should say, "But was it not created on the eve of the Sabbath?"—it is not so. Rather, on the second day those divisions and judgments were perfected, and Gehenna was established within it. How do we know? As it is written <note>Isaiah 30:33</note> **"For Tophet <note>Gehenna</note> is ordained from yesterday."** And this "yesterday" is the second day, in which there is division. And therefore, "it was good" is not written regarding it...

<summary>This page explains the creation of the firmament as a synthesis of fire and water and introduces the concept of "Upper Waters" (male) and "Lower Waters" (female). It justifies the absence of the phrase "it was good" on the second day of creation by linking it to the emergence of cosmic division and the establishment of Gehenna.</summary>
<keywords>Firmament, Middle Pillar, Male and Female, Gehenna, Division, Fire and Water, Creation, Second Day</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar)

"Behold, You desire truth in the inward parts, and in the hidden part You make me know wisdom" <note>Psalm 51:8</note>. This verse has been established and the companions have established it. But come and see, this verse is as follows: it is the cry of King David at the time he was repenting before the Holy One, blessed be He, for that sin <note>The sin involving Bathsheba</note>. And he said, "Behold, [You are] truth," for You are Truth, and Your seal is Truth, and all the matters of the Torah are Truth. And the mystery of Truth is the place from which the prophets of truth draw their sustenance. And regarding this, it says "Behold, [You are] truth." "You desire truth in the inward parts <term>Tuchot: literally 'kidneys' or 'reins', representing the Sefirot of Netzach and Hod</term>." What are the "inward parts"? These are the kidneys. Just as you said <note>Job 38:36</note>, "Who put wisdom in the inward parts?"

"And in the hidden part You make me know wisdom." What is "in the hidden part"? This is that place from which the prophets draw their sustenance, and it is hidden above. And because it is hidden, he says, "and in the hidden part You make me know wisdom." For there is the place where the fountain of wisdom emerges and is drawn downward. Come and see, King Solomon said <note>Ecclesiastes 7:23</note>, "It is far from me." What is "It is far from me"? That he was not able to stand upon that hiddenness of the supernal wisdom. Yet King David said, "and in the hidden part You make me know wisdom." Did David know while Solomon did not know? Rather, David said "You make me know," for these matters are not spoken of in a revealed manner. And because it is hidden, it is said of it, "and in the hidden part You make me know wisdom."

Come and see, this is a mystery. "In the hidden part You make me know wisdom"—in that place that is neither recognized nor found. And there is the hiddenness of the Supernal Wisdom, for there the Male and Female <term>Dechura u-Nukba: the balancing masculine and feminine divine energies</term> are as one. And because of this, it is the hiddenness of wisdom. Solomon said, "It is far from me," because it is hidden and concealed, and is not recognized. It is higher than the high, the most hidden of all hidden things. And because it is hidden, he said, "and in the hidden part You make me know wisdom." Rabbi Shimon said: Happy is he who enters and exits and knows the paths and trails of the Torah. And regarding this it is written: "The path of the righteous is like the light of dawn..." <note>Proverbs 4:18</note>

# Laws

And because of this, when a person looks into the Holy Torah, it is revealed to all those children of faith that all the matters of the Torah are both hidden and revealed; the Torah in its entirety is hidden and it is revealed. **Rabbi Shimon** opened his discourse and cited the verse:
> And if a man shall open a pit, or if a man shall dig a pit and not cover it, and an ox or a donkey fall therein (Exodus 21:33).

Come and see how much people must guard themselves against their sins, for they are the opening of the pit of the "damagers" <note>original: maziqin; harmful spiritual entities or demons</note>. For the sin that a person commits before his Master opens a doorway for many Masters of Judgment who go about and prosecute him. And regarding this, the verse says, <term>if a man shall open a pit</term>. Who is the <term>man of the pit</term>? This is the <term>pit of the damagers</term> that soils the Moon <note>The Moon represents the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence, which is "blemished" by human sin</note>, for a person causes a blemish in her through his sins and opens doorways to the pit of the Great Abyss. Because of this, all the damagers and all the Masters of Judgment are all prepared to do evil to that person and to destroy him.

And regarding this, <term>if a man shall open a pit</term>—who is this "man of the pit"? This is one who opens doorways for the damagers and for harsh judgments to rest upon the world. <term>Or if a man shall dig a pit</term>—this is one who digs and digs into the pit until he brings forth bitter waters that prosecute the inhabitants of the world. And regarding this, <term>and not cover it</term>—what is "and not cover it"? That he did not return in <term>repentance</term> <note>original: teshuvah</note> before his Master. For if he had returned in repentance before his Master, he would have covered that pit, and it would not be able to rule over the world. Because repentance is a covering that covers over all the sins of a person so they are not seen before his Master, just as it is said:
> You have covered all their sin. Selah. (Psalms 85:3)

And regarding this, <term>and not cover it</term> means he did not repent. And regarding this, <term>and an ox or a donkey fall therein</term>—what are the <term>ox or donkey</term>? These are the lower crowns <note>spiritual powers</note> of the Other Side <note>original: Sitra Achra; the realm of evil</note>, which are "Ox" and "Donkey" that go and roam through the world to do evil to people. And come and see: when a person commits a small sin, those lower crowns are found upon him to do him evil; and if he commits a great sin, then the pit of damagers is opened and they all rule over him. And who are the damagers that rule over him? They are "Ox" and "Donkey," and regarding this, "and an ox or a donkey fall therein."

**Rabbi Eleazar** said: <term>If a man shall open a pit</term> or <term>if a man shall dig a pit</term> are both the same thing, because he who opens the doorways for the damagers is the one who dug the pit to do evil to himself and to the inhabitants of the world. And as for what is said, <term>and an ox or a donkey fall therein</term>—what are the ox and donkey? These are the damagers that all come from "Ox" and "Donkey," which are their roots for doing evil in the world. And come and see: a person is not liable for a pit he made except for the damage it caused to his fellow; if it did not damage his fellow, he is not liable, but if it damaged his fellow, then he is liable. Here too, a person is not liable for the sin he committed except for the damage it causes to his own soul or to another, for then the Holy One, blessed be He, judges the person, and regarding this, "and an ox or a donkey fall therein."

## Main Text (The Zohar)

**In the beginning God created.** <note>Genesis 1:1</note> When the King desired to create, He engraved engravings in the supreme purity. A **hardened lamp** <term>Butzina de-Kardinitah: a concentrated, powerful spark of divine energy</term> emerged within the most hidden of secrets, from the mystery of the **Infinite** <term>Ein Sof: God's essence before manifestation</term>, like a plume of smoke in a fog, wedged in a ring. It was not white, nor black, nor red, nor green, nor any color at all. When He extended the measuring cord, He produced colors to shine. Deep within the lamp, there emerged a single spring, from which the colors below were dyed; it remains hidden within the secret of the Infinite.

It cleaved and yet did not cleave its atmosphere. It was not known at all until, from the pressure of its cleaving, a single, hidden, supreme **point** <note>original: Nekudah; representing the first flash of Wisdom</note> shone. Beyond that point, nothing is known at all, and for this reason it is called **Beginning** <note>original: Reshit</note>, the first utterance of all.

->**And the wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.** (Daniel 12:3)<-

**Brightness** <note>original: Zohar</note>; He engraved engravings in the supreme purity, a light of the hiddenness that cleaved its atmosphere. It shone from this point. Then this **Beginning** expanded and made for itself a **palace** <note>original: Heikhala; representing the womb of creation or Understanding</note> for its glory and its praise. There it sowed a holy seed to give benefit to the world. And this is the mystery of: **The holy seed is the stock thereof** <insert>Isaiah 6:13</insert>. **Brightness**, which sows seed for its glory, is like the seed of fine purple silk, which is hidden and does not break through until, from the pressure of its cleaving, its light expands and shines within this palace, and the holy seed is found within that palace. And this is the mystery of **God** <note>original: Elohim</note>. And this is the meaning of: **In the beginning created God.**

**Brightness**, from which all utterances were created in the mystery of the expansion of the hidden supreme light. And because this **Brightness** is the seed sown for its glory—like that seed of fine silk hidden within—it made for itself a palace which is the praise and the benefit of all. Through this **Beginning**, that Unknown Hidden One created this palace. This palace is called **God**. And this is the mystery of: **In the beginning created God.**

<summary>This page describes the mystical origins of the universe, where the Infinite (Ein Sof) emanates a "hardened lamp" and a "point" of light that expands into a "palace" identified with the name Elohim. It reinterprets the first verse of Genesis as a process of divine self-unfolding rather than a simple act of making.</summary>

# Pekudei

## Main Text (Zohar)

[We have learned] that all the work and all the service that exists within those <term>Palaces</term> <note>original: "Heikhalot"; the seven celestial dwellings in the world of Creation</note> and all those <term>Chariots</term> <note>original: "Rethikin"; angelic assemblies or vehicles of divine manifestation</note> stand ready to be joined one to another so that all becomes one. Because of this, they are called <term>Common</term> <note>original: "Chullin"; non-holy or profane in a technical sense, referring to entities outside the inner sanctum</note> and are not within the secret of the <term>Holy</term> <note>original: "Kodesh"</note> because they are on the outside. And all those who come from the side of impurity are "completely common." Even at the twilight of the Sabbath eve, those who emerged from the "Other Side" <note>the realm of evil or shells</note> are for this reason called common. Furthermore, regarding these common things, some are "common things prepared in the purity of the holy," because they serve the Holy. These are found before the <term>First Palace</term>. For those lower palaces which are on the outside serve the palaces that are Holy. Furthermore, there are palaces that are within the Holy and yet are called common, because they are not the "Holy" itself. And all of them exist within the <term>Secret of Man</term> <note>original: "Raza de-Adam"; the mystical concept that the spiritual cosmos is structured in the form of a human being</note>.

In the first palace, which is the palace of the primary servants, none of them possess a form until they reach this palace; then they all exist within the Secret of Man. Because of this, they are "beautiful common things" and they all stand beneath this palace. In this manner, every work is set over another work until chariots are found upon chariots. And here, within this mystery, the Secret of Man is found in every single palace. This palace is where all those who serve on the outside stand. They stand under the mystery of one appointee and their many chariots. And the name of this appointee is **Uriel**. Under his hand are many thousands and many tens of thousands of holy angels who are appointed over that worship and over that work within this palace. And they all stand within the Secret of Man so that the preparation found within it contains all beautiful colors.

This palace has no light of its own; rather, all the lights that shine in this palace shine into it from the palace that is above it. That light descends, and when it reaches this palace, it spreads out into many lights and many sides. And this palace is the **Palace of Radiance** <note>original: "Heikhal de-Zihara"</note> because of all the colors that stand within it. In this manner, every single palace has an appointee who stands over it. And in this palace, there is found one appointee whose name is **Zahariel**, and he stands over those lights that shine...

<summary>This page describes the first of the celestial palaces, explaining the distinction between 'holy' and 'common' spiritual entities and how angels take on the 'Secret of Man' (human form) as they descend. It identifies the archangel Uriel as the primary leader of this realm and Zahariel as the overseer of its radiant lights.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion "Lech Lecha" (Go Forth), specifically focusing on Abraham’s spiritual journey and his descent into Egypt as a test of faith and wisdom.</meta>

# Go Forth

## Main Text (Zohar)

In this same manner, it is a secret that they said: a person should not travel alone on a journey, because the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed in the Zohar as the feminine aspect of God that accompanies the righteous</note> does not go with him. 
And if you say that a person should hire companions of the Torah <note>fellow scholars</note> to travel with him so that the Shekhinah will travel with him in this way—
Come and see: Abraham, who is the <term>Secret of Faith</term> <note>original: "raza de-meimanuta"; a term for the highest level of spiritual adherence</note>, did not travel alone so that the Shekhinah would not separate from him.
And regarding this it is written: **And Lot went with him** <note>Genesis 12:4</note>. Because of this, while Lot was with him, Abraham knew that the Shekhinah would not separate from him. 
Come and see what is written: **And there was a famine in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt to sojourn there** <note>Genesis 12:10</note>. For what reason did he go down to Egypt?
Because the <term>Wisdom of Egypt</term> was greater than all the other "children of the East," and from there they knew all the secrets of the Higher Wisdom and the secret of everything. 
And Abraham desired to know all the wisdoms of the world so that he would not be led astray by them, and so he would know the worship of the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> <note>The standard Rabbinic title for God</note> above all else. 
And this secret is like the manner of gold: when one wants to know its quality, he brings it into the fire to know that it is pure. 
In this same way, in order to know all the levels of wisdom and the strength of the worship of Egypt, Abraham went down there, which is the "Lower Wisdom." 
And when he knew them and gazed upon them, he returned to his place. 
And regarding this, "there was a famine in the land"—for we see that there was never a famine in the world like this one, for Abraham went down there specifically to know the levels of Egypt. 
And because of this, Abraham ascended from Egypt once he knew everything. 
And regarding this it is written: **And Abram went up from Egypt, he and his wife and all that he had, and Lot with him, toward the South** <note>Genesis 13:1</note>.
"He and his wife and all that he had"—this refers to the **Shekhinah** who traveled with him always. 
"And Lot with him"—so that [the Presence] would not separate from him. 
"Toward the South"—this is the higher level that Abraham ascended to, because he knew that the worship of Egypt and all their wisdom was nothing. 
And because of this, Abraham returned to his place. 
Come and see what is written: **And it came to pass, as they journeyed from the east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar, and they dwelt there** <note>Genesis 11:2</note>. 
And they called it the land of Shinar because there they "shook themselves off" <note>A wordplay on "Shinar" and the Hebrew/Aramaic root "na'ar," meaning to shake off or empty</note> from the worship of the Holy One, Blessed Be He, and gazed upon other levels. 
And these are the levels of the Lower Wisdom. 
And come and see: when Abraham went down to Egypt, he gazed upon them and entered into them, but he emerged from them in peace, because he knew they were a lie and they were <term>impurity</term>. 
And he returned to his place, to the <term>Higher Faith</term>. 
But those wicked ones [of the Tower of Babel] went down there in order to sin and rebel against the Holy One, Blessed Be He. 
And regarding this it is written: **And they found a plain in the land of Shinar and they dwelt there.** 
And it is written: **And it came to pass as they journeyed from the east.** What is "from the east" <note>Hebrew: "mi-kedem"</note>? From the **Ancient of the World** <note>original: "kadmono shel olam"</note>, who is the Holy One, Blessed Be He. 
And regarding this it is written, "and they found a plain," which is the wisdom of impurity, the Lower Wisdom which is a lie. 
And come and see that Abraham was chosen from all the people of the world because he was the Secret of Faith, and he knew how to distinguish between the holy and the impure. 
And regarding this it is written: **And Abram went as the Lord had spoken to him** <note>Genesis 12:4</note>. Because he knew that the worship of the Holy One, Blessed Be He, is the essence of everything, and all other wisdoms are vanity. 
And come and see: all the time that Abraham was traveling on the road, his mouth did not cease from the study of the Torah, and because of this, the Shekhinah never separated from him. 
Come and see that in every place Abraham went, he called upon the name of the Lord...

<summary>This page explains that Abraham traveled to Egypt to master worldly and "lower" wisdoms to prove his faith, contrasting his successful spiritual journey with the failure of the generation of the Tower of Babel. It emphasizes that the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) accompanied Abraham because of his constant devotion and his refusal to travel alone.</summary>

# The Pillars of the Host

...These firmaments <note>original: "reki'in"</note> offer praise before the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu," the standard Aramaic name for God</note>, at every single moment in the ->World to Come<-.

->**The Pillars of the Host**<-

They ascend above and descend below, and they are situated beneath the Throne of the King. These are the holy angels who praise the Holy One, Blessed be He... every single day. Regarding this, Rabbi Shimon said: "Fortunate is the portion of that person who knows how to offer praise to his Master..." In the first palace <note>original: "heichala kadmaa"</note>, they all ascend and join together as one. There are seventy-one appointed officials, and they stand beneath the firmament that rests upon the heads of the Living Creatures <note>original: "chayot," the high-ranking angels described in Ezekiel's vision</note>...

---

Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse:
> **The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament tells of His handiwork.** <note>Psalms 19:2</note>

Come and see: when the light shines and enters the side of the North, a spirit is then awakened... the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</note> is awakened in joy. And those angels who sing praises at night, they all stand in their places. The firmament that stands above them utters a song of praise. What does it say? **The heavens declare the glory of God.** "The heavens"—these are the supernal angels who are called "Heavens." "Declare" <note>original: "mesaprim"</note>—just as it is said (Psalms 87), "The Lord shall count <note>yispor</note> when He writes up the peoples," for they shine and radiate like the brilliance of a sapphire <note>original: "sapir," a wordplay on "mesaprim/declare"</note>. "The glory of God"—this is the Shekhinah, who is called the Glory of God.

"And the firmament tells of His handiwork"—which firmament? This is the firmament that stands above those Living Creatures. This is the firmament called (Ezekiel 1) "And the likeness of a firmament was over the heads of the Living Creatures..." And at the moment this firmament is awakened, then all the angels open their mouths and say (Psalms 8): "O Lord, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!"

## Portion of Noah

<unclear>...</unclear>
<term>Rabbi Yose said</term> <note>original: "Amar Rabbi Yose"</note>: And this is the straight path that leads before the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>The standard rabbinic title for God</note>, because this refers to the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, viewed here as a protective feminine aspect of God</note> who is in exile. The Holy One, Blessed be He, taught Noah to enter into her in order to save him and so he would be rescued from that Flood. Come and see: because Noah was a <term>Righteous One</term> <note>Tzadik; a person of perfect spiritual integrity</note>, the Holy One, Blessed be He, told him to enter the Ark, as it is written:
> **"Go, you and all your household, into the ark, for I have seen that you are righteous before Me in this generation."** <note>Genesis 7:1</note>
What is the reason? Because a person does not enter before the <term>Shekhinah</term> unless he is a <term>Righteous One</term>, as it is written:
> **"This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter through it."** <note>Psalm 118:20</note>
And regarding this, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Noah: "Go, you and all your household, into the ark."

<term>Rabbi Eleazar said</term>: When the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to create the world so that human beings would know Him, He gave them the Torah and the paths and ways of truth. Regarding this, He later sent for Noah, as the <term>Companions</term> <note>Chavrayya; the circle of mystical scholars in the Zohar</note> have already established. Come and see: from Noah onwards, the Holy One, Blessed be He, began to give a good reward to the righteous and desired to benefit them. Therefore it is written: "And the Lord said to Noah, 'Go, you and all your house...'"
Why is the Name <term>YHVH</term> <note>The four-letter Name of God representing Mercy</note> used here, while in the previous section it said <term>Elohim</term> <note>The Name of God representing Judgment</note>? <term>Rabbi Eleazar said</term>: The companions have explained this matter—in every place where <term>Judgment</term> <note>Din</note> rests, the Name *Elohim* is used, and in every place where <term>Mercy</term> <note>Rachamim</note> rests, the Name *YHVH* is used. Here, it was an act of mercy so that the Flood would not be able to have power over him; therefore, *YHVH* is written. And come and see: once Noah entered the Ark, he was hidden there, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, had mercy on him, as it is written:
> **"And God remembered Noah."** <note>Genesis 8:1</note>

---

<term>Rabbi Yose opened his discourse and said</term>:
> **"A Maskil of David: Happy is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered."** <note>Psalm 32:1</note>
What is the meaning of "A Maskil of David"? The companions have explained this verse in several places. But come and see: what is "a covered sin"? It means that at the time when human beings sin before the Holy One, Blessed be He, He covers over them so that their guilt will not be known before the <term>Masters of Judgment</term> <note>Accusing angels or divine prosecutors</note>. 

And come and see: that person who commits a sin but does not specify it before other people, but only before the Holy One, Blessed be He, alone—then the Holy One, Blessed be He, becomes the "coverer of the sin" and desires to save that person. Then it is a "covered sin," hidden in a place where the <term>Masters of Judgment</term> cannot have power over it. Regarding this, it is written: "Happy is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered." For any person whose sins are revealed, permission is not given to forgive them, because of the accusers who stand over him. But one whose sins are concealed and not revealed before the Ministering Angels, he is the "covered sin."

<meta>This page continues the discourse on the mystical significance of prayer and intention within the section of the Zohar known as the Heikhalot (Divine Palaces). It follows the discussion of how human action below awakens spiritual forces above.</meta>

## Section: Vayakhel

... For in every place, service that is not performed with the **desire of the heart** <note>Aramaic: *re’uta de-liba*; refers to focused mystical intention or *kavvanah*</note> is not considered service at all. 

Come and see: the service of **the Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note> requires the desire of the heart and the desire of the soul. For by means of that desire of the heart, the word ascends on high and clings above to all those holy **chariots** <term>Chariots: *Ratichin*; the celestial structures or angelic assemblies that support the Divine Throne</term> of the Holy One, Blessed be He, which stand above to be joined one to another. Because of this, that desire of the heart must cling to Him; for a word does not ascend unless that desire ascends and rises on high and clings to Him through the desire of the heart.

And this is the **secret of faith** <note>original: *raza de-meimanuta*</note> and the desire of the heart, which is the essence of everything: that the word ascends and rises and clings in the place where it must cling, until everything is made into **one**. 

Come and see: when a person brings forth a word from his mouth with the desire of the heart, that word ascends on high and pierces the firmaments; it goes and awakens that which it awakens <note>meaning it triggers a specific spiritual response or flow of emanation</note> until it ascends on high and stands before the Holy One, Blessed be He. Regarding this, it is written:

> "The Lord is near to all who call upon Him, to all who call upon Him in truth" (Psalms 145:18).

What is meant by "in truth"? This is the desire of the heart. And regarding this, we have learned that every word a person brings forth from his mouth—if it is in the way of truth and if it is with the desire of the heart—all those words perform work on high. But one who brings forth a word from his mouth without the desire of the heart and without truth, that word does not ascend on high, and it is found that he has uttered the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, in vain.

Come and see: **Voice and Word**. The Voice is that which issues from the mouth, and the Word is that which issues from that Voice. Voice and Word ascend as one and cling on high, and this is the secret of faith. When that Voice issues without a Word—that is, a Voice that is heard without a Word <note>perhaps referring to wordless melody or a primal cry of the soul</note>—that Voice ascends on high and pierces the firmaments and awakens that which it awakens. And all those words that issue from the mouth of a person, they all go and fly through the world.

<summary>This passage emphasizes that prayer and divine service are only effective when accompanied by "re'uta de-liba" (heartfelt intention). It explains that sincere words of prayer pierce the heavens to reach the Creator, while insincere speech is spiritually hollow.</summary>

<keywords>desire of the heart, intention, prayer, chariots, secret of faith, voice and word, Psalms 145:18, spiritual awakening</keywords>

--- Page 279 ---
<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the life of Noah, specifically focusing on the moment he departs the ark and establishes a new covenant through sacrifice. It follows the themes of cosmic restoration after the Flood.</meta>

## Portion of Noah

When Noah emerged from the ark, what is written? **"And Noah built an altar to the Lord"** <note>Genesis 8:20</note>. He built an altar to the Lord—to the One who is the Sustainer of the world <note>original: "Kiyuma de-Alma"</note>, and to this Name which is the sustenance of all. And what is written? **"And he offered burnt offerings on the altar"** <note>ibid.</note>. These were truly "burnt offerings" <term>Olot: literally "ascensions"</term>, for they ascend higher and higher into the spiritual realms.

Rabbi Eleazar said: All the sacrifices that the children of Noah offered prior to this were "peace offerings" <term>Shelamim: sacrifices shared by the altar and the person bringing them</term>. Why were they all peace offerings? Because the spiritual degree of the "burnt offering" <note>which is entirely consumed by the Divine fire</note> had not yet been revealed. And what is the reason for this? Because until this moment, the world had not yet been repaired <note>original: "it-takan," referring to Tikkun or spiritual restoration</note> and the world had not yet been settled. Once the world was settled and repaired, the degree of the burnt offering was revealed.

And what is the meaning of that which is written: **"And the Lord smelled the pleasing aroma"** <note>Genesis 8:21</note>? At the time when Noah emerged from the ark, built an altar, and offered sacrifices, come and see <note>original: "Ta Chazi," a standard Zohar opening to a deeper insight</note> what is written: "And the Lord smelled the pleasing aroma." This is the "aroma of rest," for rest was found before the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>, and anger was removed from the world. The world was repaired, and the restoration of the world was found through Noah.

Come and see, it is written: **"And the Lord said in His heart, 'I will never again curse the ground...'"** <note>ibid.</note>. This is because until now, the earth existed in a state of constant rebuke and curse, from the day that Adam sinned and the earth was cursed because of him. This is what is written: **"Cursed is the ground because of you"** <note>Genesis 3:17</note>. But on this day, the curse of the earth was removed from it, as it is written: **"I will never again curse the ground because of man."** And it is written: **"This one will comfort us from our work and from the toil of our hands, from the ground which the Lord has cursed"** <note>Genesis 5:29</note>. What is the meaning of "from the ground"? It means that he offered a sacrifice upon it, and it became settled.

Come and see what is written: **"As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease"** <note>Genesis 8:22</note>. All these are the six degrees <note>referring to the six emotive attributes or Sefirot</note> through which the world is repaired so that they shall not cease, and they shall never be nullified. This verse is the very sustenance of the world, ensuring it will never be destroyed, for it is written: **"they shall not cease."**

<summary>This page explains that Noah's sacrifice after the Flood marked the first "burnt offering," signaling the spiritual restoration (Tikkun) of the world and the removal of the curse placed on the earth after Adam's fall. The Zohar interprets the seasons and cycles of time as six spiritual degrees that sustain existence and prevent future destruction.</summary>

<keywords>Noah, Altar, Burnt Offering, Peace Offering, Tikkun, Curse of Adam, Pleasing Aroma, Six Degrees, Covenant of Nature</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical description of the Celestial Palaces (Heichalot) from the Zohar, specifically focusing on the transition between the sacred "House of Shabbat" and the punishments of the underworld.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

From within this place, a single fire emerges, along with many faithful rulers who are appointed over them, and many gates with overseers appointed over the outer gates. This place is called the **House of Shabbat**. In this place, there is comfort for the Assembly of Israel <note>The spiritual personification of the Jewish people</note> at the time when the souls of the righteous enter there. When those souls arrive to enter and rest there, all the overseers open the gates for them. There the souls dwell and are crowned with many crowns. In this place, they come to receive the light of that hour when the Sabbath enters. In this place, all the impure forces that stand beneath it are subdued. When the Sabbath enters, they all dwell in the mire, and their pride is subdued beneath the gates of this place. There, they are judged in the dark mire <note>original: "tina de-tehoma raba" — referring to the sludge of the Great Abyss</note> of a fire that is never extinguished. This is the Hell <note>original: "Gehinnom"</note> of the souls of the wicked from the "Other Side" <note>original: "Sitra Achra" — the realm of evil or impurity</note>. A single overseer dwells there named <term>Dumah</term> <note>The angel in charge of the souls of the deceased</note>, and he settles the souls of the guilty. When the Sabbath enters, they all dwell in the mire of that hole of the Great Abyss, and at that hour, they are not judged. But when the Sabbath departs, that overseer whose name is <term>Dumah</term> proclaims and says: <note>Psalms 9:18</note> "The wicked shall return to the underworld, all the nations that forget God." Then they all enter their places. When the Sabbath departs, all the souls of the righteous leave that place called the **House of Shabbat**, because that is the place established to receive the souls of the righteous. From that place, a flame of fire emerges. When that flame emerges, it divides into many flames in every direction. That flame is found to be standing ready to receive the wicked, and there, all those who transgressed the commandments of the Torah are judged. Concerning this, the scripture says: <note>Isaiah 66:24</note>
> And they shall go out and look at the corpses of the people who rebelled against Me; for their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched.
And because of this, there are many overseers who are appointed over Hell to judge the wicked and those souls of the guilty, because this is the place where the wicked are judged. When the Sabbath enters, they all find rest. In that place of Hell, there are seven compartments, and over every single compartment, there is one overseer who judges those who enter there. Over all of them, there is one overseer whose name is <term>Dumah</term>, and he settles the souls of the guilty, and by his hand they are delivered <unclear>to all</unclear>...

<summary>This passage describes the "House of Shabbat," a celestial sanctuary where the souls of the righteous rest and the punishments of the wicked in Hell are temporarily suspended during the Sabbath. It details the role of the angel Dumah and the resumption of judgment once the holy day concludes.</summary>
<keywords>House of Shabbat, Gehinnom, Dumah, souls of the righteous, Great Abyss, Sabbath rest, celestial palaces, Sitra Achra</keywords>

## Vayechi

Which is called **Loving-kindness** <note>original: "Chesed"</note>. What is the reason? Because it stands above constantly, and all its paths are according to the law of the Torah. Because of this, there is no [letter] *Nun* found within it <note>The Zohar often engages in "letter mysticism," where the absence or presence of a Hebrew letter signifies a spiritual state; here, the absence of the bent *Nun* may suggest a lack of "falling" or judgment</note>, and the pure *Nun* <note>original: "Nun Dakha"</note> which is in unity, this from that, because this is not found except at the time when they are in this world. And even though they are from the side of the Left <note>The "Left side" usually refers to the attribute of Judgment (Gevurah)</note>, the Holy One, blessed be He, precedes them with mercy because they are from the deeds of **Abraham** <note>In Kabbalah, Abraham is the human chariot for the attribute of Loving-kindness</note>. Because of this, the letter *Nun* is not found among them, for it is the *Nun* called the **Loving-kindness of Abraham**.

Come and see: at the time when that soul <note>original: "Neshama"</note> departs from this world, it enters into the lower Garden of Eden. Four letters <note>Likely referring to the four letters of the Divine Name, Y-H-W-H</note> stand over it and offer supplication for it before the Holy One, blessed be He. There is a hint here in the phrase: **"The Lord will surely have mercy on him"** <note>original: "Rachem Terachamenu Adonai"</note>. And the soul stands there and is clothed in a single garment that resembles [the body of] this world, because the forms of this world are found there, for the gaze of the Holy One, blessed be He, is constantly upon them. 

From there, that soul departs and goes to stand before the Holy One, blessed be He. It gazes upon that Light which stands above, and it remains there until the time arrives for those bodies to be found in this world. Then the Holy One, blessed be He, prepares that soul to enter into that body, because the form of that body is carved above in the **Secret of Faith**. Because of this, it is found to be called **Loving-kindness**. 

Come and see: if you say that at the time the soul departs from this world and enters the lower Garden of Eden, and enters and gazes above at the light that shines—where is that place where it stands until the time comes for the body to be found below? Come and see: there are three places found where the soul stands.

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Torah portion Vayera (Genesis 18:1) in the Zohar. It follows the previous discussions on Abraham’s journey and focuses here on the mystical significance of his circumcision and the divine revelation that followed.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

**And the Lord appeared to him by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat at the door of the tent in the heat of the day.** <note>Genesis 18:1</note> Rabbi Hiyya opened his discourse and said: **"For the Lord God is a sun and shield; the Lord bestows grace and glory; no good thing does He withhold from those who walk uprightly."** <note>Psalms 84:12</note> This verse has already been established and discussed. But come and see: "For the Lord God is a sun and shield." "Sun and shield" is well-stated. But why "the Lord God" <note>original: "YHVH Elohim"</note>? It is because a sun is never found without a sheath <note>or "case"</note> that shields it. In the same way, the name *Lord* <note>YHVH, representing Mercy</note> is never found without the name *God* <note>Elohim, representing Judgment/Structure</note>. For this reason, He is called "sun and shield."

And the secret of this "sun and shield" is the mystery of the **Holy Covenant** <term>Berit Kadisha; the sign of circumcision</term> which is called "sun." And it is a "shield" to protect a person. And then, "the Lord God bestows grace and glory." Why does it say "the Lord" again at the end? This verse is difficult. Because at the beginning it says "the Lord God," and at the end it says only "the Lord." Rather, "the Lord bestows grace and glory" means: Grace above and Glory below. Grace above is the mystery of the **Righteous One** <term>Tzadik; the divine channel of Yesod</term> who is called "Grace." And Glory below is the **Divine Presence** <term>Shekhinah</term> who is called "Glory," for she is called "the Glory of the Lord." Therefore, "the Lord bestows grace and glory"—referring to the One in whom the Holy Name is complete. "No good thing does He withhold from those who walk uprightly"—this refers to the Righteous One who pours out blessings from above to below.

And regarding this, it is written: "And the Lord appeared to him." To whom does "to him" <note>Hebrew: *elav*</note> refer? This is the Holy Covenant. And the secret of this is that Abraham circumcised himself, and this is the meaning of "appeared to him." And because of this, it happened "by the oaks of Mamre." What are the "oaks of Mamre"? It is the place where Mamre <note>Abraham's ally</note> gave him counsel, <unclear>and for this reason it is called</unclear> so. <unclear>Come and see:</unclear> until Abraham was circumcised, the Holy One, blessed be He, did not speak with him except in the degree of <unclear>a vision</unclear>...

<summary>This page explores the mystical connection between Abraham's circumcision and his merit to receive a direct revelation of the Divine Name. It explains the relationship between the sun and its shield as a metaphor for the union of different aspects of God (Mercy and Judgment).</summary>
<keywords>Abraham, Circumcision, Holy Covenant, Sun and Shield, Divine Names, Shekhinah, Tzadik, Oaks of Mamre</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic commentary on the Book of Genesis, specifically focusing on the aftermath of the primordial sin in the Garden of Eden. It transitions from the nature of Adam's initial state to the necessity of his expulsion to prevent him from grasping eternal life while in a corrupted state.</meta>

## Section: Genesis

...What did he leave and what did he give from this side? For this reason, a person needs to look and gaze into this verse:
> **And the Lord God said: "Behold, the man has become as one of us, to know good and evil; and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever."** <note>Genesis 3:22</note>

What is this saying? When Adam was found in this level we have mentioned, what is the meaning of **"as one of us"**? Rabbi Abba said: **"As one of us"** means like the One who is uniquely attached to the Tree of Life <note>The "One" refers to the Divine unity; Adam originally reflected this singular spiritual focus</note>. And if you say, "But surely he sinned and was withheld from it?" He replied to him: You have spoken well. When he sinned, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: "Behold, he was **as one of us**." For before he sinned, Adam was unique in the world, and he was attached and cleaved to the Tree of Life, and he did not know the "Other Side" <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of evil or impurity</term> at all. But once he sinned and cleaved to the Other Side, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: "Behold, he was **as one of us**" regarding what he was previously. But now, he is "to know good and evil," for he has cleaved to both this and that. He is found to be a knower of both good and evil. And because of this: **"And now, lest he put forth his hand and take also of the Tree of Life."**

What is the meaning of **"And now"**? Rabbi Yehuda said: **"And now"** is necessary because we were [originally] in the world [of eternity]. Now, because he knows good and evil, "lest he put forth his hand," etc. Rabbi Eleazar said: When Adam sinned, that light that shone within him departed from him, and his intellect was diminished. Because of this, it is written "now," lest he put forth his hand. Rabbi Isaac said: The verse comes to show that the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the immanent presence of God</term> would not dwell upon Adam because he was a sinner. For this reason, he was driven out of the Garden of Eden, so that he would not eat from the Tree of Life, which contains life that never ceases. For when he ate from it [the Tree of Knowledge] at first, he sinned because he was found in both this [good] and that [evil].

Rabbi Shimon opened and said:
> **"My son, if your heart be wise, my heart will be glad, even mine."** <note>Proverbs 23:15</note>

Regarding what was this verse said? It is said regarding the time when a person performs the commandment of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Divine Presence dwells upon him. The Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices in that man and calls out regarding him: **"My son, if your heart be wise..."**

Come and see: when Adam sinned and stretched out his hand and took that which was not necessary <note>referring to the forbidden fruit</note>, what is written? **"And the Lord God sent him forth from the Garden of Eden..."**

Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Isaac were walking on the road. Rabbi Yehuda opened and said:
> **"And he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water..."** <note>Psalms 1:3</note>

Fortunate are those who occupy themselves with the Torah <note>original: "Oraita"</note>, for they are like that tree...

<summary>This page explores the ontological change in Adam after the Fall, explaining that his "knowledge of good and evil" created a duality that necessitated his removal from the Tree of Life. It emphasizes that spiritual wisdom and Torah study are the means to restore the lost connection to the Divine.</summary>

<keywords>Adam, Tree of Life, Tree of Knowledge, Good and Evil, Sitra Achra, Shekhinah, Garden of Eden, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, Torah study</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the soul's journey after death, specifically focusing on the "spiritual garments" earned through righteous deeds. It corresponds to the Zohar, Volume I, page 217b, within the portion of Vayechi.</meta>

## The Radiance of the Soul’s Garment

[...of theirs, which are the limbs of the body...]
[...of the Holy One, blessed be He...]

**Rabbi Shimon wept and said:** Woe to the world, for the children of men have closed hearts and sealed eyes; they do not know and do not perceive the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He. See how the wise of heart, through the striking of their eyes by the supernal lights, are filled with vision, their eyes opened to every side. 

Come and see: That soul which a person merits—when it departs from this world, it goes and clothes itself in the radiance of the splendor <note>Aramaic: *Zahara*; refers to a mystical brilliance</note> of that garment created through the commandments of the Torah. It ascends and enters into the Garden of Eden, and in that garment, it appears before its Master. We have established that the guardians of the gates of the Garden of Eden give the soul that garment; it clothes itself in it and stands there in its joy. And the Holy One, blessed be He, calls out concerning it:

-> **Open the gates, that the righteous nation that keeps faithfulness may enter.** <note>Isaiah 26:2</note> <-

Come and see: Every single soul of this world that did not merit to be clothed in the garment of the radiance of splendor does not enter into the Garden of Eden and does not appear before the Holy One, blessed be He. For whoever does not merit to be clothed in that garment of the radiance of splendor is not seen before the Holy One, blessed be He. And regarding this it is written: **And the naked shall not see My face.** <note>A paraphrased mystical application of Exodus 23:15 and 34:20, "None shall appear before Me empty," interpreted here as "empty of garments/deeds."</note> 

Come and see: There is a garment called the "Garment of the Canopy" <note>Aramaic: *Chuppah*; suggesting a bridal or protective covering</note> in which the souls of the righteous were clothed at Mount Sinai. In that same garment, Moses clothed himself when he ascended the mountain, as it is said:

-> **And Moses entered into the midst of the cloud, and went up into the mount.** <note>Exodus 24:18</note> <-

What is the meaning of "into the midst of the cloud"? It means he entered and clothed himself in that cloud. In that garment, he entered into the fire and derived benefit from it. For this reason it is written that the naked shall not see My face. Come and see: When the soul is clothed in this garment, it is worthy to see and enjoy the light that shines above and below. And because of this it is written:

-> **To behold the beauty of the Lord, and to inquire in His temple.** <note>Psalms 27:4</note> <-

And that light is called the "Beauty of the Lord" <term>Noam Y-H-V-H: the pleasantness or sweetness of the Divine</term>, which is the light that comes from the World to Come <note>Aramaic: *Alma d'Atey*; the hidden realm of future reward and spiritual source</note>.

<summary>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai explains that the soul requires a spiritual garment, woven from its performance of the commandments, to enter the Garden of Eden and perceive the Divine light. Without this "radiant garment," the soul remains "naked" and unable to endure the presence of God or the celestial fire.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

**Come and see:** All the people of the world, when they sleep upon their beds and their souls depart from them, they all taste the taste of death. And because they all taste the taste of death, this spirit of impurity is found upon them, for the body remains without a soul. The spirit of impurity is ready and dwells upon it, for it is found in a place that is not under the authority of the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>, but rather remains without a soul. For this reason, a person should not pour water on the hands of another in the morning, for that other person is found with the spirit of impurity upon him; if one pours on his hands, that spirit will deviate from his hands and dwell upon the one who poured. It is forbidden for a person to walk four cubits <note>approximately 6-8 feet</note> without the washing of the hands <term>Netilat Yadayim: the ritual washing of hands to remove spiritual impurity</term> because he is impure. The Holy One, Blessed be He <term>Ha-Kadosh Baruch Hu</term> desires that man should be pure and never become defiled, and regarding this it is written:
> And to Him you shall cling <note>Deuteronomy 10:20</note>

What is the meaning of "And to Him you shall cling"? Is it possible for a human being to cling to the Divine Presence <term>Shekhinah: the feminine, indwelling aspect of God</term>? Is it not written:
> For the Lord your God is a consuming fire <note>Deuteronomy 4:24</note>

Rather, "And to Him you shall cling" means as we have said: that a person should not become defiled, and the **Other Side** <note>original: "Sitra Achra" — the realm of evil or impurity</note> should not dwell upon him. He should be pure, and it is his duty to be pure, for if he comes to purify himself, they assist him from above, and he will be clinging to the Divine Presence constantly, as it is written:
> Sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy <note>Leviticus 11:44</note>

Behold, here is a hint that one who sanctifies himself from below, they sanctify him from above. Now one must look into this matter: one who is holy, certainly his clinging is to the Holy One, Blessed be He. Why? Because holiness is above, and one who is found in holiness is clinging to the holiness above. But the side that is impure is clinging to impurity.
...
<note>The text continues discussing the nature of impurity during sleep and the requirement for ritual purification upon waking.</note>

<summary>This passage from the Zohar explains that during sleep, the soul partially departs, allowing a spirit of impurity to rest on the body. It emphasizes the mystical importance of ritual hand-washing (Netilat Yadayim) immediately upon waking to remove this impurity and maintain a connection to the Divine.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of Parashat Lech Lecha, focusing on the divine names and the nature of the Torah. ## Portion of Lech Lecha

[...these are...]

Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse, quoting: **"For the Lord God is a sun and a shield..."** <note>Psalms 84:12</note>. Come and see: **"A sun and a shield"** refers to <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>The standard Rabbinic title for God, often abbreviated as HKH"B</note>. Just as the sun shines and is ready to provide light, so too <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> shines and is ready to provide light. This "sun" is indeed the celestial sun, as it is written <note>Malachi 3:20</note>: **"But for you who fear My name, the sun of righteousness shall rise with healing in its wings."** And "shield"—this refers to <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> who is called a shield, as it is written <note>Genesis 15:1</note>: **"I am a shield to you."**

And the secret of the matter of **"For the Lord God is a sun and a shield"** is this: **"Sun"** corresponds to the name <term>Y-H-V-H</term> <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God representing Mercy</note>, and **"Shield"** corresponds to the name <term>Elohim</term> <note>The name of God representing Justice and Judgment</note>. For the two of them are as one; sun and shield are united as one, so that the perfection of the <term>Holy Name</term> may be found as is fitting. It is for this reason that He is called "Sun and Shield, Y-H-V-H Elohim." When they are together, the perfection of this Name emerges. Regarding this it is written: **"The Lord will give grace and glory."** When they are as one, **"Grace"** flows from above and **"Glory"** arises from below. **"No good thing does He withhold from those who walk uprightly"**—this refers to the supernal path that shines and moves forward, and is found within the **"Good,"** as it is written <note>Genesis 1:4</note>: **"And God saw the light, that it was good."**

Rabbi Elazar was sitting before his father, Rabbi Shimon. He said to him: It is written <note>Psalms 2:12</note>: **"Kiss the son [Bar], lest He be angry and you perish in the way."** What is the meaning of **"Kiss the son"**? He replied: "Kiss the son" refers to the secret of the <term>Torah</term> which is called "Bar" <note>The Aramaic word 'Bar' can mean 'Son' or 'Pure'</note>, just as it is written <note>Psalms 2:11</note>: **"Serve the Lord with fear..."** and then it is written **"Kiss the son."** Why is it called "Bar"? As it is written <note>Psalms 24:4</note>: **"He who has clean hands and a pure [Bar] heart,"** and it is written <note>Song of Songs 6:9</note>: **"She is the pure [Barah] one of her who bore her."** This refers to the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note> who is called "Bar."

**Rabbi Yitzchak said:** "Bar" refers to the Torah, as we have said, for it is written: **"Kiss the son."** And if you ask—regarding what we said that this is the secret of the Torah—why then is it written **"Lest He be angry"**? He replied: Anyone who does not labor in the <term>Torah</term>, which is beloved to the Holy One, Blessed be He, causes anger to fill the world against him. Because the Torah is the peace of the world, when one does not labor in it, anger fills [the world]. **"And you perish in the way,"** as it is written <note>Psalms 1:6</note>: **"But the way of the wicked shall perish,"** for such a person has no path or way to walk upon. **"Happy are all those who take refuge in Him."**

<summary>This page explores the mystical unity between the Divine Names Y-H-V-H and Elohim using the metaphor of a sun and shield, and interprets the word "Bar" (Son/Pure) as a reference to both the Torah and the Shekhinah.</summary>
<keywords>Sun and Shield, Divine Names, Torah study, Shekhinah, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, Psalm 2, Light and Protection</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic commentary on the Torah portion Mishpatim (Laws).
