## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Do not be righteous**<-
overmuch, neither make yourself overwise; why should you destroy yourself? <note>Ecclesiastes 7:16</note>
Come and see: The Holy One, blessed be He, <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> gave man the path of life and the path of death.
And He gave him the counsel of the Torah <note>original: "Oraita"</note> which teaches a person when he is meritorious and when he sins. For when a person sins,
he causes a defect in his own soul. And when he is meritorious, he adds strength to appear before his Master. And as for what is said, **"Do not be righteous
overmuch,"** is there then a pious man <note>original: "Chasid"</note> who should not be as righteous as he possibly can? Rather, we have established it thus: when he separates himself
and acts overwise beyond measure. This is one who makes himself like someone who has the authority to decree judgment
and to judge more than is required. And when he does this, he causes evil to his own soul, because it says **"Do not be righteous overmuch"**
so that you do not bring guilt upon your soul. Rather, act as one who has the authority to judge. And there is a wise man who does not act overwise.
And you might ask: how do we know that when a person sins, he defects his soul? As it is written:
> But as for me, I will walk in my integrity; redeem me, and be gracious to me. <note>Psalms 26:11</note>
What does "be gracious to me" <note>original: "chaneni"</note> mean? It is as you would say: "and he shall be gracious and pay." <note>note: implying a restoration of what was lost or damaged</note>
And when he acts thus, a man is called "pious." Rabbi Yose said, for it is written:
> It is well with the man who is gracious and lends. <note>Psalms 112:5</note>
And when he is pious, it is written:
> For this let every pious man pray to You in a time of finding. <note>Psalms 32:6</note>
What is the **"time of finding"**? <note>original: "et matzo"</note> Rabbi Eleazar said: this refers to the Woman <note>note: a reference to the Shekhinah, the feminine Divine Presence</note>, and when does she have a "time"? When she is ready to receive what
is taught. And when she is taught and filled with all goodness, she is called "a time of finding." Furthermore, when a person is meritorious,
 the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> walks with him. Because the Divine Presence dwells within him, a person has no right to defect
his soul; and one who defects his soul because of sin, it is as if he caused a defect in the Divine Presence. And if
you say this causes a defect in the Divine Presence, come and see Phinehas, who was zealous for the Holy One, blessed be He; what is written
of him?
> Behold, I give to him My covenant of peace. <note>Numbers 25:12</note>
For Peace <note>note: the Sefirah of Yesod</note> was joined to him and he acquired it. And when does one acquire it? When he sins, he defects it, and when is it perfected?
When he is pious and performs kindness, and the Holy One, blessed be He, gives him the Divine Presence and Peace is joined to him. And regarding
this it is written that the Divine Presence is revealed when he is pious. Rabbi Isaac said: When Rabbi Eleazar came, he saw
Rabbi Shimon saying:

->**All the days**<-
of the poor are evil, but he who is of a merry heart has a continual feast. <note>Proverbs 15:15</note> What is the **"poor"**? <note>original: "ani"</note> Rabbi Eleazar opened and said:
this is one who is poor in Torah and poor in commandments. But it is written:
> Neither shall you favor a poor man in his cause. <note>Exodus 23:3</note>
What is the **"poor man"** <note>original: "dal"</note> here? We have established that this is the <term>Evil Inclination</term> <note>original: "Yetzer ha-Ra"</note>. For he is "low" and he is "poor" in the commandments of the Torah, for he
has no authority in them at all. And when is he poor? When he dwells within a wicked man who has no
commandments of the Torah. And regarding this it is written **"All the days of the poor are evil."** These are the days of the wicked
who walk in an evil path. And who are the "days of the poor"? These are the <term>Husks</term> <note>original: "Klipot" - the shells of impurity that conceal holiness</note> of uncleanness that cover
the <term>Divine Presence</term> <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> because of the sins of mankind. For these Husks cause her to be found
impoverished and without blessings. And we have established that this is the "poor one" who has no light except by means of
the Torah and the blessings from above. And all those "evil days" go without kindness and without
blessings. "But he who is of a merry heart has a continual feast"—this is the <term>Good Inclination</term> <note>original: "Yetzer ha-Tov"</note> which is watered constantly
by the Torah and the blessings from above. And this one is "rich," for he has all blessings and all
goodness. And he has a "continual feast" because he has importance before the Holy One, blessed be He.

<summary>This page discusses how human sin or merit directly impacts the soul and the Shekhinah (Divine Presence), interpreting the "poor man" as the Evil Inclination and the "merry heart" as the Good Inclination nourished by Torah.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Sabbath from the Zohar, specifically focusing on the elevation of the spiritual realms into the Sefirah of Binah (Understanding), often called the "Upper World" or "World to Come."</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

...Because she <note>referring to the Shekhinah or the Sabbath Queen</note> ascends from within the multitude and stands opposite it, for all blessings above and below are blessed from him <note>the foundation/source</note>. Because within him the beginning of all is joined, and from him flow and emerge all blessings. At that time, he is called **Holy of Holies** <note>original: *Kodesh Kodashim*</note> and shines backward until all those levels are formed and ascend upward from the multitude, clinging to one another. Then it is called **Sabbath**, as we have established. For behold, the Upper Sabbath is the Sabbath of the Sabbath Eve <note>The "Upper Sabbath" refers to the Sefirah of Binah, while "Sabbath Eve" refers to the lower Shekhinah</note>. And because of this, all those armaments <note>spiritual forces or "garments"</note> that were prepared above and were separated from within the Upper Sabbath, they all come to the Sabbath day. And because all the limbs of the body are all clinging to it on the Sabbath, therefore it is a day of souls and not a day of the body. Because of this, it is a day of joy—the joy of all. On this day, all levels, supports, and hosts are sanctified with the holiness of the King, with the holiness of the Sabbath. And these are the **Five Voices** <note>original: *Chamsha Kalin*</note> which are all one, and each one is five, and one voice is heard from within the five. These five spread out to every side. One voice brings forth five, and these five are those that flow and are drawn from the World to Come <note>original: *Alma de-Atei*, referring to the realm of Binah</note>. And for this reason, there are five prayers on this day <note>referring to the five services of Yom Kippur, which is the "Sabbath of Sabbaths"</note> corresponding to these five voices. Five sanctifications <note>original: *Kedushot*</note>, because he is holy and within him the Holy of Holies is joined. On this day, the world is sanctified with an upper holiness, and then holiness is added upon holiness. Fortunate is the portion of Israel who inherit this inheritance. And regarding this it is written:
> And you shall call the Sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, honorable (Isaiah 58:13)
<note>Zohar identifies 'Holy to YHVH' with Yom Kippur/Binah</note>
What is "the holy of the Lord, honorable"? This is Yom Kippur <note>The Day of Atonement</note>, which is the "holy of the Lord, honorable," in which there is no eating or drinking, and in it, he is called "Honor." Because this day is called "Honor" since it includes the five voices as one. And this day is the "holy of the Lord" because the Holy of Holies is joined within it, and then it is "honorable." And regarding this it is written:
> A Psalm, a Song for the Sabbath day (Psalms 92:1)
"A Psalm, a Song." This is the day from which the Torah emerges. "A Song." This is the day in which the five voices of the Torah are included. For it is the day from which everything emerges. Because within it is joined...

<summary>This passage explains the mystical nature of the Sabbath as a day of the soul rather than the body, linking it to the "Five Voices" of the Torah and the sanctity of Yom Kippur. It describes the flow of divine blessing from the "Upper Sabbath" (Binah) down to the lower realms.</summary>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

[... Come and see:] Just as the Tabernacle <term>Mishkan; the portable sanctuary built by the Israelites in the desert</term> exists below, [so it exists above.]
And everything is according to this pattern. [And because of this, in every place]
where there is a Tabernacle, it is the mystery [of the body, in this very likeness.]
[There is a Tabernacle above and there is] a Tabernacle below. [And come and see] the mystery of the Tabernacle:
It is just like all the limbs <term>sheyfin; refers to both limbs and organs</term> of the body [of human beings.]
[They all stand, limb upon limb, and are joined] one to another,
[and they are a single body. So too the Tabernacle:] it is all made of various limbs,
[and they are joined one to another, and it is a single body.]
[...]
Just as it is with human beings, who possess limbs
both large and small, and they are levels upon levels <note>original: "dargin al dargin"</note>
joined one to another to form a single body—in this same way
are all the works of the Tabernacle. They are all various limbs,
and they are according to the pattern of that which is above. When that body is completed
with all those limbs, only then does the spirit rest upon it.
So too with the Tabernacle: when it is completed with all those limbs,
only then does the [Divine Presence <note>Shekhinah</note> / Holy One, Blessed be He] rest upon it.
[...] from this side [...]
[...] it is [...]
[...] from which was created [...]
[...] which is [...]
[...] because of this [...]
[...] and this is [...]
[...] in this likeness [...]
[...] and because of this [...]
[...] in every place [...]

<summary>This passage from the Zohar explains that the Tabernacle is a physical manifestation of a divine "body," mirroring the structure of both the human form and the celestial realms. It emphasizes that the Divine Presence only dwells within the structure once all its constituent parts are perfectly joined together as a unified whole.</summary>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

->**And it came to pass on the eighth day**<-

**Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse** <note>quoting Psalms 107:8</note> >"Let them praise the Lord for His goodness, and for His wonders to the children of men."<
Come and see: every single day the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> is prepared to be in the joy of the Assembly of Israel <note>original: "Knesset Yisrael," a mystical term for the Divine Presence or Shekhinah</note> in order to delight in those souls of the righteous that enter before Him. It is as the verse says <note>Isaiah 14:14 - with a variation in the phrasing</note> "I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the Most High." When a soul departs from this world, it enters into those places it is required to enter until it reaches the Garden of Eden. And in the Garden of Eden, the righteous delight in it, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, delights in them.

And that day which is the "eighth" is a day that is the completion of all. Come and see: on the day that the Tabernacle <note>original: "Mishkana"</note> was established below, in that same manner the Tabernacle was completed above. On that day, there was joy before the Holy One, Blessed be He, such as there had not been since the day the world was created. For it is written <note>Leviticus 9:1</note> **"And it came to pass on the eighth day."** "And it came to pass" <note>original: "Vayehi"</note>. Rabbi Yose said: everywhere the word "Vayehi" appears, it is a language of sorrow. Why is there sorrow here? It is because until this moment, the world had not been perfected as was fitting. But on this day, the world was perfected. Thus it is found that this day was like the day on which heaven and earth were created.

Come and see: during all those seven days of consecration <note>original: "shivat yemei ha-miluim"</note>, the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> did not dwell in the Tabernacle until this day. And on this day, the glory of the Holy One, Blessed be He, was revealed to all the people, as it is written <note>Leviticus 9:23</note> >"And the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people."< And because of this, it is written "And it came to pass" <note>Vayehi</note>, for until now the world had not yet settled upon its foundation.

Rabbi Yehuda said: when the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world, it did not stand upon its foundation until Adam was created. Once Adam was created, it was found that he was the foundation of the entire world. Here too, even though the Tabernacle was built, it did not stand upon its foundation until the Priest <note>original: "Kahana," referring to Aaron</note> was prepared for the service of the Holy One, Blessed be He. And on this day, everything was completed.

<summary>This page discusses the mystical significance of the eighth day of the Tabernacle's inauguration, comparing the completion of the sanctuary to the creation of the world and the first man. It explains that the Divine Presence only fully rested upon the community once the priestly service began.</summary>

<keywords>Tabernacle, Eighth Day, Shekhinah, Creation, Aaron the Priest, Garden of Eden, Souls of the Righteous, Joy and Sorrow</keywords>

### Summary and Commentary
This manuscript page contains a portion of the Zohar on the Torah portion **Vayishlach** (And He Sent). 

1.  **The Mystery of Holiness:** The upper half of the page discusses the nature of the "Holy" (<term>Kadosh<gloss>The Hebrew word for "Holy," often associated with the divine attribute of Beauty or Tiferet</gloss></term>) and why the angels and the people of Israel recite the <term>Kedushah<gloss>The "Sanctification" prayer where humans mimic the angelic choir</gloss></term>. It explains that "Holy" signifies the elevation of all things into a unified divine source.
2.  **The Dots on "And he kissed him":** The lower half focuses on the verse: 
    > "And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and **kissed him**: and they wept." (Genesis 33:4)
    The Zohar notes the dots (<term>nekudot<gloss>Scribal markings placed above specific words in the Torah scroll</gloss></term>) over the word **And he kissed him** (<note>original: "Vayishakehu"</note>). Rabbi Simeon bar Yochai and his colleagues discuss whether this kiss was an act of genuine love (<term>rehimuta<gloss>Aramaic for love or affection</gloss></term>) or a remnant of Esau's eternal enmity. They use these scribal marks to uncover the hidden spiritual dynamics between the "Other Side" (the realm of spiritual impurity represented by Esau) and the realm of holiness (represented by Jacob).

<summary>This page explores the mystical meaning of the Kedushah prayer and interprets the symbolic dots over the word 'Vayishakehu' in the story of Jacob and Esau's reunion.</summary>
<keywords>Zohar, Vayishlach, Kedushah, Jacob and Esau, Vayishakehu, scribal dots, Kabbalah, holiness, angels</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the spiritual purification of the Levites as described in the Zohar on the Torah portion Behaalotcha. It focuses on the metaphysical transition from the sin of the Golden Calf to the establishment of the Tabernacle, emphasizing the Levites' role in the "Left Side" (the attribute of Judgment).</meta>

# Behaalotcha

And because of this, it is written <note>Numbers 18:22</note> **"The children of Israel shall no longer come near the Tent of Meeting, lest they bear sin and die."** Now, we have established that they [the Levites] are the ones who draw near to this Tabernacle. And because of this, it is written <note>Numbers 17:28</note> **"Everyone who comes near, who comes near to the Tabernacle of the Lord, shall die."** Therefore, those who draw closer must be more cautious. Come and see: on the day the children of Israel sinned with the Calf, they became attached to the side of death. As it is said <note>Psalms 82:6-7</note> **"I said, 'You are angels, and all of you are sons of the Most High'; but like men you shall die."** And the <term>Other Side</term> <note>original: "Sitra Achra," referring to the realm of evil or impurity</note> became mixed among them. But then the Levites were recognized by their banners, and all of them were clinging to the <term>Holy Name</term>. The <term>Other Side</term> did not become mixed among them. Then the Holy One, blessed be He, said <note>Numbers 8:14</note> **"And the Levites shall be Mine."** What is the meaning of **"And they shall be Mine"**? It is as you say <note>Job 9:28</note> **"I know that You will not hold me innocent."** <note>The Hebrew word for "to me/Mine" (Li) is linked here to the attribute of Judgment</note> What is **"Mine"**? This is the <term>Side of the Left</term> <note>original: "Sitra de-Smala," the divine attribute of Gevurah or Strength/Judgment</note>. For this side rules over them, and because of this, **"And the Levites shall be Mine."** And it is all one. What is "one"? Because this one is on the left and that one is on the right. And because of this, the secret is made known. And when he said more: Come and see, on the day the Tabernacle was established below, Moses established it. And your sign is <note>Exodus 40:18</note> **"And Moses established the Tabernacle."** It was established by the hand of Moses. And this is the secret we have established, as it is written <note>Psalms 127:1</note> **"If the Lord does not build a house, its builders labor in vain."** And this refers to Moses. Because he was found in this place, the Tabernacle stood. And at the time it stood, the Levites raised up a song in order to cling to their side above and below. And because the Levite clings to the Left, peace was then found. And come and see: on this day, the Holy One, blessed be He, clung to this Tabernacle. As it is said <note>Numbers 9:15</note> **"And on the day the Tabernacle was established."** For we have learned: what is the meaning of **"on the day the Tabernacle was established"**? For it had already been established previously! Rather, on this day, peace was found in the world. And because of this, it is written <note>Leviticus 9:23</note> **"And Moses and Aaron went into the Tent of Meeting, and they came out and blessed the people, and the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people."** And then joy was found above and below.

Rabbi Shimon opened and said <note>Psalms 51:4</note> **"Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin."** What is <margin>The Discourse of the Levites</margin> **"thoroughly"**? Because when a person sins, just as the guilt is found above, it is found below. For a <term>spirit of impurity</term> <note>original: "Ruach Mesava"</note> rests upon that person. And at the time he comes to be purified, he must be purified from this side and from that side. Regarding this, David said, **"Wash me thoroughly."** Come and see: at the time the Priest enters the Sanctuary, he then needs to be purified even more, because he stands to offer the sacrifice and to purify the sins of man. And regarding this, it is written <note>Leviticus 16:24</note> **"And he shall wash his flesh with water in a holy place."** And for this, he needs to be sanctified with the holiness of his Master. And the secret of this is what is written <note>Zechariah 3:3</note> **"And Joshua was clothed in filthy garments."** And this is why a person needs to be purified, and their clothing needs to be found clean. And because of this, the Levites, who come from the <term>Side of the Left</term>, needed to be purified even more, as it is written <note>Numbers 8:7</note> **"And thus you shall do to them to purify them: sprinkle the water of purification upon them."** And they were required to remove [shave] their hair, because hair comes from the side of <term>Harsh Judgment</term> <note>original: "Dina Kashya"</note>. And because of this, they were required to remove the hair. Come and see: at the time the Levites are prepared for their <term>service</term> <note>original: "Pulchana," divine worship</note>, they then need to remove—

<summary>This page explains the spiritual necessity for the Levites' rigorous purification, linking their service to the "Left Side" of divine Judgment and the removal of "Harsh Judgment" symbolized by hair. It highlights the transition from the spiritual death caused by the Golden Calf to the restoration of peace through the Tabernacle's establishment.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the Torah portion Miketz (Genesis 41:1–44:17). The text explores the mystical relationship between the various "Chariots" (celestial arrays) and the Divine Name, transitioning into a symbolic analysis of Joseph's actions toward his brothers and the pregnancy of Tamar.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

We have learned: When we were sitting before Rabbi Shimon, he said to us: When those holy chariots <note>original: *retichin*—the celestial structures or "vehicles" of divine energy</note> all join together as one, lights revolve within lights by the permission of their Master. One supreme chariot is found, which is the "Light of Uprightness"; it is a harsh light that rises upward. This is the mystery of a single chariot when all the chariots are joined as one. This chariot is called by the name of His holy name; it is the supreme chariot called *Adonai* <note>The Divine Name associated with the Sefirah of Malchut/Kingship</note>.

This mystery is called a "parable" <note>original: *mashal*</note>. Why is it called a parable? Because through it, the radiance of the Holy One, Blessed be He, becomes known to them, for no human being is able to perceive or see Him directly; therefore, it is called a parable. As it is said:
> (Song of Songs 5:16) His palate is sweetness, and he is altogether desirable; this is my beloved and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

For behold, they all cleave to Him and they tremble before Him. What is the mystery of this? It is that all the lights that shine send their radiance into that one light, and it is a "parable" over them all. He is "Holy, Holy, Holy," and is blessed from Him when He joins as one with the Supreme Light. The Holy One, Blessed be He, is perfect, and He is the one called a "parable" over all. When those chariots tremble before Him, they open their mouths and say:
> (Ezekiel 3:12) Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place.

And when they all join together as one, then He is called "Lord of all the earth." We have learned: At first, all the chariots that are on the outside shake and tremble and fear before Him; but when they all join in Him as one, then "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place" is said, and then He is called "Lord of all the earth." And it is written:
**And he took** Simeon from them and bound him before their eyes. <note>Genesis 42:24</note> What is the meaning of "And he took"? It is as it says:
> (Leviticus 9:3) Take for yourselves a male calf for a sin offering.

Here too, "And he took"—he took him from them to be under his own authority. "And he bound him before their eyes"—he placed him before their eyes so they would know that he had sinned against their father, and for this reason "he bound him." "Before their eyes"—so that they could see his punishment. Come and see: Joseph knew that their punishment was deserved because of their selling of him, and he wanted to show them that when a man sins before the Holy One, Blessed be He, he is delivered into the hands of those who confront him. And it is written:
**And it was** about three months later, and it was told to Judah, saying: "Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the harlot." <note>Genesis 38:24</note> The Rabbis have established that at that moment when Judah was found righteous in judgment, that accusation against him was silenced. Because Joseph guarded the Covenant <note>original: *Brit*—referring to sexual purity and the Sefirah of Yesod</note> and Judah merited to bring the Covenant out into the open <note>referring to the birth of his sons</note>. Therefore, that accusation was handed over to Joseph, and it came to be settled through him. Therefore: "And it was about three months later." Come and see what is written:
> (Genesis 38:27) And it came to pass at the time of her giving birth, that behold, there were twins in her womb.

And it is written elsewhere:
> (Genesis 25:24) And behold, there were twins in her womb. <note>Referring to Rebekah</note>

What is the difference between this one and that one? Come and see: regarding Tamar, "twins" <note>original: *te'omim*</note> is written in full <note>with the letters Aleph and Vav</note>, whereas regarding Rebekah it is written deficiently <note>original: *tomim*, lacking the Aleph</note>. This is because regarding Tamar, she was worthy that two kings should come forth from her to the world: Perez and Zerah, and from one of them comes King David. We have learned: At the moment Tamar entered to approach the judgment, Judah was at that moment afraid and trembling; at that moment...

<summary>This page provides a Kabbalistic interpretation of the Divine Name 'Adonai' as a 'parable' for the unknowable God, and links the biblical stories of Joseph and Judah through the themes of judgment, the 'Covenant,' and the righteous lineage of Tamar.</summary>
<keywords>Chariots, Adonai, Joseph, Judah, Tamar, Twins, Covenant, King David, Divine Lights, Judgment</keywords>

**Rabbi Eleazar opened his discourse and said:** >**“Teach me, O Lord, Your way; I will walk in Your truth; unite my heart to fear Your name”**< <note>Psalms 86:11</note>. This 
verse must be examined. Did King David not know the ways of the Holy One, Blessed Be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu," a standard Aramaic name for God</note>, 
that he should say **“Teach me, O Lord, Your way”**? Indeed, many times he said, **“Teach me, O Lord, Your way.”** Rather, David said before the Holy One, Blessed Be He: Master of the Universe, 
the way of the Holy One, Blessed Be He, is not like the way of human beings. For when human beings do a kindness 
with another person, they boast about it, and this is the way of human beings. But 
the Holy One, Blessed Be He, is not so. Rather, He loves everyone and has pity on everyone. And concerning this 
he said: **“Teach me, O Lord, Your way. I will walk in Your truth.”** This is the way of truth. **“Unite 
my heart to fear Your name.”** What is the meaning of **“unite my heart”**? Rather, David said: let my heart be unified from all 
the distractions of the world, and let my heart not be divided here and there, but rather be singular 
in You. Because a person possesses two inclinations: the <term>Good Inclination</term> <note>Yetzer Tov: the impulse toward moral and divine good</note> and the <term>Evil Inclination</term> <note>Yetzer Hara: the impulse toward selfish or physical desires</note>. And David desired 
that these two inclinations should be united in one will to fear His name. And concerning this he said: 
**“Unite my heart to fear Your name.”** Come and see: what is different here where it is written **“And He called to Moses”** 
and it is not written "And the Lord called to Moses"? It is because He called to him from the <term>grade</term> <note>original: "Darga," referring to a specific level or Sefirah in the divine hierarchy</note> of Moses, 
which is his own level. As it were, He called Moses to the <term>grade</term> that is the level of Moses...

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Book of Leviticus (Vayikra). The previous context likely established the relationship between the soul's ascent and the divine call. ## Main Text (Zohar)

It is found that they take them below because this is the image <note>original: *dyukna*, meaning a divine form or prototype</note> of that which is above. 
And the soul from above remained, for they did not find a way to take it. 
Until they bring it down to a place where a certain bird is revealed; one of its wings is on this side and its other wing is on that side. 
And he takes it and gathers it with another and carries it, saying to it: "I adjure you, O wings of the bird, 
beautiful and prepared, that you shall ascend above and see who is your redeemer, and you shall go and return to your place." 
In this manner, the holy soul is placed upon this bird, which is Metatron <note>The supreme archangel and celestial scribe in Kabbalistic tradition</note>, 
who goes out from that palace which emerges from beneath that Throne <note>The Throne of Glory</note>. And he is the place found before the soul 
which is from above, and he bestows perfect joy. And this bird, which is Metatron, takes it and brings it before the Holy One, 
blessed be He. And there it sees what it sees. Because of this, it is found that He is holy and His dwellings are holy; 
there are dwellers within and dwellers without. Those without are the dwellers of the bird. Those within are the holy soul.

And regarding this it is written, **"And He called to Moses"** <note>Leviticus 1:1</note>. The "calling" from above was the Holy One, blessed be He, who called to him, 
because everything is found within the Palace, and from the Palace the voice is heard, and this is the meaning of "And He called." 
Come and see: there is no service like the service of human beings at the time when they pray their prayers in their place. 
In the days of King Solomon, when human beings were virtuous, the action below was in the likeness of that which is above. 
And when he desired to know all those supernal secrets, the wisdom of Solomon would come, and he desired 
to know those supernal matters and actions. It was found before King Solomon—he knew through his wisdom—
that everything is found in the likeness of that which is above. And everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, made on earth, all of it 
is but a reflection of that which is above. And of everything He made above, there is not a small thing that does not have a counterpart 
below on earth. And because of this, all the worlds are bound one to another. And regarding this it is written, **"And He called to 
Moses,"** as we have established, from that supernal holiness. He called to him from within the Palace. Because 
it is found that he [Moses] is this holy secret. As it is written: 
-> "But I, through Your great love, will enter Your house; I will bow down toward Your holy temple in awe of You" <note>Psalm 5:8</note>. <- 
"Enter Your holy temple." And all this is so that everything shall be on the side of holiness. 
And come and see: once human beings sinned and the Palace was nullified and the supernal holiness departed, as it were, and when 
the Sanctuary below was destroyed, it was found that everything was nullified, and as it were, the work above was nullified, and on...

## Main Text (Zohar)

The term **"Burden"** <note>original: "Massa" (משא); in Hebrew, this means both a prophetic oracle and a physical weight or burden</note> implies that this secret is found within those **three husks** <note>term: "Husks" (Qelipin); the Kabbalistic shells of evil that conceal the inner light of holiness</note> of the **primordial serpent**, who is evil and intensely evil. From him, all other evils in the entire world branch out. He is the **"end of thought"** <note>A mystical concept suggesting that the lowest point of the demonic realm is the final manifestation of their dark intentions</note> of all those who reside on this side. <note>Cf. Zohar III:204b</note> Regarding this, it is said: "He shall rebuke the face of the wicked," and the "wrathful face of the wicked" is on this side. The end of all is **Lilith**, who is the "end of thought" of them all; she is a sharp husk derived from the primordial serpent that emerged outward. This is the secret of this level upon which the **"Burden"** rests, which comes from the smoke of a light that is not found <note>i.e., a dark, non-existent light or a "black light" that lacks holiness</note>.

She takes the spirit of the thought of the thorn, which is the end of all levels. It is the level of the "wrathful face of the wicked" and the "end of thought" for those wicked ones who walk on this side. And behold, we have said that all of them are found in this level. The term **"Burden"** rises and signifies that it is the "end of thought." Some say that on this side, there are **husks within husks**. Certainly, all of them exist within the **Other Side** <note>term: "Sitra Achra"; the realm of evil or the demonic "Left Side" in Kabbalistic thought</note>, for on the side of holiness, this is not found at all.

For behold, all things are under the authority of the **Holy One, Blessed be He**; even when the wicked perform evil, they exist within the "Other Side," and it entangles them. Regarding this, it says that there are times when they exist on the **Left Side**, and the side of holiness is not found there at all. Come and see: all the levels on this side exist in a form of unity and are not separated. The "Master of Thought," which is the spirit that entangles, all exist as one.

Because of this, we call them the "end of thought." Because of the smoke of the light, they are not separated, for it is the end of all. Therefore, he is stuck within it, and there is no one to hinder him. Regarding this, it is written: *The wrathful face of the wicked, He shall rebuke them* <note>A composite or paraphrased reference to the divine judgment against the forces of the "Other Side"</note>. In this level, all the wicked exist; those who are on this side have no flaw <note>meaning they are entirely composed of "flaw" or impurity, leaving no room for repair</note>, and therefore they have no healing at all. The "Master who is stuck within it," who is the "end of thought," is on this side, and from him, all branch out. All of them come from the **primordial serpent**, who is the head of all that is on this side. And regarding this, it is written...

## Main Text (The Zohar)

...for if the Holy One, Blessed be He, were to look upon this world <note>in its current state of impurity</note>, there would be no rest within it. For then it is written: **He will swallow up death forever; and the Lord God will wipe away tears from off all faces** (Isaiah 25:8).
At that time, the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to remove the spirit of impurity from the world, as it is said: **And I will cause the spirit of impurity to pass out of the land** (Zechariah 13:2).
And then the earth shall remain in a settled state as is fitting, as it is written: **And my people shall dwell in a peaceable habitation, and in sure dwellings, and in quiet resting places** (Isaiah 32:18).
Until the Holy One, Blessed be He, looks upon this world and renews it as it was at the beginning.

-> ## Vayeshev (And He Dwelt) <-

**And Jacob dwelt in the land of his father’s sojournings, in the land of Canaan** (Genesis 37:1). Rabbi Hiyya opened <note>a formal discourse</note> saying: **Many are the evils of the righteous, but the Lord delivers him out of them all** (Psalms 34:20).
How many "evils" are done to the righteous in this world? Evils? What are these "evils"? Rather, these are literal evils that come from the <term>Other Side</term> <note>original: "Sitra Achra," the realm of spiritual impurity or demonic forces</note>.
And because of this, they are called "evils." But the Holy One, Blessed be He, delivers them from them all. Come and see: how many righteous and pious ones are there in the world who are not reached by these evils at all?
Rather, this verse says as follows: "Many are the evils of the Righteous." Who is "the Righteous"? This refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He, who is called "Righteous," as it is said: **The Lord is righteous in the midst thereof; He will not do iniquity** (Zephaniah 3:5). And what is meant by "many evils"? These are the things that come from the Side Above. As it is said: **And multiplies my wounds without cause** (Job 9:17). And what are these "evils"? These are actually merits <note>or "purifications"</note>. As it is said: **He that spares his rod hates his son; but he that loves him chastens him betimes** (Proverbs 13:24).
Because the Holy One, Blessed be He, loves the righteous man, He gives him a cup of bitterness to drink. As it is said: **As a man chastens his son, so the Lord your God chastens you** (Deuteronomy 8:5).
And all this is in order to purify him so that he may be absorbed into the <term>World to Come</term> <note>original: "Alma de-Atei," the spiritual realm of reward</note>. **And Jacob dwelt.** Rabbi Pinchas opened saying: **They that go down to the sea in ships...** (Psalms 107:23).
Come and see: at the hour when the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world, He placed it upon pillars. And who are these pillars? They are the seven pillars upon which the world stands, as it is said: **She has hewn out her seven pillars** (Proverbs 9:1). And what is that which stands upon them? This is the "Righteous One" <note>referring to the Sefirah of Yesod</note> upon whom the world stands.
As it is said: **But the righteous is an everlasting foundation** (Proverbs 10:25). And the earth stands upon that Righteous One, and he waters her and satiates her in every place.
And he brings forth for her fruits and produce. And who is this "Righteous One" upon whom the world stands? This is the <term>Holy Covenant</term> <note>original: "Berit Kadisha," often referring to the sign of circumcision and the Sefirah of Yesod</note>, which is the Righteous One upon whom the world stands.
And come and see: in this same manner it is below. At the time when a righteous man is found in the world, the Holy One, Blessed be He, rejoices in this world.
And He blesses it because of that righteous man. And in the time when there are righteous ones in the world, the world stands in its existence and fears nothing.
**And Jacob dwelt.** Rabbi Shimon opened saying: **Thy people also shall be all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever...** (Isaiah 60:21). Come and see: Jacob was a "Righteous One," because the Holy Covenant was fulfilled through him. For it is written: **Thou wilt perform the truth to Jacob, and the mercy to Abraham** (Micah 7:20). And his image was like the image of the first man, Adam.
And when the Holy One, Blessed be He, created Adam, the world was established through him. But when Adam sinned, the world <unclear>shuddered</unclear>...

->**Leviticus**<-
> **And He called to Moses, and the Lord spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying** <note>Leviticus 1:1</note>

Rabbi Judah opened the discussion: Come and see, what is different here that it is written **"And He called to Moses"** first, and afterward **"and the Lord spoke to him"**? For in all other places it is written, "And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying." Rather, it is because Moses was attached on high in a place where there is no separation at all. And the secret of the matter is that **"And He called to Moses"** refers to a calling <note>original: "keriah"</note> that comes from above...

---

> **And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder was set upon the earth, and its top reached to heaven; and behold, angels of God were ascending and descending on it** <note>Genesis 28:12</note>

Come and see that ladder which stands upon the earth and its top reaches to heaven. What is this ladder? This is the ladder to which all other levels <note>original: "madregan"</note> are bound. And the secret of the matter is that it is the mystery of that place called "Ladder." And it "stands upon the earth"—what is this? This is the earthly Jerusalem below. And "its top reaches to heaven"—this is the heavenly Jerusalem above that stands over against it. <term>Angels of God</term> <note>original: "Malakhei Elohim"; divine messengers or spiritual forces</note> were ascending and descending on it. They ascend first and afterward they descend. Come and see: those messengers that the Holy One, blessed be He, sends into this world, who emerge from Him—they all ascend by means of this ladder...

---

> **And Jacob awoke from his sleep, and he said: "Surely the Lord is in this place, and I did not know it"** <note>Genesis 28:16</note>

Come and see: when Jacob said this, he was terrified and said, **"Surely the Lord is in this place."** What is the meaning of **"Surely"** <note>original: "Akhen"</note>? It is as you would say, "Surely the people are grass" or "Surely like men you shall die." This is a word that exists within the secret of faith <note>original: "meimanuta"</note>... <unclear>the Divine Presence (Shekhinah)</unclear> dwells in this place and I did not know.

## Main Text (Zohar)

...to the dream and does not see it. And if you should say: behold, we see from the pursuit of Laban, who went after Jacob after five days, that he opened for his own existence joy and a vision of merit; and because of this, the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>, made an opening in him and a voice in his ears. And all this was because the Holy One, Blessed be He, had pity on that opening from which emerged that deed which Laban thought to do. And you see that Laban was wicked, yet the Holy One, Blessed be He, appeared to him in a dream of the night. However, it is because he is the "opening of those two nostrils" <note>A reference to the spiritual anatomy of the "Other Side" or the lower levels of emanation</note>, and He appeared to him at that time and opened for him an opening in which no other dream was found, for the sake of the love of Jacob. Rabbi Isaac opened his discourse and said:
> **"Had not the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Dread of Isaac, been with me, surely now you would have sent me away empty-handed. God has seen my affliction and the labor of my hands, and He gave judgment last night."** <note>Genesis 31:42</note>

Come and see: because the Holy One, Blessed be He, had pity on that opening and loved him as we have said, for this reason He appeared to Laban. Rabbi Isaac said: When people awaken from their sleep, does the Holy One, Blessed be He, not see them? He said to him: Those who enter the cave <note>Likely referring to the Cave of Machpelah or a spiritual state of deep meditation</note> see the Holy One, Blessed be He, face to face. He said to him: Come and see, when a man sleeps, he knows Him through a dream; and that which he saw, the Holy One, Blessed be He, performed in him, and He is the support and the shepherd, appearing to him so that he may cleave to Him. And if you should say he did not know the opening or anything at all—he saw, and He opened it for him, for the dream is revealed upon that opening. Once he sees it, he is bound to it, and He opens for him an opening to see the wisdom of the dream. For we have learned that Rabbi Judah said: What is the meaning of that which is written, "And I shall see him and his form shall be removed from his wisdom"? It is because those colors are seen, and it appears to him in the dwellings of light, for from there wisdom is hinted at.

Rabbi Yose said: You have nothing in the world that does not have a spiritual counterpart <note>original: "dugma," an archetype or example</note> above, and because of this it is written:
> **"And I saw visions of God."** <note>Ezekiel 1:1</note>

Come and see: when a man is in his bed and desires to sleep, his soul <note>original: "nishmata"</note> goes out and goes and wanders in the world, and enters into that level which is necessary for it. And behold, they have established that the soul ascends above, from level to level, until it goes and takes and finds itself in that place which is necessary for it. And there it knows what it knows, and at that time wisdom is revealed by means of that opening of the dream...

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Tabernacle (Mishkan) from the Zohar, specifically focusing on the structural and spiritual unity required for the Divine Presence to dwell within it. It transitions from the general concept of unity to the specific anatomical correspondence between the Tabernacle and the human body.</meta>

## Contribution (Terumah)

...in a single vision on this side and on that side, so that all are joined as one, and all ascend and are crowned within the **Holy Name** <note>original: "Shma Kadisha"</note> as one. Thus, the whole became like a single body. Because of this, the **Divine Presence** <note>original: "Shekhinah" - the feminine aspect of God that dwells among humanity</note> does not dwell except in a place that is complete, and in a place where **male and female** are found together. 

For this reason, if the Priest—who represents the high holiness of the realms above—is not found as "male and female" <note>meaning he must be married to be spiritually complete</note>, the Divine Presence does not dwell within him and he cannot perform the sacred service. Consequently, all blessings only rest in a place that is complete, for a place that is lacking cannot host a blessing from above. Thus, the Divine Presence does not dwell in a place of deficiency, and the same applies to all blessings.

The way of the Tabernacle <note>original: "Mishkan"</note> followed the supernal vision of the realms above. In this manner, it was shown that the way of the higher realms is for all parts to be bound together; they come as one on the side of the right arm, on the side of the left arm, on the side of the body, and on the side of all other parts. Regarding this, it is written:
> For over all the glory shall be a canopy. (Isaiah 4:5)

And they are all one. Regarding this, it is said:
> And the Tabernacle shall be one. (Exodus 26:6)

This refers to the "body" of the whole, modeled after the Holy Name, for all are the **mystery** <note>original: "Raza"</note> of Oneness. Therefore, it is written with emphasis: "And the Tabernacle shall be one." 

Happy is the portion of the righteous who know the ways of the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, and walk in the path of truth. Concerning them, it is written:
> Happy are those upright in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord. (Psalms 119:1)

Even though we have already established in the Section of Genesis <note>Zohar I, 45a</note> the mystery of the Supernal Tabernacle, and that the Supernal Matron <note>The Shekhinah in her royal aspect</note> only dwells within the mystery of Oneness, what is meant by "And the Tabernacle shall be one"? It means that the right, the left, and the body are all unified as one, and then "the Tabernacle shall be one."

**Rabbi Yose** opened his discourse:
> And you shall set up the Tabernacle according to its fashion, which was shown to you on the mountain. (Exodus 26:30)

Happy is the portion of those human beings who know how to arrange the **service** <note>original: "Pulchana" - referring to ritual worship or labor</note> of their Master in the proper place. This is the mystery of the Divine Presence, which dwells to receive this service just as it is found above. For this service below corresponds to the service above. Just as it is below, so it is above; as the Tabernacle is below, so it is above. Therefore, a person must prepare the service and the holiness below to correspond to the above, so that they may become as one.

Come and see <note>A common Zoharic invitation to contemplate a deeper truth</note>: the mystery of the Tabernacle corresponds to the body of a human being, which is divided into many **limbs** <note>original: "Sheyfin"</note>. All of these stand level upon level, yet they join as one to become a single body for the soul to use. So too, the Tabernacle is divided into many limbs, but they all join as one. When they are joined as one, the Holy Spirit dwells upon them, and this is the mystery of "And the Tabernacle shall be one."

Do not read "according to its fashion" <note>Hebrew: *kemishpato*</note> but rather "according to its garment" <note>Hebrew: *kemalbusho*</note>, as has been explained. This is the image of the human body which is found to be in the likeness of the Tabernacle. Therefore, all the "limbs" of the Tabernacle correspond to the limbs of the body, and the body corresponds to the limbs of the higher realms, one matching the other. Because of this, the Tabernacle corresponds to the human body. We have established that the Divine Presence has no restoration or perfection until the higher and lower realms are joined as one, and the whole becomes...

<summary>This passage explains that the Tabernacle (Mishkan) is a physical mirror of both the Divine Name and the human body, emphasizing that the Divine Presence only dwells where there is unity and "wholeness" (male and female). It introduces the mystical concept that the Tabernacle's components function like human limbs to house the Holy Spirit.</summary>

<keywords>Tabernacle, Mishkan, Shekhinah, Divine Presence, Unity, Human Body, Macrocosm and Microcosm, Priesthood, Marriage, Spiritual Service</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Rabbi Eleazar opened his discourse and said: <note>Psalms 106:2</note> **"Who can express the mighty acts of the Lord? Who can declare all His praise?"** Come and see: when the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to bring the world into being, He brought forth a single light—a light that included all other lights and was included within them. From it, He brought forth all other lights, which branched out from it, and the world was made. That light emerged and was found **upon the earth**, and from that light, the lower Garden of Eden was fashioned. He surrounded that light with other lights that do not shine as brightly as it does, and from there, the lower world is nourished.

And when that light emerged and was found in the world, the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to hide it so that the wicked of the world would not benefit from it, as it is written: <note>Job 38:15</note> **"And from the wicked their light is withheld."** He stored it away for the righteous in the time to come, as it is written: <note>Psalms 97:11</note> **"Light is sown for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart."**

We have learned: when that light emerged, it brought forth from itself another light that shines, and that light is called *Gevurah* <note>original: "Gevurah," meaning Strength or Severity; the second of the emotive Divine attributes</note>. From the side of *Gevurah*, another light emerged which is called "Darkness." It is found that this darkness originated from the side of *Gevurah*, and for this reason it is called darkness: because it extinguishes <note>or "dims"</note> that light which is above.

Come and see: this darkness, which is **from the left side**, is not "darkness" in the literal sense, but rather a light that does not radiate. Because it does not radiate, it is called darkness. In this manner, Rabbi Shimon said: the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note> comes from the side of *Gevurah*, and for this reason, she is called "Night." This has already been stated.

<summary>Rabbi Eleazar explains the creation of the primordial light and its subsequent concealment for the righteous, while describing how "darkness" and the Shekhinah originate from the Divine attribute of Gevurah (Strength).</summary>
<keywords>Primordial Light, Gevurah, Darkness, Shekhinah, Creation, Garden of Eden, Rabbi Eleazar</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the Zoharic exposition on the work of Creation, specifically focusing on the Second Day. It explores the mystical identity of the "Firmament" and its role in balancing the cosmic forces of Mercy and Judgment.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The "eye"—this refers to the entire source of the <term>Kingdom</term> <note>original: Malchut; the tenth and final emanation of the Divine</note> from that upper land and from that abyss. And because of this, it dwells above, upon the highest heavens and beyond, but no further. **And Joseph was**. This refers to the **Upper Joseph**, who is the **Life of the Worlds** <note>original: Chai Ha-Olamim; a title for the Sefirah of Yesod, the foundation and procreative force</note>. And he is the one who rests upon that row. And from that row, this entire lower realm receives its sustenance at the time when the hands cease. Because of this, greatness was increasing, and because of this, they gazed into this "eye" <note>Refers to the "eye" of the divine providence</note>. This is the light that shines. This **light** is the dominion that was Judgment in its essence, and the faith of the world could not be established until he saw the opening and it was opened. He opened and said: **"Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters"** <note>Genesis 1:6</note>. Because of this, **"Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters"** is what he saw as the source. For the "opening" is the <term>Foundation</term> <note>original: Yesod</note> of Joseph, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, opened and there was a firmament above and a firmament below. For there is a firmament below, which is the **Kingdom** <note>Malchut</note>, and there is a firmament above, which is **Understanding** <note>original: Binah; the motherly source of the emanations</note>. <margin>A firmament in the midst of the waters</margin> <note>Discussion of the firmament separating upper and lower waters</note> to separate between water and water. And this firmament is the **Righteous One** <note>original: Tzaddik; another name for Yesod</note>, who is the firmament that takes all those waters from above and brings them out below. And because of this, he is the firmament: **"Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters. And let it divide between water and water"** <note>Genesis 1:6</note>.

What is meant by "divide"? Some say this firmament, which is the **Foundation** <note>Yesod</note>, separates between the upper waters and the lower waters. For behold, those waters above are sweet waters, which are **Mercy** <note>original: Rachamim</note>. And the waters below are bitter waters, which are **Judgment** <note>original: Din</note>. And concerning this it is written: **"Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters and let it divide between water and water"** <note>Genesis 1:6</note>. And it is written: **"And God made the firmament and divided"** <note>Genesis 1:7</note>. And it is written: **"Between the waters which were under the firmament and the waters which were above the firmament"** <note>Genesis 1:7</note>.

What is this firmament? This is the **Righteous One** <note>Tzaddik/Yesod</note>. **"And He divided"**—this is the separation that the Holy One, Blessed be He, makes between the waters above and the waters below. The firmament, which is the Righteous One, distinguishes between the upper waters and the lower waters. And he is the Foundation, who is the **Life of the Worlds**, separating between those sweet waters above and those bitter waters below. Because he is the Cause of Causes for everything above and below. **"And let it divide between water and water"**—this is the separation made by the Righteous One, who makes peace. For he distinguishes between Mercy and Judgment. **Upper waters** are **Mercy**. **Lower waters** are **Judgment**.

<summary>This page provides a mystical interpretation of the Second Day of Creation, identifying the biblical 'firmament' as the Sefirah of Yesod (the Righteous One), which balances the sweet waters of Mercy with the bitter waters of Judgment.</summary>
<keywords>Creation, Firmament, Yesod, Joseph, Mercy and Judgment, Upper and Lower Waters, Sefirot, Zohar</keywords>

## Main Text (The New Zohar)

...the world from which it separated, it enters into the World to Come. At the time when the soul departs from the world, its merits are counted one by one. And at the time that same soul enters the Garden of Eden, see how many voices and how many heralds go before it! Until it enters, they prepare themselves before the King on the Throne of Light. It is beautiful even here: from the day that this work was completed by the hands of the **Companions** <note>original: "Chavrayya" - the circle of mystical scholars surrounding Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note>, they all rejoice and are counted, and heralds proclaim before them, saying: "Rejoice, rejoice in the holy work that stands before the Throne of the King!" Worthy are you, Companions, for your works shall stand and be considered according to the secret of the matter they reached. It is as if those worthy ones come with their garments upon their souls—the garment of the image which is the excellence of their order.

Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Phineas were sitting when <unclear>one of them</unclear> opened his discourse, raised his eyes, and said:
> **"His lips are like lilies"** <note>Song of Songs 5:13</note> etc.

This refers to the **Assembly of Israel** <note>The Shekhinah, the feminine divine presence</note> at the hour when **The Holy One, Blessed Be He** <note>The primary name for God in the Zohar</note> enters the Garden of Eden to delight with the righteous. He holds that lily when it is completed, at the time it ascends, etc. And when its garment is completed, it ascends and descends, as it is written: "dripping with flowing myrrh." The King and all the Companions sit surrounding her. And who has seen the love of the Companions? Who has seen the peace between them? For though these matters come from the "side of the serpent" <note>A reference to the struggle with base inclinations or the external forces of judgment</note>, they are considered like rushing waters until **The Holy One, Blessed Be He** binds them from the side of the Spirit. I trembled at the depth and measure of the words I heard, which have not yet left my mouth.

Rabbi Judah saw him on their throne, and all who are beloved before Him were rejoicing, for the Holy Soul rested upon the book. Worthy is the portion of the righteous in their spirit... more than all nakedness, etc. Rabbi Phineas opened and said:
> **"Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad"** <note>Psalms 96:11</note> etc.

At the hour when those voices are felt above, so shall it be below. And that voice shall be above just as we heard the voice of the one calling. Rabbi Abba was sitting, and he became thoughtful and said:
> **"When the morning stars sang together"** <note>Job 38:7</note> etc.

All the morning stars exist to bless the King... Worthy are the Companions who sit with other Companions, whoever they may be, etc. And our measure, after they sat, increased, for it is the work of the Companions. Worthy are the Companions who arrange words in the **Skull** <note>original: "Galgalta" - a high Kabbalistic level of the Divine Head/Will</note>; this is the work of this... the beginning and the end and the sign of life. For it is like a man who finishes a volume of the Talmud and makes a celebration, a feast, joy, and peace.

[6] when the sun is fixed in its degree and the day is prepared and shining. "But the way of the wicked is like deep darkness," etc.

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic discourse on the spiritual mechanics of the Tabernacle and the union between the divine realms. It follows the themes of the indwelling of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) within the earthly sanctuary.</meta>

## After the Death <note>original: "Acharei Mot" — the name of the Torah portion</note>

Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse and said: *“And let the favor of the Lord our God be upon us; and establish the work of our hands upon us; yes, the work of our hands, establish it.”* <note>Psalm 90:17</note> This verse is difficult, for it is written "establish the work of our hands *upon us*" and then "the work of our hands, *establish it*." <note>The original Hebrew uses two different forms: "konnah" (establish it for us) and "konnehu" (establish him/it)</note> Why "establish it for us" and why "establish him"?

Rather, "establish the work of our hands upon us" refers to the world above, while "the work of our hands, establish him" refers to the world below. At the moment when that **Supreme Favor** <note>original: "No’am" — a technical term for the divine emanation of Binah/Understanding</note> rests upon the world, everything is sustained above and below. Regarding this, Moses—who was a man of **Supreme Wisdom**—knew this secret. And one who is a man of wisdom does not speak a word except regarding a mystery.

**Come and see:** *“I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey...”* <note>Song of Songs 5:1</note> This verse has been established by the colleagues. However, "I have come into my garden" is as you would say, *“A garden locked is my sister, my bride.”* <note>Song of Songs 4:12</note> "My sister, my bride" is as you would say, *“Say to Wisdom: You are my sister.”* <note>Proverbs 7:4</note> This refers to the **Upper Garden**. "My sister, my bride" refers to the **Lower Garden** <note>The Lower Garden represents the Shekhinah or the Assembly of Israel in the earthly realm</note>. At the time when the Lower Garden is prepared, it is called "Garden" on its own. But at the time when it is bound above and shines from above, then it is called "My sister, my bride."

"I have gathered my myrrh with my spice"—these are the offerings of the **Lower Sanctuary** which shines from above. "I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey"—this is the offering of the Lower Sanctuary which is on the **Right side** <note>The side of Mercy/Chesed</note>. "I have drunk my wine with my milk"—this is from the **Left side** <note>The side of Judgment/Gevurah</note>. At the time when the Lower Sanctuary is prepared and joins with the Upper, then everything is complete and shines with a single light.

Regarding this, **the Holy One, Blessed be He**, said: "I have come into *my* garden." For the verse says "into my garden" and does not say "into the garden." This is because that garden is exceedingly precious to Him. At the time when the will of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is found within the **Assembly of Israel**, then He says: "I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride."

And the scripture says: *“And I will make them joyful in my house of prayer.”* <note>Isaiah 56:7</note> It says "My prayer" without further specification. It is not written "in a house of prayer," but "My prayer." This is because within the house of prayer, that which is "My prayer" is found. And "Prayer" is a known entity <note>A reference to the Shekhinah, who is herself called "Prayer"</note>. Therefore, "I will make them joyful in my house of prayer," because within it is the joy of the worlds. In this same manner, "I have come into my garden"—this is the Assembly of Israel, as you would say, "A garden locked is my sister, my bride." "My sister, my bride" is the Lower Garden, as we have said. Then everything is in complete joy.

**Come and see:** On the day that the **Tabernacle** was established below, the Tabernacle was established above. It was prepared and it shone with joy...

<summary>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai explains how the earthly Tabernacle and the Assembly of Israel (Shekhinah) act as a "Lower Garden" that, when properly prepared, unites with the "Upper Garden" of the divine realms to bring joy and light to all existence.</summary>
<keywords>Shekhinah, Tabernacle, Song of Songs, Upper and Lower Gardens, Assembly of Israel, Divine Union, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, Kabbalah</keywords>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

And see, how meritorious is the portion of Israel, who sanctify the Holy King at every single season, so that they may be increasingly sanctified <note>original: "yitir mekudashim"</note>, as it is written: *And you shall be holy unto Me, for I the Lord am holy* <note>Leviticus 20:26</note>. This is so that they may be nourished and blessed from His blessings, and all the sustenance and blessings of the Ancient Ones <note>A reference to the highest, most primordial levels of the Divine</note>, and from that which shines from the portion and delight of that River that flows and goes out from Eden and joins together, and all are blessed by it through a supernal holiness. As it is written: *He shall be called holy, every one that is written unto life in Jerusalem* <note>Isaiah 4:3</note>. Happy is the portion of Israel in this world and in the world to come.

->**Vayelech**<-
<note>The Torah portion "And He Went," Deuteronomy 31:1</note>
*And Moses went and spoke these words unto all Israel.* Rabbi Eleazar opened his discourse: *The end of the matter, all having been heard...* <note>Ecclesiastes 12:13</note>. "The end of the matter, all having been heard"—this refers to the end of all the degrees <term>degrees: the Sefirot or spiritual levels</term>, for everything is bound up within it. And because of this, "the end of the matter, all having been heard," because everything is bound to that place. Therefore, *thou shalt fear the Lord thy God*—this is the end of the degrees, and this is the "end of the matter."

->**Acharei**<-
<note>The Torah portion "After," Leviticus 16:1</note>
*After the death of the two sons of Aaron...*
->**Rabbi Shimon**<- opened: *Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily...* <note>Ecclesiastes 8:11</note>. The companions have already established the meaning of this verse, but come and see what the Holy One, Blessed be He, has taught us: that a person should never withhold himself from prayer and supplications before the Holy One, Blessed be He. Even if he is guilty before the Holy One, Blessed be He, he should not despair of mercy. He should not say, "Because I have sinned before the Holy One, Blessed be He, I have no opening to enter before Him."

**And it came to pass** after the death... Rabbi Eleazar opened: *Serve the Lord with gladness; come before His presence with singing* <note>Psalms 100:2</note>. The companions have established this verse, but come and see: a person needs to show joy before the Holy One, Blessed be He, for in joy is everything found. Even a person who is in sadness because of his sins and seeks mercy before the Holy One, Blessed be He, must enter before Him with joy, so that there should be no sadness in him. For joy comes from the side of the "World to Come" <note>The Sefirah of Binah, the source of liberation</note>, in which no sadness is found at all...

<summary>This page discusses the sanctity of the Jewish people and transitions between the Torah portions of Vayelech and Acharei Mot, emphasizing that prayer must be performed with joy even when seeking atonement for sins.</summary>

## Noah

And if you should say: Did the Holy One, blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu," the standard Zoharic name for God</note>, know that human beings were destined to sin? It was for this reason that the Supreme King did not establish the world until He had prepared **Repentance** <note>original: "Teshuvah," literally meaning "return"</note> for it, which is the healing of the world and acts with mercy toward humanity. Regarding this, the Holy One, blessed be He, said:
> (Psalms 90:3) *You turn man back to contrition, and say, "Return, O children of men."*

And it has been stated that the **Torah** preceded the world by two thousand years. And if you should say: "Who was there at the time the Torah existed?"—it was not so <note>meaning, it did not exist in a physical sense</note>. For the Torah was hidden on high, standing before the Holy One, blessed be He. When the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to create the world, He looked into the Torah and created the world. In every single act that the Holy One, blessed be He, performed in the world, He looked into the Torah and created it. This is what is written:
> (Proverbs 8:30) *Then I was beside Him as a confidant; and I was daily His delight, rejoicing before Him at all times.*

Do not read the word as **confidant** <note>Hebrew: "Amon"</note> but rather as **architect** <note>Hebrew: "Uman." The Zohar uses a wordplay to suggest the Torah was the blueprint used by the Divine Builder</note>. And regarding this it is written: (Genesis 1:1) *In the beginning God created.* **In the beginning** <note>Hebrew: "Bereshit"</note> refers to the Torah, as it is stated: (Proverbs 8:22) *The Lord possessed me at the beginning of His way.* Therefore, fortunate is the person who labors in the Torah. For whoever labors in the Torah, it is as if he labors in the Work of Creation, and the Holy One, blessed be He, gazes upon him.

---

**Rabbi Isaac** opened his discourse and said:
> (Psalms 119:1) *Happy are those whose way is blameless, who walk in the Torah of the Lord.*

**Fortunate is the person** who labors in the Torah and walks in the path of truth before the Holy One, blessed be He. Come and see: whoever labors in the Torah labors in the path of truth, because the Torah is the path of truth. All the matters of this world are nothing but vanity and emptiness, but the path of the Torah is the path of truth and a supreme light. Therefore, fortunate is the portion of that person who labors in it.

---

**Rabbi Judah** opened his discourse and said:
> (Isaiah 2:5) *O house of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the Lord.*

Come and see: because the Torah is light, as it is stated: (Proverbs 6:23) *For the commandment is a lamp and the Torah is light.* Whoever labors in the Torah merits to walk in that light of the World to Come. He also merits to walk in this world so that his feet shall not stumble, because the supreme light goes before him. Regarding this, it is written: *Let us walk in the light of the Lord.*

<summary>This page explains that God used the Torah as a blueprint for Creation and established Repentance before the world began to account for human frailty. It emphasizes that studying Torah is equivalent to participating in the act of Creation and provides spiritual light for the soul.</summary>
<keywords>Torah, Creation, Repentance, Teshuvah, Divine Light, Rabbi Isaac, Rabbi Judah, Blueprint of the World</keywords>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

He went about in the commerce and trade of the horses <note>original: "susya" - likely a mystical reference to the "chariots" or forces of the divine realm</note> as we have said regarding the four portions on every side, to the place that is seen as including the King of Israel for the sake of the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence, viewed as the feminine aspect of God</note>. Because the Shekhinah dwells on the side of the Transjordan, Israel is profaned among the nations; these are the souls of the ancients of the land. And between the branches of the Tree, left and right, he has no portion. And through it, the Holy One, blessed be He, bestows kindnesses <note>original: "gamil" - to requite or bestow</note> despite the hardships that come upon the world. And they are destined to be a portion to be rebuilt in glory among the other branches that are destined to be glorified through Him. And he lived and was awakened by his pains, for he was pained over the merit of the **Shekhinah** which was found after they went into exile. The names [of the horses?] that are here are because this is the awakening of the spirit of holy wisdom that he sees. And this spirit goes and roams in the paths of the wings of the wind, and all those [hosts?] above come and hear this word. And fortunate is he who awakens this word, for concerning him it is written: <note>Isaiah 58:8</note> > *Then your light shall break forth like the morning, etc.* <margin>Sign 71</margin>
And when he sits and this spirit is awakened further by this, the Holy One, blessed be He, sees him and goes and brings the news to the **Shekhinah**. Because this word stands in two [realms?] to make a single bond. And because of this, it is more important to remember all these and for these hardships to be guarded before the King.

-> **And the King Heard** <-

Rabbi Isaac opened and said: <note>Leviticus 26:42</note> > *Then I will remember My covenant with Jacob, and also My covenant with Isaac, and also My covenant with Abraham I will remember; and I will remember the land.* <margin>Leviticus 26</margin> The colleagues have already established the meaning of this verse. But come and see: there are five levels here, and each and every one has "remembrance" associated with it. And even though Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are a single bond, why does it say "remembrance" for each and every one? It is only to show that they are all in a different high degree and in perfect joy. Wise and praising, and he knew my portions...

<summary>This page discusses the mystical relationship between the Shekhinah in exile and the spiritual "awakening" caused by human study and prayer. It also begins an analysis of the three Patriarchs as distinct yet unified spiritual grades (Sefirot) linked by divine remembrance.</summary>

It transitions from a general discussion of divine unity and prayer rituals (specifically the morning service and Tefillin) to the specific biblical verse where Moses assembles the community of Israel.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

The first, and concerning this I say that it is the primary of all heights, for they all awaken above. And this corresponds to it, increasing mercy in the same manner as in the psalm <note>referring to the liturgy</note> "Blessed is He and Blessed is His Name," <note>original: *Baruch Hu u-Varuch Shemo*</note> the Name and the Remembrance. **Because of them**, there is a cry of obligation for one who dons Phylacteries <term>Tefillin: ritual leather boxes containing Torah verses worn during prayer</term> and stands before the Master of the Universe. For it is an obligation for anyone who is crowned with them; it is found that he is in a state of obligation for the whole world. And behold, during the Morning Prayer <note>Shacharit</note>, at that hour, in the way of heaven and earth that is conducted by the secrets of the Torah, at that hour the Ancient One <note>a reference to a high level of the Divine, the *Atika Kadisha*</note> remembers the Master of the Heights. And it is sufficient for him because he brings the desire <note>original: *re'uta*</note> close. We have no one who comes into the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, who will not be properly accepted, for they all rise in a single thought. And even though this was the first, they rise above as one, because it is the Name that his thought intends to bind and to bring before the heavens, higher and higher. And because he is found within it, for at that hour the Matron <note>the Shekhinah or Divine Presence</note> of all their dominions and greatness is awakened and rises above. For above all of them, nothing is found like it. And that which he opens with at this hour is in the manner of the psalm "Blessed is He," which is the Name that rules over all life. And all those above and below, the angels of the psalm, are the rulers who hear the voice. This is what they say: "Blessed is He," and meritorious is his portion, for this is the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He. And regarding one who unifies the Name of his Master—concerning this, we have no one who unifies the Name of his Master as is fitting and strikes the voice in holiness. Fortunate is this one, for the [influence of the] Beard <note>original: *dikna* — a kabbalistic metaphor for the flow of divine mercy from the highest source</note> pours upon him, for he is certainly found before the Master of heaven and earth.

---

->**And Moses assembled** all the congregation of the children of Israel, and said unto them: These are the words...<-
<note>Exodus 35:1</note>

Rabbi Eleazar opened and said: Why does the scripture say here "all the congregation of the children of Israel"? It is because they are all before their Master, all as one in unity, as is fitting. Rabbi Hezekiah said: What is the reason it says **"all"**? This means all of them as one, like one who comes toward all of them as one.

**And Moses assembled** all the congregation of the children of Israel to let us know that Moses was supported from above. Because of this, he knew how to gather them all and for them all to be as one. Even though the scripture says that Moses placed a veil over his face when he spoke with them, he invited them and at the time he commanded them. Rabbi Eleazar said: At that hour, Moses was crowned because of all of them in a single thought, to be bound as all of them as one. And the Holy One, blessed be He, took delight in him, and it was sufficient for him that they were all in the obligation of a single thought, and it rose before Him, and it was sufficient for Him.

<summary>This page discusses the mystical power of communal unity and focused intent during prayer, specifically through the donning of Tefillin and the Morning Service. It explains that Moses's assembly of Israel was not merely a physical gathering but a spiritual unification that allowed the community to rise as a "single thought" to the Divine.</summary>
