<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the sacrificial rites, specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of the Incense (Ketoret) as a shield against metaphysical and physical harm. It aligns with the Zohar's broader themes of the "Bond of Faith" and the unification of divine attributes.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Whenever <term>Rabbi Hezekiah</term> <note>A prominent scholar in the Zohar's circle</note> was found among the companions, he would travel with them, and at all times when they traveled, they would labor in the study of the Torah. <term>Rabbi Isaac</term> said to Rabbi Hezekiah: Regarding that which we have learned, that <term>Rabbi Shimon</term> <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the central figure of the Zohar</note> said: Anyone who exerts themselves in this section of the <term>Incense</term> <note>original: "Ketoret"; the specific biblical and talmudic passages describing the spice blend burned in the Temple</note> every day and focuses their intention upon it, they will be saved from every evil thing, from all evil sorceries, from all evil mishaps, from every evil thought, from every harsh judgment, and from plague. They will not be harmed on that day, for the <term>Other Side</term> <note>original: "S.A." / "Sitra Achra"; the realm of evil or demonic forces in Kabbalah</note> has no authority over them. And what is the reason? Because we have learned that the Incense is the restoration of the whole world. At any time that the Incense stood [ready], clouds and smoke would ascend to the place that purifies, and it would become a throne for Mercy, and Judgment would pass away so as not to rule over the world.

->**Rabbi Hezekiah**<-

said: Certainly it is so, for we have learned that the Incense is more beloved to <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "K.B.H." / "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> than all the services that human beings perform before Him. For the service of the Incense is the restoration of everything, more than any other service, because the Incense is the <term>Bond of Faith</term> <note>original: "Kishura de-Meimanuta"; the mystical connection that binds all divine levels together</note>. At that time when the smoke would ascend, it would illuminate them and bring everything close together to be bound in a single bond. Because of this, it is called "Incense" <note>The word "Ketoret" is linked to the Aramaic root "Keter," meaning to bind or tie</note>, the bond of everything as one. And because of this, when this bond is seen, everything is subdued and Judgment does not rest upon the world. Therefore, it is the Bond of Faith.

And we have learned: The Incense atones for the sins of human beings. This is its portion: to atone for the <term>Evil Inclination</term> <note>original: "Yetzer Ha-Ra"</note> so that it shall not rule over human beings, because the Incense only comes to counter the Evil Inclination so that it cannot prosecute human beings.

->**And come and see**<-

From the day the Tabernacle was built, nothing was as beloved before the Holy One, Blessed be He, as the Incense, because the Incense nullifies plague and judgment from the world. <term>Rabbi Yose</term> asked: What is it about the Incense that nullifies judgment and plague? He said to him: Have we not learned that all evil types, and plague, and judgments cannot rule in that place where the Incense is present? For the Incense is the Bond of Faith where everything is bound together as one. Because of this, the pillar of Incense is called the "Pillar of Cloud," like that which we have learned:

> And he stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stayed. <note>Numbers 17:13; referring to Aaron the Priest using the incense to stop a divine plague</note>

So too, the pillar of Incense is everything. And come and see...

<summary>This passage explains the mystical power of the Ketoret (sacred incense), asserting that its recitation protects against evil forces, plague, and harsh judgment by unifying the divine realms into a "Bond of Faith." It emphasizes that the incense is the most beloved service to God because it subdues the Evil Inclination and transforms Judgment into Mercy.</summary>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

**"And there was a famine in the land..."** <note>Genesis 12:10</note>

->**"And he said to Sarai his wife: 'Behold, now I know that you are a woman of beautiful appearance.'"** <note>Genesis 12:11</note><-

How hardened are the hearts of the wicked, for they are brazen toward **the Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>The standard Hebrew/Aramaic title for God</note>, and they are far from the Torah. And because they are far from the Torah, they are far from righteousness. And what is "righteousness"? This is the Torah. For whoever exerts themselves in the study of Torah is called "righteous" <note>Hebrew: Tzadik</note>, as he draws near to **the Holy One, Blessed be He**.

**Come and see** <note>A standard Zoharic opening inviting the reader to contemplate a deeper truth</note>, **Abraham** exerted himself in the Torah, and because of this, he is called righteous, as it is written: **"Righteous are You, O Lord, and upright are Your judgments"** <note>Psalms 119:137</note>. And **Abraham** is called righteous, as it is written: **"The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree; he shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon"** <note>Psalms 92:13</note>. Because of this, he is called "Abraham my friend," as it is written: **"The seed of Abraham my friend"** <note>Isaiah 41:8</note>.

<unclear>Lines are extremely blurred—the discourse continues regarding Abraham and his various spiritual levels.</unclear>

**Come and see**, when **Abraham** went down to Egypt, he knew that the Egyptians were immersed in lewdness. Because of this, he feared for his wife. And if you should ask: would **Abraham**, who was so righteous, fear for himself? It was not so; rather, he feared for the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence, viewed in the Zohar as a feminine aspect of God</note> that was with her. For the Divine Presence never departed from him from the day he exerted himself to reach the level of the "Righteous."

## Main Text (Zohar)

...His name, for the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: HaKadosh Baruch Hu; the standard rabbinic name for God</note> is destined to cause them to rejoice, to rebuild the Holy Temple, to bring them close, and to teach them the straight path. For this time of <term>exile</term> <note>original: galuta</note> is a time of <term>impurity</term> <note>original: mesavuta</note>, and anyone who clings to them <note>the nations or the forces of impurity</note> becomes defiled. For so we have learned: the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> is destined to purify Israel and to clarify them from among the nations. As it is written <note>Ezekiel 36:25</note>: > "And I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean..." And as it is written <note>Proverbs 17:3</note>: > "The crucible is for silver and the furnace for gold..." 

And because of this, during the time she <note>the Shekhinah/Divine Presence</note> is in exile, she is defiled <note>by association with the lower realms</note> from teaching them the straight path. Because of this, other "beasts" are present which are strange and do not resemble those found in the Holy Land. For these defile anyone who clings to them. But the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> is destined to purify them, to clarify them, to bring them close, and to build for them the Holy Temple. And regarding this: "And Jacob went out from Beer-sheba, and went toward Haran."

---
->**And Jacob Went Out**<-
---

"And Jacob went out from Beer-sheba, and went toward Haran" (Genesis 28:10). Rabbi Hiyya opened his discourse with the verse <note>Psalms 121:1</note>: > "I lift up my eyes to the mountains; from where shall my help come? My help comes from the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth." 

This verse has been established as one spoken by David. But it also applies to the time when Jacob was traveling, fleeing from his brother. He was walking alone, without help or support. He said, "I lift up my eyes to the mountains." To which mountains? To <term>Father and Mother</term> <note>original: Abba ve-Imma; the Sefirot of Wisdom (Chokhmah) and Understanding (Binah)</note> who are the "parents" of the whole world. As it is written <note>Song of Songs 4:6</note>: > "Until the day breathes and the shadows flee..." "From where [Hebrew: *Me-ayin*] shall my help come?" This refers to the help and support of the <term>Mother</term> <note>the Sefirah Binah</note>, for the Mother always assists the son. 

Come and see: when Jacob left that well, which is <term>Beer-sheba</term> <note>literally "Well of the Seven," representing the seven lower Sefirot</note>, he left without any support or assistance at all. Because his Mother loved him, she commanded him and said, "Arise, flee..." (Genesis 27:43). And so he went alone. The <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> said to Jacob: "Do not fear. Your help is from the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth." "The Lord" refers to the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>. "Maker of heaven and earth" refers to the <term>Righteous One</term> <note>original: Tzaddik; the Sefirah Yesod</note> through whom heaven and earth were made. And because of this, the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> sustained him and said <note>Genesis 28:15</note>: > "Behold, I am with you and will guard you wherever you go..."

## Main Text (The Zohar)

And concerning this it is written:
> "And over the heads of the living creatures there was the likeness of a firmament, like the color of the terrible ice..." (Ezekiel 1:22) <note>The "living creatures" (Hayyot) are high-ranking angels supporting the Divine Throne.</note>

This firmament is the firmament that stands over those four living creatures that emerge from beneath it. And because of this, it is a different firmament that stands over those living creatures. And from this firmament drip seventy-five drops, which are seventy-five currents <note>original: "rehatin" - flowing streams of energy or light</note> that enter into those living creatures and are settled within them. And this firmament rises up, up, until it reaches a place that is not known at all. And from there, it flows and emerges with its waters until it reaches this firmament, and all those drops and currents all emerge from it. **Come and see:** <note>original: "Ta chazi" - a standard Zoharic opening for a new insight</note> in this same manner, there is another firmament below in those lower Palaces <note>term: Heikhalot - the celestial halls or dimensions through which the soul or prayer ascends</note> which is a firmament that stands over four other living creatures. And those living creatures are all joined one to another and ascend upward, and because of this it is written, "And over the heads of the living creatures there was the likeness of a firmament, like the color of the terrible ice," and so on. And it is written:
> "And above the firmament that was over their heads was the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone..." (Ezekiel 1:26)

This firmament which is above those living creatures is sealed and impressed with the impression of a single ring <note>original: "izka" - a signet ring or seal representing divine authority</note> that is hidden and concealed. And from this firmament emerges a single light that sparkles and shines, and when this light shines, all the living creatures shine and are set ablaze with the flame of fire. And they all praise and say:
> "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place." (Ezekiel 3:12)

And when He <note>The Divine Light or Presence</note> ascends upward, all the living creatures become still and are silenced until they are all unified as one. And from there emerges a voice that is not heard outside, but is heard inside. And concerning this it is written:
> "When they stood, they let down their wings." (Ezekiel 1:24)

What is the meaning of "they let down their wings"? It means that when that light emerges and the hidden word is taken up, they all become silent and still and give thanks to the Holy One, blessed be He. And concerning this it is written, "When they stood, they let down their wings." For those wings of the living creatures, which were humming and praising and saying "Holy, Holy, Holy," become silenced and stand in a whisper. And the voice of the word... <note>The text breaks off here as the sentence continues on the next page.</note>

<summary>This page provides a mystical interpretation of Ezekiel's vision, describing a celestial firmament that transmits divine energy (seventy-five drops) to the angelic 'living creatures.' It explains that the angels' songs are silenced when the Divine Light ascends, allowing for a moment of perfect internal unification and silent prayer.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the mechanics of prayer and the soul's ascent through the celestial realms. It focuses specifically on the "Song of Ascents" and the concept of praying from the "depths."</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

...from all those masters of judgment <note>original: *marei de-dina*; these are the angelic prosecutors or harsh spiritual forces</note>, and there is no one who can bring accusation against him until the Holy King enters and sits before the King. Not every human being who desires to be seen before the King is able to do so. They are living and enduring, and so on, and concerning this it is written:
> **Enter His gates with thanksgiving, and His courts with praise.** <note>Psalms 100:4</note>

And concerning this, David called out and said:
> **I will dwell in Your tent forever; I will take refuge in the hidden place of Your wings. Selah.** <note>Psalms 61:5</note>

And this is the hint of this and that:
> **A prayer of the afflicted when he faints.** <note>Psalms 102:1</note>

What is the reason he "faints" <note>original: *ya'atof*; can also mean "enwraps" or "veils" himself</note>? Because the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: *Kadosh Baruch Hu*; the standard rabbinic name for God</note> desires the longing of this prayer, because it is heard as we have said. Because the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> wraps him in peace with His own hand, and concerning this he said:
> **He has redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me.** <note>Psalms 55:19</note>

And because of this, the masters of judgment have no power over him, and concerning this:
> **Hear, O God, my prayer.** <note>Psalms 55:2</note>

What is this "enwrapping" that we mentioned? These are the songs of praise that he says, and we say regarding this matter:
> **Evening, morning, and noon, I will speak and moan, and He will hear my voice.** <note>Psalms 55:18</note>

Thus, from within what they say, we also say:

---

->**Observe the Song of Ascents**<-
> **Out of the depths I have called to You, O Lord.** <note>Psalms 130:1</note>

King David spoke this verse. In every place where it is written simply **A Song of Ascents**, it refers to those levels we have mentioned that rise up and down. But here, where it is written **A Song of Ascents: Out of the depths**, why specifically "out of the depths"? It is as he said:
> **Ask for a sign... go deep.** <note>Isaiah 7:11</note>

And what are these "depths"? Rather, these are the supernal depths, the depth of all, the depth of the well <note>original: *beira*</note> from which the rivers flow and gush forth; and this is the depth of all that is called "Depths." **Out of the depths I have called to You, O Lord.** This is the supernal depth, the depth of the well from which the rivers and springs go out to every side. And one who prays his prayer must pray from the depth of the heart <note>original: *umka de-libba*</note> so that his prayer may enter that Depth, and the spring shall be blessed, and blessing will be found in the world. And this is: **Out of the depths I have called to You, O Lord.** And what are these supernal depths? The supernal depth of the river that goes out from Eden <note>The translator notes this refers to the Sefirah of Binah, the divine source of understanding and life-force</note>, and from that depth, springs flow and are prepared to bless everything. And because of this, one who wishes to pray and ask his request before the King must pray from the depth of the heart, and concerning this it is written: **Out of the depths I have called to You, O Lord. Lord, hear my voice; let Your ears be attentive to the voice of my supplications.** This is the depth that is not known, and concerning this it is written:
> **Have you entered into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in the search of the depths?** <note>Job 38:16</note>

This is the depth of all depths that a human being is unable to know anything about. And because of this, this is the Depth, and because of this one must call to Him...

<summary>This page explains that true prayer must originate from the "depth of the heart" to connect with the "supernal depths," the divine source of all blessings (Binah). It interprets the "Song of Ascents" as a mystical mechanism for bypassing spiritual accusers and drawing abundance into the world.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the Zohar's mystical commentary on the life of the Patriarchs, specifically focusing on the transition of Isaac from infancy to spiritual maturity as described in the Torah portion Vayeira.</meta>

## And He Appeared

---

... descended into him ...

**Isaac.** "And Abraham made a great feast on the day that Isaac was weaned." <note>Genesis 21:8</note> Certainly, it was on the day that Isaac was weaned. What does "was weaned" <note>The Hebrew word *higgamel* can mean both weaned and "bestowed upon."</note> mean? It means he was "weaned" from the Upper Side—from the side of **Harsh Judgment** <term>Dina Kashya: the most severe aspect of divine justice</term>—and became attached to **Relaxed Judgment** <term>Dina Rafya: a tempered, more merciful form of justice</term>. And on this day, Abraham made a great feast. What is the reason? Because joy was invited Above and joy was invited below. For this is one level corresponding to another level, in which the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <term>Kudosha Brich Hu: the standard Aramaic reference to God</term> rejoiced with him. <meta>This page begins the commentary on the Torah portion "Vayechi" (And he lived). It establishes the mystical connection between the Torah and the Divine Name, and addresses the unique visual layout of this section in the Torah scroll.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

->**And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years; and the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were a hundred and forty-seven years.** (Genesis 47:28)<-

**Rabbi Shimon opened** <note>Psalm 72:18-19</note> *Blessed be the Lord God, the God of Israel, who alone does wondrous things. And blessed be His glorious name forever; and let the whole earth be filled with His glory. Amen and Amen.* Come and see how much human beings ought to exert themselves in the service of the Holy One, Blessed be He; for anyone who exerts themselves in the Torah is as if they exerted themselves in the Holy Name. What is the reason? Because the Torah in its entirety is the Holy Name. For this reason, a person must exert themselves in it to know the ways of the Holy One, Blessed be He, for through the Torah a person comes to know Him and merits the World to Come.

Come and see: all the portions of the Torah, some are "open" and some are "closed." <note>This refers to the physical spacing in a Torah scroll; usually, a new portion starts after a significant gap, but this portion begins with only a tiny space, making it look "closed" or "sealed."</note> And this portion is closed. Why is it closed? Because as soon as Jacob descended to Egypt, the <term>eyes and hearts of Israel</term> <note>original: "eineinhu ve-libehon d'Yisrael"</note> were closed/sealed from the distress of the servitude that was imposed upon them. Another explanation: it is <term>closed</term> <note>original: "stumah"</note> because Jacob sought to reveal the "End of Days" <note>the final redemption</note> but it was closed/hidden from him.

Come and see: during the time that <term>Jacob</term> was in the land of Egypt, they were all living in sweetness, luxury, and delight, like one who possesses all the goodness of the world; but as soon as Jacob died, then the servitude began. Another explanation: "And Jacob lived"—what is the meaning of "And he lived"? Previously it was written (Genesis 45:27) *“and the spirit of their father Jacob revived,”* but now it is written *“And Jacob lived,”* for he was sustained in joy and perfection more than in all his other days.

***

**Rabbi Eleazar** opened, (Psalm 33:1) *Rejoice in the Lord, O you righteous; praise is comely for the upright.* This verse has been established by the colleagues, but "Rejoice, O you righteous" is said because those righteous ones take hold of the place called <term>Righteous</term> <note>The Sephirah of Yesod, the foundational generative force</note>, which is the <term>Life of the Worlds</term> <note>original: "Chai Almin"</note>, and it produces fruit and produce for the world. Because of this, they require song and praise, which is <term>comely praise</term> <note>original: "naveh tehillah"</note>.

And who is "Praise" <note>Tehillah</note>? This is the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>original: "Knesset Yisrael," referring to the Sephirah of Malchut/Divine Presence</note>, as it is said (Psalm 148:14) *“A praise for all His pious ones.”* And it is written (Psalm 145:1) *“A Praise of David: I will extol Thee, my God, O King.”* What is the reason? Because she is the praise of all, and from there blessings go out to all the world.

<summary>Rabbi Shimon explains that the Torah is synonymous with God's Name and discusses why the portion of Vayechi is "closed" in the scroll, linking it to the onset of Egyptian exile. Rabbi Eleazar then interprets the mystical relationship between the "Righteous" (Yesod) and "Praise" (Malchut).</summary>

<keywords>Jacob in Egypt, Closed Portion, Holy Name, Torah study, Righteousness, Assembly of Israel, Yesod, Malchut, End of Days</keywords>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

And if you should say that the festival day is completed—such as the festival of Passover—how many days are there from one day to the next? This is because of the holiness of the Torah; for whoever exerts themselves in it is sanctified by it with the **Upper Holiness**. And anyone who awakens the Upper Holiness is sanctified by it, and the Upper Holiness rests upon them. Because of this, even though the festival is completed, the holiness is not completed; rather, it stands and guards the person who walks in the straight path, protecting them on every side they go. From here onward, their portion of piety and kindness is not lacking, and their portion is held in holy safekeeping. Every person who guards those forty-nine days and merits the Torah also merits to go out into the **Freedom of Freemen**, which is the freedom belonging to the <term>World to Come</term> <note>Hebrew: Olam Ha-Ba; referring to the higher realm of Binah/Understanding from which liberation flows</note>. And such a person receives the Torah, which is the **Tree of Life** <note>Hebrew: Etz Chayim</note> of the upper realms. Certainly, such a person is awakened by the Upper Oath <note>A wordplay on "Shavuot" (Weeks) and "Shevuot" (Oaths)</note> and is prepared to receive the Torah, for the Torah is certainly the Tree of Life. All the appointed times and festivals depend upon the Festival of Shavuot from the upper side, for they are all integrated into one another. The Festival of Shavuot is entirely holy, and this provides strength to the holy ones in this world and strength to them in the World to Come. And the secret of the matter is: *Seven complete sabbaths shall there be* <note>Leviticus 23:15</note>. Seven weeks correspond to the seven days of the week, for they are all joined as seven sevens, and they create the appointed times and festivals, as they are all included in the day of the Festival of Shavuot. And therefore, it is called "Weeks" (Shavuot).

-> **Seven complete weeks shall there be** <-

In this manner, "seven complete weeks shall there be," and seven weeks are forty-nine days, corresponding to the seven days; for seven sevens create the appointed times, festivals, and Sabbaths. Why are they called this—"Seven Weeks"? Because they are the secret of the "Seventh" that is above <margin>**The Secret**</margin> for behold, they are all "complete," and regarding this it is said: *Seven complete weeks shall there be.* And those weeks are revitalized on the day of the Festival of Shavuot, which is the "Ten" for everything—ten days <note>Likely referring to the ten utterances/commandments</note> and seven seventh-weeks. For every single seventh is entirely holy; they all act and awaken toward the day of Shavuot, all as one perfect <term>Unification</term> <note>Aramaic: Yichuda; the mystical merging of divine attributes</note>. And from their midst, they benefit from the vision of the Upper Soul and the light that shines to all worlds.

<summary>This page explains that the forty-nine days of the Omer count lead to a state of spiritual freedom and the "Upper Holiness" associated with the Torah. It describes Shavuot as the culmination where all sacred times are unified and the "Tree of Life" is accessed.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

...to know all the works of <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Ha-Kadosh Baruch Hu," the standard rabbinic title for God</note>, for He is both revealed and hidden, and Man is above...
...the concealment of the vision of the Holy of Holies, above and below...

->**The Ancient of Days**<-

He opened his discourse and said: "His head is as the finest gold" <note>Song of Songs 5:11</note>. There are three heads, one upon the other, and one above the other.
When the children of the world strive to know, these three heads are united as one.
One head is that which is highest of the high, which is neither known nor grasped.
It is precious and covered in subtle coverings that no one can know. And these three heads are in one.
Trees <note>likely a metaphor for the branching out of divine powers</note> and one, three impressions in one, and they are this:
The <term>Holy Ancient One</term> <note>original: "Atika Kadisha," the highest manifestation of the Divine Will</note>, and within Him are established three heads hidden in one, and three
in which the Hidden of the Hidden dwells. And afterwards, they stand upon these three heads
in those channels that prepare <unclear>the oil</unclear> and they flow upon this Supernal Brain
which is hidden and sealed within. When they flow and spread out, there are shells upon shells <note>layers of concealment or protection</note>, and brains
hidden within their shells, and a brain hidden within its shells. And they are distinguished after the brain of this
[source] of all, which is pressed and hidden so that nothing is known of it at all, except for those three heads
themselves, hidden <unclear>in the brain</unclear> that is not settled except for this...
And these are the three hidden heads, and the Master of All, and the <term>Holy Ancient One</term> is the Hidden One
who is not known. And if this joy is from above, and this holiness is from above to... the joy of every heart.
And He is the concealment of a great vision, and He is blessed above, the <term>Ancient of all Ancients</term> <note>original: "Atika de-kol Atikin"</note>, who is
hidden and not revealed... when His face is pressed away from the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note>, then a supernal darkness
is darkened... and so they come to know the Beard of the <term>Holy Ancient One</term>, from all that is highest of all,
which is nourished from the <term>Holy Ancient One</term> by the waters of the Torah, and they praise... Him, for they are
from every essence of the Male <note>the active/giving aspect of divinity</note> that is pressed and hidden, except in the renewal. And this is what we say: "All that lives,"
for they are from Him and within Him. When it is pressed for us, it emerges, and this is sweeter than all that they say: "Holy,"
and it is seen... to Him, and a portion of supernal joy that never ceases.

It emphasizes the unity of these three aspects within the Holy Ancient One (Atika Kadisha) and their role in channeling divine sustenance to the lower worlds.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar - The Lesser Assembly)

**Rabbi Shimon** opened and said, it is written:
> And let the beauty of the Lord our God be upon us; and establish the work of our hands upon us; yes, the work of our hands establish it. <note>Psalm 90:17</note>

The companions have already established the meaning of this verse. But come and see: <term>Beauty</term> <note>original: "No'am"</note> refers to the <term>Holy Ancient One</term> <note>original: "Atika Kadisha," the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine</note>. In every place where this "Beauty" is found, all the worlds are in joy, in perfection, and in all goodness. "And establish the work of our hands upon us"—this is the place where the bond of all supreme mysteries resides, which is <term>Understanding</term> <note>original: "Binah," the Divine Mother</note>, for she is the "work of hands." Just as it is said:
> The Lord by wisdom founded the earth; by understanding He established the heavens. <note>Proverbs 3:19</note>

"Establish it upon us"—this is the <term>Divine Presence</term> <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note> who is bound within Understanding. "And the work of our hands establish *him*" <note>note: the Hebrew suffix "-hu" can mean "him" or "it"</note>—this is the <term>Righteous One</term> <note>original: "Tzadik," referring to the sefira of Yesod, the foundation</note>. For there is "establish *upon us*" and there is "establish *him*." "Establish upon us" is as you say:
> And these are the names of the children of Israel who came to Egypt. <note>Exodus 1:1</note>

This refers to the Shekhinah. "Establish *him*"—this is the Righteous One who is called "He" <note>original: "Hu"</note>. "Establish him" is the mystery of which it is said, "The righteous is the foundation of the world." <note>Proverbs 10:25</note> Come and see, it is written:
> And the Lord God built the rib which He had taken from the man into a woman. <note>Genesis 2:22</note>

What is the meaning of "And He built" <note>original: "Vayiven"</note>? This refers to <term>Understanding</term> <note>original: "Binah," sharing a linguistic root with "building"</note>, through which everything is built. "God" <note>original: "Elohim"</note> refers to the <term>Holy Ancient One</term>, who dwells at the head of Understanding; in Him is "Beauty" found, and through Him is everything built. "From the man"—this is the <term>Primordial Man</term> <note>original: "Adam Kadmon"</note> of the World of Emanation <note>original: "Atzilut"</note>. For there is a "Man" of the World of Creation, and there is a "Man" of the World of Emanation, who is the Supernal Man. "Which He had taken from the man"—this is the Supernal Man. "Into a woman"—this is the <term>Shekhinah</term>, for she is called "Woman." "And He brought her to the man"—this is the Supernal Man who is called "Man," because he clings to her; for without her, he is not called "Man." Come and see that "Man" is not found except in a place where <term>Male and Female</term> are found, as it is written:
> Male and female He created them, and blessed them, and called their name Man in the day when they were created. <note>Genesis 5:2</note>

Literally "Man"; no other word is written, but rather "Man" to establish that one is not called "Man" unless they are as one. Come and see another matter regarding the mystery of the Supernal Man: anyone who separates them <note>the male and female aspects</note> is as if he causes a separation Above. For Above, blessing is not found except in a place where there is male and female, as it is said: "And He blessed them and called their name Man in the day when they were created." When they were as one, blessing was found; when they were not as one, blessing was not found at all. And anyone in whom male and female are not found as one does not...

<summary>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai explains the mystical architecture of the Divine, emphasizing that the title "Man" and the flow of Divine blessing only exist when the masculine and feminine principles (Binah, Shekhinah, and the Supernal Man) are in perfect union.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

<margin>Page 86</margin>

We have learned: waters descend from above to below, and these are the waters of life called the <term>Well of Living Waters</term> <note>Hebrew: *Beer Mayim Chayim*. In Kabbalah, this often represents the feminine divine principle (Malchut) receiving the flow from the higher realms</note>. It is called the Well of Living Waters more so because of the excellence of the sound that comes from the waters found in this place without a voice; and because of this, it is called the Well of Living Waters.
Regarding the matter of the "voice"—the voice that exists and the voice that descends from above to below—nothing is found to speak more than the <term>gushing</term> <note>Aramaic: *nevi'u*, referring to the bubbling source or spring</note> that comes from the waters called the "gushing of life." # Vayakhel (And He Assembled)

## Main Text (Zohar)

At any time that a person arrives early to the synagogue <note>original: "bei knishta"</note> so that he is one of the ten <note>The Minyan, or quorum of ten men required for full Jewish communal prayer.</note> who are prepared to mention the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He <term>the standard rabbinic title for God</term>, the Divine Presence rests upon him even before the rest of the ten arrive. And once the ten have arrived and prayed, the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed in mystical thought as the feminine aspect of God that dwells among humanity.</note> rests upon them, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives them a portion and says: "I am prepared to give my first arrival his portion," for he entered first. Concerning such a person it is written: -> "And He said to me, You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified" <- <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>. <term>To say to him</term> that He comes together with those ten, aside from the matter of the Sanctification <note>The Kedushah prayer</note>. <term>To say to him</term> that He dwells in the synagogue among them. What is the matter? Because there are ten <term>limbs</term> <note>original: "shayfin"</note> of the body, <term>to say to him</term> that the mouth is like the voice of a human which contains ten limbs <note>In Zoharic anatomy, the production of the human voice is often linked to ten physical components or spiritual forces</note>, for the <term>Voice</term> is made of ten, and they use them for Torah and for prayer. 

And at the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, comes into the synagogue and does not find ten, even though all the "limbs" are ready <term>to say to him</term> to act, He is prepared as a Voice, but there is no one to cry out. The Voice is ready to be in the synagogue, but it does not enter; and this Voice is like a mother who has no ten to support her and thus she becomes diminished. And regarding this, the Shekhinah is the time of the holy ones who come and are found. For eight limbs, there is no "Voice" limb, and this is the day of the count where it is not found, and one wonders at the Voice which is ready but not found. <term>What is the reason?</term> Because the count of ten is the Shekhinah, for such and such is the Voice. And because of this, the limbs of the count are all destined to be found as forty. Let there be a Voice in the count, because this is the support of the ten, and it shall certainly be a Voice. And because of this, the Shekhinah considers the count as ten limbs ready to produce a Voice, and when <term>to say to him</term> it is ready but is not there, it is not from these. It was ready to give a Voice, but the time was turned back. <term>To say to him</term> it was ready but not found, for the time of this is held above in the count of ten, which is in a great light. <term>What is the reason?</term> Like the letter *He* <note>The letter H, numerically 5, often representing the Shekhinah</note>, who is the Shekhinah of eight...

-> **The Matter of the Voice** <-

And regarding what I said, that it is called "Voice" because of the limbs of the six <note>Referring to the six directions or the six emotive attributes (Sefirot)</note> of the count that are ready. It is called "Voice" from it, for the limbs are <term>to say to him</term> eight limbs that were among them in the count, and it is increased, and when it is a Voice, it is certainly a Voice. For behold, everything is found within it, the Shekhinah of the count, upon the portion...

***

<summary>This passage explains that the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) dwells in a synagogue even for the first person to arrive, but emphasizes that a quorum of ten is required to manifest the mystical "Voice." This "Voice" is described as a composite of ten spiritual "limbs" necessary for the Shekhinah to be fully realized in the community.</summary>

He created the world after the pattern of the world above, and He built this world according to the likeness of the world above. For this reason, the Holy One, Blessed be He, made this world with the letter *Dalet* and created it with the letter *He*, as we have established. And thus we have rightly said: everything that exists above exists below. Your sign for this is: "All the souls that came with Jacob..." <note>Genesis 46:26</note> When they were in a single union, then all were joyful and the levels were all as one...

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Vayakhel, specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of the daily prayer cycle and the sacrificial offerings in the Temple.</meta>

## Section: Vayakhel

...[of the house of judgment]. And because of this, the beginning of the sacrificial offering was in the morning, as it is written <note>Exodus 29:39</note> **"The one lamb you shall offer in the morning."** At that time, that "Morning of the Ancient One" <note>original: *Boker de-Atika*; a reference to the highest, most merciful aspect of the Divine, the Sefirah of Keter</note> is found, and all faces shine, and joy is found in all worlds. All the gates of freedom are opened, and the poor stand in prayer and are given [sustenance] through mercy and joy. 

Because of this, when the morning awakens, it is a "time of favor" <note>original: *Et Ratzon*</note> for everyone. A person should rejoice in the joy of the Torah and in the joy of the Torah's commandments, and direct their heart and will in prayer to draw upon themselves the "thread of loving-kindness" <note>original: *Chut shel Chesed*</note>. They are then given a portion in this Morning, and one must strive to merit it. 

But when the morning passes and midday <note>original: *Palgut Tihra*</note> arrives, then all those gates of freedom and mercy are closed. Harsh Judgment <note>original: *Dina Kashya*</note> awakens and is found in the world. A person must then watch themselves and know that Judgment dwells in the world. Regarding this time, it is written <note>Isaiah 5:11</note> **"Woe unto them that rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink; that continue until night, till wine inflame them!"** 

"Until night" refers to midday, for then the "twilight" begins to face toward the evening. A person needs at this time to awaken mercy so that the harsh judgment dwelling in the world does not rule over them. For this reason, the <term>Twilight Offering</term> <note>original: *Korban de-bein ha-arbayim*; the afternoon sacrifice in the Temple</note> is the sacrifice called *Minchah* <note>literally "an offering" or "gift"</note>. Because of this, the Patriarch Isaac established the Afternoon Prayer (*Minchah*), and a person must focus their will in this prayer because powerful Judgment rules the world.

In the morning, a person should rejoice and know that the morning is the time when the mercy of the "Holy Ancient One" awakens. At the afternoon prayer, one must know that powerful Judgment awakens and must watch themselves. At the evening prayer, one must know that the night spreads its wings over the world, and all those masters of judgment—the lower judgments—rule in the world, and one must watch themselves...

<summary>This passage explains the mystical significance of the three daily prayer times, linking the morning to divine mercy (Chesed) and the afternoon and evening to increasing levels of divine judgment (Din).</summary>
<keywords>Morning Prayer, Minchah, Mercy, Judgment, Ancient One, Sefirot, Isaac, Sacrifices, Vayakhel</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar)

->**Leviticus**<-

**"When an ox, or a sheep, or a goat is born..."** <note>Leviticus 22:27</note> Rabbi Shimon said (referencing page 18b): We have learned that at the hour this verse was stated, it was the hour when the structure of the Moon <note>original: "Sihara" — representing the Shekhinah or Divine Presence in its receptive aspect</note> was completed, and everything was perfected. It was an hour when joy flowed to all worlds, and all joys and all lights shone. At the moment this completion occurred, it was fitting to say, "An ox, or a sheep..." When the firmament rises upon a single thread from below and speaks within the firmament, because it rises and goes forth as we have learned. This verse was recited during a time of distress by those who said, "Remember and have mercy," and they called out. Then it returned and went forth; this is the hour that called to us, for behold, it is **the son of the eighth day** <term>Son of the eighth day: A reference to the requirement that an animal be at least eight days old before being sacrificed, which mystically links to the eighth Sephirah (Binah) or the transcendence beyond the natural seven-day cycle</term>. Is there not an "eighth day" in the mystery of faith? It is diligently called the "Holy Eighth," as it says, "And it came to pass on the eighth day," calling it a holy calling, a mystery in which glory is seen. In the mystery of this opening, where there is no report <note>perhaps referring to a state of pure being beyond verbal description</note>, it is prepared. At that time, the "ox" <note>symbolizing strength or the left side of the divine attributes</note> hears the debt of his children through the mercy of their lamentation and the prayer of that **sacrifice** <term>Korban: Literally "drawing near"; an offering intended to bring the human and divine closer together</term>. Then the name of the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <term>Kudsha Brich Hu: The standard Aramaic reference to God in the Zohar</term> rises in joy even higher above, and joy flows from the foundations of those three others in light, and all those others are rectified. I know that it is written, "An ox, or a sheep, or a goat"—see the deeds that emerge from this act, which teaches of the deeds above and the deeds below, that one should walk in them. Therefore, it says "And it was on the eighth," a language implying that they joined the upper and the lower. May He grant us mercy and may they be examined even higher above, because this is the deeper mystery of "An ox, or a sheep..." and then all are found in joy. The light rises to hear, so that the upper and lower may be joined through it. We find ourselves within this time, prepared and standing. Does the verse not say "when it is born"? This refers to the mystery above, for behold, Isaac <note>representing the attribute of Gevurah or Strength/Judgment</note> is above them. What was it that returned this in joy? It was for the sake of the highest level, which flows like a soul to the body, erecting everything. Joy is prepared for them even more. "An ox or a sheep"—see the support that is seen in this calculation and in the mystery of this verse regarding the "eighth," as we have said.

->**And He Called**<-
> And the Lord called to Moses and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying. <note>Leviticus 1:1</note>

Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse,
> O Lord, I have heard the report of You, and I am afraid; O Lord, revive Your work in the midst of the years, in the midst of the years make it known; in wrath remember mercy. <note>Habakkuk 3:2</note>

The companions have already established the meaning of this verse, for every single word of the Torah contains <term>higher secrets</term> <note>original: "razin ilain"</note> and hidden things of wisdom. Come and see: at the moment when the Holy One, blessed be He, awakened to create the world, it arose in His will to create the world with the letter *Bet*. This is because *Bet* signifies "Blessing" <note>The Hebrew word for blessing, *Berakhah*, begins with the letter Bet</note>, and through it, the world was created. But the letter *Aleph* is the secret of "One," which is the <term>Supreme Crown</term> <note>Keter Elyon: the highest and most primordial of the ten Sefirot, or Divine emanations</note>.

And come and see, in this verse that says "And He called to Moses," the letter *Aleph* [at the end of the word *Vayikra*] is a "small *Aleph*." Because of this, one must know the secret of this matter. There are three letters that comprise the secret of faith, and the *Aleph* is the portion of the Supernal realm.

<margin>Because of this, it is a small Aleph</margin>

And when Moses awakened in prophecy, the Holy One, blessed be He, called to him from the Tent of Meeting. This is the secret of the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine aspect of God</note>, who is called the "Tent of Meeting." From this vantage point, Moses was permitted to see what other prophets were not able to see.

---

->**And Now**<-
> And now, I pray, let the power of my Lord be great, just as You have spoken, saying. <note>Numbers 14:17</note>

Come and see this verse: why did Moses say, "And now, let the power of my Lord be great"? It is because this is the secret of the All, which is the strength of faith. At the moment when mercies are awakened in the world, as it were, the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, is glorified.

And because of this, blessing only rests in a place where the male and female are found as one. <note>In Zoharic thought, "male and female" refers both to human marriage and the mystical union of divine attributes.</note> And for this reason, blessing rests upon the Land of Israel more than all other lands, for in this place the male and female dwell, and He joins them together as one. Rabbi Eleazar said: And even if they saw those thirty-four types of sorcery <term>kesamin; divination or magical arts</term> that the false prophets practiced, and the three knots <note>mystical bindings or connections</note> which are all secrets of sorcery that humans cannot [ordinarily] comprehend, and they were to arrange them before you to show that they are all nothing but the secret of the **Name of Falsehood** <note>original: "Shema de-Shikiru"; a mystical designation for the source of deceptive spiritual power</note>—these are the thirty-four types of sorcery.

And because of this, they have no permission to say that this world is anything other than under the authority of the Holy One, Blessed be He. For those thirty-four [types] of the Name of Falsehood are certainly held in His hand, for the whole world is conducted through them. "From the mountains of the East" <note>original: "Me-harerei kedem"</note>—this is the secret of the Name of Falsehood where he dwells, and the dominion of those secrets is held within them. And this is the secret of Balak, King of Moab.

And the secret of **Zippor** <note>literally "Bird"</note> is the secret of the sorcery of that bird that knew what was [happening]. And the Jewish sages said that because of it, he would perform divinations; within it was the secret of sorcery. And regarding this, it is written:

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Zohar, the foundational work of Jewish mysticism (Kabbalah). ## The Opening of the Book of Splendor

[...understanding in the world how many commandments and blessings apply to all the Divine qualities]

**Hezekiah opened** and said: "Like a rose among the thorns" <note>original: "Kevarda bein hachochim"; quoting Song of Songs 2:2</note>. What is this rose? It is the **Assembly of Israel** <note>Knesset Yisrael: a mystical personification of the Jewish people and the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note>. Just as a rose contains <term>red and white</term> <note>symbolizing the balance of Justice and Mercy</note>, so too does the Assembly of Israel contain <term>judgment and mercy</term>. Just as a rose has <term>thirteen petals</term>, so too does the Assembly of Israel have thirteen attributes of mercy that surround it on every side. 

So too, the name <term>God</term> <note>Elohim</note> mentioned here <note>in the first verse of Genesis</note>, from the moment it is mentioned, it brings forth thirteen words to surround the Assembly of Israel and to protect her. After this, the name is mentioned another time. This is because there are five strong petals that surround the rose, and these are the five gates of salvation that spread over her. Regarding this it is written: "I will lift the cup of salvations" <note>Psalms 116:13</note>. This is the "Cup of Blessing" which must be held by five fingers, just like the rose which sits upon five strong petals, corresponding to the pattern of the five fingers. And for this reason, the name <term>God</term> <note>Elohim</note> is mentioned a second time. From this point forward, it is written: "Let there be light." 

And this is the light that was created and then hidden, and it entered into the <term>Covenant</term> <note>Brit: referring to the mystical sign of the covenant and the sefirah of Yesod</note> which entered the rose and produced seed within her. This is what is called "a fruit-bearing tree whose seed is within it" <note>Genesis 1:11</note>. And this seed truly stands within the Covenant. Just as the Covenant is found in forty-eight pairings, so too is this seed found in the forty-eight modes by which the Torah is acquired. All of this stands upon the <term>secret of the Covenant</term>. And regarding this it is written: "In the beginning, God created."

Rabbi Shimon opened and said: "The buds appeared on the earth" <note>Song of Songs 2:12</note>. These "buds" are the generations of the world. When did they "appear on the earth"? On the third day of creation, as it is written: "And the earth brought forth" <note>Genesis 1:12</note>. "The time of pruning has arrived"—this refers to the pruning of the tyrants of the world. "And the voice of the turtle-dove"—this is the <term>voice of Jacob</term>. As it is written: "The voice of the turtle-dove is heard in our land." In "our land" literally. As it is written regarding your first day <note>of Sukkot</note>, which is the day that atones <unclear>for all</unclear> <unclear>deeds</unclear>; this is the seventh day. And why the seventh day? Because it is the Sabbath of the Moon <note>the Shekhinah</note> <unclear>which repairs</unclear> the <unclear>sinners</unclear> of the world...

<summary>This opening passage of the Zohar uses the imagery of a rose among thorns to explain the mystical nature of the Assembly of Israel and its protection by the thirteen attributes of Divine Mercy. It links the act of Creation in Genesis to the symbolic "buds" of the generations and the "Covenant" that sustains life.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse of the Zohar regarding the spiritual significance of gender and unity. It focuses on the ontological necessity of the union between male and female principles for the manifestation of holiness and the reception of divine blessing.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

Holy are those in whom the male and female are found, for in them resides the names of the Holy King. They are seen to be from the side of the holiness of the Holy King. However, all those in whom the male and female are not found as one are from the side of the "lower name" <note>original: "shema de-letata"; referring to the sitra achra or the unrectified realms</note>, as the companions have established. In every place where male and female are not found as one, they are not from the side of holiness.

And this is the <term>secret</term> <note>original: "soda"; a hidden mystical truth</note> that Rabbi Shimon (may his memory be a blessing) said: In every place where male and female are found, but male and female are not as one, the <term>blessing</term> <note>original: "birchata"</note> from above does not rest upon them, just as it is said:
> "He blessed them and called their name Adam on the day they were created." <note>Genesis 5:2</note>

"Adam on the day they were created," etc. For behold, the blessing does not rest except in a place where <term>male and female</term> <note>original: "dechar ve-nuqba"</note> are found as one. And because of this, one is not called <term>Adam</term> <note>The Hebrew word for "Human" or "Man"</note> except when male and female are as one.

Come and see, for regarding the holiness above it is said: "Maintaining kindness for thousands," etc. <note>Exodus 34:7</note> "Maintaining kindness for thousands"—and the female of the male is not called Adam except within the holiness above. Come and see, for male and female together are called Adam, and concerning this it is written:
> "Then I will remember My covenant with Jacob, and also My covenant with Isaac, and also My covenant with Abraham I will remember; and I will remember the land." <note>Leviticus 26:42</note>

And this is the secret of "I will remember My covenant with Jacob," etc. Jacob and David are found as one. This is the <term>mystery</term> <note>original: "raza"</note> of the matter: male and female as one. For it is written, "I will remember My covenant with Jacob," etc. This is the mystery of male and female as one, because the <term>covenant</term> <note>original: "berit"; often associated with the sefirah of Yesod, the procreative/unifying force</note> is male and female as one. Male and female together are called Adam, and therefore the covenant together is called Adam.

Come and see, the covenant is called <term>Joseph</term> <note>In Kabbalah, the biblical Joseph represents the sefirah of Yesod, the "Sign of the Covenant"</note>, and Joseph is male and female as one. Because of this, it is written: "I will remember My covenant with Jacob, and My covenant with Isaac, and My covenant with Abraham I will remember, and the land I will remember." All of them are as one; they are one single mystery. And concerning this it is written: "I will remember My covenant with Jacob."

## Main Text (The Zohar)

Come and see <note>original: "Ta chazi"</note>: just as a female receives from a male, so too does this Moon <note>The Moon represents the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence</note> receive from the Sun <note>The Sun represents Tiferet, the central divine beauty/harmony</note>. All those lower levels receive from this source. We have already established that this Sun shines upon the Moon, and when it shines upon her, then all those lower levels and all those who guard the commandments of the Torah are blessed. Then, everything is in joy; everything is in perfection. Because of this, Israel below—who take hold of the <term>Secret of Faith</term> <note>The mystical understanding of the unity of the Divine</note>—how fortunate is their portion in this world and in the world to come! For the Holy One, Blessed be He, blesses them and illuminates them from above, and then everything is in joy. Look at what is written:

> "And over the heads of the living creatures there was the likeness of a firmament, like the color of the awesome ice..." <note>Ezekiel 1:22</note>

And we have learned: what is this "firmament"? This is the firmament that is above the Living Creatures <note>The Chayot, high-ranking angels in Ezekiel's vision</note>. This firmament shines upon all the Living Creatures, and from this firmament go forth all those lights that illuminate them. From this firmament, all the Living Creatures are nourished and shine. We have established that this firmament is the one that stands over them all, and it holds them all in its authority. Because it holds them all, it is called "Heaven" <note>Hebrew: Shamayim</note>, as it is said: <term>the Heavens</term> <note>referring to the particle "et" in Genesis 1:1</note>—this comes to include all those hosts and camps that go forth from it. This firmament, which is above the Living Creatures, is what shines upon them and teaches them the paths and ways to gaze upon the glory of their Master. And come and see: when this firmament shines upon the Living Creatures, they all then rejoice in joy. And come and see what is written:

> "And the living creatures ran and returned like the appearance of a flash of lightning." <note>Ezekiel 1:14</note>

What is the meaning of "ran and returned"? It is because they cannot stay in one place. Why? Because when this firmament shines upon them, they shine and rejoice and run to receive that light; but when that light is hidden from them...

<summary>This page uses the metaphor of the Sun and Moon to explain how divine energy flows from the higher realms to the lower worlds, specifically interpreting Ezekiel's vision of the "firmament" as the source of angelic nourishment and movement.</summary>
<keywords>Shekhinah, Tiferet, Ezekiel's Chariot, Living Creatures, Firmament, Divine Light, Secret of Faith</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of Jethro’s advice to Moses, specifically focusing on the mystical interpretation of "And you shall discern" (Exodus 18:21) as a foundation for the Kabbalistic science of physiognomy.</meta>

## Jethro

**"And you shall discern from among all the people"**—these are additional matters. When they came before Moses, he said, "This is not before me, but before the King of the whole world." And because Jethro said to Moses, **"And you shall discern,"** and he said **"from among all the people"** <note>Hebrew: *mi-kol ha-am*</note> and did not simply say "from the people," but rather **"from among all the people,"** it implies that from within the entirety of the nation one must recognize who is wise. As it is said (Proverbs 10:8): **"The wise in heart will receive commandments,"** etc. **"And you shall discern"** refers to the markings <term>Sirtutin: the lines or features of the body</term>, for there are four masters of markings who are recognized by the primary markings. When a person enters before the King and is recognized by them, then the wise gaze upon him and recognize who he is. These are: the markings of the hands, the markings of the forehead, the markings of the face, and the markings of the lips. Through these, one is recognized by the Holy One, Blessed be He—whether he is righteous or whether he is wicked.

And this is the meaning of **"And you shall discern from among all the people"**—through the markings that you see in the face, in the hair, in the markings of the forehead, in the eyes, in the lips, and in the markings of the hands. These six features are those by which Moses recognized people. And King Solomon, when he built the Temple, gazed and recognized everyone; the masters of wisdom were before him and they recognized every single man. For these markings exist within Man, and the secret of this is (Genesis 9:6): **"In the image of God He made man."**

It is through the "Image" <note>Hebrew: *Tzelem*</note> that a person is recognized. And if you should say that it has already been established that all human beings are recognized by a single image—it is not so. Rather, there is a supreme secret in this matter that we have learned: the image of human beings changes from one to another, and they are not equal. This is the secret: the image of human beings contains a supreme mystery. And thus it was taught: there are four letters belonging to the Holy One, Blessed be He, which are Y-H-W-H <note>The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter divine name</note>, and they are hinted at within Man. This is the secret: the **Y** <note>Yod</note> is the head; the **H** <note>Heh</note> is the body; the **W** <note>Vav</note> is the right arm; the **H** <note>Heh</note> is the left arm. <note>This describes the human form as a physical manifestation of the Divine Name.</note> This is the supreme secret by which a person is recognized, and the secret of the verse that is written (Psalms 39:7): **"Surely man walks in an image."**

<summary>This page explains the Kabbalistic practice of physiognomy, asserting that Moses and Solomon could discern a person's character through physical traits like facial lines and hand markings, which reflect the Divine Name (Y-H-W-H) imprinted on the human form.</summary>
<keywords>physiognomy, markings, Sirtutin, Divine Image, Tzelem, Tetragrammaton, Moses, Solomon, Jethro, character discernment</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar - The Great Assembly)

... from the line of the white thread of the hair <note>original: "ku chivarta de-sa'arei"</note> that is found within it, from all these others, and because of this we call it the **Holy Ancient One** <note>term: Atika Kadisha; the most primordial, "ancient" manifestation of the Divine</note> who is found within the whole. And thus all are included within Him. Within Him, it is because **three heads are found, one upon the other, and one above the other.**

One head is the **Concealed Wisdom** <note>term: Chochmah Setima'ah; the first flash of intuition or potentiality</note> which is covered and not revealed. And this Concealed Wisdom is found above the head of the Ancient One. And because this is not distinguished, it is not known and not recognized; and because this Concealed Wisdom is not distinguished and not revealed in the head, we call it **Nothingness** <note>term: Ayin; representing the infinite source that is "nothing" to human perception because it is beyond all "things"</note>.

And because of this, it is the beginning of the head which is not a head. And because it is not a head, we call it the "Head that is Not Known." And because of this, it is the beginning of all Wisdom, which is the beginning of all the limbs of the body; through it they spread out and in it they are found.

And this Concealed Wisdom is the second head. And within it are found the seven strengths of the hair that go out from it. And the impression of each and every one is found. And this is the head called Concealed Wisdom. The impression of the flaming fire is crowned with thirty-two paths <note>original: "taltin u-trein shevilin"; the 32 paths of wisdom through which the universe was created</note> that go out. And this is the Wisdom that spreads to all sides. And this Concealed Wisdom is found as the second head in this manner.

The third head, which is above them all, is called the **Holy Ancient One**, the most concealed of all concealed things. And this Holy Ancient One is not recognized and not found, and in the secret of the word it is written:
> No eye has seen a God besides You <note>Isaiah 64:3</note>
And because of this it is written:
> And Wisdom—from where [Ayin] shall it be found? <note>Job 28:12; the Zohar reads "Ayin" not as "where" but as the name of the source: "Wisdom is found from the Void"</note>

And because of this, the beginning of all beginnings is called **Nothingness**. And this Concealed Wisdom which is within the secret of the second head is the beginning of all Wisdom. And because it is the beginning, there are found within it **thirty-two paths**, which is the Wisdom that goes out from the Holy Ancient One. For when this Holy Ancient One—who is the third head—shines, He illuminates this Concealed Wisdom, which is the second head. And from this Concealed Wisdom, Wisdom spreads to all sides. And because it is the Wisdom that comes from the Ancient One...

<summary>This passage describes the "Three Heads" of the Divine crown, explaining how the unknowable source (Ayin) transitions into Concealed Wisdom and then into the 32 paths of creation. It emphasizes that the highest level of divinity remains entirely beyond human perception.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Vayechi (Genesis 47:28–50:26). The text focuses on the spiritual mechanics of Jacob’s prophetic vision and the necessity of grounding mystical wisdom in the biblical text.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

Rabbi Eleazar said: Anyone who speaks a word of wisdom <note>original: *milla de-chokhmata*</note> and does not derive it from the Torah is as if he has destroyed and corrupted it. For this reason, it is good to learn one word from another, to join them together, and to know their root. From where do we learn this? Rabbi Simeon said: At the time we see a person lifting his eyes upward to know the Most Precious of all precious things, [we see] if it is the time to receive that soul, and a glory rises greater than any glory. Woe to the one who does not know how to discern this! For the Holy One, blessed be He, delighted in the desire of Jacob’s soul. From here we learn a word of wisdom, as it is written: *Now the eyes of Israel were dim with age, so that he could not see* <note>Genesis 48:10</note>, yet it is also written: *And Israel saw Joseph’s sons, and said: "Who are these?"* <note>Genesis 48:8</note>.

Rabbi Judah said: This verse indicates that he did see them! So what is the meaning of *he could not see*? It means he did not see them with a perfect light. But at the time he brought them close to him to be blessed, what is written? *And he kissed them, and embraced them* <note>Genesis 48:10</note>. At this point, he saw with a perfect light that he was not able to achieve before.

And regarding this, *And Israel saw Joseph’s sons*—he saw them through the light of prophecy <note>original: *nehorah de-nevuata*</note>. He saw the three levels that would emerge from them later, and thus it is written: *And he said: "Who are these?"* Joseph said to his father: *They are my sons*—and this taught Jacob that they had entered beneath the wings of the Divine Presence <note>the *Shekhinah*, the feminine immanence of God</note>. Therefore it is written: *whom God has given me in this [place]* <note>Genesis 48:9</note>.

We learn a word of wisdom: regarding anyone who is seen, [God] gazes upon him with prophecy. And anyone who lifts his eyes in the Torah <note>original: *Oraita*</note>, the light of the Holy One, blessed be He, rests upon him. In the Torah, when the heart is revealed and there is no [foreign] heat in it, through it he learns and inherits his inheritance. As it is written: *And he blessed them that day, saying: "By you shall Israel bless..."* <note>Genesis 48:20</note>. The Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to bless Israel and to give them complete authority in all this world, and all the nations who worship stars and signs shall fall before them, as it is written: *And afterward...*

->**Vayechi (And He Lived)**<-

Rabbi Yose opened: *And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years...* <note>Genesis 47:28</note>. We have established before him that all the days he entered Egypt, his life was completed in the light of the Holy One, blessed be He, which was unified over him. All the peoples of the earth saw [this], etc. This day, the portion of Jacob was greater.

# Portion of Genesis

It emerged from within the concealment of Thought, which no one can grasp.
And the **Upper Point** <note>original: "Nekuda Ila'ah," referring to the first manifestation of wisdom (Chokhmah)</note> emerged from Thought, and there is no one who can grasp it or what is above it.
It is **Thought** <term>Thought: "Machshavah," the divine conceptual realm where all existence is pre-formed</term>. And even though it is the Thought that is the concealment of all,

no end <note>original: "sof"</note>, and the will of Thought is within it, and no one can grasp it as we have said.
And because of this, it is called **The Infinite** <term>Infinite: "Ein Sof," the Boundless Divine before any attributes or emanations appear</term>. And it is within the hidden Thought of Thought.
They coupled with one another and were called "Thought," and one was hidden within the other.
And because they are hidden and never known, it is called "The Infinite" when it stands
in the six hundred and thirty <note>A mystical numerical configuration of divine forces</note> where one is included within the other. When the light expanded

within it—that letter *Yod* which is the **Upper Point**—there emerged from it this secret: one within
that Point. It brought forth a Will, and one was built within the other, and one was hidden within the other,
until it brought forth **Seven Paths** <term>Seven Paths: "Sheva Shivilin," the seven emotional attributes or days of creation</term> which are seventy voices outside the light,
light upon light, and hidden outside of the Point. And it is Thought, and it is called

## Portion of Terumah

Because all the heavenly hosts are illuminated by this light of which we have spoken. And this light emerges from within the Hidden of all Hidden <note>original: "Temira de-kol Temirin," referring to the most primordial, unknowable aspect of the Divine</note>, which is not known at all and is unrecognizable.

And this is the **Tree that is called Life**. It is modeled after the Supernal Tree when it brings forth life to the world. And this Tree spreads out to all sides, and its branches spread out in every direction. And concerning it, when one is found within this Tree, it is as it says:
> Under it the beasts of the field found shade, and in its branches the birds of the sky dwelt, and from it all the children of the world were nourished.
<note>A paraphrase of Daniel 4:9 or Ezekiel 17:23, used here to describe the spiritual sustenance provided by the Divine</note>
This Tree is magnified and honored above all other trees. And because of this, it is called the Tree of Life. And regarding this it is written:
> It is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it
<note>Proverbs 3:18</note>
and it is written:
> And the tree of life was in the midst of the garden
<note>Genesis 2:9</note>
Literally in the "midst of the garden"—in the very center of the Garden of Eden. For that place is called **Garden of Eden**, and in its center is this Tree. This is because there lies the root and the essence of all the trees in the Garden, and from it are drawn all the other trees and all those delights and all those good things found there. In this same manner, this Supernal Tree is concealed and hidden high above, and from its radiance all other hosts and all other levels are illuminated.

And if you should ask: "What is this Tree?" These are the seven supernal levels <note>The seven lower Sefirot or divine emanations</note> which are called the "Seven Days." And because they are all united in it in a single bond, and it emerges from all of them and connects with all of them, it is called the Tree of Life—of actual Life—for all life above and below depends upon it. Therefore, the seven levels are the seven branches of this Tree. And because every single branch is a level unto itself, it is called a Tree over all its branches <unclear>for the time...</unclear>

<summary>This page describes the "Tree of Life" as a central mystical structure that emanates from the unknowable Divine to nourish all worlds. It identifies the Tree with the seven supernal levels (Sefirot) that unify the spiritual ecosystem of the Garden of Eden.</summary>

<keywords>Tree of Life, Garden of Eden, Sefirot, Divine Light, Seven Days, Hidden of all Hidden, spiritual nourishment</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar/Commentary)

Because the Form is greater than anything when the Grace <note>Aramaic: *Chesed*</note> rises or is uplifted, which comes from the Fortune <note>Aramaic: *Mazal*, referring here to the beard of the Ancient Holy One as a conduit of influence</note> and within it they are planted. The prayer is well-prepared; the Grace of the supreme restoration goes forth, which rises into the Thought <note>The hidden mental realm of the Divine</note> that is certainly known. And the seed of the Fortune shall come upon it when it comes from the supreme Thought. And when it is found and the Male and Female are uplifted, they rise up to the Fortune of the Ancient Wisdom, which is the foundation of all things above. And it is not seen except by the Elder of the Ancient Holy One <note>Aramaic: *Atika Kadisha*, the highest manifestation of the Divine</note>, and every holy place cleaves to Him. And when it descends and is prepared for the levels <note>original: "למדרי'", abbreviation for *madregot*</note>, the Male and Female are seen and known together as Jacob, and he is called "Heaven," and he is the beauty <note>Aramaic: *Chen*</note> of all worlds. For there is no Presence <note>Hebrew: *Shekhinah*</note> of the Lord except when He is within it, and He shall sanctify it. And the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "קב"ה"</note>, sanctifies it, and because of this, it is called concerning Him: *The Lord shall reign forever and ever* <note>Exodus 15:18</note>. ## Main Text (The Zohar)

And because of this, when blessing is found in the world, everything is found in joy.

Because the city of **Edom** <note>Symbolically representing the forces of strict judgment and historical oppressors</note> is from the side of **Harsh Judgment**, and therefore He remembers them <insert>Israel</insert> so that mercies will be awakened for them. 

Come and see: when judgment is found in the world, the **Holy One, Blessed Be He** remembers Israel, though they do not know it; He remembers them for good, as it is written: ->"I remember for you the kindness of your youth"<- etc. <note>Jeremiah 2:2</note>. And then mercy is found upon them. 
In every place where judgment is found...

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Torah portion of Shemini, specifically focusing on the spiritual mechanics of repentance and restitution as outlined in the Zohar. It bridges the legal requirements of the Torah (Exodus, Leviticus, and Numbers) with the Kabbalistic understanding of the soul's restoration.</meta>

# Shemini

## Main Text (The Zohar)

One who takes a debt <note>original: "hova" - can mean a financial debt, a sin, or a legal obligation</note> from his fellow, the law is that he must pay him back restitution in the exact measure of that debt which he took. Come and see: one who sins before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and returns in repentance <note>original: "teyuvta" - the act of returning to God</note>, just as the law for this person who took a debt from his fellow is to pay back that debt, so too is the law for a person before the Holy One, Blessed be He. Come and see: one who steals, or robs, or oppresses his fellow, and it is clarified that he has committed a legal wrong, what is written?
> (Exodus 22:8) "For every lost thing... he shall pay double to his neighbor."
And the sages established that if he confesses on his own, he only pays the principal amount. And so it is before the Holy One, Blessed be He: one who sins and incurs guilt before Him, and returns in repentance and confesses his sin on his own, the Holy One, Blessed be He, atones for him for everything. But if he does not confess on his own until the judgment comes upon him, then it is written:
> (Exodus 22:8) "Whom the judges <note>original: "Elohim" - here interpreted as the court or the attribute of Justice</note> shall condemn, he shall pay double to his neighbor."
And this is "one for two" <note>meaning a double payment</note>. And regarding this it is written:
> (Proverbs 28:13) "But whoever confesses and forsakes them shall have mercy."
Because anyone who confesses his sins on his own, the Holy One, Blessed be He, pushes the judgment away from him and has mercy on him. Come and see: one who takes a debt from his fellow, such as a theft or a robbery, just as there is restitution to the owner, so too there is restitution to the Holy One, Blessed be He. And regarding this it is written:
> (Leviticus 5:24) "Or all that about which he has sworn falsely; he shall restore it in its principal, and shall add the fifth part more unto it."
What does this teach us? It is because he sinned against the Holy One, Blessed be He, and looked at Him and dealt falsely with Him; because of this it is written:
> (Leviticus 5:21) "And commit a trespass against the Lord, and lie unto his neighbor."
And because of this it is written, "and shall add the fifth part more unto it." What is this "fifth part" <note>Hebrew: "Hamishito"</note>? This is <term>Repentance</term> <note>Teshuvah - the return to the source</note> which is called by the letter *He* <note>The fifth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, numerically 5, representing the Sefirah of Binah/Understanding, the source of Repentance</note>. And this is "one for two." And come and see: one who performs repentance causes there to be restitution for that debt before the Holy One, Blessed be He. And regarding this it is written:
> (Numbers 5:7) "Then they shall confess their sin which they have done: and he shall recompense his trespass in its principal <note>literally: "in its head"</note>, and add unto it the fifth part thereof."
What is meant by "in its principal" <note>Hebrew: "Berasho" - at its head</note>? This is the restoration of the "Head," which is Wisdom <note>The Sefirah of Hokhmah</note>. And "its fifth" is Repentance, as we have said. For anyone who performs repentance restores everything. He restores that flaw which he caused by sinning. And regarding this it is written:
> (Ezekiel 18:21) "But if the wicked will turn from all his sins that he hath committed..."
Happy is the person who performs repentance before his Master, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, accepts him and forgives him for all his sins. And not only this, but they raise him up on high and call him a "completely righteous man."

<summary>This passage explains that voluntary confession and repentance (Teshuvah) mitigate divine judgment, transforming a legal obligation into a spiritual restoration that reaches the highest mystical realms of Wisdom and Understanding.</summary>
<keywords>Repentance, Teshuvah, Restitution, Confession, Sefirot, Binah, Hokhmah, Divine Mercy, Justice</keywords>
