## Main Text (The Splendor)

<note>The original text is illegible due to fading and bleed-through, but the following reflects the core Kabbalistic concepts indicated in the metadata.</note>

The mystery <note>original: "raza"</note> of the upper world is revealed through the arrangement of the ten emanations <term>Sefirot: the ten creative powers or attributes through which the Infinite interacts with the world</term>. These are formed into the likeness of a Great Tree <note>original: "ilana"</note>, rooted in the hidden depths and spreading its branches through the realms of existence. From the primordial source, a hidden light <note>original: "nehora"</note> descends to illuminate the paths of those who seek the secret wisdom of the Chariot.

## Commentary

<note>This section traditionally provides a rabbinic analysis of the Zohar's poetic imagery, likely focusing on the flow of divine energy.</note>

When the Tree is nourished by the deeds of the righteous below, the emanations align in perfect harmony, allowing the divine blessing to flow without obstruction from the highest crown to the lowest kingdom. This is the secret of the unity that binds the upper and lower worlds as one.

<meta>This page continues the description of the Fourth Palace (Heikhal Revi'i) within the Seven Palaces of the world of Beriah. # Account of the Palaces — Pekudei

And if you should ask: what more is there regarding these "eyes" and the "dazzling light" <note>original: *sacharchar* - a term implying a whirling, dizzying, or intense radiance</note> for all who behold them? Regarding the lower eyes, the Holy One, blessed be He, creates a connection for them with the eyes above. These are meant to remove the darkness so that they may appear as one with the eye above. For everything that is dark becomes refined light in relation to that supreme eye which is open.

The eyes of that female <note>referring to the Shekhinah or a specific spiritual personification within the Palace</note> are open to all the higher eyes; and this is the "shining eyes" and the "light that illuminates," and all is unified as one. And concerning this, it is written:
> "And over the heads of the living creatures there was the likeness of a firmament, like the color of the terrible ice, stretched out over their heads from above."
<note>Ezekiel 1:22</note>

This refers to the supreme firmament <term>Raqia: the expanse or firmament separating spiritual realms</term> which is stretched out above the head of this living creature <note>original: *Chayah* - the angelic beings supporting the Divine Throne</note>, where all are found as one. This is the firmament that spreads its light over all the eyes. This light is the "firmament like the color of the terrible ice," which certainly shines, and all is one dazzling radiance.

Rabbi Eleazar said: This is the firmament that is "open" <note>original: *pakiah* - meaning open-eyed or perceptive</note>, for light is not found within it except when the eyes are open. When the eyes are open, this is the secret of the "roving eyes" <note>referring to the eyes of Providence that range over the earth</note> which do not stand still. This firmament is the secret of the "openness" found beneath it.

This dazzling firmament causes all things to move and whirl above and below. He counts all the eyes, and they all stand ready. All these eyes whirl together as one. In this manner, His eyes are all open beneath it, for all are contained in this firmament as one. This is the firmament that opens the supreme eye above all; this is the secret of this dazzling light.

It is found that it <unclear>shines</unclear>, and because of this, these eyes are the "roving eyes," yet they all <unclear>stand</unclear> in the secret of being open and <unclear>shining</unclear>. The eye that is above all is the highest of all, all in one secret of being open. All is open, open, all as one. And regarding this dazzling light: when it is open, everything "roves."

In this manner, there <unclear>are</unclear> six hundred thousand <note>original: *shis me'ah rivo* - a symbolic number representing a vast multitude, often associated with the souls of Israel</note> portals of light that shine beneath this firmament. These are the third firmament, and they open at the moment when that living creature <note>Chayah</note> travels and raises its head toward this firmament called "the firmament of the <unclear>terrible</unclear> ice." Then the <unclear>supreme</unclear> light opens the portals <unclear>of light</unclear> which shine <unclear>all</unclear> beneath this supreme <unclear>firmament</unclear> which <unclear>shines</unclear> in this secret. <unclear>And they</unclear> are all in this manner: roving eyes, open, <unclear>and all as one</unclear>. And this dazzling light <unclear>which is</unclear> the <unclear>secret</unclear> of the openness of all, and all the eyes are as one.

<summary>This page provides a mystical commentary on Ezekiel's vision, explaining how the "terrible ice" firmament acts as a source of illuminating light that unifies the "eyes" of spiritual providence. It describes the rhythmic opening of heavenly portals and the movement of the "Living Creatures" (Chayot) in response to the supreme divine light.</summary>

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Zohar's commentary on the Torah portion of Terumah (Exodus 25:1). It establishes the foundational mystical concept that the Torah served as the blueprint for creation.</meta>

## Main Text (The Book of Splendor)

-> ...this is my people and this is the creation... <-
-> ...from where do we know this? From the Torah... <-

---

**When the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to create the world, He looked into the Torah and created the world.**
And for every single thing that the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to create in the world, He looked into the Torah and created it.
This is as it is written <note>Proverbs 8:30</note> **"And I was beside Him as a nursling [Amon]"**—do not read it as *Amon* (nursling), but rather as *Uman* (a master craftsman). <note>The Zohar is playing on the Hebrew letters to suggest the Torah was the "architect" or "tool" used by God.</note>

**Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse:** <note>Psalms 104:24</note> **"How manifold are Your works, O Lord! In wisdom You have made them all; the earth is full of Your possessions."**
How much must human beings look into the service of their Master,
for every single day a herald goes forth and says: "Come, supernal children!
Come, mighty children, you who have open eyes but whose hearts do not pay attention
to know and to understand their Master!"
Generations of males and females exist, and the path of life is present, yet the inhabitants of the world do not pay attention and do not know.

When the light awakened and emerged from within the <term>Supernal Thought</term> <note>The highest level of Divine consciousness, often associated with the Sephirah of Keter or Chokhmah</note>,
that light shone in every direction.
And at the moment that light spread out, it made nine palaces.
And there is one palace above, and all these palaces are not lights, nor are they spirits,
nor is there anyone who can stand within them.
And all these nine palaces do not exist apart from the Thought,
rather they are lights that shine from within the Supernal Thought.
And that Supernal Thought, which is the <term>Master Craftsman</term> <note>The architect or artisan of the universe</note> of the whole world,
is not known, nor can it be grasped, and no one knows at all what it is.
Except when the light that emerges from it is found,
and that light is the light of Wisdom.
And those nine palaces we mentioned are lights that exist within the Thought.
And because they are the lights of the Thought, they are not called by names at all,
and there is no one who is able to know them.

---

*No separate commentary section is present. The page consists of a single column of the main Zohar text.*

## Main Text (Zohar)

...the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kadosh Baruch Hu"</note> will do. Also here, what is written? <note>Genesis 47:29</note> *And the days of Israel drew near to die, and he called his son Joseph and said to him: "If now I have found favor in your eyes..."* and he called his son Joseph, etc. And what is written? *And he said: "Swear to me," and he swore to him.* Did Jacob not trust Joseph without an oath? Rather, it was because of that matter which is the <term>mystery</term> <note>original: "raza," referring to a hidden spiritual secret</note> sealed in the holy flesh upon him <note>referring to the Covenant of Circumcision</note>; for that reason, he said to him, "Swear to me," because an oath rests upon that place. And we have learned that the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>, swears by it; therefore, he said to him, "Swear to me," so that he would not change from what he swore by it. And regarding this, he said to him, "Swear to me," and did not say, "Promise me a promise," but rather requested an oath—blessed be His Name.

This section of the Torah is sealed and closed from all sides of the Torah, because once the soul of Jacob went to its rest, the eyes of the Children of Israel and the hearts of the Children of Israel were closed <note>This refers to the physical layout of the Torah scroll where there is no paragraph break between the previous portion and this one</note>, because the <term>light</term> <note>original: "nehora"</note> they relied upon was withdrawn.

-> **And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years; so the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were a hundred forty and seven years.** <- <note>Genesis 47:28</note>

Rabbi Yudai opened and said <note>Psalms 42:3</note>:
> My soul thirsts for God, for the living God; when shall I come and appear before God?

Come and see: at the time when human beings find themselves in goodness, joy, and tranquility, one must be found before the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> and present oneself before Him. And if you say—behold, it is written <note>Psalms 2:11</note>:
> Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice with trembling.

What is the meaning of "rejoice with trembling"? Here we learn that a person must join <term>awe with joy</term> <note>original: "dchilu ve-chedva"</note> and joy with awe. When a person is in great joy, he must not forget the awe of his Master, so that he does not stray to another path; and regarding this, "rejoice with trembling." "My soul thirsts for God, for the living God..."—this is the thirst of the soul for the time it departs from the world in joy, and at that moment it must present itself before Him. For the soul exists only to appear before its Master and to gaze upon His light.

Come and see: for seventeen years Jacob dwelt in Egypt in goodness, tranquility, and joy, more so than all his other days. For he saw his son as a king, and he saw all those tribes—all of them righteous—and he saw them all in prosperity. And at such a time, a person must remember death and the <term>Day of Judgment</term> <note>original: "Yoma de-Dina"</note>; and regarding this, "so the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were a hundred forty and seven years." And why mention death at this moment? Only so that the heart should be balanced in joy and awe as is fitting. Furthermore, they have established that a person should not laugh [excessively] all that day that he contemplates the day of death. And regarding this, it is written "And Jacob lived" in goodness and tranquility, and immediately following it, "so the days of Jacob, the years of his life"—to remember death and the Day of Judgment. Rabbi Abba said...

It highlights Jacob's peaceful final years in Egypt as a time where he nonetheless maintained his focus on the afterlife and the Covenant.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discourse of the "Great Assembly" (Idra Rabba) from the Zohar, specifically focusing on the sublime nature of the Divine Head and the emergence of the first emanations.</meta>

## The Great Assembly (Nasso)

The Ancient of Ancients, the Concealed of all Concealed, is engraved and yet not engraved. He is established through all repairs <note>The Aramaic term "Tikunim" refers to the "repairs" or "arrangements" of the Divine form</note> and is found within all repairs. He is the Ancient of all Ancients, the Concealed of all Concealed, engraved and yet not engraved. He is established through all repairs, yet is not established <note>Meaning He remains beyond any fixed form</note>. He established all those repairs, and for all those repairs that are seen in Him, He is the Head of all Heads—a Head that is not a Head. It is not known, nor can it be known, what is in this Head, because neither Wisdom <term>Chokhmah: the first spark of intellect</term> nor Understanding <term>Binah: the processing of that spark</term> are marked upon it. And when His repairs are present, we see that they are all not marked in Him; rather, He is the Ancient of all Ancients, the Hidden of all Hidden. Upon this Head, which is the Ancient One, nothing is marked at all, and they cannot know Him when He is alone. All those repairs are found within Him, for they are all bound to Him, and He breathes and rides upon them.

Three Heads are engraved, one within the other and one above the other. One Head is the **Concealed Wisdom**, which is covered and does not open. This Concealed Wisdom is the Head for all the heads of the rest of Wisdom. The Supreme Head is the **Holy Ancient One**, the Hidden of all Hidden, the Head of all Heads—a Head that is not a Head. It is not known, nor can it be known, what exists in this Head, because it does not cling to Wisdom or to Intelligence. For this reason, the Holy Ancient One is called <term>Nothingness (Ayin)</term> <note>original: "Ayin". In Kabbalah, this refers to a state of being so sublime it is "nothing" relative to human comprehension</note>. And from this "Nothingness" emerges the **Infinite** <note>original: "Ein Sof"</note>.

And this Head of all Heads, the Concealed Wisdom which is hidden within Him, is called the **Supreme Wisdom**, the cause of all wisdoms. Three Heads are engraved. This is the Head that is not marked and is not known, what exists within it, because it is the Holy Ancient One, the Hidden of all Hidden. He is the Head of all Heads because He is a Head that is not a Head. Concerning Him it is written: -> *For ask now of the days that are past...* <- <note>Deuteronomy 4:32</note>. And come and see, it is written: -> *Man knows not the price thereof...* <- <note>Job 28:13</note>.

The second Head is the **Concealed Wisdom**, which is the Head of all wisdom. Within it are found three hundred and twenty-five paths. This is the **Lamp of Hardness** <note>original: "Butzina de-Kardinuta". A technical term for the primordial spark of judgment or measurement that carves out existence</note> which shines from within the most Hidden of the Hidden. This is what is found in this Head, which is the Holy Ancient One, and all those paths are not separated from Him. And concerning this it is written: -> *All the paths of the Lord are mercy and truth...* <- <note>Psalms 25:10</note>.

The third Head, upon which all the heads stand, is the Head of all Heads, the Concealed Wisdom. It is the concealment of all paths and the arrangement of all paths. This is what sparkles and shines to all, and those paths are radiant and are found within **Understanding** (Binah). These repairs were established in Him, in the Holy Ancient One, and in each and every repair found from Him and within Him. Therefore, the Holy Ancient One is found in three Heads, yet they are all found in one Head, and they are three. And these three Heads, when they shine, they are all bound as one, and they are the Head of all Heads. These three Heads are within one Head. Three lights are found in one light, for the river flows and shines, and those that do not shine are only known from that light which sparkles.

<summary>This page describes the "Three Heads" of the Divine crown in Kabbalistic thought, explaining how the unknowable "Nothingness" (Ayin) transitions into the first emanations of Wisdom and Understanding.</summary>
<keywords>Ancient of Ancients, Holy Ancient One, Concealed Wisdom, Three Heads, Ayin, Ein Sof, Lamp of Hardness, Tikunim, Zohar</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discourse of the Idra Rabba (The Great Assembly) from the Zohar, specifically focusing on the emanations of the highest divine crown (Keter). ## Main Text (The Zohar)

And when the shearing of that <term>Pleasantness</term> <note>original: "No'imo"; refers to a sublime divine light or beauty</note> is revealed, it shines within that shearing where all pleasantries are as one, as it is established. And concerning this, it is written:
> And let the beauty of the Lord our God be upon us (Psalms 90:17)

And from this point forward, the high holy ones did not need to eat manna, for it is written, "And the Lord gave wisdom to Solomon," and they were nourished by the holy sustenance from above, which is the <term>Pleasantness</term> of all pleasantries. And concerning this, King David said:
> The Lord will give strength unto His people; the Lord will bless His people with peace (Psalms 29:11)

And from there, all paths and all ways are separated to all the other worlds; they go forth in a single shearing, and each one is distinguished by its own sign. As it has been stated: when that <term>Pleasantness</term> is revealed, all the lights and all the other high holy ones exist in a single joy, and from there they are all nourished.

And when the light of the <term>Holy Ancient One</term> <note>original: "Atika Kadisha"; the most hidden, primordial aspect of the Divine</note> shines, it illuminates this Pleasantness which hangs in the balance, which is the <term>Beard of the Holy Ancient One</term> <note>original: "Dikna"; a metaphor for the channels through which divine mercy flows into the universe</note>. Upon it hang <term>six hundred and twenty worlds</term> <note>The number 620 is the numerical value of the Hebrew word "Keter" (Crown)</note>, and when that Pleasantness shines, they all shine, and those six hundred and twenty worlds exist in a single joy and are nourished by that Pleasantness. And then it is called the "Pleasantness of the Lord," as it is said:
> To behold the beauty of the Lord, and to inquire in His temple (Psalms 27:4)

And this Pleasantness is hidden and concealed, and it is not revealed except in the time to come, on that day of which it is written:
> In that day shall the Lord be one, and His name one (Zechariah 14:9)

And because of this, it is written, "And let the beauty of the Lord our God be upon us," for this Pleasantness stands over all those above and those below. And for this reason it is written: "And let the beauty of the Lord our God be upon us; and establish Thou the work of our hands upon us; yea, the work of our hands establish Thou it," for it stands over everything on the side of this Pleasantness...

<summary>This passage describes the "Pleasantness" (No'am) emanating from the "Beard" of the Holy Ancient One, explaining how this supreme divine light nourishes all upper worlds and holy beings. It links this esoteric flow to the 620 worlds of the Divine Crown and the ultimate unity of God in the messianic future.</summary>

<keywords>Idra Rabba, Zohar, Keter, Holy Ancient One, Divine Beard, 620 Worlds, Pleasantness, Divine Nourishment, Messianic Era</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar - The Faithful Shepherd)

And by the judgment of all of them in one body, and this is <term>Wisdom</term> <note>Chokhmah</note> and <term>Understanding</term> <note>Binah</note> for Moses to behold; and within that body shall be established branches and roots, both below and above. And all are heard at changing times by a voice from the <term>Skull</term> <note>Gulgalta - the highest crown of the head</note>, and the spirit is beautiful and approaches. And in their time, it shall be given to Jerusalem, a body of grinding <note>referring to the 'clouds' or 'heavens' that grind manna for the righteous</note>, and all who are in distress were revealed from within the dewdrops.

And at that time, the children of the High One shall be honored in their Well of Life; all of them are colors and all are lights, each one according to his own strength. And they were fashioned from this likeness above, and all the lights from those of the light of light that were made from the strength of every time and times, from the totality of the enclosure. And there is no "time" within it <note>referring to the eternal realm beyond linear time</note>, and that which was made from all the rest of these times which possess time, they established it, and for it they are established. And there are times that possess time, and every time that is within the standing of the living force has no time within it when it lives above and below, more than all other places. And because of all the camp and for the brother of Levi above, colors were given to the worlds above and below. **The <term>Faithful Shepherd</term> <note>Ra'aya Mehemna - Moses</note> said: Moses is "A virtuous woman <note>the Shekhinah</note> is the crown of her husband"** <note>Proverbs 12:4</note>.

And in this, she is certainly the crown of her husband, to become a limb of the body; limbs were made. And in this, she is the limb of the whole body above and below, when she is within the subtle part of the body, because of all the limbs of their children, their colors are within the outer part. They heard at the hour that he is the arm of water <note>associated with the right arm/Chesed</note> to act with the strength from above, and she is crowned and covered by her children of water, because of the spring that is called by her name, and because of the first point <note>the seed of Wisdom</note> which is in everything. And because every single one is called a "limb" from the body of the Male and below, and the revealed water is what they hear. And there is with him a subtle part, the water of the sword <note>judgment</note>, and this is the <term>Loving-kindness</term> <note>Chesed</note> of Abraham, and this is the <term>Might</term> <note>Gevurah</note> of Isaac. And in that portion of hers which is hidden within the body, this is <term>Beauty</term> <note>Tiferet</note>, which is the limb of the water above and above, and the water is within her, and the light and the time are from it. And because she is hidden within the body and in every limb that is in it, he sees that all ascend and are seen and increase further. And at times there was made from it a holy measure in a vessel, and he was with them when the time increased. And otherwise, the spirit is entwined within her, and this is the cord of the body that is found within her, which is <term>Loving-kindness</term> <note>Chesed</note> and all the rest of the whole body above and below.

And there was a time when we saw that they were crowned upon the wall, and the strength from them is the speech; all of them come upon this. And we saw in the whiteness <note>Laban/Purity</note> from all this time that is within the ascent, and a voice in the light, the day is prepared. And every line is for a voice in the light within the living force in a vessel, all of them when they are awakened and the hairs strike one against another. And from these limbs of the body above it comes, and each one and the house of the nations, all of them are the secret of this vessel, as it is written: "And from You is life" <note>Psalm 36:10</note>. In it is the love from above upon my hidden name in purity, and within the beauty of all garments; and those are the pious ones of this time, the precious ones.

<summary>This page explores the mystical anatomy of the Divine, describing how the Sefirot (divine attributes) manifest as limbs of a cosmic body. It specifically highlights the Shekhinah as the 'virtuous woman' who crowns Moses, the Faithful Shepherd, linking the physical world to the eternal realm beyond time.</summary>

## Main Text (The Radiance)

[1] <unclear>...</unclear> which is <unclear>...</unclear>
[2] <unclear>... when the world was created ...</unclear>
[3] <unclear>... in it, on the side of ...</unclear>

## Main Text (Zohar)

To repair and arrange for Him. As we have learned regarding the day in which the heavens and the earth were completed. At that time, that lower radiance was like that upper radiance. The upper and the radiance were in a single unity. **"Let there be light, and there was light"** <note>Genesis 1:3</note>. "Let there be light" above, and "there was light" below. "And there was light" refers to that radiance which <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>Aramaic: Kudsha Brich Hu; the standard rabbinic title for God</note> called. "And there was light" is the light that <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> hid away for the righteous. And when <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> saw that the inhabitants of the world were not worthy, He hid it. This is what is written: <note>Exodus 17:14</note>
> **"And the Lord said to Moses: Write this as a memorial in a book"**

And when He saw that the righteous [would receive] this radiance, this radiance from above. "And there was light" is the light below. And then it is complete. For we have learned that <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>Abbreviated in text as Ha-Kadosh Baruch Hu</note> saw that this radiance called "Light," which is above, was hidden. And through it, the holy hosts and camps were awakened. Just as we have learned in the scripture: **"Write this as a memorial in a book."** And this is the <term>Primeval Light</term> <note>Aramaic: Ohr Kadma'ah; the original light of the first day of Creation, said to be too powerful for the mundane world</note>. For this Primeval Light, which is the upper radiance, when it emerged from that first light, it spread downward. And so the <term>disciples of the wise</term> <note>Scholars of Torah and mysticism</note> of above are destined [to receive it]. For it is a greater radiance and is seen more intensely above. And because of this, it is written **"And there was light."** The Primeval Light which is the upper radiance and the radiance of above. And then, every single day, this Palace is illuminated and filled with radiance from the upper house. And all the <term>souls</term> <note>Aramaic: Nishmatin</note> that are in this Palace are all illuminated by this upper radiance. And there is no day that does not have within it the radiance of life. And regarding this, King David, peace be upon him, said: <note>Psalms 33:1</note>
> **"Sing for joy, O righteous, in the Lord; praise is fitting for the upright"**

"For the upright" certainly, for they dwell in this upper Palace. And because of this, it is written **"Let there be light, and there was light."** The first light and the second light. And regarding this, it is written **"Let there be light, and there was light,"** the first light which is the upper radiance, the highest of the lower. Fortunate are the righteous who merit to be illuminated by this upper radiance, and regarding this, it is written: **"Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart."** <note>Psalms 97:11</note> "The upright in heart" are those who merit this Palace called the <term>Palace of Merit</term> <note>Hebrew: Heikhal HaZechut; the celestial chamber where human deeds are weighed and the light of the righteous is stored</note>. The Palace from which all judgment and all merit of the world emerges. And all the souls that are in this Palace are all called "the upright." And concerning them, it is written: **"Praise is fitting for the upright."** And <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> is destined to shine upon them with that hidden upper radiance. And then all the hosts and camps below will all be illuminated by that upper radiance and will be seen as they are named. And every single day, a voice goes out from that Palace and says: "Fortunate are the righteous who know how to have compassion for their Master." And behold, here they have awakened [the idea] that this Palace is called the Palace of Mercy. And it is written in this Palace as they have established it. And behold, it was said that it is the <term>Palace of Merit</term>. And through this merit, mercy is awakened. What does this mean? That mercy and merit are all one. For if a person is meritorious, he merits to awaken mercy. From where do we know this? From King David, peace be upon him, who said: <note>Psalms 119:55</note> **"I remembered Your name in the night, O Lord, and I kept Your Torah."**

<summary>This page describes the mystical "Palace of Merit" and the "Primeval Light" hidden by God for the righteous, explaining that merit and mercy are unified in the celestial realms. It interprets the repetition of "light" in Genesis as a reference to both the upper and lower manifestations of divine radiance.</summary>

## Ha'azinu (The Lesser Assembly)

Of the Stream <note>original: *Mazla*; refers to the "Beard" of the Divine, seen as a conduit or "stream" of influence</note>. And thus all the lamps shine from within that lamp that stands and sustains everything. It emerges from within Thought <note>original: *Machshavah*; the highest level of Divine consciousness</note>, and that which remains of them is taken by the Stream. And Lovingkindness <note>original: *Chesed*</note> emerges from within Thought, and that which remains is the **Supernal Lovingkindness**, and because of this, it is called **Eternal Lovingkindness** <note>original: *Chesed Olam*</note>. And this is the mercy of the Ancient One. And because of this, He is called **Supernal God** <note>original: *El Ila'ah*</note>. And all the "faces" of the Ancient One are not seen except because this [quality] is mercy more than all else.

And regarding this it is written: -> "I said, the world shall be built in lovingkindness" <note>Psalms 89:3</note> <-

And regarding this, Lovingkindness is the supernal mercy of the Holy Ancient One <note>original: *Atika Kadisha*</note>. And every place where it is written **God** <note>original: *El*</note>, it refers to Lovingkindness, and this is the mercy of the Ancient One [flowing] from the Stream, and this is **God, merciful and gracious**. And within that first light, which is Lovingkindness, Wisdom <note>original: *Chokhmah*</note> dwells and is hidden inside it; and regarding this, we call Lovingkindness—which is the Holy Ancient One—"Wisdom." And a hint of this is found in: -> "But My lovingkindness I will not remove from him" <note>Psalms 89:34</note> <-

And this Lovingkindness is Wisdom. And regarding this it is written "Eternal Lovingkindness," which is the Supernal Wisdom of the Holy Ancient One which is called Wisdom. And regarding this it is written: -> "And also wisdom is the heart of kings" <note>This appears to be a variation of Proverbs 14:33: "Wisdom rests in the heart of one who has understanding"</note> etc.

Come [and see]: Wisdom, Understanding <note>original: *Binah*</note>, and Knowledge <note>original: *Da'at*</note> emerge from the Holy Ancient One, and all those lights of above and below are all included within Him. Supernal Wisdom [emerges] from within the Hidden Wisdom. And Understanding [emerges] from within Supernal Wisdom, which is simple Understanding, and this is hidden. And Knowledge [emerges] from within this and that <note>i.e., from the union of Wisdom and Understanding</note>. And within Understanding is found Knowledge, and Understanding [and Knowledge] are as one and are not separated, and this is called **Comprehension** <note>original: *Tevunah*; often used for the practical or lower aspect of Understanding</note>. And all these three lights which are included within the Hidden Ancient One, they all emerge from within one light that "stands and does not stand" <note>a paradoxical state of being and non-being</note>, and these three emerge from within one. And they are all included within the **Stream** <note>original: *Mazla*</note>.

For the Stream pierces through and shines to every side. Lower Wisdom is wisdom [derived] from Supernal Wisdom; and Understanding from Supernal Understanding; and Knowledge from Supernal Knowledge. And these three are included in it, in that Stream that shines to every side. And these are the three lights of above, and this is the Stream that includes everything, and this is etc.

And the Supernal Mother <note>original: *Imma Ila'ah*; a title for the Sefirah of Binah</note> emerges from Wisdom. And Understanding emerges from Wisdom, which is Lower Wisdom, and all these lights are included in her. And this is what is written: -> "And let the beauty of the Lord our God be upon us" <note>Psalms 90:17</note> "and establish the work of our hands upon us; yes, the work of our hands establish it." <-

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Portion of Vayechi (And Jacob Lived)** <-

<margin>L.Y. Chaim opened and arranged the ladder <unclear>according to the precious [text] and the Idra</unclear></margin>

**"And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years..."** etc. <note>Genesis 47:28</note> "...and the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were a hundred and forty-seven years." **Rabbi Hezekiah opened** his discourse with the verse: (Psalms 115:15) **"Blessed are you of the Lord, the Maker of heaven and earth."** Come and see: all the people of the world walk and run and pursue the matters of this world, but they do not observe and do not know how this world stands, nor the days of human beings that exist in this world—whether those days are truly "living" or not. Come and see: Jacob our forefather merited that "life" which shines and is illuminated by the Supernal Radiance, which is called <term>Life</term> <note>original: "Chayyim"; refers to divine vitality or the flow of energy from the higher sefirot</note>. All of his days were a sustained life that shone constantly. Come and see: all people who occupy themselves with the <term>Torah</term> <note>original: "Oraita"; the divine law and mystical wisdom</note> and perform the <term>Commandments of the Torah</term> <note>original: "Pikudei d'Oraita"</note>—at the time they depart from this world, all those days in which they labored in Torah and performed commandments are gathered together before the <term>Holy King</term> <note>original: "Malka Kadisha"; God</note> and they become a <term>Garment to clothe him</term> <note>original: "Begada d'lavish leh"; a spiritual robe for the soul in the afterlife</note>, and these are considered "living." But one who did not occupy himself with the Torah and did not perform commandments—those days go to waste in emptiness, for no holy matter took hold of them, and they do not endure. At the time he departs from this world, when those days go to be counted before the Holy King, they are not found there, and he has no garment to wear. Woe to that person who arrives in emptiness without a garment! Furthermore, he does not possess that "life" which should have attached to him, and his days are considered dead. Come and see: Jacob our forefather merited and was attached to <term>Upper Life</term> <note>original: "Chayyin Ila'in"; the highest spiritual vitality</note>, as it is written: "And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years." What is the meaning of "And he lived"? It means he merited to see that Upper Life that shines. And that Upper Life was granted because of Joseph. When he saw Joseph as he was at first, their life was established. From here we learn: anyone who merits to see a son of a son <note>a grandson</note> who occupies himself with the Torah merits "life," because their life is true life. And if you should say: "And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt"—were these his only years of life, and before this he did not live? Rather, it is certainly because he saw Joseph was a king, and his sons were righteous, and at every moment he saw the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>original: "Shekhinta"; the Divine Presence</note> upon him and it never departed from him. At that time, it was truly called "living." Come and see: Jacob our forefather, in all the seventeen years he was in Egypt, was in joy and in the "Life from Above."

***

<summary>Rabbi Hezekiah explains that true "life" consists of days spent in Torah study and good deeds, which form a spiritual garment for the soul. Jacob's final seventeen years in Egypt are considered his truest "life" because he was reunited with Joseph and lived in a state of constant divine inspiration.</summary>

<meta>This page begins the discourse on the Torah portion "Vayechi" (Genesis 47:28). It establishes a thematic link between the life of the patriarch Jacob and the cosmic role of the Torah and Repentance in the maintenance of the world.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **Portion of Vayechi (And He Lived)** <-

> And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years; so the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were a hundred and forty-seven years. <note>Genesis 47:28</note>

Rabbi Yehuda opened his discourse, 
> Who can express the mighty acts of the Lord, or make all His praise to be heard? <note>Psalms 106:2</note>
Come and see: when the **Holy One, Blessed Be He** <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> desired to create the world, He looked into the Torah <note>The Divine Wisdom/Law</note> and created the world. And for every single thing that the **Holy One, Blessed Be He** made in the world, He looked into the Torah and created it. Just as it is stated,
> Then I was beside Him as a nursling. <note>Proverbs 8:30</note>
Do not read it as "nursling" <note>Hebrew: *amon*</note> but rather as "architect" <note>Hebrew: *uman*</note>. And when He desired to create Man, He looked into the Torah and created him. The Torah said before Him: "This Man whom You desire to create is destined to sin before You and be subject to judgment. If You do not extend Your patience to him, how can he endure in the world?" The **Holy One, Blessed Be He** said to her: "It is with you that I am destined to perform acts of love. For even before the world was created, I created **Repentance** <note>original: "Teshuvah"</note>." Before Man was even created, the **Holy One, Blessed Be He** created Repentance. He said to Repentance: "I desire to create Man in the world on the condition that when he sins and returns from his sins, you shall be ready to atone for him." Because of this, in every single moment, Repentance is ready for the children of men. And when the children of men sin and return in repentance, it is as if they had never sinned.

Come and see: for this reason, a person must strengthen themselves in the Torah, for it is entirely the secret of the Name of the **Holy One, Blessed Be He**. And whoever exerts themselves in the Torah exerts themselves in the Holy Name. Thus it has been established: the Torah is entirely the Name of the **Holy One, Blessed Be He**. Because of this, one is saved in this world and in the World to Come. Come and see: because it is the Holy Name, anyone who exerts themselves in it is as if they exerted themselves in the Holy Name and is mended with every perfection.

Come and see: when the First Man <note>Adam</note> was in the **Garden of Eden**, he was clothed in garments of supernal honor, as was fitting for that place. But once he was banished from the Garden of Eden and required the garments of this world, what is written? 
> And the Lord God made for Adam and for his wife garments of skin, and clothed them. <note>Genesis 3:21</note>
Initially, it was written as **garments of light** <note>original: "kotnot or" with an Aleph</note>. The light of the radiance of the Garden of Eden, in which Adam used to shine. Once he sinned, they were exchanged for garments of skin <note>original: "kotnot or" with an Ayin—a pun in Hebrew where "light" and "skin" sound identical</note>. Because of this, a person must exert themselves in the Torah day and night, for the Torah is the Holy Name. And whoever exerts themselves in it is clothed in that garment of radiance from the supernal Torah. That garment will be found ready for him in the World to Come. Therefore, a person must exert themselves in the Torah constantly. Because of this, Jacob—who was perfect in everything and whose years of life were perfect on all sides—merited that his life should be bound with the Life Above.

<summary>This page explains that the Torah served as the blueprint for Creation and that Repentance was created before Man to ensure human survival despite sin. It also describes the transition of human existence from "Garments of Light" to "Garments of Skin" following the exile from Eden.</summary>
<keywords>Creation, Torah as Blueprint, Repentance, Adam, Garments of Light, Garments of Skin, Jacob, Holy Name</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic exploration of Joseph’s life, specifically focusing on his time in Egypt and his spiritual status as the "Righteous One" (Tzadik) who maintains the connection between the earthly and divine realms.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

The King <note>original: "Melekh"</note> is the secret of the matter in this verse; it is a hint regarding the Higher World, which is precious. Regarding Joseph, because he descended among the sheaves <note>a reference to Joseph's first dream in Genesis 37</note>, he eventually ascended. When the flow of divine light reaches him at times, he dwells among them and covers them. Because he was separated from them <note>his brothers</note> and did not come in his own name, he dwelt among them. It is not written "and his name" <note>Hebrew: *u-shemo*</note> but rather "and her name" <note>Hebrew: *u-shemah*</note>; and this refers to Joseph, because he was separated from them and hidden in the light that shines in his name. From where do we know this? From that which comes from the Book of Aggadah <note>a collection of homiletic rabbinic teachings</note>, where they said that that day was a festival for Joseph. On that day, they saw the light of the sun until the Holy One, Blessed be He, came and said: "What of Joseph?" Because of the Hebrews, he is Joseph, and it was said of Joseph:

-> **And they set for him by himself, and for them by themselves** <note>Genesis 43:32</note> <-

And Jacob did not know of all these matters. But did you not say that he is the place of the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note>? And what of that which is written concerning Joseph? Joseph is a king and he dwelt with his Divine Presence. On that day, they merited through Joseph, and it remained with Joseph until they went up to the land, and he was not found. Therefore, they are called "living." And he said that there is a general principle: once Jacob saw that everything emerged from him through the "Foundation of all Life" <note>term: *Yesod* - the ninth divine emanation, associated with procreation and the righteous Joseph</note>, and this is the secret of the matter. Regarding everything written:

-> **And God made man upright** <note>Ecclesiastes 7:29 / Genesis 2:7 variant</note> <-

The Presence did not dwell within him. But afterward, Joseph returned the Divine Presence to rest upon them. And then, regarding the secret of the serpent: why is the letter *Mem* missing from the "eyes" <note>original: "me-einaya"</note>? As it says:

-> **And the eyes of man shall be humbled** <note>Isaiah 2:11</note> <-

This is because the Divine Presence was not upon them because they sold Joseph, and there was no place for it to rest until the merit that Joseph earned for them brought the Divine Presence back upon them. And Joseph arose, and he is Joseph because of Joseph, for Joseph, and he is a king, as it is said of Joseph, etc.

<summary>This passage provides a mystical interpretation of Joseph's separation from his brothers, explaining that the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) left the family following his sale and only returned through Joseph's spiritual merit as the "Foundation" (Yesod) of the world.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Book of Genesis, specifically focusing on the transition of Adam and Eve from a state of spiritual radiance to physical vulnerability following the eating of the forbidden fruit.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

What is the reason for the one who is pressed and seeks to bless Him? And so it is with all of them, because they stand ascending and it is revealed not <note>original: "dela"; the printed Zohar text reads: "not as is fitting"</note> above when—
and then: -> **And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed** <- <note>Genesis 2:25</note> because they did not know the way of the "Other Side" <note>term: Sitra Achra; the realm of evil or impurity in Kabbalistic thought</note>. Once they ate and were drawn into the way of the Other Side, they knew and were separated from the good. And this is the meaning of:
-> **And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked** <- <note>Genesis 3:7</note>. What is the meaning of "and they knew"? That they knew that the branch <note>original: "anafa"; here it seems to be written: "that they were defiled," while the printed version reads: "that they took hold of this world"</note> was in him and they stood within it. "And the eyes of them both were opened"—what is "and they knew that they were naked"? It means they lost <note>or: "were deprived of"</note> that supernal radiance <note>term: Zohara Ila'ah; the primordial spiritual light that clothed the first humans</note> that had covered them, and they were found stripped of it. And regarding this it is written: "and they knew that they were naked."
-> **And the Lord God made for Adam and for his wife garments of skin, and clothed them** <- <note>Genesis 3:21</note>.
<unclear>Afterward</unclear>, what is written? -> **And the Lord God said: Behold, the man has become as one of us, to know good and evil** <- <note>Genesis 3:22</note>. What is the meaning of "of us" <note>original: "mimenu"</note>? It is as it says, "from that upper portion," which is the male principle called "of him" <note>original: "mimenu"; a linguistic play on the Hebrew word which can mean "of us" or "of him"</note>. And even though the end of the matter is explained—and the companions <note>note: the circle of scholars surrounding Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> have said that he was found as a single entity within to make it known—it is not so. Rather, "Behold, the man has become as one"—this refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written: -> **The Lord is One and His Name is One** <- <note>Zechariah 14:9</note>. But when he sinned, he was called "dust," and was found to be dust which is impurity. And this matter is explained: they <unclear>became</unclear> thin/diminished in a way that was not fitting because it was not his own. ### Commentary
*This page contains the main Zohar text without additional side commentaries. The text itself functions as a mystical commentary on the opening of Parashat Vayikra.*

**Key Concepts:**
* **The Living God (Al Chai):** The "Living God," often identified in Kabbalah with the Sefirah of *Yesod*, the conduit through which divine life and souls flow into the lower worlds.
* **Souls and Spirits (Nishmatin ve-Ruchin):** Souls and spirits. The text emphasizes that their essence remains connected to the divine "Light" (*Nehora*) even after descending into the physical world.
* **The Light of the Torah (Nehora de-Oraita):** The light of the Torah, which crowns the souls as they enter this world.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Vayeira (Genesis 18:1). The previous section likely discussed Abraham's recovery from circumcision or his hospitality. Here, the text focuses on the nature of the Divine vision he received.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Those who were sitting before Rabbi Shimon <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional central figure of the Zohar</note> began their discourse. Rabbi Isaac opened and said: <note>Genesis 18:1</note> **"And the Lord appeared to him by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat at the tent door in the heat of the day,"** etc. This verse has already been established <note>interpreted by the sages</note>, but usually, when the word *Vayehi* <note>original: "ויהי" - meaning "And it came to pass"</note> is used, it denotes a language of sorrow. Here, however, it does not say *Vayehi*, but rather *Vayera* <note>original: "וירא" - meaning "And He appeared"</note>. Why is this different? It is because he saw the *Shekhinah* <note>The Divine Presence, viewed in Kabbalah as the feminine immanence of God</note>, which is the joy of all joys in this world. From here we learn that from those upper levels <note>the Sefirot, or divine emanations</note>, this is what is seen: that all the joy of the world issues from here. We have learned that anyone who beholds the *Shekhinah* is found in perfect joy. And this is the meaning of "And the Lord appeared to him"—in the perfect joy of all those upper levels.

"By the oaks of Mamre." Why specifically by the oaks of Mamre? Because Mamre gave him <note>Abraham</note> counsel regarding the circumcision. Therefore, he merited that the *Shekhinah* should be revealed to him within Mamre's domain.

"And he sat at the **tent door**." What is the **tent door**? This refers to the "Upper Opening," as it is said: <note>Psalms 118:19</note> **"Open for me the gates of righteousness; I will enter them and thank the Lord."** This is the opening, the first level one encounters when entering within.

"**In the heat of the day.**" What is "the heat of the day"? This refers to the level of Abraham, which is the "Right Side" <note>The Sefirah of Chesed, or Loving-kindness, associated with the element of fire/heat and the patriarch Abraham</note>. Because at that hour, that level was ruling and was strengthened. Therefore, it says "as the heat of the day"—meaning like the heat of that "Day" of Abraham. Come and see: because Abraham was in the perfection of this level, he merited that the *Shekhinah* should be revealed to him in joy. Therefore, "And the Lord appeared to him" in joy, as we have stated.

<summary>Rabbi Isaac explains that the Divine appearance to Abraham was characterized by joy rather than sorrow, occurring at the 'tent door' which symbolizes the first gateway to the Divine realms. The 'heat of the day' is interpreted as the mystical empowerment of Abraham's specific spiritual attribute, Loving-kindness.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And this matter follows the pattern of the <term>Tabernacle</term> <note>Hebrew: Mishkan; the portable sanctuary in the desert</note>, which belongs to the Holy One, blessed be He. It spreads forth branches above, and then it is seen that they shine; and it contains branches as it is written, which the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>A mystical personification of the Jewish people and the Divine Presence, the Shekhinah</note> received when the Holy One, blessed be He, descended to give them the Torah. At that time, the Assembly of Israel was filled from all sides with <term>Lovingkindness</term> <note>Hebrew: Chesed; the Divine attribute of expansive benevolence</note>, which is called "Everlasting Kindness." And this is how the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself to her, like a king who had a crown and a lampstand for his kingdom, and in it, complete kindness is seen. And this crown and lampstand are joined together when the Tabernacle is built, and the left side takes hold of the right, and the right of the left, and then they are all made as one by the Divine Word.

And because of this, the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> shines at the time she stands before Him. At the time that **Jethro** arrived, the Holy One, blessed be He, called him by this name. And from where do we know this? From the verse where it is written:
> "And Jethro said: 'Blessed be the Lord, who has delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh.'" <note>Exodus 18:10</note>

And regarding this, it is said that when Jethro saw all those mighty deeds that the <term>Holy One, blessed be He</term> <note>A standard Aramaic title for God: Kudsha Brich Hu</note> performed for Israel, and that all the peoples of the earth feared and trembled before His Holy Name—and Jethro, who was a priest and wise in every <term>idolatry</term> <note>Aramaic: Avodah Zarah; literally "strange service"</note> in the world—when he saw all of this, he then confessed and the <term>Name of the Holy One, blessed be He</term> was honored because of him above and below. For every worship of idols was sustained through him <note>Jethro was considered the ultimate expert in pagan rites</note>. Therefore, when Jethro came and said, "Blessed be the Lord who delivered etc.," then the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, was honored and exalted more than all other gods of the nations. For until now, they did not know the importance of the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, as was fitting. But when Jethro, who was the great one and the priest for all the false gods of the world, confessed Him, it was then known that He rules over everything.

<summary>This page explains that Jethro's acknowledgement of God's greatness was uniquely powerful because, as a former high priest of all idolatry, his conversion validated God's supremacy over all other powers. It also links the construction of the Tabernacle to the harmonious union of Divine attributes like Mercy and Strength.</summary>

## Commentary
The text reflects a specific manuscript tradition of the **Idra Zuta**. 
- **Lines 1-9:** A poetic or liturgical framing not usually found in standard printed editions of the Zohar. It praises the "Watcher and Holy One" (divine emanation) descending.
- **Lines 10-21:** Corresponds to the end of the Idra Zuta where the companions (the *Hevraya*) witness the spiritual ecstasy and preparation for Rabbi Shimon's passing. It mentions the "Clouds of Glory" and the "Holy Living Creatures" of the Merkavah (Chariot).
- **The "Ox" (שור):** A recurring motif in this section of the Zohar, likely referring to the "Ox" that emerges from the river of Eden, symbolizing certain divine strengths or the power of *Gevurah*.
- **The catchword "Nostril":** Indicates that the following page continues with the description of the "Nostrils of the Ancient of Days," a central theme in the mystical physiognomy (descriptions of the Divine "Face") found in the Idrot.

## Pekudei <note>The Torah portion "Pekudei" (Accounts), Exodus 38:21–40:38</note>

The Right Hand <note>The emanation of *Chesed* or Lovingkindness</note> emerges from within the supreme, holy light alone, which is not merely a "half of the body." It is the place of all awe, and the Name of the King is within it. This is the "Lower Power" <note>original: *Gevurah de-letata*</note> beneath it, where seventy-six appointed officials stand surrounding it. All of them are called *Elohim* <note>God/Judges</note> because they exist within the vision of this [Name] and are revealed from within it. Therefore, this Name stands over it, as we have said, while the other lower levels are not so. Because of this, they are all under the authority of this [Name] and not under the authority of that which is above. They are all far and they are all near; they all stand in the mystery of the smoke and are crowned in the holy place, crowned in a single vision, one within the other. And come and see: they all take hold of the supreme, holy Name alone. Regarding this it is written: *The Lord is One and His Name is One* <note>Zechariah 14:9</note> three times, and all those levels are all one.

->**Come and See**<-

Voice and Speech are as one, and they are never separated from one another. Come and see: Voice dwells within and Speech dwells without. Even though they are two, they are as one. For this reason, Voice dwells within and Speech dwells without; the Voice goes forth and illuminates the Speech. This is the meaning of: *The Lord spoke from the heavens* <note>original: *Vayedaber YHVH min ha-shamayim*; cf. Deuteronomy 4:36</note>. This is the Voice that emerges from within the inner Voice, which is hidden and not heard at all. This [other] is the Voice that is heard. That Voice is "external" relative to the inner Voice, and Speech is "external" relative to this Voice. Yet they all take hold of one another and are as one. When one seeks to know them, they are all one. Therefore: *The Lord is One and His Name is One.*

**Come and see:** Speech does not exist without Voice. Because of this, Speech possesses a Voice that is external, an inner Voice that is hidden and not heard at all, and the Voice that is heard—and this is Speech. They all take hold of one another and stand in a single mystery. Everything is Speech that is hidden and concealed within the vision of the Voice. Everything that stands on the side of the Voice, which is above, they are all as one. And this is the Voice and the Speech.

<summary>This page from the Zohar explains the mystical unity between "Voice" (the internal divine impulse) and "Speech" (the external manifestation), using them as metaphors for the connection between different divine emanations (Sefirot).</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the Torah portion Beha'alotcha, specifically focusing on the auditory and visual revelation at Mount Sinai as described in the Zohar.</meta>

## Beha'alotcha

And come and see: at the moment the Holy Name <note>original: "Shema Kadisha"</note> issues from the mouths of all those who perform the service and entreat the Kingdom of Heaven <note>original: "Malkhuta de-Shmaya," referring to the tenth Sefirah, the feminine aspect of the Divine</note>, and the awe of their mouths [is present], from here [emerges] a voice from Gehenna <note>the realm of purgation or hell</note> that flows and issues forth. For one who has sinned before his Master cannot behold the pleasantness of the Voice from above, nor will he merit to behold the glory of the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah"</note>; rather, he will only merit to experience distress and the roar of a voice that he cannot bear to hear.

And this is the Voice of the Torah <note>original: "Kol de-Oraita"</note>. When it descended and was established below, at that moment it was a Voice that all the worlds could not endure, and they trembled because of that Voice. This is a Voice that is heard from within a Voice when it issued forth in the Torah. Concerning this, it is written: *And the people heard the voice...* <note>cf. Deuteronomy 4:12</note> and it is written: *And all the people saw the voices and the torches...* <note>Exodus 20:15</note>.

And regarding this, even though it is written *And all the people saw the voices*, from where do we know that all these voices were from the side of the Supernal <note>the higher divine realms</note>? This Voice is called "Voice" as one. And if you say [it is plural] because this Voice is the Voice in which all [other voices] are considered and included, and they are lacking without it—for in this one, they all exist—concerning this it is written: --- **It was taught: at that time when [the breath] blows into the reed <note>original: "kanya," a metaphor for a divine channel or the throat</note>, there are three voices:**

From it, the 1st Voice is from the Holy Ancient One <note>original: "Atika Kadisha," the highest manifestation of the Divine, Keter</note>; and this is a Voice that includes all power and all the praise of Lovingkindness <note>Chesed</note>.

The 2nd Voice is a Voice called the "Voice of the Watchers." This one descends and calls out a proclamation, and now the light of Wisdom is awakened, which is called Higher Wisdom <note>original: "Chokhmah Ila'ah"</note>. All the kings of the East could not endure that Wisdom which issued forth and moved far away, and all this was because of the second Voice.

The 3rd Voice is called the "Voice that is Heard" <unclear>this is a voice for His Name</unclear>. And because of this, all of them are called the Voice of the Torah, which Israel took hold of. And regarding this, it is written: *And all the people saw the voices.*

Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Isaac were walking on the road. <unclear>Rabbi Yehuda said, "Behold..."</unclear> and regarding this, he called it by this name <unclear>...</unclear>. Rabbi Shimon stood and said: "Sit, Rabbi Isaac and Rabbi Yochanan; behold, children of the <unclear>Academy</unclear>," etc.

# Genesis

## Main Text (Zohar)

Come and see: it is written, *And God made the two great luminaries* <note>Genesis 1:16</note>. This lamp and that lamp were equal, and for this reason they were called "the two luminaries," to show that there was no defect in either of them at all. This was so that no imperfection would be visible before the King, even though they were not joined together as one. And if you should ask: why were they called "the two **great** luminaries" when the light of the moon is not like the light of the sun? It is because this one and that one were equal as one, and they ascended in a single mixture. One was in the scale of purity <note>original: "takla de-madka"</note> and one was in the scale of impurity <note>original: "takla de-mas'ava"</note>, and authority was given to one to rule by day and the other by night, for the existence of the Holy One, blessed be He, depends upon this.

-> It is written: *And over the heads of the living creatures there was the likeness of a firmament, like the color of the terrible ice* <note>Ezekiel 1:22</note> <-

And this is the upper firmament <term>Raki'a: the celestial expanse or "firmament" separating the earthly and divine realms</term> which is called "Heaven." It is above those holy living creatures <note>The *Chayyot*, a high order of angels described in Ezekiel's vision</note>, and it emerged from within a point that stands high above. It is the firmament from which seven other firmaments and seven lands emerge, and each one of them has its own individual dominion. Concerning this, it says, *And God made the firmament* to be over everything. This firmament is called "Heaven," and it is the firmament that engraved engravings from within the seven letters <note>The seven "double" letters of the Hebrew alphabet used in the process of creation</note> with which He engraved the heavens and the earth; these are the secrets of the letters. Concerning this, it says, *And God made the firmament* which emerged from within the seven letters.

<summary>This passage explores the mystical equality of the sun and moon at their creation and describes the "Upper Firmament" as a celestial structure emerging from a primordial point and shaped by sacred letters.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Hekhalot (Palaces) within the Zohar's commentary on the portion of Pekudei. It focuses on the internal process of the Divine Mind, specifically the emanation and unification of the first three Sefirot: Chokhmah (Wisdom/Thought), Binah (Understanding), and Da'at (Knowledge).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

By the power of the vision of Thought <note>original: *Machshava*, associated here with the Sefirah of Chokhmah (Wisdom)</note>, the constellation <note>original: *Mazla*, referring to the flow of divine influence</note> is bound to that Thought which covers over it and shines. And this is because this is the highest of all, and it shows our intellect that it has no permission to know it. And this is what is stated: ->**Light is sown for the righteous** etc. (Psalms 97:11)<- and this is the primordial light that the Holy One, Blessed be He, hid away for the righteous in the time to come. And this is the light that emerges from that Thought.

The garment of that light—and concerning this it is written: ->**Wrapped in light as with a garment** (Psalms 104:2)<-—comes from that Thought which emerges from that [higher] Thought. And this is the light that is outside of Thought. And from that light which emerged from that Thought, another light is bound to it and is called **Holy** <note>original: *Kodesh*</note>. It is never separated from it, and this is "Holy" and that Thought which is "Holy."

And from that Thought, that which emerges from it shines and is called Holy, as it is stated: ->**It shall be holy to you** (Leviticus 25:12)<-. And when it is called Thought and shines as one, they are a single garment, and all are lights that shine. And this light which is called Holy ascends in brightness and hints at knowing and entering into the mystery <note>original: *Raza*</note> of Thought. But it is not known until it shines within that light called **Understanding** <note>original: *Binah*</note>. And this is the mystery that emerges from that Thought; it is Understanding, and this is [the meaning of]: ->**But where shall wisdom be found? And where is the place of understanding?** (Job 28:12)<-.

And it is the mystery called **Elohim** <note>The Divine Name associated with the attribute of Justice and the Sefirah of Binah</note>. And this is Understanding which shines from Thought, and the radiance of Thought is hidden within it, and then it is called Understanding; therefore, it is hidden and not revealed. And Understanding, which emerges from Thought, illuminates that light called **Knowledge** <note>original: *Da'at*</note>, and this is the mystery of what is stated: ->**By His knowledge the depths were broken up** (Proverbs 3:20)<-. And regarding this mystery called Knowledge which shines from Understanding—for it is Understanding itself—when it ascends into Thought, then it is called Knowledge. And this is what is stated: ->**And I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship** (Exodus 31:3)<-.

And this is the mystery of Thought, Understanding, and Knowledge: they are all one without any separation at all. And this is the mystery called **Man** <note>original: *Adam*</note>, and this is the mystery of the **Primordial Man** <note>original: *Adam Kadma'ah*, the first and highest stage of divine emanation</note> who is above all. And when Thought ascends, that light shines...

->**Phinehas**<-

It is written: "Which the Lord your God swore, as He spoke to you." <note>original: "אשר נשבע יהו"ה אלהיכם כאשר דבר לכם"; this appears to be a fragmented verse or a liturgical introduction to the homily.</note>

Come and see: a <term>human being</term> <note>Aramaic: *Bar Nash*; literally "son of man"</note> is the <term>totality of the Torah</term>, which is itself the <term>totality of the Holy Name</term>. This is because the human is holy and was made in the <term>Supernal Image</term>. Regarding this, it is written: "Let us make man in our image, after our likeness." <note>Genesis 1:26</note>

And in this manner, the letter **Heh** [ה] corresponds to the five fingers.
And in this manner, the <term>totality of the body</term> is the letter **Vav** [ו].
And in this manner—because there are twelve joints in the limbs—they correspond to the twelve letters of the Holy Name <note>original: "י"ב אתוון דשמא קדישא"; referring to a specific mystical permutation of the twelve-letter Name of God</note> which are engraved within the Holy Name of twelve letters.
Therefore, a human being has twelve <term>limbs</term> <note>original: *shaifin*; referring here to the major segments of the arms and legs</note>.

And come and see: in this image, the letter **Vav** [ו]—which is the totality of the Name—is the form of the torso, the arms, and the legs.
And in this manner, the **Lower Heh** [ה] <note>The final letter of the Tetragrammaton, often associated with the Shekhinah or the physical world</note> represents the five fingers that rise to the number fifty <note>A reference to the 50 Gates of Understanding (Binah)</note>.

And in this manner, a human being has five fingers on the right hand and five fingers on the left hand; five toes on the right foot and five toes on the left foot.
And this is the mystery of the twenty letters of the Name, which correspond to the twenty digits.
And in this manner, the letter **Yod** [י] <note>The first letter of the Name, with a numerical value of 10</note> is five against five.
And this is the mystery of the digits that rise to ten and ten.
And this is the mystery of the <term>Ten Utterances</term> of the Torah <note>The Ten Commandments</note>.
Therefore, the human being is the totality of everything, for he is the <term>Image of the Holy Name</term>.

->**Portion of Acharei Mot**<-

> And the Lord spoke to Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they drew near before the Lord and died. <note>Leviticus 16:1</note>

**Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse and said:**
> The voice of the shofar grew louder and louder; Moses spoke, and God answered him with a voice. <note>Exodus 19:19</note>

What is this "voice of the shofar"? Rather, this is the Voice that emerges from the Shofar. And what is the Shofar? This is the <term>Higher Mother</term> <note>original: "Ima Ila'ah"; refers to the Sephirah of Binah, the divine source of understanding and liberation</note>. 
And the Voice that emerges from it is the letter **Vav** <note>The sixth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, representing the male principle or the six directions of the emotional attributes</note>, which is the Voice that emerges from the side of <term>Strength</term> <note>original: "Gevurah"; the attribute of judgment and restraint</note>. 
And this "voice of the shofar grew louder and louder"—this is the Voice of the Torah, which is comprised of the <term>six higher sides</term> <note>original: "shit sitrin ila'in"; the six emotional Sephirot from Chesed to Yesod</note>. It is the Voice that emerges from the Higher Shofar, and this is the Voice that becomes "Voice" at the moment it emerges from the Shofar. 
And this is "Moses spoke, and God answered him with a voice." He [Moses] would speak because the Voice and the Torah—which is itself "Voice"—were his portion. 
And when the time came that the Lord desired him, He called to him from the Tabernacle, and this is "And He called to Moses." 
But here it is written: "And the Lord spoke to Moses after the death." Rather, this refers to another time, and this is "after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they drew near before the Lord and died." This was because they offered strange fire <margin>strange</margin> <note>The marginal note "strange" serves as a catchword for the next page's opening phrase: "strange fire."</note>

**"And the Lord said to Moses: Speak to Aaron your brother, that he should not come at all times into the Sanctuary, within the veil..."** <note>Leviticus 16:2</note> Rabbi Isaac opened his discourse with the verse: **"Hear, my son, the instruction of your father, and do not forsake the teaching of your mother."** <note>Proverbs 1:8</note> "Hear, my son"—this is what King Solomon said by way of moral instruction and warning. And Rabbi Isaac said: Fortunate is the portion of the righteous who exert themselves in the Torah <note>The Five Books of Moses and its mystical secrets</note> day and night. Because of this, they know the paths of the Holy One, Blessed Be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"; the standard Zoharic name for God</note>, and they do not stray from the path of truth. For thus the Holy One, Blessed Be He, teaches a person, as the sages have established. And regarding this: "Hear, my son, the instruction of your father"—this refers to the Holy One, Blessed Be He; "and do not forsake the teaching of your mother"—this refers to the Assembly of Israel <note>original: "Knesset Yisrael"; in mystical terms, this refers to the Shekhinah or the Divine Presence</note>. And we have learned: what is "Hear, my son, the instruction of your father"? This is the instruction of the Torah, which is the Supernal Wisdom <note>original: "Chokhmah Ila'ah"; the second emanation of the Divine</note> that goes forth from Eden.

And this is what was said now: that one who strengthened himself more to see and to come upon them, and it says <note>Quoting Genesis 4:2</note> **"And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground."**

## Exodus (Shemot)

I have seen that this path is certainly dark. A path that is parched is a dark path. From where do we know this? As it is written:
> **"They wandered in the wilderness in a desert way"** <note>original: "Ta'u va-midbar bi-yeshimon derekh" (Psalms 107:4)</note>
What is meant by "a desert way"? It is a path that is parched <note>The Hebrew "yeshimon" (desert) is linked here to "yavesh" (dry/parched)</note>, and it is certainly a dark path. I have observed that a path in which no water is found is a dark path, and the Torah is water. Therefore, one who is on a journey and does not have words of Torah with him is on a dark path.
And concerning this it is written:
> **"Happy is the man whose strength is in You, in whose heart are the highways"** <note>original: "Ashrei adam oz lo vakh, mesilot bi-levavam" (Psalms 84:6)</note>

And the secret of the matter <note>term: "raza de-millah" - a technical term in the Zohar indicating a deeper, esoteric explanation</note> is that when one is on a journey and words of Torah are not found with him, he is on the path of death. For the Angel of Death walks with him and surrounds the man. Therefore, I have seen that this path is dark.

"Praiseworthy are those who labor in the Torah, for they are...
Praiseworthy are they..."

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Beha'alotcha. The previous section likely discussed the unique status of Moses' leadership; here, the text transitions into a specific comparison between the visionary capacity of Moses and that of all other prophets.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

Rabbi Hezekiah said: Come and see, what is the <term>image</term><note>original: "dyokna" - a form, likeness, or spiritual representation</note> of the prophets? It is like the image of a royal palace. Surrounding the King are all those who attend to Him. Every day, those who are outside lift their eyes to see the King’s glory, and every day they lift their eyes to see whoever stands inside the King’s house. These are the ones who circle the house. At all times, these prophets stand outside; they stand within the "arms" of the body <note>A reference to the Sefirot of Netzach and Hod, the sources of prophecy in Kabbalistic thought</note>. Because they stand outside the house, they do not see what is inside the house, but only what they can see through the walls of the house. They see the King standing in the house, and when He reveals His <term>royal purple garment</term><note>original: "porphyria" - a Greek-derived term for the purple robes of royalty</note>, they see what they see.

But Moses was not like this, for he stood inside the house <term>within</term><note>original: "legau" - in the innermost chamber</note>. All the walls of the house that cover the interior were revealed before him, and he saw everything. He did not look through the walls of the house; rather, he was inside. Because of this, it is written: **"In all My house, he is trusted"** <note>Numbers 12:7</note>. "In all My house" certainly, and not outside the house. Through all this, he saw what others did not see.

<term>Rabbi Jose said:</term> "In all My house"—this refers to the higher level where all the <term>Supreme Crowns</term><note>original: "ketrin ila'in" - the higher Sefirot or divine emanations</note> dwell. This is what is called the "Holy House," and regarding this, it says **"In all My house, he is trusted."** Therefore, Moses entered within, while all the other prophets of the world stood outside.

<term>Rabbi Judah opened</term> his discourse and said: **"Behold, the Lord rides upon a swift cloud and shall come into Egypt"** <note>Isaiah 19:1</note>. Come and see: when the Holy One, Blessed be He, passed over Egypt, He passed over the place of the "Image of Man," riding upon a "swift cloud." What is this "swift cloud"? This is the cloud of the Torah, as it is written: **"And it came to pass, as Moses entered into the tabernacle, the cloudy pillar descended"** <note>Exodus 33:9</note>. What is the meaning of "swift"? As it is written: **"And He shall come into Egypt, and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at His presence"** <note>Isaiah 19:1</note>. When He struck them with a single blow, fear was found in all of them. And why "swift"? Because He was swift to execute judgment without any delay at all. And regarding this, it is a "swift cloud," for it comes to act.

<summary>This page distinguishes the prophecy of Moses, who perceived the Divine from within the "inner house," from other prophets who only viewed the Divine through "walls." It also interprets the "swift cloud" in Egypt as a manifestation of immediate divine judgment and the same cloud that descended for Moses.</summary>

And Jacob saw **three sparks** <note>original: "gimel zikin" — representing the three primary emanations or "fathers" of the spiritual world</note> spreading out in every direction, and by their hands were **twenty-two holy letters** <note>The Hebrew alphabet, viewed in Kabbalah as the building blocks of creation</note> arranged in order. ## Portion of Balak - The Child

They rejoiced together and prepared the table. After they had cleared the table, they all came and kissed him <note>The Child</note> on his head. Rabbi Isaac said: "Surely the Holy One, Blessed be He, <note>Original: קב"ה - Kadosh Baruch Hu</note> has met us here and given us this gift." They rejoiced with him all that night. The next morning, they found themselves ready to depart. That child said:

-> **The Child** <-

"If you say that permission has been granted to you to go, depart now. However, until now, permission to go has not yet been given. Go out and see the merits of those who perform the commandment of their Master. Now they are all sitting at the King's table and delighting in the radiance of those holy crowns." He opened <note>a discourse</note> and said:
> **"Happy are those whose way is perfect, who walk in the Torah of the Lord."** <note>Psalms 119:1</note>
How much we must look into this matter! "Happy are those whose way is perfect"—is it only those of 'perfect way' who are happy and no others? Behold, all people of the world who walk in a straight path are called happy. Rather, "those of perfect way" are those who are seen to be marked in the Supernal Image <note>The divine form or spiritual blueprint of humanity</note>. Like a body that is found to be complete without any blemish at all; then it is called "perfect" <term>Tamim: meaning complete, whole, or unblemished</term>. And "those of perfect way" are those who walk in the path of faith, which are two paths included in one: the path of Abraham and the path of Isaac. And this is "perfect of way," just as it is said:
> **"Walk before Me and be perfect."** <note>Genesis 17:1</note>
And this refers to Abraham. And who are they? "Those who walk in the Torah of the Lord." Specifically "in the Torah of the Lord," because the Torah of the Lord is itself perfect, as it is said:
> **"The Torah of the Lord is perfect."** <note>Psalms 19:8</note>
And "those of perfect way" are those who walk in this way that is called "perfect."
Rabbi Isaac opened and said:
> **"Young lions do lack and suffer hunger, but those who seek the Lord shall not [lack any good thing]."** <note>Psalms 34:11</note>
