## Main Text (Zohar)

...under His wings <note>original: "tachat knafoy" - a reference to the Divine Presence</note>. And because of this, you companions, I did not sit in this place. Thus, meritorious is this one; from his understanding <note>original: "bina"</note> I know that God is with you. <meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Vayishlach (Genesis 32), focusing on the spiritual encounter between the patriarch Jacob and the celestial guardian of Esau. The text interprets this physical struggle as a cosmic blueprint for the historical exiles of the Jewish people.</meta>

## And He Sent (Vayishlach)

Jacob saw that place where his children would eventually pass through <note>original: "מדבחא" - likely referring to the altar or the path of sacrifice</note> and he drew his path near. He found that it was prepared, and he drew close before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and offered his prayer. Once he had prayed and desired to depart, an angel began to stand against him <note>or: to say to him</note> to wage war with him. That night represented the Exile of Edom <note>The Roman/Western exile</note> in which the children of Jacob draw near. After the children of Jacob are in exile, he began to contend with Jacob at every single moment until the light of day ascended. And this was the Exile of Edom which is characterized by darkness; and this darkness was what came upon Jacob, and the children of Esau multiplied at that time. When the light ascends, which is the Sun that begins to shine, it shall come upon the children of Esau, as it is written:
> But unto you that fear My name shall the **sun of righteousness** arise with healing in its wings. <note>Malachi 3:20</note>
And at that time, Israel shall dwell in tranquility and the children of Esau shall cease, because their light is consumed. And this "sun" that rose upon Jacob was the sun that was added to him from the Supernal Light <note>The divine radiance from the higher spiritual realms</note>.

Rabbi Shimon said: regarding the fact that [the angel] struck the hollow of his thigh, he intended to go and remain silent. And this thigh, which is the right side, is considered of great importance. For at that time when he prayed for the thigh, he saw that it was closed off from all sides; and since he saw it was closed and he was weak in it and could not prevail over him, he told Jacob to return because of it. And his image, which was perfected, he saw approaching him and he could not prevail over him. Because he saw that he [Jacob] was in his strength, he began to strike the hollow of his thigh, and because of this, he remained weak. That which comes from the weakness of the **Other Side** <term>Sitra Achra: the realm of evil or impurity in Kabbalah</term> is weak, and it came upon him and cut him where he was attached.

Rabbi Isaac and Rabbi Judah were walking on the road. Rabbi Judah said: this verse concerning Jacob where it is written:
> And the **sun rose** upon him <note>Genesis 32:32</note>
[means] when he saw the angel and he was made whole by him. Upon him—this was the "Tent of Torah," for he remained dwelling in his tent, which is bowed <unclear>...</unclear> Rabbi Isaac said: Fortunate is the portion of the righteous, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, rejoices in them <unclear>...</unclear> forever and for all eternity.

For purity, and to restore health to this [the soul], and then there is holiness for the people. ## Main Text (Zohar)

To the one who sanctifies within it subtle clouds <note>original: "ananin dekikin"</note> below, through which the sun <note>A reference to the sephirah of Tiferet, the divine masculine principle</note> is seen to shine. ->**Beshalach**<-

> And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not... <note>Exodus 13:17</note>

Rabbi Isaac said: What is the meaning of that which is written, "And it came to pass when Pharaoh sent [the people]," while it is also written, "And the Living God brought us out"? <note>original: "Elohim Chayim"</note> Why does it say "Pharaoh sent"? Rabbi Eleazar said: Heaven forbid that *he* [Pharaoh] sent them! Rather, by the hand of Pharaoh they were pushed out, and he sent them with these words of his when he said, "Rise up, get you forth from among my people" <note>Exodus 12:31</note>. It was this speech that caused them [to leave], and he was the one who "sent" them, for as soon as he saw that he had fulfilled his duty to them, that speech caused them to be pushed out. He was the "sender" because the one who told them that the deposit was fulfilled for them acted so that it would be thus. However, as for the phrase "The Living God brought us out"—this refers to God <note>Elohim</note> who is the Life that endures. For the One who brought them out did so to bring them to perfection. Therefore, it says "The Living God brought us out" so that perfection would be found above and below, in order for the Holy Name to be complete.

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the Festival of Sukkot, specifically focusing on the symbolic meaning of the Four Species and the transition from the seven days of Sukkot to the eighth day, Shemini Atzeret.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

And if you say that the <term>willow</term> <note>original: *arava*; the fourth of the species taken on Sukkot, characterized by having neither taste nor smell</note> is excluded from the joy of those other six <note>referring to the other three species—palm, citron, and myrtle—which together with the willow represent the seven lower emanations or *Sefirot*</note> that are joined as one to show that they are all in joy and there is no separation between them to receive them in joy—it is not so. For although the willow is "shadowed" <note>or "silent/tasteless"</note>, it is only so in relation to those it joins with. And if you say that it has no taste and no smell, it is not actually thus; rather, it has nothing of its own. But because it takes hold of those other six and is attached to them, it has no taste or smell of its own, but only what it clings to and receives from them. Then it possesses taste and smell. And this is the mystery: that everything is found as one in the mystery of the seven days and no less. For all is in joy; all seven days are found in joy and are found on the "Right Side" <note>the side of Mercy and Lovingkindness in Kabbalistic thought</note>. Therefore, we must rejoice in the joy of these seven days. And these are the seven days of <term>Sukkot</term> <note>The Feast of Tabernacles</note>, for they are the seven days of the festival where <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>A standard Rabbinic title for God</note> invites us together to eat and drink with Him, and gladdens us with the joy that is in Him. Therefore, we must rejoice in Him with joy, and it should be a complete joy, and no other "mixture" <note>referring to foreign thoughts or "Other Sides/Evil"</note> should be found between us and <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term>. Then, that eighth day, which is <term>Shemini Atzeret</term> <note>The "Eighth Day of Assembly"</note>, is the gathering of the joy of the Lord <note>original: *Y-H-V-H*</note>, which is the gathering of Israel into the King’s palace with joy of heart. As we have established, these eight days are the joy of all.

And if you say that the Festival of Unleavened Bread <note>Passover</note> also consists of seven days of joy—there, the <term>Lulav</term> <note>The palm branch</note> and its species are not present, for the Lulav is the mystery of joy and of unity as one. Because of this, the seven days of Sukkot are considered of higher status. And on the <term>Sabbath</term> <note>Shabbat</note>, we do not take the <term>Lulav</term>, because the <term>Sabbath</term> is everything; in it are found all the six <note>the six days of the week/six directions</note>, and in it they are in joy. They do not need to awaken another joy, for the Sabbath is everything, and from it all are blessed, and from it all are sustained. And those six weekdays are found within the Sabbath, for each and every one <unclear>is found</unclear> <unclear>in its day</unclear>.

<summary>This page explains the mystical unity of the Four Species, arguing that even the "tasteless" willow shares in the divine joy by its attachment to the other branches. It highlights the unique status of Sukkot and Shemini Atzeret as times of intimate joy with God, distinct from other festivals.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

As we have established regarding the verse: > Open the gates, that the righteous nation which keeps faithfulness may enter <note>Isaiah 26:2</note>

It means that anyone who prays properly and focuses their intention on "Blessed be He and Blessed be His Name"
and "Amen," we call them a "keeper of faithfulness," for the Holy Name is blessed through them.
And regarding this: <term>Amen, may His great Name be blessed forever and to all eternity</term> <note>The central response of the Kaddish prayer</note>

<term>be the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, above all blessings and songs.</term>
In this same manner, anyone who says <term>Amen</term> <note>The word Amen shares a root with *Emunah* (faith)</note> sustains that which is above,
acting as a "keeper of faithfulness," which is the **Righteous** <note>Yesod</note>, as it is written: > Your people shall all be righteous; they shall inherit the land forever <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>
And it is written: > But the righteous is an everlasting foundation <note>Proverbs 10:25; *Yesod Olam*</note>. And because of this, when the **Righteous** <note>The masculine principle, Yesod</note> joins
with **Righteousness** <note>The feminine principle, Malkhut/Tzedek</note>, he gives birth to souls and holy beings, and produces the fruits and produce
of the worlds. Then the worlds are blessed as one, for there lies the "faithfulness"

## Pekudei

## Main Text (The Zohar)

As we have said, they ascend into it from within the **World to Come** <note>The "World to Come" refers to the Sefirah of Binah, the divine source of understanding and the "womb" of emanation</note>. Because of this, on the Sabbath, the Bride—who is the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note>—is blessed and prepared for the King, all in a single desire.

->**Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever**<-

And for this reason, it is the mystery of "One" and the mystery that includes everything; it is found that this is the mystery of "One" and that is the mystery of the "Name of His glorious kingdom." This is the unification that is below, when everything is unified as one, and this is a perfect unification. And for this reason, it is the mystery of "One" and the mystery of "Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."

And because of this, when everything is unified as one, then everything is on the side of holiness. And this is the mystery of <unclear>faith</unclear>...

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on the Torah portion Vayeshev (Genesis 37), focusing on the cosmic role of Joseph. ## Main Text (The Zohar)

Isaac, when he emerged from the place of Isaac <note>original: "Isaac from the place of Isaac" — referring to the emanation of the Sefirah of Gevurah (Strength/Judgment)</note> and was sown into the **Field of Holy Apples** <note>Aramaic: *Chakla de-Tapuchin Kadishin* — a mystical name for the Shekhinah or the Divine Presence, envisioned as a fertile orchard</note>, he fathered descendants below just as they were above, established within the Divine structure. This is the secret of the holy blessing of Isaac upon **Joseph**. Truly, he is the **Righteous One** <term>Tzaddik: the Sefirah of Yesod, which channels divine energy</term>, the Life of the Worlds. And just as he is the Life of the Worlds there, so he is here. And these are the sons of Zilpah, as it is written: "And these are the sons of Zilpah." 

As the sages established, Joseph was attached to the mystery of the Good Life <note>Joseph is identified with the Sefirah of Yesod, the "Life of the Worlds"</note>. They established these matters at the beginning of weeping and judgment, similar to what was said regarding the "soul of seven days" and "it was on the eighth day." This is the secret and the mystery of the verse: **"And Joseph was shepherding his brothers with the flock"** <note>Quoting Genesis 37:2</note>.

So it appears to me; come and see: a cloud descends beneath the Living Creature <note>referring to the *Chayah*, a high-ranking angel or divine energy</note>. This is the meaning of "and there was a cloud." There, the name of Simeon shall be living and engraved, corresponding to the speech of affliction and death that dwelled with him. Regarding the holy Isaac, from all that is found there, come and see that whoever possesses this path and acts accordingly, he is sent under the hand [of Providence]. And so it was when the brothers acted and engraved [their deeds]. 

Even though it is said that a "Righteous One" <note>Tzaddik</note> is among His servants—sometimes in concealment, sometimes revealed—what path shall we take? His garment is the voice of the wonder of Faith <note>Aramaic: *Meimanuta* — the realm of the Divine</note>, and the path remains a wonder forever. When Laban arose and acted thus, he was ensnared and they wondered; he was prepared, he bowed, and he went before you. 

The Righteous One and the Judgment are as it is written: **"And Israel strengthened himself"** <note>Reference to Genesis 48:2</note> and he lives forever through his deeds and in security. This is why the Righteous One sat by the hand of the pious ones; the elder Isaac saw what was said regarding the "Good" that he sent. **"And Joseph was in the house of his Egyptian master"**—this means he was in his name and his standing, dwelling even with a servant. Come and see how the pious ones behaved in this mystery; they saw to it to guard the "Living Creature," those servants of Jesse, and they inherited the life of the strength that was bestowed upon him.

***

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of sacrificial elements, specifically focusing on the spiritual essence of salt as described in the Zohar (the foundational work of Jewish mysticism). It likely follows a discussion on the meal offering (Mincha).</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

For we have learned about salt. And we have learned <note>Leviticus 2:13</note> **"Season all your grain offerings with salt."** What is the reason?
Because salt is a covenant. And the covenant is the mystery of the Holy One, Blessed be He, which sustains
the world. Because of this, salt sweetens judgment. And it was taught: this salt
is a covenant. As it is written <note>Numbers 18:19</note> **"It is an everlasting covenant of salt."** Why is it called
a covenant? Because it is the sustenance of the entire world. Come and see: salt is
the mystery of water that has been completed by fire. For salt comes from water,
and through fire it becomes salt. Therefore, it sweetens judgment.
And this mystery is the mystery of the Holy Covenant, which is the sustenance of the world.
And because of this, it is written: **"Season with salt."** "And do not allow the salt of the covenant of your God to be lacking."
Why does it say "your God" <note>original: Elohecha</note>? Because salt sweetens judgment. And "your God" <note>Elohim</note> refers to Judgment.
And it is sweetened by the salt. Therefore it is written: **"It is an everlasting covenant of salt."**
A covenant which is the sustenance of the world, as we have established.

Come and see: the covenant is Mercy <note>Chesed</note> and it is Judgment <note>Din</note>. Why is this?
Because it emerges from water, which is Mercy, and is completed in fire, which is Judgment.
Therefore it is a covenant, for it includes one within the other: <term>Mercy and Judgment</term> <note>The union of the Sefirot Chesed and Gevurah</note>.
And Judgment is sweetened by Mercy. This is the mystery of salt.
Because salt is the sustenance of everything. Therefore, a sacrifice is not found
without salt. For sustenance is not found above or below
except through the mystery of the covenant.

<summary>This passage from the Zohar explains the mystical nature of salt in biblical sacrifices, describing it as a "covenant" that balances the opposing cosmic forces of Mercy (water) and Judgment (fire). By combining these elements, salt "sweetens" harsh judgment and provides the essential foundation for the world's existence.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the spiritual rewards of Torah study, specifically focusing on the soul's ascent and the divine delight taken in the righteous. It aligns with the Zohar's commentary on the portion of Lech Lecha.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

And when the Holy One, blessed be He <note>Aramaic: Kudsha Brich Hu; the standard rabbinic title for God</note>, comes to enter the Garden of Eden to rejoice with the **righteous ones**, He looks up and says: "Whoever among them has perfected the name of Heaven, he is my treasure and my charge." And we have learned: "Pious one, pious one!" <note>A term of endearment or address for a mystic</note> A beloved word of Torah ascends before the Holy One, blessed be He, regarding a matter that is higher than high, as it is written: "And my words which I have put in your mouth." 

Come and see: as it were, the Holy One, blessed be He, said "from your mouth" it is revealed, and from the "mouth of your children's children, from now and forevermore." And we have learned that the pious one sees at that hour...

<summary>This passage from the Zohar describes the divine joy and angelic praise triggered by those who study Torah, explaining how their words of study become spiritual crowns that ensure a multi-generational connection to God.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exposition of the creation narrative in Genesis, specifically focusing on the unity of opposites within the divine structure. It transitions from the creation of light and darkness to the ontological unity of male and female principles.</meta>

## Genesis

## Main Text (The Zohar)

[...] and **light and darkness** <term>Light and Darkness: In Kabbalah, these are not just physical phenomena but represent the divine attributes of Mercy (Right) and Judgment (Left)</term> were both found as one. 
And this is the secret of everything: that Right and Left are found together. 
In the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>, all is the Right. 
But in the place where the Right is found, the Left is also found. 
He is the Day, and He is the secret of the Night. 
From this side, Day is found; and from that side, 
Night is found. Right and Left were both found 
as one. And because of this, it is Day, yet the secret of Night 
is found within it. From the side of the Right, it is Day. 
And from the side of the Left, it is Night. And come and see:

> And there was evening and there was morning, one day <note>Genesis 1:5</note>

What is "one day"? It is that the night is included in the day, and the day in the night, 
so that all becomes one. In this same manner, Adam <note>The first human, or the primordial human archetype</note> is 
**male and female**. And the female was found within him on the

## Main Text (Zohar)

The strength and the power of every lower **Might** <note>Hebrew: *Gevurah*; the divine attribute of judgment and restraint</note> is taken from there, and it is a judgment of harsh judgment. This is the craftsmanship of craftsmen, for all colors are united therein, and they include five thousand five hundred and eighty—in total 130—that hang from the **Curtain** <note>Hebrew: *Parokhet*; the veil separating the Holy from the Holy of Holies</note>.

For we have learned that every deed performed by human beings is engraved there, except for that which remains in **Thought** <note>Makhshava</note> and what is done in secret. Rabbi Judah said: every hidden state of the soul that does not yet have a body but is destined to be, and all those who have come into the world, are engraved there. All of them existed at the time the soul emerged from the **Holy Thought** <note>Aramaic: *Makhshava Kadisha*; the highest level of divine emanation</note>. All of this is according to what is found. Do not wonder at this, for all this is the life and the life of the wise. This existed before then, at the time they were exiled to the Babylonian exile, at the time the Holy One, blessed be He, showed Ezekiel the glory of His throne. And concerning this:

And this is comparable to a man who has a throne; he sits upon it, enjoys it, and rules over it. Everything he possesses and everything he prepares is well-protected. Regarding this, it is written: *Blessed be the Lord forever, Amen and Amen.* This is the **Secret of the Matter** <note>original: "Raza d'Millah"</note> as we have said, because it is the **Secret of the Faith** <note>original: "Raza d'Meimanuta"</note> of all Israel. It is all for the purpose that the **Secret of the Faith** shall dwell upon them alone, and the **Other Side** shall not be mixed within it. Therefore it is written: *Blessed be the Lord forever, Amen and Amen...*

<meta>This page continues the mystical discourse on the power of speech and Torah study, specifically focusing on how human words of Torah ascend through the celestial realms to trigger divine blessing.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

Come and see: all those who labor in the Torah <note>The Zohar emphasizes "labor" or "exertion" in study as a creative act</note>, the Holy One, Blessed be He, praises them every day. And those words that are renewed in the Torah through the mouth <note>original: "בפומיה" (in his mouth). This refers to the "Chiddush" or novel insight shared by a scholar</note> of the Torah—when they seek to come before the Holy King, they emerge from a place that is unknown and ascend above and below before the Holy King. They are crowned by Him, and a single, complete firmament <note>term: Firmament (Raki'a). In Kabbalah, this refers to a spiritual layer or "heavenly expanse" created by human action</note> is made.

And concerning this, it is stated: *“For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I am making...”* <note>Isaiah 66:22</note>. Note that it does not say "I have made," but rather "I am making," for He makes them in each and every moment. And upon whom do they all depend? Upon those who labor in the Torah.

And concerning this, it is written: *“...and from speaking a word [on the Sabbath] from pursuing your own business”* <note>Isaiah 58:13</note>. Is speech not an action? Indeed, that word which emerges from the mouth performs power and becomes an actual "deed" above. Because of this, "speaking a word" is considered like "doing your own business," for the Holy One, Blessed be He, loves that word and is crowned by it above. He calls this an actual "work" and a "deed."

That word ascends and is crowned upon the head of the **Righteous One, the Life of the Worlds** <note>term: Tzaddik Chai HaOlamim. A mystical name for the Sefirah (divine attribute) of Yesod, which acts as the funnel for divine energy</note>. It flies from there and ascends higher into the seventy-two lights that shine. All those lights are crowned by that word, and they ascend higher until it reaches the **Ancient of Days** <note>term: Atik Yomin. The highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine Will</note>. From there, that word is crowned and ascends higher and higher until it reaches the place that is the **Source of Influence** <note>term: Mazal. Literally "constellation," but here meaning the ultimate source from which divine grace "flows" or "drips" down</note> for all.

From that place, blessing descends to all worlds. And that word which emerged from the mouth of that human being is what caused this. Fortunate is the portion of that person!

Come and see: *“And it came to pass, when the ark set forward...”* <note>Numbers 10:35</note>

<summary>This passage describes how novel insights in Torah study physically create new spiritual heavens and trigger a flow of blessing from the highest divine source (Atik Yomin) down to the physical world. It emphasizes that speech, when holy, is a potent form of "action" that sustains the universe.</summary>
<keywords>Torah study, New Heavens, Speech as Action, Yesod, Atik Yomin, Mazal, Divine Blessing, Isaiah 66:22</keywords>

## When the Ark Set Out

119 For they illuminate all the other lamps <note>original: "bozinim" — mystical lights or candles in Kabbalistic thought</note>, both upper and lower, and they were meant to shine. At that time, "Blessed be the Place <note>a traditional title for God</note>, Blessed be He." And regarding this, it is written: **"And it came to pass, when the ark set out, that Moses said..."** <note>Numbers 10:35</note>. For behold, these shine with beauty and radiance. And what of the Divine Presence <note>original: "Shekhinah" — the feminine, indwelling aspect of God</note> which is beneath the holiness of the lower world? Despite all this, the Hidden One could not be contained by her at all times, for there was a moment of extra deficiency. Why? Because Moses illuminates her more than all other prophets. Indeed, there is no eye or height [like his], because all of them were unable to see except for Moses. He is higher than them in height, strength, and superior vision. This [vision] rose and fell for everyone except for Moses, because they [the Israelites] are meritorious ones who see constantly. And just as they are illuminated by these [lights] at the King's table <note>original: "ptura de-malka"</note> and the bread from above which the righteous eat, they appear upright. At this time, [the light] descends to the Form, and Israel was distinguished in their time from all other nations. There was a lack of radiance in it [the world], but regarding the Holy One, Blessed be He, who encompasses them, and the sins that are beyond counting—[all was forgiven] because of the goodness of those **Six Hundred Thousand** <note>original: "shishim ribo" — the traditional number of adult males in the Exodus, representing the totality of the Jewish soul-root</note>... whose Divine Presence was hovering over them. They were the hearts that illuminated every night. And what is hinted at above? From Him, [the lights] flow to every prophet, from every prophet... they shall arise, and light was in their hearts from all the radiance. And in the time to come, they sinned, and the poor and simple in the world—all the rectifications <note>original: "tikkunim" — spiritual repairs or restorations</note> are those that they took and received, whether in honor or in cheapness, from everything. And there are those who say here: in radiance and light... revealed, and they are visible to all the nations from all the radiance in their hearts... and since they are constant in their time, they are radiant and illuminate upon the earth. This is like the secret of the heart <note>original: "raza de-liba"</note> in prophecy, and all the radiance that descends—Heaven forbid—upon the bread from every place. And in all the radiance of the Holy One, Blessed be He, may He come and bring to you a song.

## The Account of the Tabernacle

[...] <note>The text begins mid-sentence from the previous page</note> the Tabernacle of Moses, when he established it, at that same moment the Tabernacle of above was found to be present. It was in this very image <note>original: "dyukna" - a mystical form or spiritual blueprint</note> below, and through all this, it was established and stood firm. When this [earthly one] was seen, the work was established within it; through this image and through this word, the work was performed. Concerning this, the matter is precise: through the word and through the image, word taught word and action taught action. 

When Moses established the Tabernacle below as a place for human beings, the Tabernacle of above was established through all of this, and all things were found within it. This is precisely what occurred: when Moses established the Tabernacle of below, the Tabernacle of above was established along with it. This is revealed in the words spoken by Moses: "Open for me..."

-> **"Open for me the gates of righteousness..."** <note>Psalms 118:19. In Kabbalah, "Righteousness" (Tzedek) refers to the Sefirah of Malkhut, the Divine Feminine presence and the gateway to the upper worlds.</note> <-

This is the gate of the Tabernacle of above, which is called "Righteousness." The Tabernacle of below is the gateway to the Tabernacle of above. This is why it says "Open for me," precisely in word and in image. It is said that the Tabernacle was found on that day and at that very hour. 

Blessed is the one who saw the joy of the Tabernacle of above at that moment when the Tabernacle of below was established! The work here was exactly mirrored by the work there; word taught word and action taught action. This is the work of the Tabernacle, and this is the work of that day. If a wise man is found there, he will know the supernal image. This is what was found when the Tabernacle was established: the mystery <note>original: "raza"</note> found at that hour was that the Tabernacle below and the Tabernacle above were as one. This was found to be so because they were joined, one to the other [...]

<summary>This passage describes the mystical correspondence between the earthly Tabernacle built by Moses and its heavenly counterpart, explaining that the two were erected simultaneously as mirrors of one another. It interprets the "Gates of Righteousness" from Psalms as the spiritual gateway connecting the physical sanctuary to the divine realm.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

...We have learned: One day Rabbi Shimon was traveling **in Tiberias** <note>original: "be-Tiveria"; a notable variant as many versions place this in the desert</note> and with him were Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Abba, and they were speaking words of Torah. Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse and said: **"And it came to pass, when the ark set forward, that Moses said: Rise up, O Lord, etc."** <note>Numbers 10:35</note> And we have learned: What is this "Ark"? It is none other than that which is called the "Ark of the Covenant." And we have established that she <note>The Divine Presence or Malchut</note> is called *Adonai* <note>The Divine Name associated with lordship and the physical world</note>, the Lord of all the earth. And all the souls of the world [are contained in her], for she is called the Ark of the Covenant because she receives the "Covenant" <note>term: Covenant (Berit) - here referring to the flow of divine energy from the higher Sefirah of Yesod into the lower Malchut</note> for the worlds. And then she is everything, alone in the world, and in her everything is found. She is the Ark in which all blessings are found, and because of this, she is everything.

And when that which is called "Ark" moves, then all [the worlds] move, and all the heavenly hosts are stirred and move with her. Just like that voice that goes out every day and says, **"Holy, holy, holy"** <note>Isaiah 6:3</note>, they all <unclear>say</unclear> the word. And when the Ark moves, all those <unclear>above</unclear> move with it. Then they all stood and said: **"Rise up, O Lord, and let Your enemies be scattered; and let them that hate You flee before You."**

Who are these "enemies"? These are the "Lower Crowns" <note>term: Lower Crowns (Ketrin Tata'in) - the dark mirrors or demonic counterparts to the holy Sefirot</note> that come from the "Other Side" <note>term: Other Side (Sitra Achra) - the realm of evil or spiritual impurity in Kabbalistic thought</note>, who stand upon the path <unclear>to hinder</unclear> all <unclear>human beings</unclear>. And because of this, then all the <unclear>holy ones</unclear> arose, <unclear>and then they were all nullified before them.</unclear>

<summary>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai explains that the Ark of the Covenant represents the Divine Presence (Malchut), which contains all souls and blessings. When this Divine power moves, it scatters the "Lower Crowns" or spiritual forces of evil that attempt to block humanity's path.</summary>

In the school of **Rav Hamnuna the Elder**, when he would pray his prayer <note>Zohar II, 118a</note> [he would say]:
"**The Holy One, blessed be He**, You are the Supreme King, and You are the God of Truth, and Your judgment is truth, and Your word is truth, and it stands forever." [Thus] we have learned that every word that is truth stands forever. And because of this—because the Holy One, blessed be He, is Truth—He stands forever.

And the world is sustained because of Him. A judgment that is truth will endure for all eternity, but a judgment that is not truth—a <term>person</term> <note>original: "bar nash" — literally "son of man," used here for any human being</note> will not be sustained by it. 

Come and see: when a person sits in judgment, the Holy One, blessed be He, stands over him. If he judges a judgment of truth, the <term>Divine Presence</term> <note>original: "Shekhinah" — the feminine, indwelling aspect of God that wanders with humanity</note> stands over him. But if he judges a false judgment, the Divine Presence departs from him, and a <unclear>voice</unclear> goes out and says: "Woe to the wicked man! It shall be ill with him, for the work of his hands shall be done to him" <note>Isaiah 3:11. This verse suggests that the consequences of a person's actions—in this case, a corrupt judge—will return to haunt them.</note>. 

Because of this, a person must fear before the Holy One, blessed be He, when he sits in judgment, because the Divine Presence dwells upon him and he is standing in judgment before Him. Come and see: judgment that is truth is the sustenance of the whole world, and because of this, the judge of truth becomes a partner with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the <term>Work of Creation</term> <note>original: "Ma’aseh Bereshit" — the primordial act of creating the universe</note>, as they have established it [regarding the verse]: "And there was evening and there was morning, one day" <note>Genesis 1:5</note>. 

What is the meaning of "one day"? This refers to the day of the judge who judges a judgment of truth, for the Divine Presence joins with him and is crowned through him with the **crown of truth**. 

And if not for the judgment of truth, this world would not endure, nor would the upper world endure. When **Rav Hamnuna the Elder** would see a judge who judges a judgment of truth, he would say: "This is one who makes the King’s Throne whole" <note>The "King's Throne" represents the stability of the divine government; by acting justly on earth, the judge "repairs" or completes the throne in the spiritual realm.</note>.

The strength of the human body is only sustained in this place because

# Vayera

## Main Text (The Zohar)

Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse with the verse: **"And the raven, and the kite after its kind..."** <note>Leviticus 11:14-15</note> Rabbi Shimon said: Come and see how many various categories are implied by the phrase "after its kind." This is the secret of these <term>birds</term> <note>original Aramaic: *ofa*. In Zoharic thought, these are not merely physical birds but spiritual entities or "powers" that inhabit the lower realms.</note>, for all of them possess a specific power and each one conducts itself according to its own kind. Even though they are all found on one mountain <note>Likely referring to the "Mountains of Darkness," the dwelling place of fallen or impure spiritual forces.</note>, these entities possess their own power, and each one receives its own <term>portion</term> <note>original Aramaic: *chulka*; a spiritual lot or destiny assigned by the Divine hierarchy.</note>, for they were all designated, each one according to its kind.

And we have learned: all of them possess power, and each one is drawn toward many portions that depend on that specific place. All of this is because there are several birds situated upon the back of the <term>serpent</term> <note>original Aramaic: *chivya*. This refers to the Primordial Serpent, the root of the "Other Side" or the forces of evil/impurity.</note> of that portion. They are all agents of destruction who join together to bring <term>judgment</term> <note>original Aramaic: *dina*; the divine attribute of strict justice or severity which, when unbalanced by mercy, results in punishment.</note> upon the world. All those who derive their power from that place have their portion and their destiny hanging from it; for this reason, they were all appointed to that specific place.

**"And the raven, and the kite after its kind"**—for these birds all emerge from that portion of strict judgment. Because of this, they all have a designated role and are appointed over the world. Even though they are all messengers sent for the purpose of executing judgment upon the world, this is the distinction: **"And the raven"** refers to a portion that emerges from the side of judgment, while **"and the kite after its kind"** refers to a specific portion that is suspended from the source of judgment. In this way, they are all "after their kind," yet everything is bound together in a single knot and they are all appointed over the affairs of the world. Regarding this...

Furthermore, Rabbi Shimon said: Come and see how all these portions are suspended from the place of judgment... Come and see, all of them...

<summary>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai interprets the "impure birds" of the Torah as mystical symbols for destructive spiritual forces. He explains that these entities are organized into a strict hierarchy (each "after its kind") tied to the "Other Side" and the attribute of strict Judgment.</summary>

<keywords>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, impure birds, raven, kite, Sitra Achra, Judgment, Dina, Serpent, spiritual hierarchy, Leviticus</keywords>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

[Rabbi] Shimon opened his discourse and said: At the hour when the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original Aramaic: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note> is destined to redeem His children from among the nations, all those <term>Righteous</term> <note>original Aramaic: *Tzadikim*</note> who are in the Garden of Eden shall hear the voice of Shimon singing sweetly. Whoever hears Shimon's voice, they all listen and rejoice. And I come to look upon him, yet who can look upon him? For the brilliance of the light that surrounds him is such that no man can behold it.

And behold, **Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair** <note>The father-in-law of Rabbi Shimon and a renowned mystic in his own right.</note> approaches, and all the <term>celestial springs</term> <note>original: *ma'ayanin*; spiritual sources of wisdom or vitality.</note> are before him, and all the <term>Members of the Palace</term> <note>original: *Bnei Heikhala*; the assembly of righteous souls in the heavenly realm.</note> are before him. It is found that those who come to hear Shimon's voice rejoice; though they see Shimon alone, one cannot <unclear>behold him</unclear> here in the same way as he was in this world.

All these righteous ones rejoice, and I rejoice as well. They all come and share the joy, saying, "Peace be upon you!" This is granted to you because of Shimon, whom no man can look upon, unless an angel whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, appoints before him, guards him. Because of who Shimon is—for Shimon's sake—even I, from the day I went to see him, was not given permission to look upon him directly.

We were once together in this world. See how all the righteous are above! I and all of you see Shimon and behold the <term>joy</term> <note>original: *cheduata*</note> of Shimon, and I rejoice. And here we find ourselves, beholding what no man is permitted to see: the moment when the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to redeem the House of Israel. We shall see him at that hour together, for Shimon is never far from Him.

We rejoice to behold Him, and He reveals Himself because Shimon rejoices and sings before Him. I am Shimon <note>The narrator here identifies with or experiences the perspective of the soul of Shimon.</note>, and I hear his voice and I rejoice. At that hour, we were sitting before Shimon, and in all my days, I have never seen such joy as this—the joy of Shimon singing, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, rejoicing with him. Because he is Shimon, we are always found in his presence.

## Main Text (The Zohar)

<note>The beginning of this page concludes the mystical discourse on Abraham's old age, based on Genesis 24:1.</note>

He opened his discourse and said: Since it is written > **"And Abraham was old, advanced in days"** (Genesis 24:1).
What is the meaning of "advanced in days"? <note>The literal Hebrew "Ba Ba-yamim" means "came into the days."</note> It means he entered into the <term>higher levels</term> <note>original Aramaic: *darjin*; referring to the Sefirot or spiritual emanations.</note> that are called "days," as we have stated. Come and see: Abraham was worthy of those "days" and drew them near so he could be united with them. Because of this, he is called "advanced in days." It appears to me that all of them were joined as one in the path of <term>Faith</term> <note>original: *meimanuta*; in the Zohar, this often refers to the unified structure of the Divine realm.</note>, and the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: *Kudsha Brich Hu*</note> fulfills the will of those who fear Him.

---

<note>Start of a new section (Zohar Volume I, page 123a) where Rabbi Elazar, the son of Rabbi Shimon, begins a new teaching.</note>

**Rabbi Elazar opened and said:** > **"The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; a good understanding have all they that do them: His praise endureth for ever"** (Psalms 111:10).
We have established the meaning of this verse in several places. But come and see: "The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom"—what does this say? Rather, <term>Higher Wisdom</term> <note>original: *Chokhmah Ila'ah*</note> is hidden and unrevealed. When it desired to be revealed and to emerge from the hidden secret, it created a certain place to dwell within. This [place] is the "Fear of the Lord," and this is the "Beginning of Wisdom," and they are all one. The secret of this is **"The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom."** This secret is also found in the verse: > **"Open to me the gates of righteousness"** (Psalms 118:19).

This is the gate through which one enters the higher levels. All of this exists within the **Secret of Faith**. The Holy One, Blessed be He, teaches humanity that they cannot enter Him except through this gate. If one does not enter through this gate, he shall never enter at all. It is like a King who built an inner palace and made an outer gate for it, and so on. Because all the <term>inner levels</term> <note>original: *darjin penima'in*</note> only rest within this gate which is called **"The Fear of the Lord."** For this reason, it is called "Beginning."

Come and see: all the higher levels and the Secret of Faith are all joined together in this secret. What is the reason? Because it is the gate to all of them. ## Main Text (Zohar)

And we have learned: when the sun emerges from within that light, the day shines while including the night within it. For this reason, the sun is called day. Rabbi Judah opened his discourse (Psalms 106:1):

## Main Text (Zohar)

certainly fortunate is the man who returns in complete repentance before 
his Master. Because repentance is the elevation of everything and is superior to 
everything, as we have established in this book. For when repentance 
is awakened in the world, then everything is awakened in perfection, and 
everything will be settled in its place as is fitting. And <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> 
has compassion on the world and on the person who returns in repentance. And come and see: 
Repentance is a supreme <term>secret</term> <note>original: "Raza"; a hidden mystical truth.</note> from among all the secrets of the Torah, 
because concerning Repentance it is written: 
> You return man to dust <note>original: "ad daka"</note>, and say, "Return, children of men." <note>Psalms 90:3</note>

<summary>This passage describes the spiritual mechanics of repentance, explaining how sincere Teshuva purifies the soul of sin, removes the "pressure" of external destructive forces, and allows it to finally enter its designated place in the Garden of Eden.</summary>

[This is the place] of the ten types of precious stones that we mentioned previously. All of them originate from this side. "Let there be light" refers to the upper light. "And there was light" refers to the lower light. This is the starting point for adhering to the innermost realm. # Va'etchanan

## Main Text (Zohar)

> **"When you beget children and children’s children, and you have grown old in the land, and act corruptly, and make a carved image in the form of anything, and do evil in the sight of the Lord your God to provoke Him."** <note>Deuteronomy 4:25</note>

Rabbi Abba opened [the discourse]: "When you beget children and children’s children..." This verse has already been established by the colleagues, but come and see: At the time when **the Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>The primary name for God in the Zohar, emphasizing His transcendence and His relationship with the world.</note> desired to create the world, all those **souls** <term>nishmatin; the highest level of the human soul, representing the divine spark</term> that were destined to be given to human beings were all standing before Him in their exact **form** <term>diyokna; a spiritual prototype or "image" that corresponds exactly to the physical appearance the person will have in this world</term>, precisely as they appear in this world. 

And at the time when people in this world desire to unite in a sexual union, the Holy One, Blessed be He, signals to the angelic appointee who is in charge of all those souls, and says to him: "That specific soul is going to be placed in the body of so-and-so." At that moment, the Holy One, Blessed be He, charges that soul with several **commandments** <note>original: pikkudin; divine instructions or charges</note> and commands it to keep His charges. 

He says to the soul: "Behold, I have given you a place in this world; be careful to fulfill My commandments and My Torah, for if you do not, you will be cast out into **Gehinnom** <note>original: Gehinnom; a place of spiritual purification or punishment after death</note> and into the place called **Sheol** <note>original: Sheol; the biblical term for the underworld or the depths of the grave</note>." And when a person is born into the world, that soul does not depart from him, as the colleagues have already established.

The Holy One, Blessed be He, warns the person and says to him: "When you beget children and children’s children." This is because the soul was not fully settled in the person until he had children. For so the colleagues have established: that anyone who does not beget children is not a **complete man** <term>adam shalim; the Kabbalistic concept that a human being only reaches their full spiritual potential and "completeness" through marriage and procreation</term>, and such a person is considered lacking. 

Because of this, the verse says: "When you beget children and children’s children, and you have grown old in the land," for it is only then that the soul is fully settled in its place. Therefore, the Holy One, Blessed be He, warns the person and says to him: "...and act corruptly and make a carved image in the form of anything..." This is because until this point—until the person has children and is "grown old" or established—divine punishment did not fall upon him in the same way, because he was considered "lacking" or incomplete. What is the meaning of **"and you have grown old"**? It is as you would say:

> **"My eye is dimmed with grief; it has grown old because of all my enemies."** <note>Psalms 6:8</note>

And what is the meaning of **"it has grown old"**? It is as you would say:

> **"And the rock is moved from its place."** <note>Job 14:18; the Zohar is making a linguistic connection between "growing old" (atkah) and being "moved" or "established" (ye'etak) in a permanent state.</note>

<summary>This page explores the Kabbalistic doctrine of the pre-existence of souls and the spiritual significance of parenthood. It explains that a person only becomes a "complete man" and fully responsible for their spiritual actions after having children and becoming "established" in the world.</summary>
<keywords>pre-existence of souls, diyokna, procreation, Adam Shalim, Gehinnom, Sheol, Deuteronomy 4:25, Rabbi Abba, spiritual completeness</keywords>

# Genesis

## Main Text (Zohar)

-> **In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth** <-

Rabbi Hezekiah opened [the discourse]:
> **"As a rose among the thorns, so is my beloved among the daughters."** <note>Song of Songs 2:2</note>

What is the **rose**? It is the Community of Israel <term>Knesset Yisrael; the spiritual archetype of the Jewish people and the divine feminine presence known as Malchut</term>. For there is a rose, and then there is a rose. Just as a rose among the thorns contains **red and white** <note>original: "sumak ve-chiivur"</note>, so too the Community of Israel contains **Judgment and Mercy**. Just as a rose has **thirteen petals**, so too the Community of Israel has the thirteen attributes of mercy <note>The thirteen ways through which Divine compassion flows into the world</note> that surround it on all sides.

Likewise, the name **God** <note>original: "Elohim"</note> mentioned here in the verse <quote>In the beginning God created</quote>—when He brought it [the Community of Israel] forth, He brought it forth with thirteen words to surround it and protect it. After this, what is the second word? It is the one written as "God" [the second mention of the name in the Torah] which brought forth **five strong petals** that surround the rose. And these are the five gates of salvation. And regarding this mystery, it is written:
> **"I will lift up the cup of salvation."** <note>Psalms 116:13</note>

This is the **Cup of Blessing** <note>The cup used during the Grace After Meals or Sanctification (Kiddush)</note>. The Cup of Blessing must be supported by five fingers, just as the rose sits upon five strong petals, which correspond to the five fingers. And this rose is the Cup of Blessing.

From the second mention of the name "God" until the third mention of the name "God" [in the creation story], there are five words. From here He brought forth the heavens to protect the rose and plant it. As it is written: **the heavens**. These are the five who stand over the rose. From here they were created, and from here they were established. "In the beginning God created." What is **Bereshit**? It means **He created six** <note>original: "Bara Shit"; a mystical wordplay on the word "Bereshit," where "Shit" is Aramaic for "six"</note>. These are the six petals that rose from this rose. And these are the six sides <note>The six directions of the physical world: North, South, East, West, Up, and Down</note>—the six levels—upon which the whole world stands. And these are the six days...

<summary>This opening page of the Zohar uses the symbolism of a rose to explain the relationship between the Divine and the Community of Israel, mapping the structure of the rose onto the opening verses of Genesis. It introduces the concept of the thirteen attributes of mercy and the six directions of creation.</summary>

# Portions of the Law: Behar (Leviticus 25)

## Main Text (Zohar)

This implies that the gathering of all the lower hosts, who come from every place below, desire to dwell upon **the Holy One, Blessed be He**, for He dwells within them and from Him. Yet [at certain times] the external forces are all cast outside, and this state is called <term>common</term> <note>original: "chol"; referring to the "profane" or weekday state where the Divine Presence is not overtly manifest</note>. Regarding this, it is written: "And you shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout the land unto all the inhabitants thereof; it shall be a jubilee unto you; and you shall return every man unto his possession, and you shall return every man unto his family" <note>Leviticus 25:10</note>. This state is the <term>Jubilee</term> <note>original: "Yovel"; kabbalistically associated with the Sefirah of Binah, the "Upper Mother" and the source of ultimate cosmic freedom</note>. Regarding this, it is written: "A jubilee it is; it shall be holy unto you."

And when is it called "Holy"? It is at the moment of the gathering of all the upper hosts, when they come toward Him and "you proclaim liberty" to them, for they all go out into freedom. Because of this, it is said: "you shall return every man unto his possession, and you shall return every man unto his family," for this is the mystery of **the Holy One, Blessed be He** at the time when the upper building is established in its proper arrangements, which is the <term>World to Come</term> <note>original: "Alma de-Atei"; referring to the continuous flow of Divine consciousness from the higher realms</note>.

And because of this it is written: "A jubilee it is; it shall be holy unto you." "Seven sabbaths of years," "seven years seven times," which are forty-nine years—for they are all one single mystery and are sanctified, as they are all considered as one. This mystery applies to all of them because **the Holy One, Blessed be He**, who is the "link" <note>original: "chulya"; suggesting a segment of a chain or a spinal vertebra, indicating how the Sefirot are interconnected</note>, is the <term>seventh</term> <note>original: "shevi'it"; referring to the Sefirah of Malkhut, the seventh of the lower emanations</note> counted from Him.

At the time when these two workings—the "common" and the "Sabbath"—stand together in one mystery, it is to show that all is one. At the time when this "seventh" is called <term>Sabbath</term>, then everything is called Sabbath. But at the time when this "seventh" is called "common," then everything is called "common." Therefore, it is not called "Sabbath" except at the moment when He dwells upon the Earth; then He is called "Sabbath," and the Earth is called "Sabbath," and all is one. For then the Earth stands in the upper perfection and is blessed by all the upper hosts that dwell upon it. They are all considered within the mystery of the Sabbath, which is the seventh, and therefore the "seventh" is counted from it. But at that time when [the Divine Presence] does not dwell upon the Earth, then it is called "common," and the Holy One, Blessed be He, and all His hosts are cast outside <note>This describes the state of exile, where the Divine Presence is withdrawn and the world feels "common" or disconnected from its source</note>.

<summary>This page explores the mystical relationship between the Jubilee year (Binah) and the Sabbatical year (Malkhut), explaining how the indwelling of the Divine Presence transforms the "common" earth into a state of "Sabbath" and freedom.</summary>
<keywords>Jubilee, Yovel, Sabbath, Shevi'it, Binah, Malkhut, World to Come, Freedom, Holy One Blessed Be He, Common/Profane</keywords>

# Portions of the Law: Behar (Leviticus 25)

## Main Text (Zohar)

This implies that the gathering of all the lower hosts, who come from every place below, desire to dwell upon **the Holy One, Blessed be He**, for He dwells within them and from Him. Yet [at certain times] the external forces are all cast outside, and this state is called <term>common</term> <note>original: "chol"; referring to the "profane" or weekday state where the Divine Presence is not overtly manifest</note>. Regarding this, it is written: "And you shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout the land unto all the inhabitants thereof; it shall be a jubilee unto you; and you shall return every man unto his possession, and you shall return every man unto his family" <note>Leviticus 25:10</note>. This state is the <term>Jubilee</term> <note>original: "Yovel"; kabbalistically associated with the Sefirah of Binah, the "Upper Mother" and the source of ultimate cosmic freedom</note>. Regarding this, it is written: "A jubilee it is; it shall be holy unto you."

And when is it called "Holy"? It is at the moment of the gathering of all the upper hosts, when they come toward Him and "you proclaim liberty" to them, for they all go out into freedom. Because of this, it is said: "you shall return every man unto his possession, and you shall return every man unto his family," for this is the mystery of **the Holy One, Blessed be He** at the time when the upper building is established in its proper arrangements, which is the <term>World to Come</term> <note>original: "Alma de-Atey"; the realm of Binah, characterized by perpetual flow and restoration</note>.

# Genesis

## Main Text (Zohar)

...and it is divided into three...
And all of them are within three names, and these names are all one.
And this light <term>Light (Nehora): In the Zohar, light represents divine energy or emanation</term> which is above, when it shines and brings forth the other lights—those from the right side and those from the left side—it stands in the middle. This is the secret of the three names, and all are as one.

Concerning this, it is written of Him: **with [the letter] He He created them** <note>original: "be-He bera'am"; a wordplay on Genesis 2:4</note>, which is the secret of the Holy Name <note>original: "shma kaddisha"; referring to the Tetragrammaton, the four-letter name of God</note> that takes hold in its levels <note>original: "dargin"; the Sefirot or stages of divine manifestation</note>. From here, they all spread below in the likeness of that which is above; the secret of the Holy Name and those names all connect as one.

And this is the secret of what is written: 
> The face of a lion to the right for the four of them, and the face of an ox from the left for the four of them <note>Ezekiel 1:10; referring to the four "living creatures" in the Prophet Ezekiel's vision of the Divine Chariot</note>
And the face of an eagle and the face of a man; all of them are held in one secret within that light called **He** <note>The fifth letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note>. Concerning this: **with He He created them**, He created the world. Behold, we have said that everything is within one secret. 

And concerning this, it is written: 
> These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created <note>Genesis 2:4</note>
Do not read the word as "when they were created" <note>original: "be-hibbaram"</note>, but rather read it as **with [the letter] He He created them** <note>original: "be-He bera'am"</note>. 

For this reason, the Holy One, Blessed be He, makes Himself known <note>original: "ishtamoda"</note> in all those levels—in order to be known by the children of men. For behold, there is no one who can know Him <note>The Infinite God, the Ein Sof</note> at all, except through those levels and those lights that spread forth from Him. And concerning this: "These are the generations..." etc.

# And He Lived (Vayechi)

## Main Text (Zohar)

...they will summon him. He said to him: these are words of ethical instruction and the ways of [the path of] life to set people straight. For whoever does this has no portion in the <term>World to Come</term> <note>original: "Alma de-Atey"; the spiritual realm of reward or the future state of existence</note>. As we have taught, these seven have no portion in the World to Come: 
*   one who uses his bed <note>a euphemism for marital intimacy</note> by the light of a lamp; 
*   one who uses his bed in the presence of a Torah scroll; 
*   one who speaks words of Torah in a filthy place; 
*   and one who speaks words of Torah <note>Zohar I 130b lists several prohibitions here leading to the loss of the World to Come, emphasizing that physical impurity or disrespect for sacred objects severs one's spiritual connection.</note>

And through all of this, he causes himself to have no portion in the World to Come. Because of this, they shall not rise in the <term>Resurrection</term> <note>original: "Techiyata"; the bodily revival of the dead in the Messianic age</note>, nor shall they merit the life of the World to Come. But all that he learns and says while walking on the way...

The <term>Companions</term> <note>original: "Chavrayya"; the circle of scholars surrounding Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> investigated this verse: whoever labors in the Torah has a portion in the World to Come, because the Torah emerges from the World to Come. Whoever labors in it takes hold of the World to Come and inherits it. Therefore, fortunate is the portion of one who labors in the Torah! He is fortunate in this world and fortunate in the World to Come. 

Come and see: anyone who labors in the Torah, it is as if he labors in the <term>Holy Name</term> <note>original: "Shema Kadisha"; the essential nature of God expressed through the Hebrew alphabet</note>. Therefore, he is one who takes hold of the Holy Name, and whoever takes hold of the Holy Name takes hold of that World to Come, which is truly the Holy Name itself. Come and see that this is so: anyone who labors in the Torah merits the Torah and everything he labored in, for not a single word of the Torah that he spoke or labored in is ever lost from him...

---

->**And the days of Israel drew near to die, and he called his son Joseph** <note>Genesis 47:29</note><-

Come and see: all those days that human beings exist in the world, they are "in his days" <note>referring to a person's lifespan</note>. Yet they are not literally "days" in a physical sense; rather, they are all those days in which a person performed good and merit. Fortunate is he who labors in the Torah and the commandments of the Torah, for all those [meritorious] days are bound within him...

Come and see: "And the days of Israel drew near to die." When those days drew near to approach the <term>Holy King</term> <note>original: "Malka Kadisha"; a reference to the Divine aspect of Tiferet or the Godhead in general</note>, that is the "death" of the righteous. This is not "death" in the literal sense of ceasing to be, but rather the <term>clinging</term> <note>original: "devekut"; a state of mystical union or profound attachment</note> of the soul to the Holy King...

To know and to observe the <term>subtle spark</term><note>original: "zika dakik"; a minute, intense point of divine illumination</note> that shines in one hundred and twenty-seven worlds. Because the supernal light that emerges—all of them shine and are properly <term>arranged</term><note>original: "at-taknu"; referring to the "tikkun" or restoration of divine emanations</note> as one. And because of that which emerges within that spark, it goes out to know and to bestow beneath "Holy, Holy," and they are as one. For this reason, all are within a subtle illumination that performs the restoration for it. 

And in that which is entirely holy, it spreads its light toward all things, and they are all found [within it]. It is visible and yet hidden. And that which emerges within the "all" enters and all are found [there]. And that which emerges within and ascends to the three [higher lights]. And that which enters and comes to shine into a single <term>hidden place</term><note>original: "ganiza"; a treasury or concealed realm</note> and is hidden there. Because the lights that shine and hold... it holds for all the <term>members of the palace</term><note>original: "bnei heichala"; the inner circle of mystics or angelic beings who dwell in the divine presence</note>, and they are all seen entering within, and the light... 

Every hidden light joins as one in it, and there is no one who knows them in that first subtle illumination, regarding what exists within it. And the members of the palace who see and are found, they are all in one, and [the light] holds them all as one within that <term>precious Influence</term><note>original: "mazala yakira"; literally "precious constellation." In the Zohar, this refers to the thirteen "curls" or flows of mercy from the beard of Arich Anpin (the Long-Suffering/Infinite Face), which "trickles" or "flows" (mazal) down to the lower worlds.</note>. And this is called [the balance] between Judgment and Mercy; the "Precious One" in which all are found, in the illumination from above that is internal. And the wise, and the pious, and the <term>most pious</term><note>original: "chasidi chasidi"; the highest grade of the righteous</note> are in the light of the Influence that ascends on high. 

And the hidden Influence takes hold of it for the sake of the "One" within it, so that all are known, yet there is no one who knows. And in the "hands" of the <term>Ancient One</term><note>original: "Atika"; the highest, most ancient manifestation of God (Keter)</note>, He spreads His light below to know and to observe the illumination of <term>loving-kindness</term><note>original: "chasiduta"</note> that emerges from Him toward the Holy King. And every light that ascends above from this Influence, for whom does it stand? It is joined from Him—He joins them and takes hold of it above, and it travels through all those sources from the "Calling of the River" that flows and emerges. 

> "No eye has seen, O God, besides You." <note>Isaiah 64:3; the Hebrew original is "עינא דא לא חזת אלהים זולתך"</note>

And according to the "hour" of the Ancient One, He ascends [and then] below, and for Judgment He descends into it. And the Influence prepares it; He gazes in it below, everything...

<summary>This page describes the "Mazal" (the Divine Influence or Beard of the Ancient One) as a balancing mechanism for the universe, through which subtle sparks of light flow to harmonize Judgment and Mercy. It emphasizes the hidden nature of this light, accessible only to the "members of the palace" and the most pious.</summary>

# Exodus

...for prayer and is restored through all those holy names above. As they have established: all these names of <term>the Holy One, blessed be He</term><note>original: "HaKadosh Baruch Hu"; the standard rabbinic title for God</note> are truly He Himself. The <term>248 limbs</term><note>original: "RAMACH evarim"; traditionally, the human body is said to have 248 limbs, corresponding to the 248 positive biblical commandments</note> in a person correspond to the 248 positive commandments, and the <term>365 sinews</term><note>original: "SHESAH gidin"; corresponding to the 365 days of the solar year and the 365 negative "thou shalt not" commandments</note> correspond to the <term>365 negative commandments</term>. Because of this, any person who does not know how to guard the honor of his Master, and does not know how to be careful and guard that <term>holy name</term><note>original: "shma kadisha"; referring to the divine soul or the human form as a vessel for God's name</note> found within him—woe to him! For it would have been better for him had he never been created, since he blemishes the <term>image of the King</term><note>original: "deyokna d'malka"; the idea that humans are made in the divine image (Imago Dei)</note>. <note>original: "al achat kamma v'kamma"; a logical argument of "how much more so"</note> How much more so does he blemish the glory above.

---

**Rabbi Isaac** opened his discourse and said:
> "And who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth..." <note>2 Samuel 7:23</note> and so on.

Come and see in how many places <term>the Holy One, blessed be He</term> called Israel by this name. To the Holy One, blessed be He, Israel is as it says:
> "Israel, in whom I will be glorified." <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>

And because of this, the <term>Assembly of Israel</term><note>original: "Knesset Yisrael"; the mystical personification of the Jewish people, often identified with the Shekhinah</note> is called "Israel." 
Come and see, it is written:
> "Prepare to meet your God, O Israel." <note>Amos 4:12</note>

What is the meaning of "prepare"? It is as you would say: 
> "And they prepared the offering..." <note>Genesis 43:25</note> and so on.

And this refers to the "restoration" of the <term>Divine Presence</term><note>original: "Shekhinah"; the feminine, immanent aspect of God that dwells among humanity</note>, just as it says: 
> "The place for Your dwelling which You, O Lord, have made." <note>Exodus 15:17</note>

Therefore, whoever approaches before the King must prepare themselves with the proper restorations as is fitting. And concerning this it says: "Prepare to meet your God, O Israel," for "to meet your God" certainly means one must stand ready by preparing oneself.

---

**Rabbi Judah** opened his discourse:
> "And behold, three men stood over him..." <note>Genesis 18:2</note> and so on.

The companions have already established the meaning of this verse. But these "three men" are **Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael**, who are the three angels that the Holy One, blessed be He, sent to the world to carry out His mission.

It also explores the mystical significance of the name "Israel" and the roles of the archangels Michael, Gabriel, and Raphael.</summary>

# Leviticus (Vayikra)

And as they opened their discourse, they rejoiced with a great joy. All those holy perfections and praises were entirely faithful. It is as you said: "**Grace and truth have met; righteousness and peace have kissed.**" <note>Psalms 85:11</note> And here, as they opened the gates of wisdom, <term>Grace</term><note>Chesed: the divine attribute of expansive loving-kindness</note> and <term>Truth</term><note>Emet: often associated with the Sefirah of Tiferet, signifying balance and the reality of the Torah</note> were his portion. For Grace rests upon his hands, and Truth rests in its proper place. He set them down and pushed them upwards, higher and higher, until they reached that <term>drop</term><note>original: "tipah"; a Kabbalistic term for the initial seed of light or the concentrated essence of wisdom (Chokhmah) that initiates creation</note> containing every delight—the summary of all that is <term>hidden and concealed</term><note>original: "ganiz ve-satim"; refers to the most interior, unknowable aspects of the Divine</note>. Everything is bound within the world of that radiant drop.

He opened his discourse and said:
> "**The Lord is righteous in all His ways, and kind in all His deeds.**" <note>Psalms 145:17</note>

Grace and the Kind One rejoice here. He said: "Take your hand to aid, for Grace is within you; the Judge of all the earth comes from the heavens to declare, 'and He is kind in all His deeds.'" In that specific hour, Grace is awakened to return to its beloved ones [...] the thirty days of Grace. My children, <term>Righteousness</term><note>original: "Tzedek"; specifically referring here to the feminine aspect of the Divine (Malchut) descending to connect with the world</note> descends from heaven upon those who are worthy of their name. The "act of Righteousness and Peace" refers to everything performed through the language of Righteousness and Peace; he performs it and seals it toward the side of Grace.

He opened again and said: "And kind in all His deeds." You spoke well regarding the realms above—take your hand, for Grace is in you. Let the <term>Righteous One</term> dwell in the level land, "and kind in all His deeds." However, when the Kind One is in his own embrace, it is written: "**Hear, O Lord, my righteousness, and attend to my cry.**" <note>Psalms 17:1</note> "And kind in all His deeds" refers to a matter they performed and awakened with every lip; "and kind in all His deeds" is found in the letter <term>Mem</term> and the letter <term>Dalet</term><note>Perhaps referring to the word 'Me'od' (very) or names of God; the text is highly symbolic here</note>.

And this is what is written: "and kind in all His deeds." The Righteous One rejoices with a great joy. A sign was given for the sake of the <term>Soul</term> and the <term>Spirit</term><note>original: "Nefesha ve-Rucha"; the lower and middle levels of the human soul which must be purified to experience divine joy</note> which were awakened. But the Kind One in the embrace—as it is written with the letter <term>Vav</term><note>The letter Vav (ו) often symbolizes the "Small Face" (Zeir Anpin) or the attribute of Truth/Beauty that connects heaven and earth</note>—asks for Grace, for everything is awakened toward him. Isaiah spoke through the Holy Spirit and said: "And he laughed as Grace arrived, the work of your hands." For "the Kind One in all His deeds" is good. Take your hand...

You said: "**And all your children shall be taught of the Lord, and great shall be the peace of your children.**" <note>Isaiah 54:13</note> [...] You shall see and behold Righteousness, and your heart shall rejoice. This is because all of Israel are the children of kings, and they are the righteous ones found at that hour.

<summary>This page explores the mystical union of the divine attributes of Grace (Chesed) and Righteousness (Tzedek), explaining how human deeds of peace and prayer awaken these forces to descend into the world. It emphasizes that the righteous of Israel are like "children of kings" who sustain the world through this divine connection.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discourse of the Great Assembly (Idra Rabba) found in the portion of Naso. # Naso - The Great Assembly (Idra Rabba)

## Main Text (Zohar)

...It was found that this is the secret of the male. Everything is contained within one **Balance** <term>Matkla</term><note>The "Balance" or "Scale" is a central concept in the Idra Rabba, representing the equilibrium between the divine attributes of Mercy and Judgment, or Male and Female, which allows the universe to exist without shattering.</note>, male and female together. Because of this, all the divine names that are found cannot exist without the female. Regarding this, it is written:
> **“He created them male and female, and blessed them, and called their name Adam on the day they were created.”** <note>Genesis 5:2</note>

Rabbi Shimon said: "O fathers of the world! Behold, we have learned that before the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>, created the world, it arose in His will to create the world. He carved and measured in all those subtle points, yet stability was not found. He carved and engraved before Him the likeness of a lamp-stand. And behold, the companions have already awakened to this discussion. Come and see what is written:
> **“And these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom, before any king reigned over the children of Israel.”** <note>Genesis 36:31</note>

These are the **Primordial Kings** <note>original: "Melachin Kadma'ei"</note> who were not formed in balance <note>original: "la it-taknu"; referring to the lack of "Tikun" or rectification</note>. Because of this, they could not endure and were destroyed, one after another. This continued until the **Balance** (Matkla) ascended; for the secret of the Balance had not yet been established. Because of this, they did not endure until this **Holy Beard** <term>Dikna Kadisha</term><note>The "Holy Beard" is a macrocosmic metaphor for the thirteen attributes of mercy that flow from the highest level of divinity (Atik Yomin). It represents the structured "channels" through which divine light is tempered and distributed.</note> was manifested and formed. For this reason, those kings were destroyed and nullified—because they were not in a state of balanced formation. And if you should say, "But it is written 'and he died, and he died' <note>referring to the list of Edomite kings in Genesis</note>," we have already established that this "death" refers to a **Nullification** <term>Bittula</term><note>In Kabbalah, "death" for a divine emanation means a descent from its high spiritual level to a lower, less conscious state, rather than total non-existence.</note>—it is certain that they descended from level to level...

<summary>Rabbi Shimon Bar Yochai explains the concept of the "Balance" (Matkla), asserting that the universe can only exist through the union of male and female energies. He interprets the biblical Kings of Edom as failed, primordial worlds that collapsed because they lacked the stabilizing influence of the "Holy Beard," the divine structure of mercy.</summary>

<keywords>Idra Rabba, Balance, Matkla, Kings of Edom, Holy Beard, Dikna Kadisha, Creation, Masculine and Feminine, Nullification, Primordial Worlds</keywords>
