# Bo (Come)

## Main Text (Zohar)

[...] wise men to whom [it is revealed] and we considered those <note>original: Zohar II, 41a</note> [...] that go out from him. [And all those who are] guilty, if they perform repentance, we have established that there [...] where they find life and joy.

**Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse and said:**
> **“And you, do not fear, my servant Jacob, and do not be dismayed, O Israel; for behold, I will save you from afar, and your children from the land of their captivity.”** <note>Jeremiah 30:10</note>

Behold, the companions <term>Chavrayya</term><note>The "Companions" refers to the circle of disciples surrounding Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai.</note> have established this verse as referring to the exile in Babylon and the exile in Edom <note>original: "Edom"; traditionally referring to Rome or the Western world</note>, and everything has been said. But come and see: in the days of the **King Messiah**, it is written:
> **“As in the days of your coming out of the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders.”** <note>Micah 7:15</note>

For He shall redeem Israel with a complete redemption, and afterward, they shall [not] go into exile again. And come and see: at that hour when the King Messiah comes, all the generations that suffered [in Egypt] and in all other times will be awakened to have a partnership in the redemption that comes [...] for it shall be found within them.

And come and see that it is written thus:
> **“And it shall come to pass, when your children say to you, ‘What is this service to you?’”** <note>Exodus 12:26</note>

And all of this is a secret of the word. And come and see what is written regarding that time, [and specifically] on the day of **Passover** <note>original: "Pesach"</note> when miracles were performed.

**Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse and said:**
> **“And it was on the day that Moses finished setting up the Tabernacle.”** <note>Numbers 7:1</note>

The companions established this verse to mean that at the time Moses established the Tabernacle below, the [heavenly] **Tabernacle** <term>Mishkan</term> was established [on high]. And all those holy **Chariots** <term>Rethikin</term><note>The "Chariots" refer to the angelic hosts and divine structures that support the throne of God.</note> and hosts were all established and prepared [...] open your eyes and see what is written: “on the day that Moses finished <note>original: "Kallot"; a wordplay on "Kallah" meaning Bride</note> setting up the Tabernacle,” precisely.

And regarding this, the companions differ, but Rabbi Shimon said [...] as it is written:
> **“On the eighth day he sent the people away, and they blessed the King.”** <note>1 Kings 8:66</note>

[...] the time of the **Redemption** <term>Purkana</term> is mixed with everything, and in it is life and joy [...] and because of this, the companions established that at every time the redemption is stirred...

***

<summary>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai discusses the future redemption of Israel, drawing parallels between the historical Exodus from Egypt and the coming of the Messiah. He explains that the establishment of the earthly Tabernacle by Moses triggered a simultaneous awakening of the divine realms above.</summary>

# Terumah (Contribution)

## Main Text (Zohar)

In this manner, those holy celestial chariots <term>ratichin</term> <note>original: "ratichin"; referring to the angelic structures or "vehicles" that carry the Divine Throne.</note> are those who are sanctified by this holiness below. They wrap themselves in the **wrapping of the commandment** <note>original: "itufa de-mitzvah"; referring to the act of donning the Tallit or prayer shawl.</note> here, just as we have established. And because they are sanctified and wrapped here, then the **soul** is found and prepared in this wrapping, in the same manner as it is above. Regarding this it is written: ->**"Wrapped in light as with a garment..."**<- <note>Psalm 104:2</note>

What is meant by "Wrapped in light"? This is the primordial light which [the Holy One] bestowed; this is the **Secret of Faith** <term>Raza de-Mehemanuta</term> <note>original: "Raza de-Mehemanuta"; a central Zoharic concept referring to the inner mystical structure of the Godhead and the unity of the Sefirot.</note>. Because of this, a person must wrap himself in it, for it is the Secret of Faith. All those who are found within this secret must therefore wrap themselves in this holiness. Then the **Holy One, Blessed be He**, spreads over them the wings of the **Shekhinah** <note>The Shekhinah is the feminine, indwelling aspect of the Divine Presence on earth.</note>, and they are wrapped in them.

Regarding this it is written: ->**"He will cover you with His pinions, and under His wings you shall find refuge."**<- <note>Psalm 91:4</note>

This is the secret of the commandment of the **fringes** <term>Tzitzit</term> <note>original: "Tzitzit"; the ritual fringes attached to the corners of the Tallit as commanded in Numbers 15:38.</note>, for this is the commandment. We have established that it is the Secret of Faith, and all of these things are one single secret. Therefore, those who wrap themselves in those holy wings are those who perform this commandment. Fortunate are those who perform this commandment properly, for it is the secret of the supreme **Holy Name**, which is the <unclear>Secret of Faith</unclear>. <unclear>And everything is on this side.</unclear>
...

<summary>This passage explains the mystical purpose of wearing the Tallit and Tzitzit, asserting that wrapping oneself in the prayer shawl mimics the Divine wrapping Himself in primordial light and grants the wearer the protection of the Shekhinah's wings.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of redemption and divine light. ## Main Text (Zohar)

Amidst many uncertainties they had concerning the matter of extending the basket and the vine-branch, and when the **Hind of Love** <note>original: "Ayalat ha-Ahavah"; a mystical name for the Shekhinah, the feminine aspect of God, specifically in her role as the beloved in the Song of Songs.</note> is purified for the sake of the Holy Place, which is her side, the **husk** <term>Kelipah</term> <note>The "husk" or "shell" represents the forces of evil or impurity that conceal the divine light.</note> will be like a reflection <note>Likely "reflection" or "shadow"</note>—this shall be the joy, just as we have taught you. At that time, Israel will be seen as **men of change** <note>original: "gavrei chalifin"; referring to those who have undergone a spiritual transformation or "exchange" from the state of exile to redemption.</note> in their counsel, and they shall rise to have authority over all the other nations with much **truth** <term>Kushta</term> and action. He said to every single man: And you, holy sons, labor in what I have told you, for it is surely worthy to be said.

And I saw in a prophecy: when a man fears before the God of the **Messiah**, the joy of the **Messiah** shall be seen in the joy of the **garment**; they shall see the joy of redeeming and all the holy words. And so, a cloud-reflection shall be seen to shelter the **Messiah** for all the people of the world, and they shall go out to meet him. I teach you that this is the **Cloud of the Messiah**, a matter of joy and the river of the gate of Names.

The paths of the gates of the **Lord** <note>original: "H'" (the Tetragrammaton); the four-letter name of God, Y-H-V-H.</note> increase, and it is so when they cleave as one in thought with Her <note>Referring to the union with the Shekhinah.</note>. There is nothing more to say regarding the love and the word in the Name; it is perfection in joy. When the river shines, as it is said, the holiness of the **King** waters [the world] by means of the light of holiness. Then the **King** and the elite enter into joy and the everyday; and to Israel they give a portion and kindness in the Kingdom. Then there shall be strength for the Holy House.

And you, sit in the understanding that our peace, which was removed, is assisted in the world from the time of the light; and the world shall be called "joyful" so that the world may be sustained in joy. Then he said to him: This is the command, the sign, and the vessel. The command of the call is in the flash of lightning within it—the number eight <note>The number eight often symbolizes the realm beyond the natural order (seven days of creation), associated with the era of the Messiah.</note>—concerning **Benjamin**, for he is the time of **redemption** <term>Purkana</term> <note>Benjamin is often associated in Kabbalah with the site of the Holy Temple and the bridge between the upper and lower worlds.</note>.

From here on, for all the guilty, they shall not pass from here on. The portion goes to the appointed **King** and the line of the **King**, which is in the great light that emerges from within the Supernal Holiness that is within him. In life and in the World to Come, in pleasant joy, it goes out to rest the **Shekhinah** <note>The Divine Presence.</note>.

***

<meta>This page transitions from the fragmented mystical opening of Folio 133 to a focused discourse on the theology of the Sanctuary (Mishkan). While the previous folio's text was obscured by damage and dealt with the "mystery of faith," this section provides a clear Zoharic commentary on the commandment in Exodus 25 to build a home for God, emphasizing that the "Sanctuary" is not merely a building but a manifestation of the Divine Presence among the people.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

What is the meaning of that which is written <note>Jeremiah 17:12</note>: **"A glorious throne, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary."** Come and see: The **Sanctuary** <term>Mikdash; the holy site or Temple</term> is the **Divine Presence** <term>Shekhinah; the indwelling, feminine aspect of the Divine</term>. This is because the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "Kudsha Berikh Hu"</note> is Himself the Sanctuary. And for this reason, the sanctuary was made below in the likeness of that which is above.

**"And let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them"** <note>Exodus 25:8</note>. What is the meaning of the phrase **"among them"**? One would expect the text to say **"within it"** <note>meaning within the physical building itself</note>. However, we have learned: The Holy One, Blessed be He, is holy, and all His people are a **holy people** <note>original: "amma kadisha"</note>, as it is stated <note>Jeremiah 2:3</note>: **"Israel is holy to the Lord."**

For this reason, the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to dwell among them. He commanded them to make for Him a sanctuary. At the time when the sanctuary stands below, the Divine Presence rests upon it. And when the Divine Presence rests upon it, then this sanctuary below exists in the likeness of the sanctuary above. Through this sanctuary, all the people of Israel are sanctified. This is the reason for the phrasing **"and I will dwell among them,"** as we have said.

Come and see: It is in this same manner that the verse states <note>Leviticus 26:11</note>: **"I will set My tabernacle among you, and My soul shall not abhor you."** Even though the Sanctuary was destroyed, the Divine Presence has never moved from the **Western Wall** <note>original: "Kotel HaMa'aravi"</note>. In every single place where Israel was exiled, the Divine Presence went with them.

What then is the meaning of **"and I will dwell among them"**? It refers even to the time when they are in exile among the nations; if they are holy, they create a dwelling place for Her among them. 

Come and see: It is written, **"And let them make Me a sanctuary."** The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "Make for Me." Does the Holy One, Blessed be He, truly desire a sanctuary made by a **human being** <note>original: "bar nash"</note>? Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: "Make for Me"—as in, make for Me a portion. For in every place where you find holiness, I, the Divine Presence, am there. This is the same as that which is written <note>Exodus 20:21</note>: **"In every place where I cause My name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you."**

And we have learned: Wherever there are **ten** <note>original: "bi asara"; referring to a minyan, the quorum of ten required for communal prayer</note>, the Divine Presence rests among them. In every place where people offer **prayer and supplication** <note>original: "tzelota u-ba'uta"</note> before the Holy King, the Divine Presence rests there.

Come and see: Three times a day, the Divine Presence is filled with blessings from above, and from these blessings, she gives to Israel. Every time they perform proper deeds, then a holy sanctuary is made for them <unclear>to know</unclear>...

<summary>This page explains that the biblical commandment to build a Sanctuary (Mishkan) was intended to establish a dwelling for the Shekhinah (Divine Presence) among the people of Israel. It emphasizes that this Presence remains with the Jewish people through their holiness and prayer, even after the physical Temple's destruction and throughout their exile.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the mystical exploration of the Sanctuary and divine service, moving from the physical architecture of the Tabernacle discussed in the previous folio to the spiritual internal state required for atonement. While the previous page examined the "fear of God" and the celestial mirrors of the Temple, this page (folio 67a) focuses specifically on the mechanics of repentance and the sanctity of the Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur), interpreting the biblical verse from Leviticus 16:30.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

... <note>Leviticus 16:30</note> **We have learned: "For on this day He will atone for you to cleanse you from all your sins; before the Lord shall you be clean."**
This verse is difficult. For it is written, "For on this day He will atone for you," and afterwards, "to cleanse you," and afterwards, "before the Lord shall you be clean." What is this dealing with?
Rather, "On this day"—this verse, as we have established, means that the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "Kudsha Berikh Hu"</note> prepares and readies [the opportunity] for each and every person to mend [himself] by His hand.
And the verse says this because it is found that the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <term>Kudsha Berikh Hu; the standard Zoharic name for God</term> is ready for each and every person; and when a person <term>bar nash; literally "son of man," referring to a human being</term> is more worthy, what does it say? "To cleanse you."
And so we have learned: A person who sanctifies himself a little, they sanctify him much from above; and if he merits more, they sanctify him even further.
And we have established that when a person awakens [the desire for] the **Holy One, Blessed be He** from below <note>referring to the earthly, human realm</note>, they awaken Him from above <note>referring to the divine, celestial realm</note>.
And thus, the **Holy One, Blessed be He** is found ready before him to perform His commandments.
And here it is in this manner: "For on this day He will atone for you" to mend his debts <note>original: "chovoi"; referring to sins as spiritual debts</note>.
And when a person comes before the **Holy One, Blessed be He** and is found before Him to have returned in complete **repentance** <term>teshuvah; literally "returning" to God's path</term>, then [it is said], "to cleanse you."
And who cleanses him? The **Holy One, Blessed be He**, who is ready before him.
And for this reason, "before the Lord shall you be clean."
And this is on the day when atonement is found, for all his debts the **Holy One, Blessed be He** atones for them.
And then the person is purified before Him.
And if you say [it means] "from all your sins"—behold, we have learned that for sins between a man and his fellow, the Day of Atonement <note>Yom Kippur</note> does not atone until he appeases his fellow.
[Yet] here it says "from *all* your sins."
Rather, these are the sins that we have established as being from the "upper side" <note>referring to spiritual transgressions directly against the Divine</note>.
And concerning this, it says "from all your sins" that are between you and the **Holy One, Blessed be He**.
And for this reason, "before the Lord shall you be clean."
On this day, the **Holy One, Blessed be He** removes all his debts and purifies the person.
And then the person stands before the **Holy One, Blessed be He** innocent of all his sins.
And come and see <note>original: "ta chazi"; a common Zoharic formula introducing a deeper insight</note>: "On this day"—this refers to the supernal day ...

<summary>This page provides a mystical commentary on Leviticus 16:30, explaining how the process of atonement on Yom Kippur requires a human awakening from "below" to trigger a divine response from "above." It clarifies that while the Holy One atones for spiritual sins against God, transgressions against other people require personal reconciliation first.</summary>

## Vayeshev (Zohar I, 204b)

[...] went out in her, and at first He acted with a voice, and your sign is <note>Psalms 29:3</note> **"The voice of the Lord is over the waters."**
[...] for the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "Kudsha Berikh Hu"</note> called the light day and the darkness He called night. Certainly, at the time He was acting—

And Rabbi Eleazar said: These verses, as we have learned, contain supreme secrets <term>razin ila'in; hidden mystical truths</term>, and one must contemplate them.
And if you say, why is he called "with him" <note>referring to the Hebrew word "immo"</note>? Rather, it is because he is called Peace <note>original: "Shalom"</note>, just as it is said:
<note>Exodus 18:23</note> **"He shall go to his place in peace."** And "with him" is the secret of Peace, and it is all one thing, and for this reason he is called "with him."

Rabbi Abba said: And when is he called "with him"? At the time when the **Holy One, Blessed be He** comes and completes him, as it were <note>Aramaic: "kivyakhol"; a term used in Jewish thought to signify that we are using human language for God that isn't literally true of the Infinite</note>.
As we have learned, what is the meaning of that which is written: <note>Proverbs 16:7</note> **"When a man's ways please the Lord, He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him."**
What is the meaning of "with him" <note>Hebrew: "itto"</note>? As it were, literally *with Him*, for the **Holy One, Blessed be He** makes peace for him. And what does "makes peace for him" mean? It means He completes him toward Himself, so that all becomes one.
For we have learned: when is he called "Man" <note>Hebrew: "Ish"</note>? At the time when the **Holy One, Blessed be He** completes him from that which he was lacking.

And Rabbi Eleazar said: Come and see, these verses that we have mentioned all go together as one.
Come and see <term>ta chazi; the Zohar's standard invitation to a deeper mystical insight</term>, it is written: <note>Genesis 1:4</note> **"And God saw the light, that it was good."**
What is the meaning of "that it was good"? It is that the **Holy One, Blessed be He** completed it and illuminated it. And if you say this verse did not exist at that time—
Rather, this is the secret of what is written: <note>Exodus 33:19</note> **"I will make all My goodness pass before you."**
And this is the "good" of which it is written, **"And God saw the light, that it was good."** Because at that time when the light was made, the light went forth in goodness, which is when it was completed <note>The Zohar often links the word "Good" (Tov) with "Completeness" (Shalem)</note>.

And come and see, it is written: <note>Psalms 145:9</note> **"The Lord is good to all, and His mercies are over all His works."**
What is "to all"? Truly "to all," to those who come from the side above <note>original: "mi-sitra de-le'eila"; the divine realm</note>. And what are they? These verses we have mentioned are all beautiful.
What is "to all"? To all those who come from the side of Peace <note>original: "mi-sitra de-shalom"</note>. As it is written: <note>Isaiah 57:19</note> **"Peace, peace, to him who is far off and to him who is near."**

<summary>This page explores the mystical connection between "Goodness," "Peace," and "Completeness," arguing that God's presence "completes" a person and the primordial light.</summary>
<keywords>Peace (Shalom), Completeness (Shalmu), Divine Light, Goodness (Tov), Rabbi Eleazar, Rabbi Abba, primordial light, mystical union</keywords>

# Leviticus

## Main Text (Zohar)

For it is ready to receive him. As the companions have taught, so it is certainly true: whoever engages in the Torah for its own sake merits the Torah and merits everything. More than anything, the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, considered the feminine aspect of God that dwells among humanity</note> is found with him. And this is the <term>mystery</term> <note>original: "raza"; a secret or inner spiritual meaning</note> of what is written <note>Isaiah 43:7</note> **"Everyone who is called by My name, and whom I have created for My glory, I have formed him, yes, I have made him."** One who is "by My name" is certainly "for My glory I have created him," and so on, as we have said. And all things are established in a single rectification. Regarding this it is written <note>Exodus 20:24</note> **"In every place where I cause My name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you."**

What does "I will come to you" mean? This is the <term>Shekhinah</term> that comes, "and I will bless you." This is the mystery: when the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"; the standard Zoharic name for the divine masculine aspect</note> appears before a person, He first blesses him. And here, for the sake of the glory of the Holy One, Blessed be He, they perform this <term>repentance</term> <note>original: "teshuvah"; literally 'returning' to God</note> and perform the <term>sacrifice</term> <note>original: "korban"; literally 'that which brings close'</note>; certainly the Shekhinah comes to be there. Regarding this it is written <note>Leviticus 1:2</note> **"When any man of you brings an offering to the Lord..."**

The text specifies **"of you"** because repentance depends upon the person, and the sacrifice exists only for his sake. For the human being is the essence of all, and because of him, the sacrifice is found in the upper and lower worlds. This is the mystery of: "When a man brings an offering **of you** to the Lord"—specifically "of you," because sin is only found within the human being. Therefore, a sacrifice is required to maintain existence. There is the sacrifice of the "sin-offering" and the sacrifice of the "burnt-offering"; all sacrifices come because of the debt of a person. 

Regarding this it is written, "When a man brings an offering of you to the Lord," specifically "of you." Furthermore, one must awaken this secret: that the sacrifice is called "to the Lord" and not to any other spiritual degree, so that the Holy Name may be unified and all may be blessed. Regarding this it is written <note>Leviticus 1:9</note> **"A fire-offering of pleasing aroma to the Lord."** This is the mystery of all things: when the <term>male and female</term> <note>The Zoharic concept of the union of the masculine and feminine aspects of the Divine (Tiferet and Malkhut)</note> draw near as one, then it is called a "complete sacrifice." 

Because of this, a person must first bring himself near through complete repentance, and only afterwards bring the sacrifice. This sacrifice is the mystery of the "awakening" of the upper and lower worlds as one. Regarding this it is written <note>Psalms 51:19</note> **"The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise."** This is the mystery of the sacrifice, for all things are established in a single rectification. Regarding this the companions have awakened the secret of the sacrifice, which is complete in everything. And here we have learned the secret of "Man," for all sacrifices...

<summary>This page explains that the true purpose of the biblical sacrifices is to facilitate the union of the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) with the Holy One. It emphasizes that a physical offering is ineffective without the internal "awakening" of human repentance (Teshuvah).</summary>
<keywords>Shekhinah, Korban (Sacrifice), Teshuvah (Repentance), Divine Union, Leviticus, Isaiah, Psalms, Male and Female aspects</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Deep and supreme, well-prepared from the beginning—as we have learned, come and see: at the time when the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"; the primary masculine name for God in the Zohar</note> desires to create a human being, He fashions for him a **supreme form** <note>original: "tzura ila'ah"</note> and hides it away. At that same time when the soul <term>Nishmata: the highest level of the human soul</term> descends below, He hides that form behind every person. At this time, when the soul arrives to enter into this world, [the form] draws near and emerges, and because of that form, the person is seen upon the world. 

And regarding this, it is written: > This was their appearance, they had the likeness of a human < <note>Ezekiel 1:5</note>. Yet, a person has no permission to gaze upon that appearance [directly] as it truly is. And it is because of that divine image <term>Tzelem: the spiritual blueprint of the human body</term> that it is written: > Surely as a mere image does a man walk about < <note>Psalms 39:7</note>. 

From their visions: at that time when the soul descends to the world, it has no existence or standing upon the earth except by means of that **garment** <note>original: "levusha"; a celestial "suit" that protects the soul from the harshness of the physical world</note> which He prepared for it. Within this garment, it exists in this world. 

Because of this, when King Solomon desired to build the Holy Temple, he observed that the holy soul stands below through this very existence, and regarding this, he called out and said "his garment is like..." <note>original: "levushieh dmich"; possibly a variant referencing a celestial texture</note>. This is the secret that she [the Divine] gives to the upper and lower realms by means of the name of the holy **Matronita** <term>Matronita: A title for the Shekhinah, the Divine Mother or Queen</term>. Wherever those garments are spread out and that garment goes with them, worthy are the righteous who are clothed in that same garment! 

What is written? "And this was done..." <note>The text here is slightly fragmented in the manuscript</note>. This has nothing to do with the time when human beings walk and are crowned with the holy **Shekhinah** <term>Divine Presence: the feminine indwelling of God</term>. From this, it is written: > A Psalm of Thanksgiving < <note>Psalms 100:1</note>. And a woman in the matter of the Lord, and afterward they are revealed in that weaving <term>arguna: the complex structure of the human organism</term> which is called the "body." At that time, the soul descends into the garment of the physical body. Because of this, it is written: > And all the princes of Pharaoh saw her < <note>Genesis 12:15</note>—they "saw" because they perceived that garment and that form upon her which was called for.

**Rabbi Eleazar** opened his discourse and said: > The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes, leaping over the mountains < <note>Song of Songs 2:8</note>, etc. This refers to the Song of Songs, which is the song of all songs, both above and below.

# Beha'alotcha

## Main Text (Zohar)

Rather, when He reveals Himself to them, as it is revealed to him. As it says <note>Numbers 12:8</note> **"And he beholds the likeness of the LORD."** "The likeness of the LORD"—this is <term>Malkhut</term> <note>Kingship; the tenth and final divine emanation (Sefirah), representing the manifestation of God’s sovereignty in the world</note>. And the secret of the matter is: **"Sin crouches at the entrance"** <note>Genesis 4:7</note>, just as it says <note>Job 28:7</note> **"A path no bird of prey has known"** <note>original: "lo yade’ah"; the scribe mistakenly wrote "lo asah" (has not made), a common error or variant in manuscript versions</note>.

And they opened for them an entrance without a veil. And it has been stated: **"And he beholds the likeness of the LORD."** "The likeness of the LORD"—this is the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note>. In this way, Moses, at his own [prophetic] level, knew that she was this [likeness], which was not the case for other prophets. And so we have learned: anyone who sees a likeness or any form in a dream, and gazes upon it well, knows that it is only from her side <note>meaning, from the lower realm of the Shekhinah</note>. 

And therefore, **"And he beholds the likeness of the LORD,"** because Moses, at his level, knew [her] well, because he was **"face to face"** <note>Deuteronomy 34:10</note>. And it was taught that Rabbi Yose said: A person should distance himself from three things: his own should not [truly] be his own, and he should not draw near to the entrance of that gate, for there sin dwells, as it is written: **"Sin crouches at the entrance."** 

And if you say: But Moses was at his [high] level, why then is it written of him: **"And he beholds the likeness of the LORD"**? Rather, because Moses was at his level, he knew well the entrance and the secret of the "likeness of the LORD." For behold, the Shekhinah is called "the likeness of the LORD," as it is written: **"And he beholds the likeness of the LORD."** 

And it was taught that Rabbi Isaac said: This word is fitting. Rabbi Judah said: Whoever gazes into this verse knows the secret of the matter, according to what Rabbi Eleazar said regarding the secret of the "likeness of the LORD." It is like a mirror: one who looks into a mirror sees all the <term>images</term> <note>original: "dioknin"; from the Greek 'eikon,' referring to the spiritual forms or blueprints of all things</note> that look into it, while the mirror itself stands at its own level. 

**"And he beholds the likeness of the LORD,"** because Moses saw all the supernal images, all of them within the **"Luminous Mirror"** <note>original: "Aspaklaria ha-Me'irah"; a technical term for the highest degree of prophecy, characterized by total clarity without the distortion of the physical senses</note>. And what is this mirror? It is the Shekhinah, who is called the "likeness of the LORD."

<summary>This page explains that the "Likeness of the Lord" seen by Moses was the Shekhinah, which acted as a clear mirror reflecting all higher divine forms. It contrasts Moses's direct, "face to face" understanding of this divine gateway with the less clear visions of other prophets.</summary>
<keywords>Moses, Shekhinah, Likeness of the Lord (Temunat Hashem), Prophecy, Luminous Mirror (Aspaklaria), Malkhut, Rabbi Yose, Rabbi Isaac</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the exposition of the Creation narrative. While the previous page (folio 30a) concluded a discussion on the spiritual garments of the soul and the prophetic vision of Moses, this section returns to the second day of Genesis. It explores why the phrase "it was good" is missing from the second day, linking it to the emergence of the "Left Side" and the cosmic origins of conflict and Gehinnom. # Genesis

## Main Text (Zohar)

[...lower waters and upper waters...]
[...in conflict, and regarding this there is conflict...]
<term>that issues from the Left Side</term> <note>Sitra de-Smala; in Kabbalah, the "Left Side" represents the attribute of Gevurah—judgment, restriction, and the potential source of harshness or evil</note> and its strength and all [its branches].
For this reason, it is not written of the second day **"that it was good"** <note>Genesis 1:8; unlike other days of Creation, the Torah omits "and God saw that it was good" on the second day</note>, because it is the <term>Left Side</term> [that was awakened].
And upon this, when the Left is awakened, conflict is awakened [which is this];
and this conflict is <term>Gehinnom</term> <note>A realm of spiritual purification or "hell," here described as the metaphysical result of separation and discord</note>, which was ignited in that conflict [on this side].
And all those who emerge from that conflict endure forever [and for all eternity].
<term>Rabbi Shimon</term> <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the legendary 2nd-century sage to whom the Zohar is traditionally attributed</note> opened and said:
> **"And he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water, etc."** <note>Psalm 1:3</note>

This verse,
the companions have established it; but **"And he shall be like a tree planted"**—this refers to the <term>Tree</term> <note>Ilana; the Sefirotic Tree of Life, the blueprint of the divine emanations</note>
which the <term>Holy One, Blessed Be He</term> <note>Kudsha Brich Hu; the standard Rabbinic name for God</note> planted during the <term>six days of Creation</term>, and this is what is said regarding it:
"and its source is from a place that is life forever," and that is <term>Eden</term> <note>In this context, Eden refers to the higher divine source, often identified with the Sefirah of Binah (Understanding)</note>.
What are the **"streams of water"**? These are the divisions that separate from it, from that
river that flows out of Eden, as it is said:
> **"And from there it shall part and become four heads"** <note>Genesis 2:10</note>.

These are the streams of water.
**"Which gives its fruit in its season"**—this refers to the <term>Righteous One</term> <note>Tzadik; the Sefirah of Yesod (Foundation), which acts as a channel or "procreator" for divine energy</note> who sends forth his fruit,
which are the souls of human beings that all proceed in their proper time.
**"And its leaf shall not wither"**—these are all the other hosts under
the hand of this <term>Righteous One</term>, all of whom shall never wither.
**"And in all that he does, he shall prosper"**—this is because everything depends upon him;
this is as it is written:
> **"And all my desires cannot compare to her"** <note>Proverbs 3:15; the Zohar links "desires" (chafatzai) to the divine emanations or spiritual objects that find their fulfillment in the Tree of Life</note>.

<summary>This page explains that the absence of "it was good" on the second day of Creation is due to the emergence of the "Left Side" and conflict, which birthed Gehinnom. It then interprets Psalm 1:3 as a metaphor for the Sefirotic Tree of Life, where the "Righteous One" (Yesod) produces souls as fruit.</summary>

<meta>This page transitions from the narrative commentary of the Zohar on the days of Creation (found on the previous page) into a practical manual for mystical meditations, known as "Kavanot" or "Yichudim." While the previous page focused on the origins of conflict and the "Left Side," this page explores the process of "Unification" (Yichud), explaining how a practitioner can bind their soul to the Divine through the Ten Utterances of creation and the Four Worlds of existence. It is written in a typical Sephardic-Italian rabbinic script of the early modern period.</meta>

## Main Text (Kabbalistic Treatise)

The general unification, the specific unification, and the minor unification hint at the **Ten Utterances** <term>Ten Utterances; the ten commands in Genesis through which the world was created</term> which are the root of the unification of the upper and lower realms. Through these, one may cause their vital soul, spirit, and breath of life to cleave to their Creator. One raises their prayer through the unification of these two <note>original: "bi" = two</note> aspects—that is, the unification of the levels of the soul—drawing from the **Ten Utterances** with which the world was created. These correspond to the **Ten Holy Creatures** <note>Chayot Kodesh; the angelic beings seen in Ezekiel's vision of the Divine Chariot</note> and all created beings from the heavens to the earth. Through this, the practitioner awakens these forces over us alone, through the unification of the King, blessed be His Name. Therefore, the sages hinted to us in the prayer's repetition the ten Names which are the secret of the **Ten Sefirot of the World of Emanation** <term>Sefirot of Atzilut; the ten divine attributes or channels in the highest spiritual realm</term> which shine and radiate within the human soul. With these ten Names, the **Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Presence** <term>Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shekhinah; the masculine and feminine aspects of the Divine</term> are unified. From this union, the power of divine flow from above descends below.

In this Name, everything is unified, and this is what is written: that we are all in "one spirit," so long as all things are unified. This Name also hints at the **Thirteen Attributes of Mercy** <term>13 Attributes of Mercy; the divine qualities of compassion revealed to Moses at Sinai</term> which are awakened over us through this supernal unification. Thus, the lower world is unified with the vital soul, the spirit, the breath of life, and the **Holy Spirit** <term>Ruach HaKodesh; divine inspiration or prophetic spirit</term>. These correspond to the **Four Worlds** <term>ABY"A; an acronym for the four levels of existence: Atzilut (Emanation), Beriah (Creation), Yetzirah (Formation), and Asiyah (Action)</term>, which correspond to the four letters of the **Essential Name, Blessed be He** <term>Havayah; the Tetragrammaton, the four-letter Name of God Y-H-V-H</term>, and correspond to the **Ten Utterances**. And behold, they further hinted to us in this unification that through proper intention, the **Holy Spirit** dwells upon a person. This is the secret we speak of: that His Name awakens the "Attribute of Judgment" to be nullified and to transform everything into "Mercy." Then, when Mercy is awakened above, blessing and abundance will increase in all of the person's limbs and veins, and all parts of the soul will be joined in a single unification.

It correlates the human soul, the four spiritual worlds, and the Tetragrammaton as a unified system for transforming divine judgment into compassion.</summary>

<meta>This folio continues the discourse from Parashat Noah. It connects the biblical figure of Noah and his Ark to the mystical "Tree of Life" and the Sabbath. ## Main Text (Zohar)

Truly a tree, and this is the secret of the **Tree of Life** <note>original: "Etz ha-Chayim"; the divine structure of reality that provides spiritual nourishment</note> in which life is found and through which it is completed, and it is a holy sign. And it is certainly **Noah’s Ark** <note>original: "Teivata de-Noah"</note> in which Noah was hidden; upon it, every living thing depends. As we have stated, it is the secret of the **Covenant** <note>original: "Berit"; referring to the Sefirah of Yesod, the masculine generative principle</note> and it is the secret of the Sabbath. 

This is the secret of the Sabbath, for through it the **Holy Sabbath** is crowned; for every soul emerges from the secret of Noah. Even though this secret is far, far above, as we have said, the Holy Sabbath above is crowned by it, and all the secrets of the Sabbath depend upon it. 

And even though we say that the Holy Sabbath is the secret of the <gloss>Assembly of Israel</gloss> <note>original: "Keneset Yisrael"; a name for the Shekhinah, the feminine presence of God</note>, she is certainly the "Sabbath"—but "Sabbath" without "Holiness" <note>In the Zohar's gendered symbolism, the feminine Sabbath (Malkhut) receives its "Holiness" from the masculine Sabbath (Yesod/Noah)</note>. For we have said that she is certainly the Sabbath, and upon him [the Tzaddik] the Sabbath above depends. Is it then Holy Sabbath upon Holy Sabbath? Certainly, for below, the Sabbath is crowned with holiness, since all holiness and blessing depend upon him [the Tzaddik]. 

And through him it <gloss>is filled</gloss>, for within him dwell Sabbath, life, holiness, and blessing, emerging from the inner depths which are the **springs of the world**. And this is the secret of Noah, who is the **Righteous One** <term>Tzaddik; a title for Noah and the Sefirah of Yesod, serving as the channel for divine light</term> and the secret of the Sabbath. For behold, it is written:
> **Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy** <note>Exodus 20:8</note>
And it is written, "Remember," <gloss>and so on</gloss>. Is not this "Remembering" the **Righteous One**? "Remember" and "Sabbath" are all one, and upon him depends the secret of the Sabbath. 

Aside from this, the Sabbath is mentioned plainly. Because of this, we begin to bless the Sabbath day starting from the <note>original: "yoma de-revi'ah"</note> fourth day [Wednesday]. Even though the whole world changes from the days of work to the Sabbath, this is the secret: every blessing emerges from him. This is the secret of the **Life of Lives** <gloss>of life</gloss> of all worlds and all blessings. 

By this secret of the Sabbath, we say that the Sabbath is the **table** of all sustenance for every single day. For from him it emerges; the Sabbath is the table of your Master. Therefore, even though we say that the other days are blessed from it, the Sabbath is the root.

And it is one perfect name for all, and because of this it possesses many names that are explained according to every side and direction. All of them are held within it, and all are one. This is the name that is called the <term>Holy Throne</term>.

<meta>Continuing from the previous fragmentary page which discussed the Divine Name and sovereignty, this page transitions to a discourse on Parashat Noach (Genesis). Specifically, it explores the esoteric meaning of the rainbow as a bridge between the earthly and divine realms, and its connection to the Covenant.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

And the **rainbow** <note>original: "Qeshet"; in Jewish mysticism, the rainbow represents a visual manifestation of the Divine Presence.</note> at that time appears with its colors shining as is proper, and this awakens Him. Concerning this it is written: *And I will see it, to remember the everlasting covenant* <note>Genesis 9:16</note>. And this is that rainbow that the **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "Kudsha Berikh Hu"; the standard Aramaic reference to the transcendent aspect of God.</note> carries constantly. And if you say that the rainbow is certainly called "covenant," as it is written: *I have set My bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a sign of a covenant* <note>Genesis 9:13</note>, then this covenant is the **Shekhinah** <note>original: "Shekhintah"; the Divine Presence or the feminine aspect of God</note>, for she is the covenant.

This is the **mystery** <note>original: "raza"; refers to an esoteric or hidden spiritual truth</note> of the rainbow that stands above all other bows. Every rainbow below is a reflection of the one above. Because of this, through this rainbow—which is the Shekhinah—He remembers the "everlasting covenant." This is the actual everlasting covenant. The mystery of the covenant that sustains the world is the **Righteous One** <note>original: "Tzaddik"; referring to the Sefirah of Yesod (Foundation), the channel of divine energy</note>, as it is written: *And the righteous is an everlasting foundation* <note>Proverbs 10:25</note>.

And this is the covenant, and the mystery of this rainbow stands upon this foundation in order to shine from within that rainbow above, which is the Shekhinah, who is the covenant and stands upon the covenant. This is the mystery of what is written: *And I will see it, to remember the everlasting covenant*. This is certainly the everlasting covenant. Through this covenant, the Holy One, Blessed be He, looks and remembers the world.

And come and see: whenever this rainbow appears in the world, the Holy One, Blessed be He, remembers His covenant, which is the everlasting covenant. And should you say that if there were no rainbow, He would not remember—Heaven forbid! Rather, it is as it is written: *And I will see it, to remember the everlasting covenant*. For at that time when the rainbow appears, the **colors** <note>original: "govanin"; these symbolize the different Sefirot (divine emanations) which must be in balance.</note> above are awakened and it appears before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and He remembers His covenant.

And come and see that the mystery of this rainbow is the covenant that sustains the whole world. And when does He remember this covenant? When the rainbow appears in the world properly and with shining colors. When this appears, the colors above are seen, and He remembers the everlasting covenant <unclear>all of them</unclear>...

<meta>This page transitions from a previous discussion of the rainbow and the Divine Presence (Shekhinah) into the "Section of the Letters" from the Zohar’s Prologue. There is a thematic jump here from the specific imagery of the rainbow to the primordial creation of the universe through the Hebrew alphabet. I have noted that the previous page discussed the covenant of the rainbow, while this page begins the famous narrative of the letters pleading their case to be the instrument of creation.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

[...] that anyone who derives benefit from it [...]
[...] and the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world [...]

When the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to create the world, all the **letters** <note>original: "otiyyon"; in Kabbalistic thought, the Hebrew alphabet consists of the spiritual building blocks of all reality.</note> were **engraved** <note>original: "gelifin"; suggesting they were carved into the divine light or essence.</note> before Him for two thousand years before the world was created, and He delighted in them. And when He desired to create the world, all the letters came before Him in reverse order, from the last to the first. 

First, the letter **Tav** <note>The 22nd and final letter of the Hebrew alphabet.</note> came and spoke before Him: "Master of the Worlds, may it please You to create the world through me, for I am the seal of Your **signet ring** <note>original: "gushpanka"; a term for an official seal used to validate a King's decree.</note>, which is **Truth** <note>original: "emmet"; the word for truth in Hebrew consists of the first, middle, and last letters of the alphabet—Aleph, Mem, and Tav.</note>. And You are called Truth, and it is fitting for the King to begin with Truth and to create the world through me." 

The **Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "Kudsha Berikh Hu"; the standard Aramaic reference to the Creator.</note> said to her: "You are worthy and you are beautiful, but it is not fitting to create the world through you, because you are destined to be a mark upon the foreheads of the faithful who fulfill the **Torah** <note>original: "Oraita"; the Divine Law.</note> from Aleph to Tav, and through you they shall die. Furthermore, you are the seal of death <note>The Hebrew word for death, "mavet," ends with the letter Tav; the Zohar references a tradition where the letter Tav was marked on the righteous to protect them, or on the wicked to signify death.</note>. Because you are such, it is not fitting to create the world through you." Immediately, she departed from His presence.

The letter **Shin** <note>The 21st letter of the alphabet.</note> entered; she said before Him: "Master of the Worlds, may it please You to create the world through me, for in me Your Name **Shaddai** <note>One of the biblical names of God, often associated with divine protection and boundaries.</note> is called, and it would be fitting to create the world through a Holy Name." 

He said to her: "You are worthy, you are beautiful, and you are true. But since the letters of **falsehood** <note>original: "shiqra"; referring specifically to the letters Kof and Resh.</note> take you to be with them, I do not wish to create the world through you. For **falsehood** <note>original: "sheqer"; the Hebrew word for a lie.</note> is not seen to stand unless the Shin enters at their head. Because anyone who wishes to tell a lie first takes a foundation of truth and then brings the lie upon it. For the Shin is a letter of truth—the letter of the truth of the Patriarchs <note>The three branches of the letter Shin (ש) are often interpreted as representing Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.</note> who are found within it. But **Kof** and **Resh** are letters found on the **evil side** <note>original: "sitra bisha"; the "other side" or the realm of spiritual impurity.</note>, and in order to stand, they take the Shin and 'falsehood' is made." Once she saw this, she departed from His presence.

<summary>This page describes the primordial letters of the Hebrew alphabet appearing before God to request that the world be created through them, specifically detailing why the letters Tav and Shin were rejected.</summary>
<keywords>Creation, Hebrew Alphabet, Truth (Emmet), Falsehood (Sheqer), Signet Ring, Shaddai, Holy One Blessed be He, Patriarchs, Sitra Achra</keywords>

## Main Text (Zohar)

...and the spirit of all this travels and connects into one, and this is it. In this are found the Names above and below, within the supreme Name called <term>El</term> <note>original: "El"; a primary Hebrew name for God. In Kabbalah, this name is specifically associated with the Sefirah of Chesed (Lovingkindness) and the expansion of divine light.</note>. Because of this, He is called "El, the All in all." All the treasures and springs of longing are so named when the radiance of each one is found, for the radiance of all the garments are bound as one. The spirit is found within them, whereas the radiance of all other lights does not contain the spirit, because this [light] is the most hidden of all hidden things.

It is the light of all lights. When this shines, it is called "Light," and from it all others shine—one within another, and one within another. Upon it depends the **will** <note>original: "re'uta"; refers to the divine desire or intentionality that sustains existence.</note> of all things, and all are attached in a single will. This is because this is the holy light of all; for the **Holy Spirit** <note>original: "Ruach Ha-Kodesh"</note> is found only in a place that is holy light, and this is called the "Love of all."

Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse and said: Regarding the entrance of the Tabernacle, as it is written: 
> Moreover you shall make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twisted linen, and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; with cherubim, the work of a skilled workman, you shall make them. <note>Exodus 26:1</note>
Come and see: In the same manner as what we have said, all those Names and **letters** <note>original: "otiyyon"; the Zohar views the Hebrew alphabet as the structural DNA of the universe.</note> are all joined to one another until they are made as one. This is the secret of the <term>Tabernacle</term> <note>original: "Mishkan"; the portable sanctuary built by the Israelites in the desert, seen here as a physical microcosm of the divine realms.</note>—for these ten curtains are the secret of the <term>ten Sefirot</term> <note>The ten attributes or emanations through which the Infinite God acts in the world.</note>, which are according to the supernal pattern. Because they were ten, they were called "ten curtains," for they cover one another, and all of them follow the pattern above, so that this [the earthly] may be like that [the heavenly]. <meta>This page transitions from the previous discussion of the Tabernacle's construction (Parashat Terumah) to a discourse on Parashat Vayechi (the final portion of Genesis). # Vayechi

## Main Text (Zohar)

And he said: whoever performs with strength as is fitting, does so because of the Master of strength. <note>original: "Heila"; This refers to God as the source of all spiritual power. This passage is from Zohar I, 235b.</note>
And when he finds within a person an emptiness of all good things, where good deeds are not found,
concerning this, the scripture says: *“And I returned and saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun;* <note>Ecclesiastes 4:1</note>
*and behold, the tears of the oppressed, and they have no comforter.”* And this verse is difficult, for it is written:
*“And behold, the tears of the oppressed, and they have no comforter.”* And immediately it turns back and says, *“and on the side of their oppressors there was power, but they have no comforter.”*
Why is "they have no comforter" mentioned twice? Rather, come and see that this
<term>Comforter</term> <note>original: "Menahem"; in Kabbalah, this is a title for the spirit that provides solace to the exiled and suffering.</note> is the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>original: "Shekhintah"; the Divine Presence, often viewed as the feminine or indwelling aspect of God that shares in human suffering.</note>, who is the comforter for all those whom people have oppressed.
But because of the sin of those people who removed the Torah from the earth and pressured
the Shekhinah, concerning this it says, "and they have no comforter." For this Comforter ascended on high
and was not found with them below. And when those other oppressed ones saw that this
Comforter, who used to descend and be found with them, had ascended away from them because of those
oppressors, then "they have no comforter" as before. For this reason, twice it says
"they have no comforter." Come and see: who are these "oppressed"? These are the <term>infants</term> <note>original: "tippelin"; specifically refers to very young children or sucklings who die before their time.</note>
who are found in the generation, and their souls were oppressed because of the sins of their fathers.
And the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Berikh Hu"; the standard Aramaic name for God in the Zohar.</note> makes for them vessels for the spirit and vessels for the bones. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, makes
for them strength, as it is said: *“and on the side of their oppressors there was power.”* <note>The Zohar re-reads the word "Koach" (power/strength) as a gift given *to* the oppressed children rather than belonging to the oppressors.</note> This is the strength of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
which He gives to them inside <term>Paradise</term> <note>original: "Gan Eden"; the celestial Garden of Eden where souls reside after death.</note>. This is strength to be companions to their Master; strength
for the Holy One, Blessed be He, to delight in them. And concerning this it is written, *“and on the side of their oppressors there was power”*—actual power [strength]—
because within their very death, power and strength were given to them. And concerning this, King Solomon
the King said: *“And I praised the dead who have already died more than the living who are* <note>Ecclesiastes 4:2</note>
*still alive.”* Who are "the living who are still alive"? These are
the generations of the wicked in the world, who are called "living" as before, even though they are [actually] dead.

<summary>This page provides a mystical interpretation of Ecclesiastes, explaining that children who die young ("the oppressed") receive special divine strength and companionship with God in Paradise to compensate for their suffering on earth.</summary>

# Zohar Parashat Balak

## Main Text (Zohar)

And he saw that everything the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"; the standard Rabbinic name for God, emphasizing both transcendence and immanence.</note> made above and below is all in one pattern. Everything found on the earth is a reflection of what is found above, and everything found on the other sides is a perversion.
They made that which they worship and fear—whoever takes the form of those stars of heaven and assigns to them a portion above. They [the stars] receive it above and bring down strength and power to them [the worshippers], and they consider themselves significant through that worship of theirs. They are able to perform evil through this, and He grants power to the vision that clings to them until they prevail and are crowned in this world through their worship. 
This is the service of the <term>Evil Side</term> <note>original: "Sitra Bisha"; the demonic or dark side of the spiritual realm in Kabbalistic thought.</note>, and from them comes all goodness, sustenance, life, children, and everything they need—and all this is because they gave them a portion. They are called the "Host of Heaven" because of this. Afterward, they merit what they merit, but the portion of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is distinct from all, and He is over all in His own way, and through Him and from Him everything exists. However, they cling to these powers so that blessing and sustenance and all good things descend, and in them, they find refuge.
> For all the gods of the peoples are idols
<note>Reference to Psalms 96:5, variant reading. The text suggests these "idols" are actually lower celestial powers that people mistakenly worship.</note>
And they know how to focus upon them and cling to them. This is the wisdom to which the <term>Sons of the East</term> <note>original: "Bnei Kedem"; traditionally associated with ancient eastern magicians or astrologers in the desert.</note> in the desert clung. King Solomon spoke of it, as it is written:
> And Solomon’s wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east, and all the wisdom of Egypt.
<note>1 Kings 5:10</note>
Solomon desired to know all these forms of wisdom, even those rituals of other nations. Because of this, it is written:
> And Solomon did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord.
<note>1 Kings 11:6</note>
This was because he sought to know this wisdom and how they performed their service—not that he performed actual idolatry, heaven forbid! Rather, because he knew their root and their side and upon what they relied, it resulted in him neglecting the service of his Master. 
The same applies to Balaam, who knew this wisdom, and all the priests of Egypt who were experts in sorceries. All these wise men among them knew this wisdom, yet they worshipped only those powers and that which their portion relied upon. This entire portion is of importance to the <term>Other Side</term> <note>original: "Sitra Achra"; the realm of impurity.</note>. Heaven forbid one should think they did not know there is a Holy One, Blessed be He, above them! Rather, they knew Him in their own way and through their wisdom, but they believed that everything was under the portion of the appointed powers over them. This is why Balaam came and sought to rely on his own ritual...

<summary>This page discusses the Kabbalistic concept of "as above, so below," explaining that King Solomon's "sin" was his intellectual investigation into the dark wisdom and astrological powers used by the "Sons of the East" and Egypt.</summary>
<keywords>King Solomon, Balaam, Sons of the East, Sitra Achra, astrology, idolatry, celestial powers, wisdom of Egypt</keywords>

This section describes the mystical transition from the weekday to the Sabbath, focusing on the unification of the Divine Presence (the Shekhinah) with the higher realms and the departure of all harsh judgments and "evil sides."</meta>

# Parashat Terumah

## Main Text (Zohar)

...And from when this sign arrives, which is **One**, we must know that this is a mystery <note>original: "raza"; a secret or mystical principle.</note> that has no partnership with another. And for this reason, when this sign comes, it stands alone. 
And if you should say: "But we have already established that they are four and three, and all is one?" 
Come and see <note>original: "Ta Chazi"; a standard Zoharic opening to a mystical explanation.</note>: at the hour when the **Assembly of Israel** <note>original: "Knesset Yisrael"; the mystical personification of the people of Israel and the Divine Presence, or Shekhinah.</note> unites above in oneness, then all are included in one. And this is the mystery of the verse: **"Blessed be the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever."** 
This is the unification where she [the Shekhinah] is alone, and those six sides <note>original: "shita sitrin"; referring to the six emotional Sefirot or divine attributes—Kindness through Foundation—that channel light into the world.</note> are all included in one. And if you should say: "But there are six?" It is not so. For they are all included in one, and there remains only the mystery of **One** alone. 

**Just as this is the case, so too is the Sabbath**, which unites in the mystery of "One" so that the mystery of "One" may rest upon her. The prayer of the Sabbath Eve <note>The evening service (Ma'ariv) marking the beginning of the Sabbath on Friday night.</note> is when the **precious, holy Throne** <note>original: "kursaiya yakira kadisha"; a reference to the Shekhinah as the vessel that holds the Divine light.</note> is unified in the mystery of "One" and is prepared so that the **Holy Supernal King** <note>original: "Malka Kadisha Ila'ah"; the masculine aspect of the Divine.</note> may rest upon her. 

When the Sabbath enters, she [the Shekhinah] is unified and separated from the **Other Side** <note>original: "Sitra Achra"; the realm of darkness, impurity, or "evil" in Kabbalistic thought.</note>, and all judgments pass away from her. And she remains in the unification of the holy light, and she is crowned with many crowns before the **Holy King**. And all powers of wrath and masters of judgment all flee and pass away from her, and there is no other authority in all the worlds...

# Parashat Bo

## Main Text (Zohar)

And because of this, all the worlds above and below are not [called] by a single name, so that the King's glory <note>original: "yikra de-malka"; the honor or manifest presence of God</note> is not seen [identically] in every place. And because of this, He has several names, and from here the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Berikh Hu"; the standard rabbinic way of referring to God, often abbreviated as K.B.H.</note> opened for them a gateway to the heavens and to all the supernal names. And all those names and vessels <note>original: "manin"; the tools or instruments through which the Divine light is channeled into the world</note> from which this world was built—consequently, He has many names and many appellations.

And every appellation rests upon those [forces or angels] appointed beneath Him, according to the specific work that He performs through them. And all those names and appellations [exist] because if it were not so, His creations would not be able to cleave to the Torah or [understand] the names in every generation that are like this—except for the <term>Ineffable Name</term> <note>original: "shama perisha"; the distinct, four-letter Name of God (YHVH) that is not pronounced as written</note>, which is [above] all names and is the hidden treasury of all the names in the world. And this is His Name that creates light, corresponding to what we say: "The Holy One, Blessed be He, taught us ways and paths when He created this world with supernal names."

And after those lights were perfected in the supernal splendor—in the light that returns and ascends above—for this reason He has many appellations. All this is because there are many letters of fire, letters of air, letters of water, and letters of earth <note>The four elements: fire, air, water, and earth</note>, and all the names of the Holy One, Blessed be He, are supernal mysteries. And the Holy One, Blessed be He, established those names so that we might know the paths of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and to know how many lights there are that appear outwardly from within that "Concealed of all Concealed" <note>original: "setima de-khol setimin"; the most hidden, infinite level of the Divine (Ein Sof)</note>.

This is to know that all those names are <term>members of the Supernal Body</term> <note>original: "sheyfin de-gufa ila’ah"; a metaphorical description of the Sefirot (Divine attributes) acting as "limbs" through which the Divine "Soul" acts in the world</note>. And because of this, there are many names and many appellations for each and every one, according to the deeds He performs through them. And because of this it is written:

> I am the Lord, that is My Name; and My glory I will not give to another, nor My praise to graven images. <note>Isaiah 42:8</note>

And because of this, all the names that are appointed above and below are all built from the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, which is the sum total of all names. And even though He has many names, all those names we mention are "outer" names, intended to be included within the names of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and therefore they all cleave to Him. And in each and every name He is revealed according to the work He performs. And the Sages returned and said: every single name that rests upon them is meant to be included in the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, because this is the hidden treasury of all the names in the world.

<summary>This page explores the Kabbalistic theology of Divine Names, explaining that while God is essentially one, He uses various "appellations" (titles) and "limbs" (Sefirot) to govern the world and remain accessible to human understanding. It emphasizes that the Ineffable Name (YHVH) remains the hidden source and "treasury" for all other manifestations.</summary>
<keywords>Divine Names, Ineffable Name, Supernal Body, Sefirot, Four Elements, Isaiah 42:8, Kabbalistic metaphysics, Divine manifestation</keywords>

## The Palaces of the Other Side (Sitra Achra)

In this manner, ten appointees were separated from behind the Throne, who sit within this palace, and all of them surround this palace from the side that is not holy. And every time a human <note>Aramaic: *bar nash*, literally "son of man"</note> prays their prayer, when that prayer descends toward this palace, those ten appointees emerge. They are called "distressors" and "accusers" <note>original: *me'ikin* and *mastanin*</note>, and they act to delay the prayer so that it shall not enter that holy palace above.

And there, those ten appointees are also called "biters" <note>original: *neshikhin*</note>. And at the time when these ten biter-appointees go out, ten other biters emerge from them, and from that place, many angels of destruction emerge who roam throughout the world.

And this palace is called the "Palace of Fire" that has no light. And here is found the "light" of the <term>Husks</term> <note>original: *Kelipot*; the shells of impurity that conceal divine light</note> which darkens the light from above, and here it is called "Darkness." And these ten appointees are all joined to one another in a circular fashion.

This palace stands to push a person away from the good path toward the evil path. And when a person walks on a straight path, they all descend upon him to prosecute him. ## Main Text (Zohar)

Because for everyone who exerts effort in this world, <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kadosh Barukh Hu", the standard rabbinic title for God</note> watches over him, as it is said <note>Zechariah 4:10</note> -> "The eyes of the Lord roam through the whole earth," <- and so forth. And it is written <note>Zechariah 14:9</note> -> "On that day the Lord will be One and His name One," <- and it is also written <note>Job 41:8</note> -> "One is joined to the other, and no air can come between them." <-

This is because one level is united with another level above it, and they become one; thus, the Name of <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> is one. Come and see: <term>One</term> <note>original: "Echad" (אחד)</note> is a mystery in which the <term>male and female</term> <note>original: "dechar ve-nukba"; in Kabbalah, these represent the balancing masculine and feminine forces of the Divine</note> are found, which constitutes the complete Name. Therefore it is written as **"One,"** and the mystery is as follows:

The **Aleph (א)** <note>The first letter of the word "Echad", with a numerical value of 1</note> is the mystery of the upper world, which is the <term>Supernal Crown</term> <note>original: "Keter Ela'ah", the highest and most hidden of the ten Sefirot or divine emanations</note>.

The **Chet (ח)** <note>The second letter, with a numerical value of 8</note> is the mystery of the eight lower levels that are united in Him.

The **Dalet (ד)** <note>The third letter, with a numerical value of 4</note> is the mystery of the <term>Moon</term> <note>original: "Sihara"; in Kabbalah, the moon represents the tenth Sefirah, Malkhut (Kingship), which receives and reflects the light of the others</note>, which by itself is the letter Dalet.

And because she <note>the Moon/Malkhut</note> is the letter Dalet <note>Dalet is the 4th letter, but here the Zohar plays on its relationship to the Chet (8)</note> existing by herself, the Name is not complete until she connects with those eight levels. This creates the combination of Chet (8) and Dalet (4), which equals **twelve**. These are the <term>Twelve Tribes</term> <note>original: "Triesar Shivtin"; symbolizing the full structural manifestation of the divine order</note>, which are the mystery of the <term>Living Creatures</term> <note>original: "Chayota", the angelic beings seen in Ezekiel's vision of the Divine Chariot</note>.

The mystery continues as the Aleph (1) joins with them, and the word **"One"** <note>Echad: 1+8+4</note> is formed. This equals **thirteen**, which is the mystery of the <term>Thirteen Attributes of Mercy</term> <note>original: "Tlisar Mekhilan de-Rachamei", the qualities of divine compassion revealed to Moses</note>. When all of them are joined together as one, then the Name is complete, and He is One. Thus it is written, "The Lord is One and His Name One," because His Name is certainly **One**. For the mystery of "One" is found when the Name is complete, and it is regarding this that "His Name is One" is written.

<summary>This page provides a Kabbalistic meditation on the word "Echad" (One), explaining how its Hebrew letters symbolize the unification of the Divine emanations, specifically connecting the highest crown to the lower levels and the Moon (Malkhut) to form the number thirteen, representing divine mercy.</summary>

"Companions"—these are the ministering angels. "Listen for your voice"—to the voice of the soul of that person. "Let me hear it"—this is <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> who says, "Let me hear your voice," when it resounds before Him in the song of the Torah. And regarding this, fortunate is the portion of whoever occupies himself with the Torah at night. Come and see: midnight...

And when the side of the North is awakened and the midnight hour is stirred, **the Holy One, blessed be He** <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>, enters the Garden of Eden to take delight with the righteous.

And then the **hind of the dawn** <note>original: "ayelet ha-shachar"—a lyrical reference to the Shekhinah as she prepares to transition from the darkness of night to the light of day</note> awakens and sings a song, just as it is said: 
> For the leader; on the **hind of the dawn**. A psalm of David.
<note>Psalms 22:1</note>

And this is the mystery of faith, where one is bound to the other so that all becomes one.

## Main Text (Zohar)

When the sun emerges, it illuminates all the stars and all those celestial hosts that exist above. All of them are gathered in before the sun and are no longer seen; only that sun remains visible alone. In this same manner, regarding the Light that is the Light of all: all things are gathered in and hidden within it—all those **chariots** <term>ritychin: the angelic structures that serve as vehicles for the Divine presence</term> and all those hosts of the upper realms. They are not seen, except for that Light which is perfect above and below. When that Light rises, which is the Light of all, they are all gathered and hidden within this Light, which is perfect in its levels as one. And then, everything exists in the **Secret of Man** <term>Raza de-Adam: the mystical concept that the universe and the Divine attributes are structured like a human body</term>. 

And if you should say that it is written: 
> And the likeness upon the heads of the living creature was a firmament, like the color of the terrible ice.
<note>Ezekiel 1:22</note>
 
Behold, it is also written:
> And upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man upon it from above.
<note>Ezekiel 1:26</note>

Certainly, it is so, for everything was established for the sake of "Man," and everything is in the likeness of Man. And concerning this, it is written: *and upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man*, which is the **form** <term>diyukna: an image, likeness, or spiritual archetype</term> that is the most perfect of all forms. 

Everything exists within the Secret of Man. Just as in the likeness of a man there are eyes and there are ears, and there is a nose and there is a mouth, hands and feet; so too, everything is in the likeness of Man. This **form** <term>diyukna</term> is the perfection of all forms in the world. In this manner, there are "limbs" and "joints," and they are all part of the Secret of Man, for they are all bound one to another and are found to be a single body.

Just as there are limbs and joints in a human being, and all are part of the Secret of Man—which is the form that is more perfect than all other forms—in this same way, there are celestial limbs and joints, and they all bind to one another and are found to be a single body. And all those chariots and hosts are all "limbs" and "joints" meant to appear as one body, which is the **Secret of Man**. 

When everything is established together as one, then it is called "Man." Just as in a human being there are inner limbs and joints that are not visible on the outside, so too there are above inner limbs and joints that are not visible on the outside. And all of them stand within the Secret of Man. When everything is established together as one, then it is called "Man"...

<summary>This page explains the Kabbalistic concept of the 'Supernal Man,' arguing that the entire celestial hierarchy of angels and 'chariots' actually forms a single, unified divine body. Using the sun as a metaphor, it describes how individual spiritual entities are subsumed into this one 'Secret of Man' once the divine light reaches its full perfection.</summary>

The previous page established that the Divine light gathers all "chariots" and "angels" into one image; this page explains that this image only truly becomes "Man" (Adam) when the masculine (Dechar) and feminine (Nukva) are joined in perfect unity, specifically manifest in the mystery of the Sabbath.</meta>

## Main Text (Zohar)

...masculine and feminine as one. And if you should say, are "Man" and his female two distinct entities? Behold, the matter is one: man and woman are one. Because of this, the whole matter is one mystery <note>original: "raza," referring to a hidden spiritual reality</note>, for the name "Man" <term>Adam: the primordial human archetype</term> is not found except in a place where masculine and feminine are found together as one. Come and see: because masculine and feminine are one, they are the secret of faith <term>mehemanuta: the holistic system of Divine reality</term>.

**Rabbi Shimon opened and said:**
> **"You shall keep My Sabbaths and revere My Sanctuary; I am the Lord."**
<note>Leviticus 19:30</note>

We have already established the meaning of this verse. However, come and see that all the Sabbaths, appointed times, and festivals are all one. It is a single matter. For the Sabbath is not called "Sabbath" except at the time when the Bride <note>The Shekhinah, the Divine Presence in its feminine aspect</note> connects with it. And if you should say: is the masculine alone and the feminine alone? It is not so. For the Sabbath is not called "Sabbath" except when masculine and feminine are as one. Because of this, the verse says "My Sabbaths" <note>in the plural, *shabbatotai*</note>—to show they are all one.

And when they are one, it is called Sabbath. **"And revere My Sanctuary"**—this refers to the Sabbath of the night <margin>The Sabbath of the night</margin> which is **Awe** <term>yirah: a state of holy dread or reverence associated with the feminine aspect, Malchut</term>, and she dwells within that awe. Regarding this, "and revere My Sanctuary" is the Sabbath of the night. **"I am the Lord"**—this is the Sabbath of the day, which is the inclusion of everything. Therefore, they are all on one single level.

Come and see what is written:
> **"For I am the Lord, I change not; therefore you sons of Jacob are not consumed."**
<note>Malachi 3:6</note>

What is the meaning of **"are not consumed"**? It is because they take hold of the Supernal **Form** <term>diyukna: the spiritual image or archetype of the Divine</term>. Just as He does not change, you also are not consumed. "But you who did cleave unto the Lord your God are alive every one of you this day" <note>Deuteronomy 4:4</note>. Therefore, the whole matter is one mystery.
