## Zohar Terumah

[1] ...of the surroundings of the Tabernacle, and these are the secrets from above, and they are the hints that include
[2] the Tabernacle on every side, and they are called curtains. Come and see, it is written: **"Goats’ hair curtains for a tent over the Tabernacle;**
[3] **eleven curtains you shall make them."** <note>Exodus 26:7</note> And these are the first ten curtains that were made in the secret of the Holy
[4] Name, so that the Tabernacle would be one. They correspond to the Ten Commandments of the Torah, and because of this, the secret
[5] of the Tabernacle is the secret of the Torah itself. Ten curtains correspond to the Ten Commandments. Eleven curtains
[6] correspond to those eleven ingredients of the incense <term>Ketoret: the sacred incense offering, which contained eleven spices</term>, which are the eleven sides that grasp onto the Evil Inclination <term>Yetzer Hara: the innate human impulse toward selfishness or evil</term>, which is called
[7] "Goat" <note>original: "Az," which means goat but also implies "fierce" or "harsh"</note> because it is nourished by it. Eleven curtains are meant to cause the holiness of the Torah to rest upon them.
[8] And because of this, it is written—and this is the secret of the bow <term>Keshet: refers to both the rainbow and a warrior's bow</term>, which stands within itself like an arrow in a bow—and this secret of the bow is
[9] to protect the Tabernacle. And concerning this: "goats’ hair curtains" which surround the Tabernacle from every side.
[10] Come and see: there are eight books, and in each and every one there is a supreme secret. And in this book
[11] which is called *Vayikra* <note>Leviticus</note>, there are hints regarding the sacrifices and hints regarding the Priests and Levites, and the secret of the Tabernacle
[12] by which the world is sustained. It is written: **"And it was on the day that Moses finished setting up the Tabernacle."** <note>Numbers 7:1</note> To set up
[13] the Tabernacle corresponds to this: "And it was on the day of *kallot* [finishing]." It is written as "Bride" <note>original: "Kallah." The Zohar frequently reads the Hebrew word for "finishing" (kallot) as "bride" (kallah) to show the Tabernacle is the wedding canopy for God and the community</note>. This is the Bride who descends from above
[14] and dwells within the Tabernacle. And about this it is written: **"And it was on the day that Moses finished [the Bride] setting up."** To set up—
[15] whom? To set up that level from above. Rabbi Yose said: What is [the meaning of] what is written: **"And the Tabernacle**
[16] **you shall make with ten curtains."** <note>Exodus 26:1</note> Ten curtains correspond to the Ten Sefirot <term>Sefirot: the ten creative forces or attributes through which the Divine is revealed</term>. Curtains correspond to the secrets of the Torah.
[17] And we have learned: ten curtains of **"fine twisted linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet yarn."** This is the secret
[18] of the four elements of the world that surround the Tabernacle. Fine twisted linen—this is the secret of Lovingkindness <term>Chesed: the Sefirah representing expansive benevolence</term>. Blue—
[19] this is the secret of Strength <term>Gevurah: the Sefirah of judgment, restraint, and discipline</term>. Purple—this is the secret of Beauty <term>Tiferet: the Sefirah that balances mercy and judgment</term>. Scarlet yarn—this is the secret of Sovereignty <term>Malchut: the final Sefirah, representing the physical manifest world and the Divine feminine</term>.
[20] And these are the hints of those four Living Creatures <term>Chayot: the angelic beings described in Ezekiel's vision of the Divine Chariot</term> that surround the Tabernacle. And they are all one secret.
[21] And here one must mention the secret of five and five, which are: **"Five curtains shall be joined**
[22] **to one another, and five curtains joined to one another."** <note>Exodus 26:3</note> This is the secret of 5 and 5,
[23] which [together] are the letter *Yod* <note>The Hebrew letter Yod has the numerical value of 10</note>. And they are the secret of the thirty-two wondrous paths of Wisdom, which ascend to 32.
[24] And here is the secret of the ten curtains. For these ten curtains of the Tabernacle are the secret of the Name
[25] of ten letters that is within it. And about this one must say...

Because of this, when a human being merits in this world and serves his Master, he merits to be in perfect joy, so that the Holy One, Blessed be He, may delight in him.

And when that meritorious soul ascends above, she is illuminated with many lights, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, recites over her several verses of affection and says: **"You are all fair, my love; there is no spot in you"** <note>Song of Songs 4:7</note>. And He says: **"Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline your ear; forget also your own people, and your father's house"** <note>Psalms 45:11</note>. Come and see: this soul is a portion from above, and when she comes to this world, she is under the authority of her Master. And when she serves and is meritorious in this world, she performs the will of her Master. Happy is the human being who merits this holy soul which is a portion from above. And concerning this it is written: **"And [He] forms the spirit of man within him,"** this is the holy soul which is within the body. And if you say the soul is from above, why is it written "He forms the spirit of man *within* him"? Rather, when a human being merits in this world, the Holy One, Blessed be He, makes for him...

## Shemini (The Eighth)

...and he called out the name through which the wealth of the lower world exists. What is the "wealth" within it? This is the <term>Assembly of Israel</term> <note>original: "Knesset Yisrael" — In the Zohar, this refers to the Shekhinah, the feminine aspect of God that sustains the world.</note>. As it is written: *If he be destroyed from his place, then it shall deny him, saying, I have not seen thee.* <note>Job 8:18</note> Within it is the "seventh," and this is the time of the building below. And concerning this, it is written:
> **And it came to pass on the eighth day, that Moses called Aaron and his sons, and the elders of Israel.** <note>Leviticus 9:1</note>

This was in order to crown Aaron with the crown of the <term>Priesthood</term> <note>original: "Kehunata"</note> and all those accompanying him. Later, when he was found to be complete along with all of them—come and see!—on the eighth day, his own completion was achieved. Come and see that on the eighth day, <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Berikh Hu" — the standard Aramaic name for God in the Zohar</note> was found in the world, for the <term>Tabernacle</term> <note>original: "Mishkana"</note> was completed. This refers to the Tabernacle that Moses established, in which the <term>Divine Presence</term> <note>original: "Shekhintah"</note> dwells below, just like the pattern of the Tabernacle above. All those days that Moses was setting up the Tabernacle, the Divine Presence was not found dwelling below until the eighth day arrived. And on the eighth day, we see that it is called "the eighth day." All those seven [previous] days were only to prepare the Tabernacle, but on the eighth day, everything was perfected. 

We have learned that in every place, "the eighth" refers to the Assembly of Israel, which is the eighth in relation to all those higher levels. Come and see: there is an "eighth" above and an "eighth" below. The "eighth above" is the high level called <term>Understanding</term> <note>original: "Binah" — the third of the ten divine emanations, representing the "Supernal Mother" from whom the lower levels emerge.</note>, which is the eighth when counting from the bottom to the top. The "eighth below" is the Assembly of Israel, which is the eighth when counting from the top to the bottom. For this reason, it is called "the eighth day," matching the pattern of Understanding, which is the eighth above. Because of this, on the eighth day, *Moses called Aaron and his sons, and the elders of Israel.* Why the "elders of Israel"? Because they sat [as witnesses] at the beginning and at the end, and through their hands the Tabernacle was established. Come and see: Aaron was called so that he would be completed first; his sons because they are close to the Holy One; and the elders of Israel to bear witness to the beginning.

## Vayechi (And He Lived)

[...Come and see!] We have established that everything <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Berikh Hu"</note> made on earth, He made according to the pattern of that which is above. And the companions explained that when the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to create the world, He cast a precious stone from beneath the **Throne of Glory** <note>original: "Korsia Yekara"</note> and sank it into the <term>Abyss</term> <note>original: "Tehoma"</note>. With that stone, the world was perfected, and for this reason it is called the **Foundation Stone** <note>original: "Even Shetiyah"</note>, because from it the world was founded. And that stone, which is the **central point** of the world, upon it stands the Holy of Holies.

[And when] the world expanded to the right and to the left and to all sides, they were settled upon it; and for this reason it is called the Foundation Stone.

Come and see: that stone which Jacob placed beneath his head was this very stone. As it is written:
> **And this stone, which I have set for a pillar, shall be God's house.** <note>Genesis 28:22</note>

Was it indeed the Foundation Stone? But they have already established that the Foundation Stone existed before the world was created! Yet he [Jacob] placed it beneath his head? Rather, thus we have established: that it was beneath the Throne of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and in that place was the <term>Great House</term> <note>original: "Bei Rav" — likely referring to the assembly of the Divine Presence or a celestial house of study.</note>. And for this reason, he placed it beneath his head. What is meant by "beneath his head"? This is the portion of the Holy One, Blessed be He, which is the **Support of the Masculine** <note>original: "Rafida de-Khura" — a mystical term for the spiritual foundation that supports the masculine aspect of the Divine.</note>, and concerning this it is written:
> **His left hand is under my head.** <note>Song of Songs 2:6</note>

And come and see: Jacob established the four pillars of the Throne, and the four faces were all [within] this single stone. This is the Foundation Stone. And all those pillars and faces were included in that stone, which is the **central point**, and for this reason it is called the Foundation Stone.

# Pekudei (Accountings)

... <unclear>of the Tabernacle, which is the spirit of Moses that emerged from within</unclear> ...
... <unclear>in that cloud, and behold, we have established as it is written:</unclear>

> **And Moses went into the midst of the cloud, and went up into the mount.** <note>Exodus 24:18</note>

What did he see there? He saw seven <term>Palaces</term> <note>original: "Heichalin" — celestial chambers or levels of spiritual reality</note> which are the palaces of the **Holy King**, and all those souls that ascend to be there. At that time, Moses gazed upon everything that was required for the construction of the **Tabernacle**.

**Rabbi Shimon opened [his discourse] and said:**

> **Fear not, thou worm Jacob, and ye men of Israel.** <note>Isaiah 41:14</note>

Why is Israel compared to this **worm**? Just as this worm has no power except in its mouth, so too Israel has no power except in their mouths—through <term>prayer</term> <note>original: "tzalota"</note> and through the <term>supplication</term> <note>original: "ba'uta"</note> they perform before their Master. Come and see: just like the nature of this worm, which is weak, yet about it is written **"and crimson [worm] yarn"** <note>original: "tola'at shani" — referring to the insect used to create the sacred red dye</note>, which is itself weak, yet with its mouth it can destroy the whole world <note>Likely referring to the worm's ability to consume and fell massive trees</note>. All those supernal **rectifications** <note>original: "tikkunin"</note> depend upon the mouth of this worm. So too, Israel are weak and have no power except in their mouth, and with that mouth they weaken the power of all those <term>appointed ministers</term> <note>original: "memunan" — the guardian angels or celestial powers assigned to the other nations</note>. And when Israel are alluded to in this matter, it is then written: **"Fear not, thou worm Jacob."** Do not read it as "worm," but rather as *the* worm—like that specific worm that weakens a great tree. Such are Israel. And regarding this, it is written when he alludes to them concerning the **Great Tree**, which is the Tree Above and Below, as we have established. And this is the **"crimson worm"** which is holy, and with it was made the <term>Veil of the Tabernacle</term> <note>original: "parochet ha-mishkan"</note> <unclear>which is the secret of the Holy Name</unclear>...

<summary>This page describes Moses' vision of the seven celestial palaces within the cloud on Sinai and presents a homily by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai. The discourse explains that Israel is compared to a worm because their true power is not physical, but resides in the "mouth" through prayer and sacred speech.</summary>

## Portion of Terumah (Offerings)

...that Shabbat is the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>original: "Shekhinta" — the Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God that dwells within the world</note>, and regarding this they established the mystery of Shabbat: Shabbat is the Shekhinah.

Come and see: just as it is with Shabbat—on the eve of Shabbat, during the night of Shabbat, and on the day of Shabbat—it is all one single mystery. And this is what Rabbi Eleazar said: that the entire day of Shabbat exists within the mystery of Shabbat, and the <term>Other Side</term> <note>original: "Sitra Achra" — the Kabbalistic term for the forces of evil, impurity, or "the left side"</note> is not found within them at all. Because of this, the Other Side has no power over anyone who occupies themselves with the Shabbat.

This mystery exists because Shabbat is the Shekhinah. Indeed, they have established that had Israel not sinned, the Other Side would not be found among them at all. On the day of Shabbat, everything is left behind, and the Other Side has no dominion whatsoever. This is the mystery of the **Torah**, as it is written:

> **And you shall keep the Shabbat, for it is holy to you.** <note>Exodus 31:14</note>

For behold, everything is holiness, and no <term>impurity</term> <note>original: "mesavu"</note> rules over it at all. Come and see: just as it is Above (as it were), so it is below. For the "Shabbat of Above" is the mystery of the **Point** that stands in the middle, with six sides surrounding it. In the same way, the mystery of Shabbat [below] is the mystery of the **Point** that stands in the middle, with six sides surrounding it. Thus, it is all one single mystery.

Come and see: just as the Shekhinah is the mystery of Shabbat, so too is the **Torah** the mystery of Shabbat. For the Torah was given from "six sides" <note>Referring to the six directions of the physical world or the six emotive Sefirot</note>, as they have established, and six sides surround it while it stands in the middle. Such is the mystery of the Shabbat of the Torah. Therefore, since it is Shabbat, the Other Side has no dominion over it at all.

In this same way, they established the mystery of the Torah: that whoever strives in the Torah, the Other Side does not rule over them at all, for the Torah is Shabbat. All those levels of the Torah are within the mystery of Shabbat, as has been stated.

And this mystery: just as the Torah is the mystery of Shabbat, so too anyone who strives in it becomes the mystery of Shabbat, and all of them are considered "the day of Shabbat." Therefore, Shabbat is the Shekhinah, just as the Torah is the Shekhinah; it is all one mystery.

Come and see the mystery of the matter: Shabbat is like the essence of all <term>Faith</term> <note>original: "meimanuta" — in the Zohar, this often refers to the entire system of Divine emanations or the truth of the Godhead</note>, for all Faith is the mystery of Shabbat. Regarding this they established: **Shabbat is equivalent to the entire Torah**, because it is all one mystery.

Come and see: Shabbat is the mystery of the <term>Covenant</term> <note>original: "Brit"</note>, just as the Covenant is the mystery of Faith, so too is Shabbat...

<summary>This page explores the mystical identity of Shabbat, identifying it as the Shekhinah and the "central point" of reality. It argues that during Shabbat, the forces of evil (the Other Side) lose all power, a state that mirrors the spiritual protection granted to those who study the Torah.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Come and see: just as a word of <term>Torah</term> <note>original: "milla d’Oraita" — the study or recitation of sacred Law</note> is perfected on high, so too is an <term>idle word</term> <note>original: "milla betela" — vain, gossiping, or meaningless speech</note> perfected on high. There is no word that does not have a place above or below; it is found in every place. Come and see: just as a word of Torah ascends on high and a single holy firmament is made from it, so too does an idle word ascend on high, and a firmament is made from it that is not holy. And all these [unholy] firmaments are inhabited by spirits of <term>impurity</term> <note>original: "ruchin d’masavuta"</note>, and from those firmaments, evil spirits, judgments, and accusers emerge into the world. 

Come and see: when a person brings forth a holy word from their mouth, they bring forth a voice that ascends on high. Because of this, a single holy firmament is made from that word and that voice, and a single precious and holy radiance is made from it over the head of that person. But when a person brings forth a word that is not holy, it is found that they bring forth a voice of vanity that ascends on high. Because of it, a firmament is made that is not holy, and from that firmament emerge evil spirits who are found to rest upon the head of that person, and impurity is found within them. Come and see, it is written:

> **You shall not make idols for yourselves, nor set up a carved image or a sacred pillar...** <note>Leviticus 26:1</note>

And all these refer to idle words. 
And this is the secret:

> **And when Abram heard that his kinsman was taken captive, he armed his trained men, born in his house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them as far as Dan.** <note>Genesis 14:14</note>

"He armed his trained men"—this refers to his mouth, which was constantly occupied with the Torah, and all those who were with him were awakened toward it and were diligently occupied with the Torah. "He armed (*vayarek*) his trained men"—just as it is said, "and they drew (*vayariku*) [the sword] after them" <note>This draws a linguistic connection between Abraham "arming/leading out" his men and "drawing" a sword, suggesting words are spiritual weapons. See Talmud, Nedarim 32a.</note>. Come and see what is written: "and pursued them as far as Dan." **Dan** is the place appointed over the judgment of the world, and it is the mystery of <term>Gevurah</term> <note>The Divine attribute of Strength or Judgment</note>, which includes both judgment and mercy. It is written, "he armed (*vayarek*) his trained men." What is "he armed"? Just as it is said, "he unsheathes his sword." Do not be surprised at this, for the Torah and all the words of Torah are all a **sword** that wins battles above and below. Because of this, "he armed his trained men" refers to the words of Torah that win battles, and "all those born in his house" are the holy words of Torah that Abraham taught them. "Eighteen and three hundred" <note>318</note>—just as it is said, "**Grace**" (*Chen*) <note>original: "Chen" — the Hebrew word for grace/favor. While the numerical value of Chen is 58, the Zohar here links the sound or essence of the number to the concept of finding favor or grace.</note>, and it is written, "Grace, grace to it." Eighteen and three...

It then interprets Abraham’s rescue of Lot as a spiritual battle fought with the "sword" of Torah study.</summary>

## Main Text (Zohar)

...from them, there is another service. And this is what is written <note>Exodus 21:1</note> **And these are the judgments which you shall set before them.**

**Rabbi Shimon** opened and said, it is written <note>Proverbs 10:22</note> 
-> The blessing of the Lord, it makes rich, and He adds no sorrow with it. <-

**The blessing of the Lord** refers to the Assembly of Israel <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The "Shekhinah" is the feminine aspect of the Divine that dwells within the world</note>, for she is the **blessing** from above, intended so that they may be blessed from her. **It makes rich**, for she is enriched from all those supreme treasures, as it is written <note>Deuteronomy 28:12</note> "The Lord shall open unto you His good treasure, the heaven." <unclear>And He adds no</unclear> **sorrow with it**, this refers to the "Other Side" <note>original: "Sitra Achra" — the realm of evil or impurity</note>, which has no portion or share in this blessing. 

And this is the meaning of **And these are the judgments**, for these are the arrangements of the transmigrations <term>transmigrations</term> <note>original: "gilgulim" — the cycle of reincarnation where a soul returns to Earth in a new body</note>, the judgments of the souls <term>souls</term> <note>original: "nishmatin"</note> where each and every one is judged according to their punishment. **Which you shall set before them**, this is the arrangement of the Torah, which is the arrangement of the faith <note>original: "raza de-meheimanuta" — the secret or mystery of faith/theology</note>. Come and see: all souls enter the cycle of transmigration, but human beings do not know the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, and how they are established. They do not know how people are judged in every single season—both before they come into this world and after they depart from this world.

They do not know how they enter the cycle of transmigration, or how many transmigrations and diverse judgments they must undergo before they find rest. How many souls enter the cycle without number! Yet humans do not know or observe how these souls meet, as it is written <note>Job 33:29</note> 
-> Behold, all these things does God work, twice, thrice, with a man. <-

**And these are the judgments**, this is the arrangement of the judgment of souls. **Which you shall set before them**, which is the mystery of faith. We have learned: Rabbi Shimon was sitting one day, and before him were Rabbi Eleazar, Rabbi Abba, Rabbi Yossi, and Rabbi Hiyya. <unclear>Rabbi Shimon said</unclear>, "How long shall we remain sitting as the support of only a single pillar? It is time to act for the Lord!" <note>The phrase "Time to act for the Lord" (Psalm 119:126) is often used in Jewish tradition to justify revealing secrets that were previously hidden, in order to save the spiritual integrity of the generation.</note>

<unclear>He opened and said</unclear>... [The text continues into the mystical allegory of the Hebrew servant].

## Main Text (Zohar)

...so that He, Blessed be He, may be seen before Him. When a person comes to offer his prayer, the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kadosh Barukh Hu"</note>, rejoices in that prayer. Blessed is the portion of that person whose prayer enters before Him, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, sits upon the Throne of Glory <term>Throne of Glory</term> <note>original: "Kisse ha-Kavod"; the seat of Divine authority and presence</note> and his prayer ascends on high.

**Rabbi Shimon** opened and said:
> **A prayer of the afflicted, when he is overwhelmed, and pours out his complaint before the Lord.** <note>Psalm 102:1</note>

Come and see <note>original: "ta chazi"—a common Zoharic invitation to look deeper into a mystery</note>, there are three prayers that are highly esteemed before the Holy One, Blessed be He: 
One is the prayer of Moses, as it is written:
> **A prayer of Moses, the man of God** <note>Psalm 90:1</note>
This was a prayer like no other achieved by any other human. 
And one is the prayer of David, as it is written:
> **A prayer of David: Incline Your ear, O Lord, answer me** <note>Psalm 86:1</note>
And one is the prayer of the poor man, as it is written:
> **A prayer of the afflicted when he is overwhelmed.**

Which prayer among these is the most esteemed of them all? You must say: the prayer of the poor <term>poor</term> <note>original: "aniy"—referring to both physical poverty and a spirit of total dependency on the Divine</note>. For it takes precedence over the prayer of Moses, and it takes precedence over the prayer of David, and it takes precedence over all other prayers in the world. 

What is the reason? Because the poor man is of a broken heart, and it is written:
> **The Lord is near to the brokenhearted** <note>Psalm 34:19</note>
And that poor man is constantly making a "quarrel" <note>original: "katata"; here meaning a persistent, demanding plea or a legal claim of the heart</note> with the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, inclines His ear and hears his words. Once he offers his prayer, it opens all the windows of the heavens <note>spiritual gateways for the movement of light and speech</note>, and all the other prayers that are ascending on high—this prayer of the poor man **pushes them aside**. The Holy One, Blessed be He, says: "Let the poor man pray..." 
...and he remains alone before the Holy King... 
...pushing aside all those other prayers...

<summary>This passage describes the spiritual supremacy of the poor man's prayer, explaining that a broken heart "pushes aside" all other prayers—even those of Moses and David—to gain immediate audience with the Divine.</summary>

<meta>This page continues from the previous discussion on the manifestation of the Holy Name and the "Architecture of Prayer." It explores the idea that miracles occur constantly in the mundane world, often without the beneficiary's knowledge, and ties these acts to the patriarchal archetypes of Abraham and Isaac.</meta>

## Terumah

... one must look into these matters of those who strive in the Torah. At the time when it is the secret <term>secret</term> <note>original: "raza"; refers to the esoteric or mystical dimension of the Torah</note> of the matter, for the companions <note>original: "havrayya"; the circle of scholars surrounding Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</note> have established it.

Rabbi Elazar said: It is written,
> **"Let them praise the Lord for His goodness, and for His wonders to the children of men"** <note>Psalms 107:8</note>

The companions have already established this verse. But come and see how much a person ought to give thanks to the Holy One, Blessed be He <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note>, for the kindness He performs with human beings every single day. For the Holy One, Blessed be He, performs miracles and wonders with human beings every day, and there is no one who knows of them except for Him.

Every single day, the Holy One, Blessed be He, saves a person from many accusers <note>spiritual forces of prosecution or hardship</note> and judgments, and from that fear that dwells in the world, yet the person does not know. The Holy One, Blessed be He, performs a miracle for him and he does not know it. And concerning this, David said, "Let them praise the Lord for His goodness"—referring to the goodness He performs for a person every day. "And for His wonders to the children of men"—those wonders that He performs among human beings, and there is no one who notices them except for Him alone.

---

Rabbi Shimon opened and said:
> **"I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense"** <note>Song of Songs 4:6</note>

Come and see that this verse is a supreme secret. "I will get me to the mountain of myrrh"—this refers to Abraham, the attribute of **Loving-kindness** <term>Loving-kindness</term> <note>original: "Chesed"; the divine attribute of expansive grace and giving, personified by the patriarch Abraham</note>. He is the "mountain of myrrh," for the Holy One, Blessed be He, holds onto him, and for his sake, He performs kindness in the world. "And to the hill of frankincense"—this refers to Isaac, the attribute of **Strength** <term>Strength</term> <note>original: "Gevurah"; the divine attribute of judgment, restraint, and discipline, personified by Isaac</note>, who is called a "hill."

And all is one secret, for within the Holy One, Blessed be He, everything is unified. Abraham and Isaac are held within Him in the secret of faith. And come and see: this verse was said concerning the Divine Presence <term>Presence</term> <note>original: "Shekhinah"; the indwelling, feminine aspect of God that interacts with the physical world</note>, for she goes out every day to watch over human beings and to perform kindness and miracles for them. Because of this, it is said, "I will get me to the mountain of myrrh"—which is the right side <note>the side of mercy</note>, "and to the hill of frankincense"—which is the left side <note>the side of justice</note>.

## Portion of Bereshit (In the Beginning)

This is the first, for this is the mystery of the Higher Wisdom <term>Chokhmah</term> <note>original: "Chokhmah Ila'ah"; the second of the ten Sefirot, representing the first flash of conscious intellect</note> which is called *Bereshit*—the mystery of the Higher Point <term>Nekudah</term>. This *Bereshit* is understood as "He created six" <note>original: "Bara Shith"; a famous Zoharic wordplay where the word 'Bereshit' is broken into 'Bara' (created) and 'Shith' (the Aramaic word for six)</note>, which is the mystery of the whole. From within the mystery of this Point, all those six higher sides <note>the six directions or Sefirot from Chesed to Yesod that form the "body" of the divine structure</note> emerged. This is the meaning of "In the beginning He created six" from within the mystery of the Primordial Point. And this is God <term>Elohim</term>, which is the mystery where *Bereshit* began to create the six. From within the mystery of this Point, everything emerged, and everything is included in this Point, which is the first of all. And through this, He created the mystery of *Elohim*, which is the mystery of God coming from within the mystery of this Point. In this, all mysteries of above and below are included. All the hidden things of the world and all the concealed things of the world are all called *Elohim*. Because this is the mystery of *Elohim*, everything is included in it. Because this is the mystery of *Elohim*, *Bereshit* began to create the six; from within the mystery of this Point everything emerged, and everything is included in this Point, which is the first of all, and through this He created the mystery of *Elohim* <note>The manuscript repeats this section, likely reflecting the scribe’s emphasis on the cyclical nature of emanation or a transcription error in the original source</note>.

---

->Rabbi Shimon opened and said:<-
> **"And those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the firmament; and those who turn many to righteousness, like the stars for ever and ever"**
<note>original: "Ve-ha-maskilim yazhiru ke-zohar ha-rakia"; Daniel 12:3. This verse provides the namesake for the "Zohar" itself</note>

This "brightness" <term>Zohar</term> <note>original: "Zohar"; meaning radiance, splendor, or brilliance</note> is the most hidden of all hidden lights. It is the mystery of the light that illuminates every single radiance. Every mystery is included in this brightness, which is the mystery of the light that shines upon all the hidden things of the world. This is the brightness that illuminates all those six higher sides. This is the brightness that illuminates all those six higher sides, and this is the <unclear>mystery</unclear> of the Primordial Point, which is Wisdom <term>Chokhmah</term>. Concerning this, it is written:
> **"The beginning of wisdom..."**
<note>original: "Reshit Chokhmah"; Psalms 111:10</note>

And this is the mystery of *Elohim*. *Bereshit* began to create the six from within the mystery of this Point; everything emerged from it and everything is included in this Point, which is the first of all. Through this, He created the mystery of *Elohim*, which is the mystery of God emerging from within the mystery of this Point. In this is included every mystery of above and below, and all the hidden and concealed things of the world; they are all called *Elohim*. In this, everything is completed, as we have established <unclear>in the mystery</unclear> of the whole...

<meta>This page transitions from the general cosmogony of the "Primordial Point" and the creation of the six directions (discussed in the previous page) to a specific metaphorical description of the Divine Light. While the previous folio focused on the beginning of Genesis (Bereshit), this page, from the portion of Terumah (Exodus), uses the physical imagery of a lamp's flame to explain the connection between the highest Divine Thought and the manifest Sanctuary.</meta>

## Portion of Terumah (Offerings)

From within that light that is not seen, all others emerge. Some are like the color of gold, and they are three hundred and sixty-five <note>This number usually corresponds to the days of the solar year or the negative commandments</note>, following the pattern on this side and on that side. And that light emerges from within **Thought** <term>Makhshava</term> <note>original: "Makhshava"; refers to the Sefirah of Binah, the Divine Intellect or "Understanding" from which all differentiated forms emerge</note>, and all of them emerge and spread out from there. All these lights are bound one to another, precious in every place, and they are drawn out into many colors.

Happy is the portion of the righteous in this world and in the world to come.

Rabbi Shimon <note>Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the traditional central figure and teacher of the Zohar</note> opened his discourse and said: Happy is the portion of one who enters and exits and knows his ways, and the ways of the Torah, so that he may walk in the path of truth. Come and see: in this same pattern, there is a lamp <term>Shraga</term> <note>original: "Shraga"; an oil lamp, used here as a physical metaphor for the spiritual anatomy of the Sefirot</note> which is the shadow of the palace that is above the earth. Within this lamp, there are several lights which resemble one another and are bound one to another. When that lamp is lit, there is a light within it which is the vision of the lamp—a dark light <term>Nehora Ukhma</term> <note>original: "Nehora Ukhma"; the blue or black part of the flame at the base, closest to the wick</note>. When that lamp is lit, many colors are seen within that light, all bound together. 

And within that light, there is another light that shines more than all of them, and it is a white light <term>Nehora Hivra</term> <note>original: "Nehora Hivra"; the bright, clear upper part of the flame</note>. When the lamp is lit, that white light shines, and the eye is unable to gaze upon it. That white light is the most precious of all. The dark light is attached to the oil of the lamp <note>original: "mashcheta"; the grease or oil that fuels the light</note> and takes hold of it; within it, many colors are found, and they are all bound together. But that white light is above them all and is attached to them all. 

And so it is in this same pattern: the lower palace, which is the **Holy of Holies** <term>Kodesh ha-Kodashim</term>, is the shadow of the dark light. The white light is above it, and it is the mystery of the light that shines from within **Thought**. And they all take hold of one another as one, in this pattern. They are bound together and shine within one another, so that they may all become one... <note>The text continues describing the unity of the lights, but becomes faded at the bottom.</note>

<summary>This page uses the metaphor of a flickering oil lamp to explain the hierarchy of Divine lights, illustrating how the lowest "dark" light connects to physical reality while the "white" light connects to the highest Divine Thought.</summary>
<keywords>Zohar, Terumah, Sefirot, Binah, Makhshava, Divine Light, Flame Metaphor, Holy of Holies, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai</keywords>

<meta>This page transitions from the previous discussion on the Divine light and the "Lamp" metaphor in the portion of Terumah to the portion of Vayechi (Genesis 47:28–50:26). While the previous page focused on the physical-spiritual structure of the Sanctuary, this page explores the "Time of Favor" and the mystical power of prayer in aligning the human will with the Divine Will, specifically regarding the deathbed blessings of the patriarch Jacob.</meta>

## Vayechi (He Lived)

This secret is that when the higher light is awakened, shining to every side and every direction, and all sides are illuminated, at that hour a person must offer their prayer. It should be the will <note>The Hebrew/Aramaic word "Ratzon" means both "will" and "favor/desire."</note> before one’s Master that this will/favor be found within the light from above. Rabbi Shimon said: Fortunate is the portion of the righteous, for they know how to align their own will before their Master, and they know how to sustain the world. Regarding this, it is written:
> **"But as for me, let my prayer be unto Thee, O Lord, in a time of favor; O God, in the abundance of Thy mercy, answer me with the truth of Thy salvation."** <note>Psalm 69:14</note>

We have established the meaning of this verse: what is a "time of favor"? It is a "time" which is itself "favor." For there is one kind of "time" and there is another kind of "time." There is a time that is favor, and there is a time that is not favor, and that is called an "evil time," as it is written:
> **"For man also knows not his time... as the fishes [that are taken in an evil net]"** etc. <note>Ecclesiastes 9:12</note>

And it is written:
> **"In the evil time."** <note>Psalm 37:19</note>

And it is written:
> **"It is a time to act for the Lord,"** etc. <note>Psalm 119:126</note>

And this is a "time" upon which everything depends, and this is "favor." When the <term>Ancient Holy One</term> <note>original: "Atika Kadisha"; refers to the highest, most hidden aspect of the Divine (Keter), characterized by pure compassion.</note>, who is the <term>Will of all Wills</term> <note>original: "Re'uta de-chol Re'uyin"; the primal, unified desire of the Infinite.</note>, is perceived and that will is revealed, all the lamps <note>original: "boztinin"; a common Zoharic term for the Sefirot or spiritual emanations.</note> shine and are all illuminated. At the hour when that higher will is present and complete, total joy is found. It is concerning this that it is written, **"But as for me, let my prayer be unto Thee, O Lord, in a time of favor."** This is literally a "time of favor" because all wills/desires are found within it, and that light shines when all the others shine. Then it is written, **"O God, in the abundance of Thy mercy, answer me with the truth of Thy salvation."** And it is written afterward:
> **"Deliver me out of the mire, and let me not sink,"** etc. <note>Psalm 69:15</note>

What is the reason for this? Because when that light and favor are withdrawn, the dominion of judgment <term>Din</term> <note>Strict justice or severity</note> takes over, and every side is found in darkness and judgment is awakened. Therefore, a person must offer their prayer before the Holy One, blessed be He, so that He may bring them out of judgment and they might not sink into the "mire," which refers to Gehenna <note>The place of spiritual purification or "hell."</note>, for it is the "miry clay" from which the higher will and the shining light have departed. In this manner, David said, **"But as for me, let my prayer be unto Thee, O Lord, in a time of favor."** In this same way, it is written in the book of Kings:
> **"And Elisha said: Hear the word of the Lord; thus says the Lord: Tomorrow about this time,"** etc. <note>2 Kings 7:1</note>

What does "about this time tomorrow" mean? It means according to that higher favor/will, at that hour which is "favor." This follows the pattern of what is written: **"And it was about this time tomorrow on the third day"** <note>A composite citation likely blending 2 Kings 7 and Exodus 19.</note> etc. And it is written:
> **"At the time of life, and behold, Sarah your wife shall have a son."** <note>Genesis 18:10</note>

What is the "time of life"? It is that hour called <term>Chayah</term> <note>original: "Chayah"; literally "Living Being," referring here to the Sefirah of Yesod or Malkhut as the source of vitality for the lower worlds.</note>, from which lives emerge and the world is illuminated, and this is the "time of favor." Now we must look into what Rabbi Shimon said regarding the time when Jacob departed from the world and blessed his sons. Why did he not bless them all as one, but rather each one individually? As it is written:
> **"And Jacob called to his sons,"** etc. <note>Genesis 49:1</note>

And it is written:
> **"Every one according to his blessing he blessed them."** <note>Genesis 49:28</note>

Yet it is also written: **"And he blessed them"** <note>implying a collective blessing</note>.

<meta>This page continues from the previous discussion on spiritual timing and alignment with the Divine Will. While the previous page (from the portion of Vayechi) focused on the "Time of Favor," this page (from the portion of Tetzaveh in the Book of Exodus) transitions into the spiritual state required for Divine service—specifically the necessity of joy—and the mystical symbolism of the thirteen materials used to construct the Tabernacle.</meta>

## Main Text (The Zohar)

For everyone who is in joy and appears in gladness, the <term>Holy One, blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Berikh Hu"</note> rejoices in him. This is as it is written:
->**"Serve the Lord with gladness; come before His presence with singing."** <note>Psalm 100:2</note><-
For this is the joy of the world above. [And it is the joy of the world below]. Because there is joy below, that hour is crowned with joy. Then that joy is completed by the higher joy, and the **World to Come** <note>The realm of eternal spiritual delight</note> is drawn down upon that hour of joy. 

There, the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells. Because of this, a person must eliminate <note>original: "leshaya’ah," to set aside or cancel</note> other types of joy and dwell instead in the **joy of a commandment** <note>The spiritual happiness found in performing a divine deed</note>. For the joy of a commandment is the joy of the Torah, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is crowned by that joy. For this reason, it is written: "Serve the Lord with gladness; come before His presence with singing." In this same way, King David would rise in the night and occupy himself with the Torah until the joy of the morning arrived. He was then crowned with joy because the Holy One, blessed be He, is revealed in that joy. Come and see: it is the same way in the realm above, and therefore those human beings who serve before the Holy One, blessed be He, are always found in joy. Because of this, at that hour, the <term>Priest</term> <note>original: "Kohen"</note> who serves in holiness is in joy and appears in gladness.

Come and see the precious matter through which the **Tabernacle** <note>original: "Mishkan"; the portable sanctuary in the desert</note> was made. There are thirteen precious materials mentioned in its construction. These thirteen correspond to the **Thirteen Attributes of Mercy** and the **Thirteen Attributes of Judgment**. Because of this, they are all within the **Mystery of Faith** <note>The Kabbalistic understanding of the unity of the Divine</note>, so that all is found to be one. In this way, the Tabernacle consists of thirteen colors/materials: 
<note>Exodus 25:3-7</note>
->**"Gold, silver, and brass; blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen and goats' hair; tanned ram skins, fine leather, and acacia wood; oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense; onyx stones and stones for setting."**<-

Come and see: these thirteen colors/materials allude to known spiritual levels. This is because the Tabernacle was made according to the pattern of the realm above. Through this, the world was sustained. Because of this, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: 
->**"And let them take for Me an offering."** <note>Exodus 25:2</note><-
It is written "take for **Me**" because all the spiritual levels are brought near within one mystery, and they shall all be within one Name. For the Holy One, blessed be He, is called by this Name. And what is it? It is the **Assembly of Israel** <note>original: "Knesset Yisrael"; in Kabbalah, this refers to the Shekhinah, the Divine Presence that dwells among the people</note>, which is the mystery of the **Holy Name**. Because of this, it is written, "take for Me an offering," for she [the Shekhinah] alone contains all of them within this mystery.

<summary>This page discusses the mystical requirement of joy in divine service, citing King David and the Priests as examples, and explains how the thirteen materials of the Tabernacle represent the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy and the unity of the Divine Name.</summary>

-> **Teaching: The Descent into the World** <-
<note>A "Matnitin" is a short, rhythmic mystical lesson in the Zohar, often modeled after the style of the Mishnah.</note>

It was taught: When the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to create the world, He made all creatures and established each and every one in its proper place. At that time, the Lamp of Lamps <note>original: "Butzina de-Butzinin," a mystical term for the source of Divine light</note> shone and brought forth lights to the worlds. And when the time appeared for the soul to descend to the world, the Holy One, Blessed be He, called to that soul and said to her: "My daughter, go to that world and enter into that body." The <term>soul</term> <note>original: "Nishmata"</note> opened her mouth and said: "Master of the Universe, it is enough for me that I dwell in this place beneath Your <term>Throne of Glory</term> <note>original: "Kursi Yekara," the highest celestial realm where souls originate</note>, and I do not wish to go to another world, for I fear that my deeds will become defiled." The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to her: "It is for this purpose that you were created: to be in that world, to exert yourself in the Torah, to know Me, and to become complete in all things." Then that soul descends against her will. And regarding this we have learned: "Against your will you are formed, and against your will you are born." <note>A quote from the Mishnah, Pirkei Avot 4:22</note>

...This is because it stands above and is called **Greatness** <note>original: "Gedulah," the Divine attribute of expansive lovingkindness</note>.

Rabbi Yosei opened:
> **"O Lord God, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness..."** <note>Deuteronomy 3:24</note>.

Behold, we have established that this **greatness** is the **Right Side** <note>the side of mercy and grace</note>. And here it is written **"Your greatness"**; what does **"Your greatness"** mean specifically? Rather, this is what we have learned: **"Your greatness"** refers to the Right Side, and **"Your mighty hand"** refers to the **Left Side** <note>original: "Smala," the side of Gevurah or strict judgment</note>. As it is written:
> **"Your right hand, O Lord, shatters the enemy"** <note>Exodus 15:6</note>.

Come and see! Many times Moses offered his prayer before the **<term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term>** <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu," the standard name for God in the Zohar</note>, and at this time, he was included within these "sides" we have mentioned. **"You have begun to show"** means he came to know that which he did not know previously. Moses saw all the **levels** <note>original: "Dargin," the stages of divine emanation</note> and the **Higher Wisdom** <note>original: "Chokhmata Ila'ah"</note> in a way that no other human ever saw. Why then is it written here **"Your greatness"**? It is because **"Your greatness"** is the level called **Greatness** (*Gedulah*), while **"Your mighty hand"** is the level called **Strength** <note>original: "Gevurah," associated with judgment and restraint</note>. This is the "harsh judgment" known as the "Mighty Hand." It was because of this that Moses offered his prayer—so that the Divine would not lead him through this particular "side" of strict judgment.
> **"For what god is there in heaven or on earth..."** <note>Deuteronomy 3:24</note>.

Come and see! There is no worship and no wisdom like the wisdom and worship of the **Holy One, Blessed be He**. Come and see, regarding the "faithful prophet" <note>Moses</note>, it is written:
> **"And Israel saw the Great Hand"** <note>Exodus 14:31</note>.

This refers to the Right Side. Concerning this, it is written **"Your greatness."** Come and see, regarding Joshua it is written:
> **"Begin the song of the Lord in Israel"** <note>original: "Hachal," a reference to Joshua's leadership or a liturgical tradition; the Zohar often draws linguistic parallels between biblical figures</note>.

In the beginning, Moses saw the **Higher Wisdom**, the supreme levels, and the vision of that "Pleasantness of the Lord" when it is revealed and present. Therefore it is written **"You have begun,"** for that is the starting point of all things.

# Pekudei

## Main Text (Zohar)

Come and see: in the same way that everything exists, these stand corresponding to those. 
The mystery of the Tabernacle is established thus: that all its components stand within the upper mystery. 
Come and see: there are fifty that stand in this side and in that side. 
Why are there fifty hooks of gold and fifty hooks of copper? 
Because there are fifty gates <note>original: "Sod khamishim sha'arei binah." This refers to the Fifty Gates of Understanding, a Kabbalistic concept representing the levels of divine wisdom through which the world was created.</note>; 
all of them stand within the upper mystery. These are from the male side <note>original: "sitra de-dkhura." In Kabbalah, the male side represents the flow of mercy and the higher divine persona, Zeir Anpin.</note> 
and those are from the female side <note>original: "sitra de-nukba." The female side represents the recipient of divine light and the persona of Malchut (Kingship).</note>. 
The fifty of gold are from the male side, which is the side of gold <note>While gold often represents Judgment (Gevurah), here it is associated with the higher masculine brilliance of the upper realms.</note>. 
And the fifty of copper are from the female side, which is the side of copper. 
This is in order to unite one with the other, so that everything becomes one. 
It is written <note>Exodus 26:6</note>: 
> "And you shall join the curtains one to another with the hooks, and the **Tabernacle shall be one**." 
**"And the Tabernacle shall be one"**—this is the mystery of the male and female joined as one. 
And for this reason, it is called "one." 
And likewise, regarding the fifty hooks of copper, it is written <note>Exodus 26:11</note>: 
> "And you shall join the tent, and **it shall be one**." 
This is the mystery of the female, who is called "Tabernacle" <note>original: "Mishkan." The Tabernacle is often used as a metaphor for the Shekhinah or the feminine divine presence dwelling among humanity.</note>, and **"it shall be one,"** all within the mystery of the upper realms.

Although the previous page discussed the "Fifty Gates of Understanding" in the context of the desert sanctuary, this page, from the portion of Balak, shifts focus to the spiritual hierarchy of human appeals to the Divine. It contrasts the formal prayers of great figures like Moses and David with the raw, desperate "Prayer of the Poor."</meta>

# Balak

## Main Text (Zohar)

When one performs this with diligence and focus of the heart, so that no other thought enters <note>The text emphasizes "kavanah," or directed intention, suggesting that extraneous thoughts act as spiritual barriers during prayer.</note> to push that person away and remove him from the world. Because of this, a person must focus his heart and his will in his prayer. This is the "service of the heart." Regarding this it is written, **"But I am prayer"** <note>Psalm 109:4. The Hebrew literally reads "And I prayer," suggesting David’s entire being became an act of prayer.</note>.

We have established that there are three specific prayers. One is **"A prayer of Moses, the man of God"** <note>Psalm 90:1</note>. One is **"A prayer of David"** <note>Psalm 86:1</note>. And one is **"A prayer of the poor man when he is faint"** <note>Psalm 102:1</note>. Which of them is most significant? You must say: the prayer of the poor man. 

This prayer precedes the prayer of Moses, and precedes the prayer of David, and precedes all other prayers in the world. What is the reason? <note>original: "m"t" - abbreviation for "mai ta'ama"</note> Because the poor man is of a broken heart, and it is written, **"The Lord is close to the brokenhearted"** <note>Psalm 34:19</note>. 

The poor man is constantly in a "quarrel" with <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu." This is the standard Zoharic name for the Divine, representing the masculine aspect of God (Tiferet).</note>, and <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> listens and hears his words. As soon as he prays his prayer, he opens all the windows of the firmaments, and all the other prayers that ascend to the heights are pushed aside by that poor man. 

Because of this, it is written, **"A prayer of the poor man when he is faint [ya'atof]"**. "Faint" is a language of "delaying" or "wrapping," just as you say, **"But when the cattle were feeble [ha-atufim], he did not put them in"** <note>Genesis 30:42. The Zohar uses a linguistic play on the Hebrew root 'Ataf'—which can mean to wrap oneself, to faint, or to be late/slow—to argue that the poor man's prayer causes all other prayers to wait.</note>. For he creates a "wrapping" (a delay) for all the prayers in the world, and they do not enter until his prayer has entered. 

And <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> says: "Let all prayers be delayed, and let this prayer enter before Me. I do not require a court of justice to judge between Me and him; let his path be made straight before Me." 

All other prayers are merely "prayers," but the prayer of the poor is a "pouring out," as it says, **"And before the Lord he pours out his plea"** <note>Psalm 102:1</note>. Why? Because all other prayers require the will and focus of the heart, but the prayer of the poor is not so. Rather, it is a pouring out of the soul and the heart and the will before <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term>. 

This is the prayer that stands before <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> constantly, and therefore it precedes all other prayers. We have established that when this prayer ascends, all those who guard the gates and openings—all of them open for it, and it is not delayed at all. And <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> takes delight in it...

<summary>This page discusses the mystical superiority of the "Prayer of the Poor" (Psalm 102) over those of Moses and David, explaining that God prioritizes the raw, emotional "pouring out" of a broken heart over formal liturgical intentions.</summary>
<keywords>Prayer of the Poor, Moses, David, Kavanah, Broken Heart, Heavenly Gates, Psalm 102, Kudsha Brich Hu, Pouring out the soul</keywords>

# Genesis (Bereishit)

## Main Text (Zohar)

And if you should ask, what is the mystery of this word *Bereishit* <note>original: "In the beginning"</note> as we have learned: "In the beginning God created" <note>Genesis 1:1</note>? It is because this word includes all supernal mysteries, and from there, all mysteries begin. Within Thought, which is **Wisdom** <note>original: "Chokhmah"</term>, the first of the emanations</note>, **the Holy One, Blessed be He** <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> gazed and fashioned everything that was needed to exist, because Thought includes everything. And regarding this we have learned: *Bereishit* [In the beginning] can be read as *Bara Shit* [He created six] <note>A classic Zoharic wordplay splitting the word 'Bereishit' into 'Bara' (created) and 'Shit' (the Aramaic word for six)</note>, because all those six supernal days <note>The six Sefirot or divine attributes that drive the creation of the world</note> are included in this place. From there they emerge, and from there they were made.

---

Rabbi Eleazar said, what is the meaning of that which is written:
> **The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands.** <note>Psalms 19:2</note>
"The heavens" refers to the supernal heavens that are suspended in that level which is the mystery of Wisdom. "Declare" refers to the mystery of the light that shines from it to all. "The glory of God" <note>original: "Kevod El"</note> is the supernal glory that shines from within the Supernal Thought. "And the firmament proclaims the work of His hands" refers to those six days that emerge from the supernal firmament.

---

**This first commandment** <note>The beginning of the exposition on the 613 commandments within the Zohar</note> is to know **the Holy One, Blessed be He**, and to know that He rules over all, and everything is within His authority, and there is nothing that is outside of His authority. And regarding this it is written:
> **Know the God of your father and serve Him.** <note>1 Chronicles 28:9</note>
And because of this, a person needs to contemplate every single day the levels of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and to know Him. And this is the mystery of *Bereishit* [In the beginning], because it is the beginning <note>original: "reshita"</note> of everything, and all mysteries, both above and below, are included in this word.

---

## Main Text (Tikkunei Zohar)

[...End of the 21st Rectification]
...for there are five openings above and two below. This is because every human being possesses five openings in the head: the two eyes, the two ears, and the mouth. There are also two below: the sign of the covenant <note>The organ of circumcision</note> and the "gate of the ring" <note>The anus</note>. These seven openings correspond to the seven "voices" mentioned by King David in the Book of Psalms: **"Ascribe to the Lord, O sons of the mighty..."** <note>Psalms 29:1. The psalm repeats the phrase "The voice of the Lord" seven times</note>. They also correspond to the seven voices spoken by the faithful prophets in the Song of Songs. Furthermore, these are the seven openings within the **Shekhinah** <term>Shekhinah: The Divine Presence, viewed as the feminine aspect of God</term> which are the seven days of Creation. They are also the seven rivers that flow out from Eden. This is because the colleagues have established the principle: "All sevens are beloved." Some of these are above and some are below. Those above are the seven heavens, and those below are the seven lands. These seven openings of the Shekhinah correspond to the seven **Sefirot** <term>Sefirot: The ten attributes or emanations through which God reveals Himself</term>. They are open in every place because every human being is made in the "image" of the Shekhinah...

---

**Rabbi Shimon said:** There are five openings that are like the five fingers of the hand. This is because every single finger has an opening within it, and that opening is positioned above the finger. These five openings correspond to the five fingers of the hand. They are "five against five," and they are all open in every place through their joints, which are arranged in order. There are also five openings in the foot, corresponding to the five toes of the foot. These are open above, corresponding to the five "Strengths" <note>original: "Gevurot"</note> which are the letters *Mantsapa"kh* <note>original: "מנצפ"ך" - The five Hebrew letters (Mem, Nun, Tsadi, Pe, Khaf) that change their shape when appearing at the end of a word. In Kabbalah, these "final" letters represent restricted energy or Judgment</note>. These five openings also correspond to the five toes of the left foot. They are five against five, representing the five Kindnesses <note>original: "Chasadim"</note> and the five Strengths <note>original: "Gevurot"</note>.

->**The 22nd Rectification**<-

**Bereishit** <note>original: "In the beginning"</note>. This can be read as *Beit-Reshit* <note>Two beginnings</note>. These are two "openings" which are **Wisdom** <note>original: "Chokhmah"</note> and **Understanding** <note>original: "Binah"</note>. The letter *Beit* <note>The first letter of the Torah, numerical value 2</note> refers to the Shekhinah, who is the "opening" or gate above all other openings. This is what is written: **"This is the gate to the Lord; the righteous shall enter through it"** <note>Psalms 118:20</note>. She is the opening to all the Sefirot. For anyone who desires to enter before the King cannot enter except through this gate. These are the two openings that are the letters *Yod* and *Heh* <note>The first two letters of the four-letter Name of God</note>. *Yod* is the opening of Wisdom. *Heh* is the opening of Understanding. These correspond to the two eyes of the head, the two ears, the two nostrils, and the two lips of the mouth...

## Main Text (Zohar)

...and he called its name <term>Gilead</term>. What does this come to teach us? It teaches that until Jacob arrived, the <term>Shekhinah</term> <note>The Divine Presence, the feminine aspect of God</note> did not dwell upon it. Once Jacob came and was joined with the <term>Shekhinah</term>, it was then called <term>Gilead</term>. **Gal-Ed** <note>The name Gilead is broken into two words: Gal (heap/reveal) and Ed (witness)</note>. He is the **Heap [Gal]** and she is the **Witness [Ed]**. What is the meaning of **Heap [Gal]**? It is as you would say:
> Unveil [Gal] my eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of your Torah (Psalms 119:18)

And **Witness [Ed]** is as you would say:
> And a witness to the lands (Isaiah 42:10 - *with a variation in phrasing*) <note>The exact verse in Isaiah reads 'His praise from the end of the earth'; the manuscript likely references a specific midrashic teaching connecting the word 'Ed' (witness) to this concept</note>

And because of this, Jacob called it <term>Gilead</term>. Now, if you should say: "But Laban was the one who called it so!" as it is written:
> And Laban said: "This heap [gal] is a witness [ed] between me and you today." Therefore was its name called Gilead (Genesis 31:48)

The truth is that Laban said it and Jacob said it. Laban said "This heap is a witness between me and you" because he comes from the side of impurity <note>original: "sitra de-masavuta" — the 'other side' or the realm of spiritual uncleanness</note> and he sought to draw that "heap" toward his own side. For this reason, Laban called it **Yegar Sahadutha** <note>original: "Yegar Sahadutha" — the Aramaic translation of "Heap of Witness"</note> in the Aramaic tongue. But Jacob called it **Gilead** in the Holy Tongue <note>Hebrew</note>, because he comes from the side of holiness.

---

**Rabbi Yehuda opened**:
> Blessings are upon the head of the righteous: but violence covers the mouth of the wicked (Proverbs 10:6)

"Blessings are upon the head of the <term>Righteous One [Tzadik]</term>." Who is the "Head"? This is the head of the entire body. And who is he? This is the <term>Righteous One [Tzadik]</term> who is the <term>Foundation [Yesod]</term> of the world. All blessings dwell within him and depend upon him, and from there they emerge to all the members of the body. And that **Righteous One** takes everything and waters all those levels below.

Come and see: all those supernal blessings are all found in that place called the **Righteous One**. Because of this, it is written: "Blessings are upon the head of the righteous." And all the blessings with which Israel is blessed, all of them emerge from that place.

---

## Main Text (Zohar)

As it is written: **"Let the pleasantness of the Lord our God be upon us; and establish the work of our hands upon us;** <note>Psalms 90:17</note>
**and the work of our hands, establish it."** "And establish the work of our hands upon us"—this refers to the <term>artistry</term> <note>original: "umanuta" — refers to the divine craftsmanship or design</note> of the upper world. "And the work of our hands, establish it"—this refers to the artistry of the lower world. And all is one. In this same manner is the artistry of the work of the <term>Tabernacle</term> <note>original: "Mishkan"</note>. For it is just like the work of the heavens and the earth. And it is just like the "work of Man" <note>Adam</note>. For all is one. This secret stands on its own, and that secret stands on its own. And regarding this it is written: **"And let the pleasantness of the Lord our God be upon us."** This refers to the **Pleasantness** <note>original: "Noam" — often associated with the Sefirah of Binah (Understanding)</note> that comes from the <term>World to Come</term> <note>original: "Olam Ha-Ba"</note>. It flows and illuminates all those lights that shine. And when this Pleasantness shines, then it is called **Peace** <note>original: "Shalom"</note>. At that time, all the worlds are in joy, all the worlds are in perfection, and all the worlds are in radiance. And regarding this it is written: **"And let the pleasantness of the Lord our God be upon us. And establish the work of our hands upon us."** This is the secret of the artistry of the upper world. Because the <term>Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>original: "Kudsha Brich Hu"</note> is the host of the upper world, and He desired to be a host below. Therefore, there is an artistry here just like the one above. "And the work of our hands, establish it"—this is the secret of the artistry of the lower world. And because of this, the word "establish" <note>Hebrew: "konana"</note> is mentioned twice: once for above and once for below. Regarding this it is written: **"The Sanctuary, O Lord, which Your hands have established"** <note>Exodus 15:17</note>. Two hands: the Right and the Left. The right arm and the left arm. For this reason, it is written "Your hands [plural] have established," and it is not written "Your hand [singular] has established." And in this manner it is written: **"And the work of our hands, establish it."** "Establish it" <note>The Hebrew suffix "-hu" in "konanehu" functions as a singular "it" but is interpreted here as a unification of the Right and Left energies</note>—this refers to the Right and the Left. For this artistry is within the Right and the Left. Because the Tabernacle exists through the Right and the Left. Therefore it is written "Establish it." And all the lights from above shone within the Tabernacle. Thus: **"Let the pleasantness of the Lord our God be upon us."** Then: **"And establish the work of our hands upon us."** Then it is called artistry, in the manner of the realm above. "And the work of our hands, establish it"—in the manner of the realm below. And all is one. Come and see: the Tabernacle above is in the likeness of the Tabernacle below. It is like the form of Man <note>Adam</note> who exists in supreme radiance, and he is comprised of Right and Left. Therefore, this artistry consists of all the works of Man. All of them are within this secret. Come and see: the Tabernacle below is...

<header>Vayishlach</header>

## Main Text (Zohar)

How do we know that all these things are found? Because they all stood before the Holy One, Blessed be He, by way of the Torah; for all the matters of the world, before they came into the world, stood before Him. In this same manner, Rabbi Elazar said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, taught Adam all those things in the world that have permanence, and they all stood before him as one.

Rabbi Shimon opened his discourse and said: **"The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament tells of His handiwork."** <note>Psalms 19:2</note> "The heavens"—this is the Holy One, Blessed be He. "Declare" (*mesaperim*)—what does "declare" mean? It means that they shine and illuminate with a radiance like the <term>splendor</term> <note>original: "Zohar"</note> mentioned in the verse: **"And those who are wise shall shine like the splendor of the firmament."** <note>Daniel 12:3</note> For they shine and sparkle. Why are they called "those who declare" (*mesaperim*)? Because they are <term>Sefirot</term> <note>original: "Sapiran" — the divine emanations or "sapphire-like" radiances</note> above and below.

"And the firmament tells of His handiwork"—these are the works of the Holy One, Blessed be He, which are performed on the earth. And these "firmaments" are open to bring forth prophecy to the world and to the prophets of truth who "tell." What do they "tell"? **"Declaring the end from the beginning..."** <note>Isaiah 46:10</note> And this is the meaning of "the firmament tells." This "firmament" is the one that contains the sun, the moon, the stars, and the constellations. And this is the firmament that is the "gate of heaven" to bring forth the <term>Secrets of Faith</term> <note>original: "Razei de-Mehemanuta"</note> to the world.

And this is what is meant by: **"Day to day gushes forth speech, and night to night reveals knowledge."** <note>Psalms 19:3</note> "Day to day gushes forth speech"—these are the holy, upper levels <note>The "degrees" or ranks of the Sefirot</note> that shine from the side above, which shines <note>The manuscript notes a possible correction here from "damiher" to "danehir" (shines)</note> to the level beneath it, for the Secret of Faith depends upon it. And this is "gushes forth speech." What is "gushes forth speech" (*yabi'a omer*)? It refers to a word that goes out from the mouth in a whisper, for "speech" (*omer*) is a whisper. It is the secret of <term>Higher Wisdom</term> <note>original: "Chokhmah Ila'ah"</note> which is not revealed, and it is called "speech" (*omer*). Because of this, "day to day gushes forth speech, and night to night reveals knowledge."

And this is the secret of the lower levels, for they all offer praise, sing songs, and laud the Holy Name, in order to show that His dominion is over them all. This is what is written: **"There is no speech, and there are no words, their voice is not heard... Their line goes out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world."** <note>Psalms 19:4-5</note> "To the end of the world" certainly, for they all come from the "end of the world," and from there the words go out. And because of this, "The heavens declare the glory of God"—"declare" (*mesaperim*) means they illuminate the world from the upper and lower Sefirot as one.

<meta>This page continues the Kabbalistic exploration of the creation narrative. It provides a mystical commentary on the origins of the universe, focusing on the transition from the infinite divine thought to the first "point" of existence and the subsequent expansion into a "palace."</meta>

<page-num>153</page-num>
<header>Vayechi</header>

## Main Text (Zohar)

[...And what was said: "In the beginning God created..." etc.] <note>Opening words are very faint; this section quotes Genesis 1:1</note>
**When the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to create the world**, He engraved an engraving in the <term>supernal radiance</term> <note>original Aramaic: *tehiru ila'ah* — the pure, blinding light of the infinite</note>.
He struck the <term>Lamp of Darkness</term> <note>original: *butzina de-kardinuta* — a powerful, concentrated force of divine judgment that acts like a chisel to carve out space for creation</note> and there emerged, at the head of Thought, a single spark of darkness.
This spark became a single <term>supernal point</term> <note>original: *nekuda ila'ah* — representing the Sefirah of Wisdom (Chokhmah), the first infinitesimal point of being</note>, and this is the most hidden of all hidden things. This is <term>"In the beginning"</term> <note>Hebrew: *Bereshit*</note>, the first utterance of all.
When this point expanded, it became a <term>palace</term> <note>original: *heikhala* — representing the Sefirah of Understanding (Binah), which acts as a vessel or "palace" for the wisdom of the point</note>. He engraved an engraving within it and was crowned within this palace. And this is the secret of: "In the beginning [He] created six." <note>The Zohar here reads the Hebrew word *Bereshit* as two words: *Bara Shit*, meaning "He created six."</note>
What is written? "In the beginning God created." This [name, "God" or *Elohim*] is the palace wherein this point is found, and for this reason it is written: "In the beginning God created."
This [the point] created it [the palace] through the mystery of the point. "In the beginning God created." He created six from this side and six from that side—from the side above and from the side below.
And these are the <term>six sides</term> <note>original: *shit sitrin* — referring to the six emotive Sefirot or the six directions of the physical world</note>, and all of them emerge from within a single point.
And there are six from this side and six from that side; therefore, it is written six times "the heavens and the earth," all according to the mystery of this supernal point.
And the mystery is: "In the beginning God created." "In the beginning" is the mystery of the supernal point. "Created" is the mystery of the palace. "God" is the name that emerges from within the palace.
"In the beginning God created." In the beginning, when this point expanded and became a <term>palace</term>,
He engraved an engraving within it and was crowned within this palace. This is
the secret of "In the beginning [He] created six." This is the secret of all hidden things:
that He created six, and the six sides are all grasped
within this point. And this is "In the beginning"...

<summary>This page explores the mystical creation of the universe, interpreting the first word of the Bible ("Bereshit") as a process where a hidden divine spark expands into a "palace" and produces the six fundamental directions of existence. It explains the divine name "Elohim" as a manifestation of this celestial architecture.</summary>

# Vayigash <note>original: *Vayigash*, meaning "And he approached." This is the beginning of the Torah portion where Judah approaches Joseph to plead for Benjamin's release.</note>

## Main Text (Zohar)

Another explanation: **"Then Judah approached him"** <note>Genesis 44:18</note>. Rabbi Eleazar began his discourse by quoting the verse: **"For behold, the kings assembled, they passed by together. They saw it, and so they were amazed; they were dismayed, they fled in haste"** <note>Psalms 48:5-6</note>. Come and see! The companions have already established the meaning of this verse. However, the phrase **"for behold, the kings assembled"** refers specifically to Judah and Joseph. They are both called "kings," and here they drew near to one another and were joined as one.

**"They passed by together"**—this is understood as it is written in the book of Job: "He passes by me and I do not see" <note>Job 9:11</note>. Just as those kings passed together, it was initially with contention and a discovery of anger between them. **"They saw it, and so they were amazed"**—when the other nations saw the union and the closeness of these two leaders as one, they were then amazed, dismayed, and fled in haste. If not for this union between Judah and Joseph, the other kings of the world would not be able to endure. Because they are united as one and there is peace between them, the other kings of the nations are dismayed and hurried away, for they are unable to exert their own rule over the world.

Rav Hamnuna the Elder said: **"For behold, the kings assembled"** refers to <term>the Holy One, Blessed be He</term> <note>The masculine aspect of the Divine, often associated with the attribute of Mercy</note> and <term>His Divine Presence</term> <note>original: *Shekhinah*. The feminine, indwelling aspect of God that accompanies the Jewish people in exile</note>, who assembled and united as one. **"They passed by together"** means that all the forces of enmity that existed in the world passed away and vanished, and the world sat in peace. **"They saw it, and so they were amazed"**—these are the other kings of the idolatrous nations who, when they witnessed the <term>unification</term> <note>original: *yihuda*. A central kabbalistic concept referring to the restoring of harmony between different Divine attributes</note> of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and His Divine Presence, they were struck with wonder. As the verse says, "They saw"—they saw, as it were, that union and that great light that shines, and the peace found in the world. Then they were all dismayed and hid themselves; they all fled and went away, unable to rule at all. All of this occurred because Judah and Joseph were joined as one.

Come and see: Judah is a king and Joseph is a king, and they approached each other and were joined as one. What is the reason for this? It is because Judah represents the mystery of the heavenly <term>Kingdom</term> <note>original: *Malkhut*. The final of the ten Sefirot (Divine emanations), associated with earthly sovereignty and the feminine principle</note>, and Joseph represents the mystery of the <term>Righteous One, the foundation of the world</term> <note>original: *Tzadik Yesod Olam*. The Sefirah of Yesod, which acts as the channel or "procreative" force that feeds into Malkhut</note>. When these two join together, there is joy in all the worlds, and all the other kings are amazed, dismayed, and flee.

And come and see the secret of the matter: when these two kings approached each other, they became joined and prepared as one, because both are kings. Judah is a king, as the sages established: "Judah is a lion’s whelp..." <note>Genesis 49:9</note>. Joseph is a king, as it is written: "And Joseph was the ruler over the land" <note>Genesis 41:43</note>. Therefore, since both are kings, they joined together. Why did they join? Because from them emerge all the heavenly hosts and camps that guard the outside. Judah takes charge of all the hosts and camps of the "Left Side," and Joseph takes charge of all the hosts and camps of the "Right Side." When these two join together, the other kings are dismayed and flee. Rav Yeiva the Elder said...

<summary>This page provides a mystical interpretation of the meeting between Judah and Joseph, viewing their reconciliation as a mirror of the cosmic union between the Divine attributes of Yesod and Malkhut, which brings peace to the world and subdues opposing forces.</summary>
<keywords>Judah, Joseph, Vayigash, Shekhinah, Holy One Blessed be He, Malkhut, Yesod, Unification, Kabbalah, Zohar</keywords>

## Tosefta (Addition)

->**Tosefta**<- <note>original: *Tosefta*, meaning "addition" or "supplement." These are additional mystical teachings often appended to the main sections of the Zohar.</note>

**At the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, desired to create the world** and He revealed His <term>Will</term>, He brought forth springs of <term>lights</term> <note>original: *nehorin*; these are the emanations of divine energy that form the building blocks of reality</note>. They were all included in a single <term>Will</term>, and this Will is the <term>secret of faith</term>. When the light shone to the four <term>sides of the world</term> <note>the four cardinal directions</note>, it spread, one within the other and the other within the one. These are the four <term>letters</term> <note>original: *atvun*</note> of the <term>Holy Name</term> <note>The Tetragrammaton, Y-H-V-H</note> which take hold of one another. This is the secret of the matter: when these four letters emerged, they were all as one. And the secret is **YaH** and it is **VaH**... <note>The letters of the Divine Name are often divided into two pairs: Y-H (representing the upper realms of Wisdom and Understanding) and V-H (representing the lower realms and the world as we experience it). Their union signifies cosmic balance.</note>

... which is the **secret of the word** in which all things are included. At the time when those lights emerged, it was found to be the <term>secret of faith</term>... and when this secret was revealed, it was as one...

[The image displays standardized color patches and a gray scale card laid over a piece of aged parchment or paper.]

**Handwritten numeral:** 78
<note>The number 78 in the upper-left corner is a modern archival mark used to track the sequence of images during the digitization process.</note>

**Technical Reference:**
*   **Color Control Patches:** These vibrant squares of color (cyan, magenta, yellow, red, green, and blue) allow digital imaging specialists to verify that the colors in the photograph are true to life.
*   **Gray Scale:** This strip of shades ranging from white to black helps in adjusting the contrast and exposure of the digital file, ensuring that the subtle textures of the ancient parchment are visible to researchers.
